home_pitcher_note: This home opener will mark the start of what Glavine hopes to be a good homecoming. The veteran southpaw, who notched his 300th career win last year, pitched in Atlanta from 1987-2002.
away_pitcher_note: Snell will be making his first career Opening Day start. Fresh off signing a multiyear deal that could potentially keep him in Pittsburgh for the next five years, he will look to repeat last year's success.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens earned a spot in the rotation with the poise and maturity he showed during Spring Training. Acquired from the Tigers in October, the 22-year-old right-hander has good control of his 93 mph fastball and has the ability to consistently throw a sharp slider for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: After leading the Pirates with 14 wins last season, Gorzelanny looks to begin just his second full season in Pittsburgh. The lefty pitched past the 200-inning mark last year and made a staff-high 32 starts. A year ago, Gorzelanny followed a shaky spring by jumping out to start the season 3-0 with a 2.05 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Hampton's first start since Aug. 19, 2005. The injury-plagued southpaw has missed the past two seasons while recovering from separate elbow surgeries.  Throughout Spring Training, he impressed with his patented sinker and a curveball that he hasn't shown since the early days of his career.
away_pitcher_note: Duke makes the start in place of Paul Maholm, who was scratched with a stiff back. In his only start against the Braves last year, Duke took the loss after allowing four earned runs in 5 2/3 innings. Overall, the Pittsburgh left-hander is 1-2 with a 3.43 ERA in his three career appearances against the Atlanta team. Duke has, however, been hit hard by Atlanta right-fielder Jeff Francoeur, who is 5-for-8 with three extra-base hits against the southpaw.

home_pitcher_note: If not for a bout of shoulder tendinitis this spring, Olsen was in line to be the Opening Day starter. Now, he is slotted fourth. The 24-year-old has top-of-the-rotation talent, but he's dealt with inconsistencies. Last year, he struggled with his command, and a high walk count led to a disappointing campaign.
away_pitcher_note: The results haven't been there for Morris this spring, but the right-hander has reiterated that he continues to feel more in sync after each subsequent start. After being acquired from the Giants last July, Morris went 3-4 with a 6.10 ERA in 11 starts for Pittsburgh. Morris, the veteran of the staff, can typically be expected to give the Pirates at least six innings per start, though it remains to be seen how successful he can still be after a few years of sub-par results.

home_pitcher_note: A six-run fourth inning on Opening Day led to a rough afternoon for Hendrickson, who makes his second start of the season on Saturday. The 6-foot-9 left-hander was tagged for those six runs in five innings. He was sailing along until he threw 36 pitches in the fourth and was unable to work out of two-out trouble. For his career, Hendrickson is 1-0 with a 3.27 ERA in two games against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm's back stiffness prompted a swap of starters for the Bucs, with Zach Duke filling in for Maholm on Thursday and Maholm slated to go in this game. Maholm opens the season as arguably the least talked about pitcher in the Pirates' rotation, but looking like he could be poised to make a big step forward in his career. He has shown an ability to rely on all four of his pitches consistently throughout Spring Training and has worked to limit the amount of walks that he issues. The left-hander came into camp in peak condition and will look to improve on his 10-win season from a year ago.

home_pitcher_note: Running up a high pitch count hurt VandenHurk in his season debut. Despite being staked to a 4-0 lead after two innings against the Mets, the 22-year-old was lifted after three-plus innings because his count was up to 76. He yielded three runs and exited without a decision. This will be VandenHurk's first appearance against the Pirates. Minimizing pitches and working deeper into games remains a work in progress for VandenHurk, who three times last year lasted as long as six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Though Snell gave up four runs in six innings of work against the Braves in his Opening Day start on Monday, the right-hander continued to show progress in being able to pitch consistently to both the inner and outer halves of the plate. With a fastball and slider anchoring Snell?s pitch repertoire, look for him to continue increasing the frequency with which he pitches inside. Snell will be looking for his first career victory against the Marlins. He has faced them twice before, allowing a total of 10 runs in 7 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After giving Ian Snell the Opening Day start, manager John Russell gave Gorzelanny the start in the team's home opener. Gorzelanny wasn't at his sharpest in his first outing of the season, though to his credit, the left-hander managed to limit the damage to just three runs in six innings. Hitters consistently went deep into the count against the left-hander, and his command was somewhat erratic throughout the night.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly will be careful with his first pitch. Milwaukee's Rickie Weeks launched Lilly's first offering this season over the left-field wall in the lefty's last start. Lilly took the loss, giving up four runs on five hits over 4 2/3 innings. He did strike out four. He struggled with his fastball -- he didn't have command or location. That's a bad combination.

home_pitcher_note: While he didn't factor in the decision last Thursday against the Braves, Duke showed some promising signs that he is back on the right track after a disappointing 2007. He is using a longer stride and lessening the time between his pitches, which seems to have the lefty much more in sync. Duke also has a newfound confidence that is a result of him finally being healthy again. Duke is 4-2 with a 2.10 ERA in eight starts against the Cubs in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster had a strong spring, and proved it was no fluke. In his first start, he gave up two runs, one earned, on three hits over six innings while striking out five. This was his first start in more than two years after being the Cubs' closer. He was relaxed, used all his pitches, and was in command. It was his first win as a starter since April 16, 2005, when he beat the Pirates, 4-3.

home_pitcher_note: Morris wasn't fooling the Marlins offense in his first start of the season, as the veteran right-hander was knocked around for eight hits and four runs (three earned) in five innings. The Marlins pushed Morris to have to throw 98 pitches, and most of what they hit was hit on the nose. Morris continues to try and tinker with his delivery and needs to find better location with his fastball. In 30 career appearances against the Cubs (27 starts), Morris is 12-8 with a 4.50 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hill gave up two runs on four hits and three walks over six innings in his first start of the season, and he pitched well. The problem was one of those walks came with two outs and J.R. Towles followed with a two-run homer. It's all part of growing pains for Hill. He didn't get much run support, something he had to deal with last year as well. The lefty ranked second in the Majors in lowest run support in 2007. Maybe he needs to take his teammates out to dinner.

home_pitcher_note: The five runs that Maholm allowed in five innings in his first start of the season mask what was an otherwise outstanding first appearance for the lefty. Maholm struck out a career-high nine hitters, but took the loss after allowing a grand slam to Florida's Mike Jacobs. Maholm has faced the Reds 10 times in his career, which is more than he has faced any other team in the Majors. The Pittsburgh lefty is 2-3 with a 4.84 ERA in those 10 appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez was sensational in his Reds debut, allowing just one run on five hits in 5 2/3 innings. He walked two and struck out eight in a 95-pitch effort before exiting the mound in the fifth to a rousing ovation from the crowd at Great American Ball Park. The 24-year-old right-hander was 2-0 with a 2.70 ERA in six spring games, including two starts. He impressed with his ability to change speeds. He could freeze hitters with an excellent changeup that worked off of his mid-90s mph fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Snell looked in midseason form his last time out, sealing his first win of the season while allowing just four hits and one earned run in six innings of work. He relied heavily on his curveball and fastball, and as a result, Snell fanned 10 Marlins hitters in the game. That total was one off his career high. Snell has not had the best of success versus the Reds in seven starts against the Cincinnati ballclub. Coming into Saturday's game, Snell is 2-4 with a 5.31 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo's pitches were tattooed often during a 5-3 loss to the Phillies on Monday afternoon at Great American Ball Park. The right-hander allowed four home runs, two by Pat Burrell, during his 5 2/3 innings. Overall, he allowed five earned runs and nine hits without a walk and six strikeouts. In two starts vs. the Pirates last season, totaling 10 innings, Arroyo was 0-1 with a 6.30 ERA with four walks and six strikeouts. He is 1-3 with a 4.65 ERA in five career starts against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: The lack of control from Gorzelanny has been a surprise in his first two outings of the season. He lasted a career-short 2 1/3 innings in his start on Monday, allowing four walks, six hits and seven runs before being pulled. He has been falling behind hitters consistently, and as a result, has been throwing too many pitches early on, which sets the tone for an early exit. Gorzelanny will be making his third career start against the Reds. He is 1-1 with a 6.75 ERA against the Cincinnati ballclub.
away_pitcher_note: Through his first two big league outings, Cueto has zero walks allowed and 18 strikeouts. The 22-year-old right hander gave up two earned runs and five hits with eight strikeouts but got a no-decision in a 3-2 loss to the Brewers in 10 innings. Cueto, who struck out the side in the second, made one mistake in the game. A slider hung over the middle of the plate and was hit for a solo homer by Bill Hall.

home_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda threw strikes and kept the Dodgers close early, but he couldn't stop the Diamondbacks from sweeping the series. Two of the four runs he allowed were unearned, but he let two leads get away, allowed nine hits and lost the game on a two-out single by Eric Byrnes. He was particularly effective throwing first-pitch strikes, but was hurt several times on 0-2 counts.
away_pitcher_note: With two strong starts under his belt, Duke continues to pile on the confidence that was missing a year ago. The left-hander set himself in great position to notch his first win of the season his last time out, but couldn't get the offensive support he needed to garner that win. Duke threw 116 pitches in seven innings in the outing against Chicago, allowing just one run, while striking out six. So far this year, he's shown a better job on maintaining his poise with runners on base and his pitches have had much better movement than they did a year ago.

home_pitcher_note: Kuo has replaced Esteban Loaiza in the rotation, in part because Loaiza had a rough first inning in his only start of the season, in part because Kuo has not allowed a run this season, in part because Kuo's brittle elbow is not well-suited for relief work. The early-season juggling is an indication that new manager Joe Torre is still getting acquainted with who his players are and what they can do. Kuo gives the Dodgers rotation a left-hander who is effective tying up right-handed hitters. The question about him has never been his stuff, but his health.
away_pitcher_note: Morris continues to battle the command and location of his pitches. As he gets into the middle of games, his pitches are getting flat and moving out and over the plate -? never a good combination. He?s not the staff ace that he was earlier this decade, though there is something positive to be taken from the fact that  he can typically be counted on to give the Pirates at least six innings per start. Morris has made 15 appearances (13 starts) against the Dodgers and is 4-5 with a 5.57 ERA against the Los Angeles club.

home_pitcher_note: What are the odds? For the second consecutive start, Brad Penny faced Jake Peavy and allowed the Padres a four-run, six-single inning. In this one, he was extended to 119 pitches over six innings, allowing 10 singles and three walks. Penny had no decisions in two starts against Pittsburgh last year.
away_pitcher_note: If it wasn't for a lengthy rain delay, Maholm would have pitched much deeper than the 5 1/3 innings his line score shows. Maholm allowed six hits, but kept the Reds scoreless before thunderstorms prompted his early exit. For the second straight start, Maholm showed excellent command of all four of his pitches, and he maintained much better consistency in getting ahead of hitters. Maholm will be facing the Dodgers for the fourth time in his career, though the lefty is still in search of his first win against the Los Angeles club. He is 0-2 with a 6.50 ERA in those previous three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hill has been tough to figure out. The lefty gave up three runs on four walks and three hits over three innings in his last start against the Pirates. He needed 30 pitches to get through the first inning, and was pulled after throwing 72. Only 34 were strikes. That ratio definitely has to improve. Lou Piniella says all Hill has to do is throw the ball. Apparently, the young lefty is trying to be too fine. He spent Saturday and Sunday of the Phillies series in the 'pen.
away_pitcher_note: Snell is the only Pirates starting pitcher to win this season; he pitched 6 1/3 innings for a 4-3 victory in his last start on April 11 against Cincinnati. He wasn't as sharp as he has been, allowing nine hits and walking two. Snell followed up a 9-2 win over Florida on April 6 despite striking out only two, down from 10 in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Making his first start in a week, Marquis held the Phillies to two runs on four hits over five innings. The right-hander had been sidelined with strep throat, and skipped one start. He pitched well, although he did walk five.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny silenced the rumors about possible shoulder problems with a solid outing in his last start on Sunday against the Reds. Coming off back-to-back ineffective outings, the southpaw hurled 6 1/3 innings and gave up just one run on four hits. He evened his record at 1-1 as the Pirates defeated the Reds, 9-1. The key for Gorzelanny was his command as he pounded the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster looks more and more comfortable as a starter. He gave up four runs on five hits and five walks over six-plus innings against the Reds in his last start on Tuesday. The right-hander, who was the Cubs' closer the last three years, has pitched at least six innings in each of his three games. He had a stellar start against the Pirates on April 9, holding them to one hit over seven scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Duke struggled with his command and location in his last start more than he had in either of his previous two. However, to the credit of the left-hander, he kept the Pirates offense well within reach of a win by limiting the damage to just three runs (two earned) in six innings. Duke continues to rely heavily on his sinker, and it?s been there for him with relative certainty all season. This will be Duke?s second start against the Cubs this season. He didn?t factor in the decision in the first one, though he allowed just one run in seven innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: To put it bluntly, Morris simply has shown very little command with his fastball in any of his three starts this season. He's rarely fooling hitters (evidenced by the 26 hits and 13 runs he's given up in 16 2/3 innings this season), and he has not been able to avoid the big inning in any of his three starts this season. Morris faced the Marlins earlier this month, allowing four runs (three earned) and eight hits in five innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: Aside from a seven-inning outing at Washington, three of Hendrickson's four starts have been either five- or five-plus-inning appearances. He comes off a 5 1/3-inning performance against the Braves, where he allowed three runs (two earned). Hendrickson is pitching to contact, as he has nine strikeouts in 22 2/3 innings. On April 5, the left-hander beat the Pirates in Miami, giving up three runs (one earned) in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Some bad first-inning bounces and a costly error rattled Maholm from the onset of his previous start and put him in a hole from which he would never climb out. He made it through five innings, but allowed a career-high 11 hits as well as six runs (four earned). Maholm's issues could be summed up in two words: poor command. His first start of the season came against the Marlins, when Florida's Mike Jacobs ruined the outing with a fifth-inning grand slam that would chase Maholm from the game. The lefty did, however, strike out nine Marlins in that game.
away_pitcher_note: The Braves uncorked on Nolasco for four homers in 4 2/3 innings in the right-hander's last start. The 25-year-old actually was one pitch away from getting out of big trouble in that game. Down by three in the fifth inning, he had two outs and an 0-2 count on Chipper Jones, who then connected on a homer to right. It sparked three straight blasts off Nolasco, who didn't last the inning. After opening the season in the bullpen, this will be Nolasco's third start. Lifetime against the Pirates, he is 1-1 with a 1.29 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Though Snell limited the Cubs to three runs in six innings of work (all the runs coming in the fourth) in his last start, he was ultimately hurt by the Pirates' lack of run support. After struggling in his previous start, Snell slowed himself down and said that he tried not to think as much about the location of his pitches. As a result, Snell's command was much shaper. Snell has faced the Cardinals eight times (seven starts) in his career, and has a 3-3 record and 3.40 ERA against the club.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer keeps getting better and keeps strengthening his case to stay in the rotation even when some of the Cardinals' injured starters begin coming back. He's averaging more than a strikeout per inning and he's totaled 20 innings over his past three starts. Wellemeyer has displayed a newfound efficiency this year, and his stuff is still impressive. It's early, but he's emerging as one of the surprise players of 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Expected to anchor the top of the rotation, Gorzelanny has had his command in just one of his four starts this year. In his previous outing, the lefty exited before finishing the third, marking the second time this season he's been chased that early in a game. Gorzelanny is consistently leaving his pitches up, and he has vowed to make sure he takes more time in between pitches. Gorzelanny is 1-2 with a 3.04 ERA in four career starts against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro seems to be healthy, but he still doesn't look very sharp. He hasn't struck a batter out yet, and he's not even missing bats with any kind of frequency. He'll never be a dominating strikeout pitcher, but Pineiro does need to get to a point where he can get at least a few swings and misses. Facing a Pirates team that strikes out quite a bit, maybe this will be the day for him to get going.

home_pitcher_note: For the first time in his now four starts this season, Duke was hit hard due to a lack of command. Though he has given up at least eight hits in each of his first three starts this season, the left-hander had mastered damage control. That is, until he faced the Cubs on Sunday. Duke lasted just four innings, giving up five runs and allowing 12 baserunners. Duke will be making his third career start against Philadelphia. He is 1-1 with a 3.65 ERA against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Eaton gave the Phillies another strong outing in his last start against the Mets on Sunday. In five-plus innings, the righty gave up six hits and four earned runs while striking out four and walking one. Eaton was especially solid until the top of the potent Mets lineup got to him in the fifth. Eaton threw 93 pitches, 56 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: In Morris' last start on April 21 at PNC Park, he got the hook early following two Marlins home runs. The veteran right-hander lasted only four innings and gave up eight runs on nine hits. It was the third consecutive loss for Morris, who hasn't won a game since Sept. 26. However, Morris does have a strong history against the Phillies. He is 5-3 with a 3.57 ERA against the cross-state rival.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander got roughed up in Denver's thin air, allowing five runs on eight hits in five innings. He luckily received a no-decision when the Phillies came back to win. Kendrick has faced the Pirates once, securing a win by allowing one run in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Though Maholm said afterward that he didn't possess his best command in his start against the Marlins on Tuesday, the lefty proved to be the stopper a spiraling rotation desperately needed. Maholm had enough command to be able to go to any of his four pitches at any given time, and finished the night with six innings of work. He allowed just one run in four hits while striking out six. Maholm will be making his fifth career start against the Phillies. He is 2-1 with a 6.50 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Myers followed two strong outings with a weaker one, though Coors Field isn't the easiest place to pitch. The right-hander gave up six runs on 11 hits in that contest, including two home runs. He's gone 2-3 with a 2.31 ERA in six career appearances vs. Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Though Santana highlighted his last start with the two doubles he hit at the plate, his pitching certainly wasn't bad, either. Lasting seven innings in all against the Nationals, Santana allowed two runs on seven hits, striking out four and walking one. He can win his fourth game of '08 against the Pirates, a team he's only faced twice in his career. He started one of those game and added a relief appearance in the other, posting a combined 1.13 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: It took Snell nine hitters, four hits and four earned runs to warm up against the Cardinals in his last start on Wednesday, but the 26-year-old right-hander settled down and threw five scoreless innings to keep the Pirates in the game. Now, Snell will face a Mets team that has hit him hard throughout his career. In four appearances against New York, Snell has given up 12 earned runs in only 17 2/3 innings. He is 0-1 with a 6.11 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Perez started out strong last Thursday against the Nationals, breezing through four innings before walking the leadoff man in the fifth. He never recovered. The walk turned into a rally, and the rally turned into three runs. By the time Perez's night was complete, he had allowed five runs in all, walking four and taking his first loss. Perez, a former Pirate, holds a 5.14 career ERA against his old team.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny's seven walks his last time out set a career high for the left-hander and were the latest evidence of his season-long command woes. His usually steady changeup was consistently missing low in his more recent loss. The lefty has now walked 22 hitters in 22 1/3 innings, though Gorzelanny has said he feels he is on the verge of breaking through the rut. His chances of turning around his fortunes against the Mets aren't helped by his history against the New York club, however. In three career starts against the Mets, Gorzelanny is winless and has allowed 12 runs in 10 1/3 innings

home_pitcher_note: On Friday, Perez pitched well against the Cubs, giving up two runs in six innings, but he ended up with his third no-decision of the season, as the bullpen was unable to protect a 3-2 lead. With the bases loaded in the eighth, left-hander Mike O'Connor walked pinch-hitter Matt Murton to force home Aramis Ramirez and tie the score at 3.
away_pitcher_note: Dealing with baserunners on an inning-to-inning basis is not going to change with Duke, whose game is making hitters put the ball in play. However, in each of his last two starts, the balls have been finding the holes, and those baserunners have been scoring. After giving up nine hits and six runs in his last start (six innings), opponents are now hitting .344 against the lefty, who is struggling to get his pitches down.

home_pitcher_note: On Sunday, Lannan showed once again that he is Washington's best pitcher. He threw seven shutout innings and helped the Nationals blank the Cubs, 2-0, at Nationals Park. One cannot say that Lannan, 23, was dominating in the game, but he showed that he could can get out of jams.
away_pitcher_note: Dumatrait replaces Matt Morris in the Bucs rotation. Dumatrait had been pitching in long relief, so he is stretched out in terms of innings. For Dumatrait, it is a second chance to start in the Majors. He was 0-4 as a starter last season in Cincinnati and posted a 15.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Just when the Nationals thought that Chico turned the corner after pitching eight solid innings against the Braves on April 11, it's time for them to ask: What's wrong with the promising young left-hander? Chico had his third consecutive sub-par outing in the Nationals' 7-0 loss to the Cubs on Saturday. He lasted four innings and gave up five runs on eight hits, falling to 0-5. In his last three games, Chico has allowed 16 runs in 13 innings. Pitching coach Randy St. Claire said that Chico is pressing on the mound. The reason St. Claire gave was surprising, because Chico is a guy who has a reputation of having ice water in his veins. Manager Manny Acta has often said he never knows how Chico is feeling because he doesn't show his emotions.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm tossed his third career complete game in a 5-1 win over the Phillies on April 27. He was outstanding, giving up one run on two hits, walking four and striking out two. In going the distance, he threw a total 99 pitches and was in the zone with 56 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Redding pitched well his last time out, tossing six innings and giving up two runs on four hits against the Braves. But he ended up with no decision. Braves first baseman Mark Teixeira scored the first run of the game in the second inning, when Mark Kotsay grounded out into a force play. But Washington came back and took the lead in the bottom of the third inning, when Zimmerman and Johnson hit back-to-back home runs. Atlanta tied the score, however, when Chipper Jones hit a solo home run off Redding in the top of the sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: After giving up a season-high five walks in his last start, Snell was visibly irritated with himself for not bearing down and pitching like he knows he is capable. Between rushing himself in between pitches and concentrating too hard on locating rather than just throwing to his strengths, Snell struggled with his command throughout much of April. Despite having made five appearances (three starts) against the Nationals before, Snell still has not registered a win or loss against the D.C. team. He has given up 10 earned runs in 23 innings, while striking out 22 and walking 11.

home_pitcher_note: Duke maintained sharp control in a solid 85-pitch outing against Washington, but left a tie game and received no decision. He showed good command of all three pitches and didn't make any major mistakes as he flew through the Nationals' lineup. Duke only needs some offensive support to get his first win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez didn't quite record a quality start in his most recent outing, but he still contributed to a victory. He allowed two runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings as the Giants outlasted Colorado, 3-2, last Wednesday. Sanchez was erratic, walking five and running his pitch count to 109. He struck out only four after entering the game with 36 strikeouts in 28 innings. He has never started against the Pirates and has appeared against them only twice in relief.

home_pitcher_note: Dumatrait moves up one day after the Pirates scratched starter Tom Gorzelanny from his expected start. However, an off-day in between Dumatrait's last start and this one will still give him a normal four days rest. Dumatrait made his first start of the season on Friday, going four innings and allowing four runs on six hits. With one start now under his belt, the lefty will likely be given the green light to go beyond the 90-100 pitch limit he was given his last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Zito returns to the starting rotation after a bullpen stint in which he didn't make a single relief appearance. The Giants demoted him on April 28, one day after he allowed eight runs in three innings in a 10-1 loss to Cincinnati. Zito, the 2002 American League Cy Young Award winner with Oakland, has allowed at least four runs in each of his six appearances, although he was plagued by five unearned runs in a two-start stretch in early April. Zito has never pitched at PNC Park, and he lost in his only career appearance last year against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm has struggled to be consistent on the road, which was evident in his Saturday start. After giving up five runs in the first two innings he settled down and threw three scoreless innings, receiving no decision in a 9-8 Pirates loss. After the game, he said he wasn't concerned about his mechanics or delivery, dismissing the bad innings as something that will happen over the course of a 162-game season.
away_pitcher_note: Cain went seven innings, giving up just three hits and two runs (two solo homers) before he came out in the eighth inning due to a tight right hamstring in his last start on Saturday in a no-decision against the Phillies. He struck out a season-high eight and walked a season-low one. It was the second quality start in the last three outings for Cain.

home_pitcher_note: Allowing four runs in six innings, Snell said he never felt like he had command of the ball. While the Pirates always count on him to deliver a solid outing, he shied away from the "ace" label, saying that his other teammates were also putting up good numbers this year. Manager John Russell wants to see Snell develop more control on his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty is still looking for his first win of the season. A victim of run support in three of his four starts (the other he was injured and left in the first inning), Glavine was spotted seven runs his last time out, Sunday against Cincinnati, but lasted only 4 2/3 innings, allowing a season-high six runs (his ERA went from 2.63 to 4.50) and an uncharacteristic five walks (also a season-high). Glavine is 22-12 career against the Bucs, with a 3.12 ERA. He got no decision in Atlanta's 2008 home opener on March 31, despite allowing only one earned run and seven hits in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: After doing some throwing on the side on Monday and Tuesday, Gorzelanny is still expected to be ready to make the start on Saturday. The left-hander had his last start skipped after being bothered by tightness in his lower back. Assuming everything goes fine during his mid-week bullpen session, however, the minor tightness that remains shouldn't keep Gorzelanny out any longer. Not only does Gorzelanny have to contend with a sore back, but he also has command issues that need to be addressed. He has averaged fewer than five innings per start in his six starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: James is expected to be called up from Triple-A Richmond to make his fourth start of the season. Since he struggled in his April 9 season debut, the 26-year-old left-hander has impressed. In three appearances for Richmond, he has posted a 1.59 ERA. In addition, he beat the Dodgers on April 19 and the Marlins on April 24. He has been attempting to regain strength in his shoulder that bothered him last year.

home_pitcher_note: Duke will take the mound after making back-to-back quality starts that appear to have the left-hander on some sort of early-season roll. He has now finished at least seven innings in half of his starts this season, and his sinker has been consistently down in the zone again, something that wasn't so much the case a year ago. Duke will get his second chance of the season against Atlanta on Sunday. He pitched 5 2/3 innings against the Braves in his first start of the season and allowed two earned runs on 10 hits.
away_pitcher_note: While allowing one run and seven hits in six innings against the Padres on Tuesday, Jurrjens arguably had his least impressive outing in three weeks. In his four previous outings, he had limited opponents to a .124 batting average. The 22-year-old right-hander has been one of the game's top rookies. But now that there are more enhanced scouting reports of him, he'll have to show his ability to make quick adjustments.

home_pitcher_note: Van Benschoten will be making his first career start against the Braves. Van Benschoten hasn't pitched in any capacity since May 3. He was 0-7 last season for the Pirates in nine starts with a 10.15 ERA. This season, he is 0-1 and has allowed two runs in 3 2/3 innings pitching out of the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since throwing a three-hit shutout against the Reds, Hudson went seven strong innings, allowing two runs on six hits in the Braves' 5-2 win over the Padres on Wednesday. Hudson was charged with a run in the first inning after his pickoff move to third base was ruled a balk. He was nearly ejected from the game for arguing, but settled down and kept the Braves in a close ballgame. Hudson has allowed just three runs on nine hits in his last 16 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse struggled Thursday, yielding seven runs on eight hits and five walks in four innings against the Rockies.  Four of the runs came with two outs in the first inning after a hard grounder to third deflected off Brendan Ryan's glove, opening the door for four hits and two walks.  Lohse couldn't get strike calls on his inside pitches, and in an effort to counteract the Coors Field factor of pitching at altitude, he abandoned his curve and tried too hard to pitch low in the zone, frequently ending up in the dirt.  Ultimately, he had to come back over the plate, and the Rockies were able to sit on his pitches and hand him a lopsided loss.
away_pitcher_note: Dumatrait picked up his first win of the season his last time out, dominating the Giants with 5 2/3 scoreless innings. He allowed just five hits and struck out five in the outing. Dumatrait, who has made just two starts since being moved from the bullpen to the rotation, continues to show more confidence in his changeup and is using that as a complement to his fastball and slider. The key for the lefty will continue to be making sure his pitches are down.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer deserved better after allowing only a pair of unearned runs in six solid innings Friday in Milwaukee, but Jason Isringhausen blew his fifth save with two outs in the ninth, and Milwaukee rallied for a victory. Wellemeyer also had a hand in the offensive part of the game, driving in a run with a single. He was one of three runners on base with nobody out, however, and the Cardinals were unable to score more than two runs in a potentially explosive frame.
away_pitcher_note: If Maholm hadn't tried to make an unwise defensive play in his last start, he may well have finished six innings of work without giving up a run. But instead, his attempt to try and snag a grounder led to four Giants runs in and a no-decision for Maholm. The lefty ran up a high pitch count early, but retired the last seven hitters he faced and did well in keeping the ball down. Maholm is 1-2 with a 2.28 ERA in three starts against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro's sinker was on fire Saturday in Milwaukee, and he left the game with a lead before earning a no-decision in the Cardinals' 5-3 win over the Brewers. Pineiro only allowed two hits -- both off the bat of Ryan Braun -- through six innings before he loaded the bases with one out in the seventh, a circumstance Pineiro said could have been related to fatigue. Though two of those runners ultimately scored, it was a great bounceback from the previous start, when he lasted only three frames.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing four runs in three consecutive outings, Snell allowed just one in a season-high seven innings his last time out. The right-hander has been struggling with his aggressiveness all season, but appeared to take a step forward in that department despite giving up a career-high six walks in the game. Snell needs to continue using both sides of the plate more effectively. The righty is 3-3 with a 3.71 ERA in nine appearances (eight starts) against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Gallagher brought a 4.50 ERA into his first Major League start after making two relief appearances. He gave up four runs on five hits and three walks (one intentional) in 4 1/3 innings, also striking out six. Cubs manager Lou Piniella said he will probably start the 22-year-old again Friday against the Pirates, and ship Jon Lieber back to the bullpen. This is Rich Hill's spot as long as he performs well in Triple-A, but the Cubs like Gallagher's stuff. He said he relied mostly on his fastball and slider Sunday, and after a one-run first inning, he worked three good ones before getting knocked around in the fifth.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny, who missed his last start due to tightness in his lower back, tossed 7 1/3 innings and allowed two runs on seven hits. He recorded four strikeouts in improving his record to 3-3 with a 5-2 win over the Braves on May 10. He is 0-1 this year against the Cubs in two starts. He absorbed a 13-1 loss on April 19 when he pitched 2 2/3 innings and allowed seven runs on six hits.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano's last start was a good one. He went 2-for-4 at the plate and also picked up the win in a romp over the Padres. Big Z gave up three runs on six hits and two walks over seven innings while striking out five, and is off to the best start of his career. The right-hander improved to 4-0 with a 1.96 ERA at home. He's probably happiest with his at-bats. Zambrano loves to hit, and he got two at-bats in the Cubs' six-run fifth inning. He now has hit safely in his last four starts, going 5-for-10 with a double and a homer.
away_pitcher_note: Duke continues to impress, as he moved to 2-0 with a 2.21 ERA in three starts this month. The lefty has now allowed three or fewer runs in six of his eight starts and continues to show quality movement on all of his pitches. Duke's most potent pitch right now, though, is his sinkerball, which is the biggest reason for the high number of ground-ball outs Duke has induced. That sinker is being complemented by an above-average changeup as well. Duke is 0-1 against the Cubs this season and has allowed six runs to Chicago in 11 innings pitched.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis had one bad inning in his last start against the Padres. The right-hander gave up four runs on nine hits over 5 2/3 innings in the loss, his third in a row. He blew a 3-0 lead, and among the hits he served up was a three-run homer to Khalil Greene. Marquis has been stronger in the first half than the second, so his struggles are tough to understand. He needs to get back on track.
away_pitcher_note: In his third start since joining the rotation, Dumatrait looked the strongest as he has all season. He extended himself out to 88 pitches and did it without tiring, which was a problem in his previous start. Using a newly invented changeup to complement his other pitches, Dumatrait limited the St. Louis damage to just a three-run homer in six innings of work. He continues to pitch with a confidence and poise that was not there a year ago.

home_pitcher_note: Despite picking up his fourth road loss of the season, Maholm was encouraged by the quality and crispness of his pitches. He did, however, allow 11 hits, a total that he has now reached twice already this season. Though don't be completely fooled by that total as four of those 11 were either infield singles or bloop hits. The good news is that Maholm's next start is at PNC Park, where the lefty is 14-9 with a 3.50 ERA in his career. This will be Maholm's first start against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: In his eighth start, Parra worked more than 5 1/3 innings for the first time this season and was in line to win for the first time since his season debut on April 5, only to see the Dodgers rally late at Miller Park. Parra should have been through the seventh inning with a 4-1 lead, but a couple of miscues behind him forced Parra to settle for 6 2/3 innings with seven hits and three runs, just one of them earned. It was a big step forward for Parra, who touched 96 mph on the stadium radar gun and worked more aggressively than in previous outings. He has never faced the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Snell continues to be mystified by his season-long struggles. The right-hander's pitches haven't been crisp. His command hasn't been sharp. And now his confidence is beginning to waver. Venting visible frustration after his last start, Snell said he is now at a loss for what the culprit is for his struggles. Snell has never faced the Brewers, but will head into the start trying to do less nibbling around the plate and get back to trusting his stuff.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets is coming off a strange start against the Dodgers in which he allowed two hits and no runs through six innings, then surrendered six runs and three home runs in the seventh. Manager Ned Yost said Sheets had no physical ailments, and Sheets admitted he didn�t know what went wrong. "I'd like to say I know what went wrong," Sheets said after suffering his first loss this season. "I'd like to be able to fix something." He called it the worst inning of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Mercifully, Gorzelanny won't be facing a club with 'Chicago' laced across the front of its uniform. Take away the left-hander's woes against the Cubs this season (three starts, 11 total innings, 21 runs), and Gorzelanny's numbers aren't so bad. His command has only sporadically matched that which he showed a year ago, however, and his fastball still clocks in about two to three mph slower than it did in 2007. The lefty needs to get his pitches down.
away_pitcher_note: Bush has had some trouble of late getting the third out. All five Red Sox runs against him in Game 2 of a doubleheader on Saturday scored with two outs, though one was unearned. Bush surrendered a two-out, two-run double to Mike Lowell on a curveball down and away in the first inning, then misplaced a fastball to Lowell in the third and saw it go for a two-out, two run home run. Thirteen of the 28 earned runs that Bush has surrendered this season have scored with two outs.

home_pitcher_note: Despite leaving with a lead, Duke didn't pick up a decision in his last start. He allowed three runs early, but settled in to allow just one in his final five innings of work. The left-hander will be facing the Cubs for the second consecutive start and will take the same approach into this game as he did into the last. Duke mixed up his pitches and limited the number of first-pitch fastballs that he threw in order to keep the free-swinging Cubs off balance.
away_pitcher_note: "Big Z" had his worst start of the season, getting pulled with no outs in the fifth in the Cubs' 7-6 loss to Pittsburgh on May 17. Zambrano gave up three runs in the inning and was off-kilter from the start. He gave up seven hits and five runs (four earned), walking three and striking out three. He hasn't lost since April 11, when he gave up five runs in six innings against the Phillies. He also broke a bat over his right knee after striking out at the plate.

home_pitcher_note: Simply put, Dumatrait didn't have any command his last time out. He walked seven Chicago hitters in 4 2/3 innings and threw more balls (53) than strikes (52) before being pulled. Both he and his manager were unable to pinpoint any particular mechanical problem, saying bluntly that Dumatrait's location was just off. On an encouraging note, though, the lefty extended himself to the 100-pitch mark for the first time this season and said afterward that he didn't fatigue.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis loves facing the Pirates. Both of his wins this season have come against them. In his last start, he held Pittsburgh to two earned runs in six innings to snap a three-game losing streak and drop his ERA below five as the Cubs closed out an 8-2 homestand. He registered a season-high seven strikeouts in an earlier six-inning, one-run win against the division foe in April. If the Cubs can get Marquis on a roll, they could have one of the finest top-to-bottom rotations in baseball.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm squeaked through his first six innings against the Brewers in his last start on Tuesday, allowing only two runs on eight hits. But then Brewers center fielder Mike Cameron sent a two-run home run to the bleacher seats at PNC Park to send Maholm back to the dugout. The loss was Maholm's third in his last four starts. But good news lies ahead for Maholm, who is a perfect 4-0 against the Cubs in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly picked up his fourth straight win in his last start against the Astros. The lefty lasted 5 1/3 innings, and wanted to finish the sixth but his pitch count was too high. He had pitched at least six innings in his last six starts. Against Houston, Lilly gave up two runs on four hits and two walks, and struck out six. He also had a single, and is batting .267. Not bad for a pitcher who spent most of his career in the American League.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto once again showed signs of his youth and that he's still adjusting when he lasted just five innings and gave up four runs -- two of them earned -- in a loss to the Dodgers on Wednesday. The two unearned runs came on a passed ball that allowed a runner to score and pickoff attempt that sailed into the seats and allowed another runner to score. He threw 114 pitches -- his highest pitch count of the season -- and allowed seven hits and three walks with a pair of strikeouts. The two strikeouts tie a season low for Cueto, who entered the game averaging almost six per outing.
away_pitcher_note: Though frustrated with the outcome (his third straight loss), Snell did look more comfortable on the mound in his most recent start. He eliminated his sinker, a decision designed to sharpen his four-seam fastball, and it seemed to work. Snell relied heavily on that fastball early and with success. Snell's last win, which came on April 12, was against Cincinnati in a game in which Snell threw a season-best 6 1/3 innings and allowed three runs on nine hits. The right-hander is 1-2 with a 4.32 ERA in four starts at Great American Ball Park.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo worked 6 1/3 innings and allowed two earned runs on seven hits in a 5-2 win over the Padres on Saturday. He walked one and struck out nine. After a rough start, in which he was 1-4 with an 8.63 ERA through his first seven starts, he is 2-0 with a 2.05 ERA over his past four starts. Arroyo's worst and shortest start of this season occurred against the Braves on May 4 at Turner Field. He lasted 1 1/3 innings and gave up seven earned runs and seven hits in a 14-7 Reds loss. Arroyo, who is 1-3 lifetime against Pittsburgh, faced the Pirates on April 12 and worked five innings, giving up three runs -- just two earned -- on six hits with two walks and three strikeouts. He did not receive a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny lasted only five innings in his last start on May 22, but the lefty was able to hold the Brewers to two runs on eight hits. However, he still walked twice as many batters as he struck out, raising his walks-to-strikeout ratio to 35-to-26. Gorzelanny is 2-1 with a 4.91 ERA against the Reds in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Harang's last appearance came in relief when he entered Sunday's 18-inning game with the Padres during the 13th and pitched four innings, giving up no runs on two hits with a walk and nine strikeouts. Originally scheduled to start Wednesday, he was moved back a day to give his arm extra rest. His streak of 15 consecutive starts of pitching at least six innings was snapped in his last start, an 8-2 loss at San Diego on Thursday. Harang lasted just 5 1/3 innings and gave up five runs on 10 hits with two walks and seven strikeouts. He once again didn't get any help from the Reds' offense, which has been particularly stagnant during his starts, averaging 3.27 runs per game in his 11 starts. He was solid against the Pirates in 2007, when he was 3-0 in four starts with a 3.52 ERA, including a complete game and a shutout.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Dumatrait was able to do what Pirates pitchers have had trouble doing all season: tame the Cubs' batting order. For five innings, he kept the Cubs off-balance until getting drilled in the thigh with a line drive in the sixth. He stayed in the game for four batters, but left the bases loaded. The bullpen had his back, though, and struck out the next batter. By moving up a day in the rotation, Dumatrait will be facing the Cincinnati club that took him off its 40-man roster after the '07 season and ultimately set up his move to Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has been as steady as any Cardinals starter this season. He's allowed more than four runs just once in 11 starts, and he's permitted three or fewer in five straight. He had a rough go in his first start against Pittsburgh this year, but in his second appearance he turned in an excellent game.
away_pitcher_note: Duke was pushed back one day in the rotation because of a callous on the middle finger of his pitching hand. Duke has battled the minor discomfort through his last two starts and the Pirates' hope is that one extra day of rest will allow it to fully heal. In his last start, on Friday against the Cubs, Duke surrendered 10 hits in four innings, giving up four earned runs. It was his shortest outing since April 20, when the same Cubs team chased Duke from the game after four innings and five earned runs. Duke is 2-2 with a 3.98 ERA in seven starts against the Cardinals, though he is winless with a 5.60 ERA in Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Parisi will make his first career start for the Cardinals in place of the injured Joel Pineiro. Parisi has pitched impressively in his first year with the club, striking out 10 batters in 15 2/3 innings with a 2.87 ERA. Manager Tony La Russa has used Parisi in multiple inning situations because he is normally a starter, and now he will get a chance to go deep against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm looked impressive at times against a powerful Cubs lineup in his last start on May 25. He pitched six scoreless innings, but surrendered five runs in two separate innings. An unlikely Pirates comeback gave Maholm a no-decision. He is 2-3 with a 4.46 ERA against the Reds in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Looper thought he was right on the doorstep of getting on a roll, but in his last start he instead took a big step backward. He hasn't been truly sharp in several starts, and the stats indicate it. In five May starts, Looper has just nine strikeouts against eight walks, with five home runs allowed in 29 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The success of 2007 continues to be missing, and Snell has gotten to the point where it is beginning to affect him mentally. The right-hander has changed his mechanics, deciding to rely on his four-seam fastball and eliminate his sinker, but that hasn't worked. He's tried to up his velocity, and that hasn't translated into success either. The consensus is that the righty needs to relax and stop worrying about throwing perfect pitches, something that likely won't happen until he gets some solid starts under his belt. Snell faced the Cardinals on May 15 and allowed five runs on 11 hits in a season-short four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright throws his second consecutive start at home, a place he has relished pitching this year. In six home starts, the Cardinals' ace has won four. Most recently, Wainwright turned in an eight-inning, eight-strikeout gem against the Astros on May 28. With two impressive starts against the Astros in the bag this year -- the other a complete game victory -- Wainwright will try to win his third start in a row against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny lasted a career-low two-thirds of an inning his last time out, leaving the lefty wondering what it's going to take for his command to come back. He has lacked consistency from one start to the next all season and his walk total has escalated to 37 in 46 1/3 innings. The key for Gorzelanny is easy: getting ahead of hitters with some consistency. He fell behind seven of the eight hitters he faced in his most recent start. Gorzelanny lost a decision to the Cardinals earlier this season when he gave up a career-high seven walks and three runs in five innings. The lefty is 1-1 with a 1.98 ERA in two career starts at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Who would have thought that Dumatrait would become the most consistent starter on this staff? His last start -- seven innings, two hits, seven strikeouts and no earned runs -- was further evidence of just that. The left-hander's confidence continues to creep higher, and matching it is the success he is having with his newfound changeup. The pitch sets up his fastball beautifully, and his propensity to throw it at any time in the count has really proven to leave hitters off guard. This will be Dumatrait's first career start against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez didn't do well in his first outing in six weeks, allowing six runs (three earned) in a loss to the Cardinals on Wednesday. The lefty threw 27 pitches in the opening frame and had thrown 76 through four. Rodriguez, who missed six starts because of a strained left groin, didn't have his curveball working, nor was his changeup very good. The left-hander was 0-2 with a 7.20 ERA over four games vs. the Pirates last year. Lifetime vs. Pittsburgh, Rodriguez is 2-3 with a 5.65 ERA over eight games.

home_pitcher_note: Duke pitched well to both sides of the plate his last time out and kept his pitches low -- always a barometer for success -- on his way to another quality start. No run support kept him from picking up his third win of the season. On another encouraging note, Duke allowed just five hits in six innings after struggling to limit the number of baserunners in most of his starts earlier in the season. Duke is winless in seven appearances (six starts) against the Astros in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt pitched well in his most recent outing vs. the Cardinals, despite taking a loss. He allowed three runs over seven frames, with the final blow being a decisive solo homer by Albert Pujols. Oswalt has a career record of 11-5 against the Pirates with a 2.49 ERA. Last year, he was 1-0 over three starts with an 0.87 ERA, allowing two earned runs over 20 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Dumatrait is scheduled to come off the disabled list after being sidelined with bursitis in his left shoulder. Dumatrait was roughed up in his two previous starts in Baltimore and Chicago prior to going on the DL, surrendering 14 runs in 10 innings. Dumatrait missed one scheduled start, on June 25 against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Backe yielded five runs in a losing effort his last trip to the mound against the Brewers on Friday. He yielded three homers, including a two-run shot to Prince Fielder. Backe had six days of rest between starts, which may have been too much of a layoff. The right-hander won his only start against the Pirates last year, holding them to two runs over six innings. Lifetime vs. the Bucs, Backe is 4-1 with a 2.86 ERA over eight games.

home_pitcher_note: Snell is in the midst of a five-game losing skid, having not won since his third start of the season, which came back on April 12. Stuck in what he will admit is the most frustrating stretch of his career, Snell has been plagued primarily by allowing a big inning for the opposing offense in each of his starts. In his last game, it was a five-run second inning. In six of his 12 starts this season, Snell has allowed at least three runs in one inning. If there's any good news to highlight, it's that Snell is 2-0 with a 2.55 ERA in four career starts against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Webb tossed a gem the last time out, pitching a shutout against the Nationals, successfully ending the Diamondbacks' five-game losing streak. Webb set a quick pace in the game, which lasted only 1 hour and 52 minutes, the shortest game in franchise history at Chase Field. The sinkerballer had 16 groundball outs and eight strikeouts as he got back to his winning ways. In Webb's first nine starts, he recorded nine wins, then followed with two losses. He has received the decision in every start this season.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny was fortunate that a timely grand slam by his teammate kept him from picking up his sixth loss in his most recent start. Trying to rebound from a career-short two-thirds inning start, Gorzelanny quickly allowed four early runs and looked to be headed to an early shower again. However, the left-hander rebounded to throw three scoreless innings to finish the outing -- something that could prove to be a huge confidence booster moving forward. Gorzelanny is 1-0 with a 2.77 ERA in two career starts against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Haren finally got the run support he needed in his last start, but all he needed was one run, as he shut out the Nationals for seven innings. The right-hander allowed just four hits and three walks. Haren also had five strikeouts and lowered his ERA to 3.40. It was his first win after dropping three of his last four starts. Haren has pitched fewer than seven innings in only one start this season.

home_pitcher_note: Dumatrait was asked if his six-inning, four-strikeout effort against the Astros on Monday was his best start of the year. The lefty, who limited the Astros to only two runs, shrugged his shoulders and answered, "Yes." Dumatrait continues to delight Pirates management with consistent play and has earned praised from skipper John Russell. He will try to continue his recent success against the D-backs, a team he has yet to face in his two-year career.
away_pitcher_note: Davis has made three starts since undergoing surgery to remove his cancerous thyroid on April 10 and two of them have been very good. He got the win May 23 in Atlanta and got a no-decision in his last outing Monday night in Milwaukee. He allowed just one earned run over six innings against the Brewers. In the start in between those, Davis allowed six runs on nine hits over five innings to the Giants. The left-hander had been on the disabled list from April 8-May 23 and made two rehab starts for Triple-A Tucson.

home_pitcher_note: Duke looked confident and in control throughout his last start. The result? His longest outing of 2008. It took Duke 108 pitches (71 strikes) to go through 7 2/3 innings, picking up his third win of the season against the Astros. He'll need to make a copy of that performance against a tough D-backs lineup, which has scored nine runs in 11 innings against Duke in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson passed Roger Clemens on the all-time strikeout list in his last outing against the Brewers. He fanned eight and now has 4,680 in his career, which ranks only behind Nolan Ryan's record of 5,714. Johnson continues to get better with each passing start. He wound up getting charged with four runs (three earned) but through six he had only allowed a pair of runs, both of which came on a Ryan Braun homer. He has 210 career double-digit strikeout games, five shy of Ryan's record.

home_pitcher_note: After letting up three runs on five hits in the first two innings of his last start, Maholm settled down and threw a near-flawless game. He retired 20 of the next 23 batters and didn't issue a walk for the second start in a row. He is 0-2 with a 6.38 ERA against Washington in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Redding lasted just 5 1/3 innings Thursday night in Game 2 of the Nationals' day-night doubleheader against St. Louis. He surrendered six runs over the start -- all with two outs -- but picked up a no-decision as the Nationals won a thrilling come-from-behind game 10-9 on a walk-off Elijah Dukes home run.

home_pitcher_note: Well, the good news was that Snell limited the D-backs to just one earned run in five innings, striking out nine in that span. However, with a pitch count of 58 by the end of the second and of 107 through five, Snell obviously needs to better his efficiency. He wasn't helped either by being struck in the lower back by a line drive, something that Snell said bothered him in his final two innings but shouldn't cause him to miss any time. Snell has not won since April 12 and has pitched more than five innings only once in his last five games. He is 0-1 with a 4.34 ERA in six career appearances (four starts) against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan turned in another strong performance Thursday in game one of a doubleheader against St. Louis. Despite struggling with his control, the left-hander only allowed two runs over six innings, dropping his ERA to 3.47. However, he picked up the loss as the Cardinals shut down the Nationals' offense in a 4-1 loss.

home_pitcher_note: The beginning of Gorzelanny's last start looked like many that preceded it: unpleasant. The lefty gave up three quick runs in the first, but settled down and allowed no runs through his final six innings, earning a no-decision in the process. Gorzelanny, who hasn't won since May 22, beat the Nationals in his only career start against them, going 7 1/3 innings with six strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Bergmann struggled mightily in his last outing, giving up eight runs -- five earned -- and 10 hits over just three innings. It was the rockiest start by far for Bergmann, who had been stellar since returning from Triple-A Columbus in May. Bergmann threw 83 pitches over the start, 51 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Burres got hit hard in his last outing, and the Orioles elected to give him an extra day before he takes the mound again. The southpaw hasn't made it through five innings in each of his last three starts, and has seen his ERA rise by nearly two runs.
away_pitcher_note: Dumatrait was once again stellar for the Pirates in his last start on Sunday. The lefty went 5 2/3 innings, allowing only two runs on four hits against a tough D-backs' lineup. Dumatrait is slowly becoming the ace of the Pirates' staff. The Bucs are now 7-1 this season when he starts a game. He has never faced the Orioles in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Liz took a mild step back in his second start, but he managed to escape some sticky situations and keep his team in the game. The rookie worked five innings -- one out shorter than his season debut -- and threw 91 pitches in a no-decision against Toronto. There is one element of concern in the way he's gotten his outs: Liz has gotten just five ground outs compared to 18 fly balls.
away_pitcher_note: Duke was masterful at times in his last start against the Diamondbacks. He outdueled future Hall of Famer Randy Johnson and continues to be the Pirates' most consistent starter throughout the year. His sinker was in peak form and he induced quite a few groundouts. This will be Duke's first career start against the Orioles.

home_pitcher_note: Cabrera is coming into this contest with the Pirates having given up three-run leads in each of his past two starts. The latest came in Boston on Tuesday, when Cabrera served up back-to-back homers in the fifth inning against the Red Sox -- Cabrera ended up with a no-decision in the contest. He's looking for his first win since going seven strong innings against the Yankees on May 20, a game in which he allowed just two earned runs in a 12-2 win.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm's last start was an odd one. He was at his best in terms of efficiency, needing just 63 pitches to breeze through six innings against the Nationals. However, despite the low pitch count -- which is encouragingly becoming somewhat of a consistent occurrence for the lefty -- Maholm had to be pulled in the seventh after allowing three solo homers. Maholm has not walked a hitter in his last 26 1/3 innings pitched. He is, however, 1-4 with a 6.83 ERA away from PNC Park this season.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez suffered his second straight loss on Wednesday, basically on the strength of one swing of the bat from Detroit's Marcus Thames. That three-run home run from Thames in the second inning did most of the damage against Vazquez  during a 5-1 loss to the Tigers. Vazquez allowed five runs on 10 hits over six innings, striking out nine and walking three. In Vazquez's last two starts, he has yielded nine earned runs on 19 hits 11 1/3 innings. Vazquez has a 4-3 career record against the Pirates, with a 4.76 ERA. He also has a 4-1 record at U.S. Cellular Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: Snell was relieved to have picked up his first win since April 12 in his last start, but more than that, he was pleased with the results. Snell allowed just one run over six innings of work in what has to be categorized as one of his strongest starts this season. His slider was particularly sharp, and his pitch efficiency -- while still leaving a little to be desired -- was much better than in his previous start. Snell faced the White Sox last season and lost the start, allowing three runs on 10 hits in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Make it three straight quality starts for Buehrle and nine on the season out of 14 trips to the mound, sort of dispelling the myth that the left-hander is having a poor year. It was vintage Buehrle on Thursday in Detroit, he was moving his pitches up and down, in and out, and holding the Tigers to one run on seven hits over eighth innings. He struck out six and walked one in a no-decision during a 2-1 victory for Detroit, dropping the White Sox record to 5-9 when Buehrle starts. Buehrle has a 2-0 career mark against the Pirates, with a 1.80 ERA, and a 1-2 record with a 3.74 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny was by no means sharp in his last outing, but once again, he limited the damage done despite not having his best stuff. The left-hander threw 5 2/3 innings and allowed three runs on six hits, issuing three walks. He also struck out six on his way to snapping a three-game winless streak. Battling without his best stuff is becoming habit for Gorzelanny these days, though encouragingly, he's been able to do so effectively. Gorzelanny has never faced the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd had his streak of three straight wins snapped Friday against the Rockies. He was fortunate not to factor into the decision, having given up four solo home runs to put him in line for the loss when he left after 6 1/3 innings. He walked three and struck out four in that game. It was in sharp contrast to his previous three starts, in which he'd compiled a collective 20-to-1 K/BB ratio. He is 1-0 lifetime against the Pirates in one career start. He pitched 6 2/3 innings against them in 2006 as a member of the Phillies and allowed one run.
away_pitcher_note: Dumatrait has been a reliable rotation option for the Pirates, but he blew a chance to post the first consecutive victories of his career with a clunker of an outing on Friday at Baltimore. The lefty gave up five runs on five hits and five walks, with two of the free passes turning into runs during a three-run fifth that got Baltimore within 6-5. Not holding a 6-1 lead isn't a confidence builder, but Dumatrait knows what went wrong and how to fix the problem. Still, he didn't improve on an impressive outing in his previous start, something the rookie must learn to do.

home_pitcher_note: Duke is looking to win his third straight decision. Against Baltimore last Saturday, Duke allowed four runs and nine hits in six innings, but John Grabow allowed a two-run home run in the seventh to deprive him of a win in his third straight start for the first time since his magical rookie year of 2005. Duke didn't walk a batter for just the second time in 14 starts and didn't allow a home run. He's given up just five in 85 innings.
away_pitcher_note: On Saturday, the Cubs forced Halladay's pitch count up to 95 after five innings, forcing Toronto's ace out of the game for his shortest start since July 12 of last season. Against Chicago, Halladay gave up six runs -- the most he'd surrendered since June 5, 2007 -- though only two were earned. The right-hander yielded five hits, while striking out five and walking one in the loss, which marked his first defeat since May 9. Halladay went 5-0 with a 2.72 ERA in his previous six outings. He's 1-0 with a 1.13 ERA in one career start against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm is trying to win his third straight decision. He hasn't lost in five starts. On Sunday, against Baltimore, he nearly won, but Matt Capps blew a save in the bottom of the ninth. Maholm walked three in his last start after walking none in his last three games. He leads Pirates starters in home runs allowed. He gave up two in his last start, and has given up 13 long balls in 89 innings. Maholm will be facing Toronto for the first time. He's the only Pirates starter with a complete game -- a two-hitter against Philadelphia on Apr. 27.
away_pitcher_note: Litsch has struggled this month, going 0-2 with a 5.60 ERA in three outings, during which he's yielded 28 hits over 17 2/3 innings. That follows a stellar showing in May, when the 23-year-old went a perfect 4-0 with a tidy 2.08 ERA over six appearances. Litsch took a loss against the Cubs on Sunday after giving up five runs on eight hits with two strikeouts and one walk over 6 1/3 innings. Litsch is 4-2 with a 3.89 ERA on the road this year.

home_pitcher_note: Every time Snell seems to take a step forward, he matches it with a step in the opposite direction. His last start was just that as he comes off another ineffective outing -- four innings, six walks, seven runs -- and one in which he didn't record a strikeout for the first time since 2005. Snell has said he will look to go back to his fastball more often, and he's got to begin trusting his stuff down in the zone again. He has never faced Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: McGowan's Jekyll-and-Hyde act between home and road starts continued on Tuesday night in Milwaukee. The right-hander gave up four runs on four hits, including three home runs, and was chased after four innings. McGowan fell to 1-4 with a 6.27 ERA on the road. At home, he is 4-1 with a 1.73 ERA. McGowan has never faced the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny was stung by the long ball his last time out, as three homers accounted for all four runs he allowed in six innings of work. Despite the homers, though, Gorzelanny's latest outing could be looked at as a small step in the right direction. He kept his pitches down with notable consistency and he bounced back to get outs a number of times after falling behind in the count. This will be Gorzelanny's second career start against the Yankees. At Yankee Stadium last season, he allowed four runs in 6 1/3 innings and didn't factor in the decision.
away_pitcher_note: Rasner rebounded in a winning effort against the Padres on Wednesday, limiting San Diego to two runs on three hits over five innings.  Rasner had four strikeouts -- all in the first two innings -- and walked a season-high five, after not issuing more than two free passes in any professional start this year. After cruising through the first two innings, the righty struggled in a lengthy third, though he limited the damage to two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Duke was brilliant in his last start against the Blue Jays. He was efficient in every facet of the game, throwing 64 of his 97 pitches for strikes. He went a solid seven innings and allowed no runs on six hits. Duke continues to be the Pirates' most consistent starter throughout the 2008 season and looks to continue his streak against the Yankees, who he has never faced in his career.
away_pitcher_note: In his fourth career start, Chamberlain pitched 5 2/3 solid innings, fanning nine in a no-decision against San Diego on Thursday. Chamberlain threw 100 pitches -- 58 for strikes -- holding the Padres to one run, four hits and three walks. Of the nine strikeouts, eight were swinging.

home_pitcher_note: Barthmaier, a 13th-round Draft pick in 2003, will be making his first Major League appearance when he makes Friday's start for the Pirates. The right-hander has combined to go 4-5 with a 4.04 ERA in 10 Double-A and five Triple-A starts. In his most recent start, Barthmaier threw six innings, allowing one run on four hits and struck out eight. He has shown better control with both his fastball and breaking ball since being promoted to Triple-A in late May, allowing just six walks in 31 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty will take Edwin Jackson's spot in the rotation, but with Monday's off-day, Kazmir will stay on a regular five-day schedule. The Rays' ace is coming off Sunday afternoon's loss against the Astros, in which Kazmir gave up two home runs -- doubling his season total -- over 5 2/3 innings. He allowed three runs on four hits in his third loss this season. Kazmir dropped his only career appearance against the Pirates, giving up nine earned runs and eight hits in a mere 4 2/3 innings at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Following Friday night's loss, the Pirates recalled Taubenheim from Triple-A Indianapolis to make the spot start on Saturday. Taubenheim, who will be making his 14th appearance (ninth start) in the Majors, is 0-5 with a 5.55 ERA in his previous eight Major League starts, all of which came with Toronto. Taubenheim has maintained a near two-to-one strikeout-to-walk ratio and should be expected to at least be around the plate with his pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson is slated to come off a five-game suspension for his role in the Red Sox melee June 5 and start Saturday night's game in Pittsburgh. The young flamethrower last tossed on June 21, at Tropicana Field. In that appearance, Jackson lasted 6 1/3 innings, allowing five hits and two earned runs in a no-decision against Houston. He has an array of filthy pitches but is at his best when he is incorporating his offspeed regularly with his fast stuff.

home_pitcher_note: Somehow, someway, Gorzelanny was able to notch his sixth victory of the year against a potent Yankees lineup. The lefty was throwing balls left and right (52 balls to only 47 strikes), but he made the big pitch when he had to, getting New York to ground into two big double plays. On the season, he has 55 walks to only 41 strikeouts. He'll have to reverse that ratio against a young and promising Rays lineup, which he has never faced in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine will close out the final contest in a six-game Interleague road trip. The crafty right-hander is coming off a no-decision vs. Florida on Tuesday night, in which Sonnanstine tossed five innings of six-hit ball. The 25-year-old will be making his 17th start this season and will look to extend on his team-leading eight victories. It will be Sonnanstine's career debut against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Harang gave up five runs on seven hits with three walks and three strikeouts in receiving a no-decision against the Blue Jays on Wednesday. He lasted just 5 2/3 innings, but threw a season-high-tying 118 pitches, 75 of which went for strikes. Harang has picked up a win just once in his last eight starts and has struggled to get run support along the way. And though he's considered the Reds' ace, his three victories this season are the fewest of any starter on the team. His 10 losses are a team-high as well. Harang's last start against Pittsburgh came in a May 29 loss, when he gave up six runs on 10 hits with a walk and two strikeouts through just four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Because Maholm threw just 2 2/3 innings in a rain-shortened game on Thursday, he has been moved up a day in the Pittsburgh rotation. Though Maholm allowed three first-inning runs on four consecutive extra-base hits, because of the postponement, none of those stats will count against him. It was, however, the latest example of Maholm being hurt by one big inning. Maholm will enter Tuesday's game having worked six innings in each of his last nine starts. He did not factor in a decision against Cincinnati back on April 11 when he allowed six hits in 5 1/3 scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez struggled with his command from the get-go and posted his shortest start of the year, lasting just 4 1/3 innings while giving up a season-high seven runs on six hits with three walks and no strikeouts. It was the first time Volquez allowed more than three earned runs in any of his 16 starts this season and was only the second time he's given up more than two earned runs. The loss also snapped his streak of 12 consecutive quality starts. Volquez last faced the Pirates on April 11 when he gave up three hits with three walks and a strikeout through five scoreless innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: Duke appeared calm against Derek Jeter and the rest of the Yankees lineup in his last start on Wednesday. He didn't have a high pitch count (79 pitches in five innings) or gave up a lot of runs (three earned), but the Pirates' offense, which was shut out for only the second time this year, didn't help their young lefty. Duke will try to notch win No. 5 against the Reds. He has a 2-2 record with a 4.57 ERA against Cincinnati in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Thompson was charged with four earned runs and eight hits over five-plus innings with two walks and two strikeouts in a 6-0 loss to the Indians Friday. Similar to his first big league start, the 22-year-old right hander repeatedly dodged danger. He stranded 12 runners over his first four scoreless innings. A Grady Sizemore homer in the fifth came with the bases empty. A five-run sixth, including three runs charged to Thompson, did him in.
away_pitcher_note: Van Benschoten gets the nod for Wednesday's spot start, which will be the right-hander's second such start this season. His previous start occurred on May 12 when he took the loss in a game against the Braves. Van Benschoten allowed six earned runs on nine hits and two walks in four innings. The key for the former first-round pick is to be aggressive around the strike zone. He showed that in a one-inning relief appearance on Saturday, but has struggled to do so in most of his starts over the past two seasons. Van Benschoten has never faced Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets was touched for five earned runs in seven innings on Sunday against the Twins in a 5-0 loss. All five runs were surrendered with two outs. Sheets will next take the mound on the Fourth of July against the Pirates. Sheets pitched a complete game on May 21 against the Bucs, striking out six and allowing only one earned run in a 4-1 Brewers victory.
