away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny allowed fewer than three earned runs for the first time in seven starts in his last outing, on June 29 against Tampa Bay. He has struggled with control problems this season, but he was a bit more effective tossing 111 pitches, 70 for strikes. Gorzelanny hurled six innings and was tagged for two runs on eight hits. He recorded eight strikeouts and received a no-decision against the Rays.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a pair of wins in which he surrendered two total runs on six hits in 15 innings, Bush didn't have it earlier in the week in Phoenix. Six of the nine Arizona hits off Bush went for extra bases, and he surrendered five runs, four earned, in five innings. He's been very good this season at Miller Park, going 3-2 with a 3.18 ERA in seven starts, but he lost to the Pirates in Pittsburgh in May, allowing six runs on nine hits.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm continues to be one of two steady presences in the Pirates rotation, and his last start as yet another example of that. Needing just 89 pitches to finish seven innings, Maholm allowed two runs on five hits as he notched his fifth quality start in his last six. The lefty seems to run into problems primarily when he rushes in his delivery, but he has shown in recent weeks that he can remedy the problem quick enough to keep it from getting him into too much trouble. Maholm lost to the Brewers back in May in a start where he allowed four earned runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan won his last start but is in a three-game funk in which he has allowed 12 earned runs and 15 hits in 12 2/3 innings. He surrendered five runs on nine hits in five innings at Arizona on Tuesday but got the win after the Brewers roughed up Randy Johnson. Suppan didn't pitch against the Pirates when the Brewers visited Pittsburgh last month, but he's 10-3 lifetime against the Pirates with a 3.95 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Duke's last start lasted just 77 pitches as the left-hander got into a bases-loaded jam in the sixth that his manager preferred his bullpen get out of. Though Duke's five-inning, one-run performance suggests dominance, in reality, Duke benefited from some stellar defense and some Houdini-like bullpen work to bail him out. It's not much a setback for Duke, though, who has gone at least six innings in 10 of his last 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Dumatrait is expected to come off the disabled list in time to make Monday's start. The lefty went on the DL with bursitis in his left shoulder, but is continuing to work through a throwing program in which he has had no setbacks. Dumatrait had been one of the Pirates' most reliable starters before his shoulder started giving him problems in June. He allowed a combined 14 runs in his past two starts (both five innings) after posting a 3.27 ERA in six May starts. Dumatrait took the loss in a start against the Astros earlier this season despite allowing just two runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez had a rough second outing, against the Dodgers on Wednesday, giving up four runs (three earned) on six hits in just five innings. He threw 79 strikes in the loss, including a solo home run to Andre Ethier. The right-hander, who now has given up seven runs on 11 hits with nine total strikeouts, has never faced Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Tuesday is the earliest that Snell is eligible to come off the disabled list, and the right-hander is expected to be ready. He took a week off from throwing to let the inflammation in his right elbow subside and has reported finally feeling better than he has in weeks. Snell threw his first bullpen session off the mound on Wednesday, and will throw at least one more before this start. Snell is 2-3 with a 3.91 ERA in nine career appearances (eight starts) against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Backe yielded five runs against the Dodgers in his most recent outing, giving up three runs in the first and solo home runs in the third and fifth frames. Backe has allowed a combined 11 earned runs over his last two outings. The right-hander has faced the Pirates once this year, allowing four runs over six innings in a losing effort. In his career, Backe is 4-2 with a 3.32 ERA over nine games versus Pittsburgh, including six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Van Benschoten jumps into the rotation as a result of the Pirates' decision to option Tom Gorzelanny to Triple-A. This gives Van Benschoten his chance to show that he is a capable Major League starter, something that he has not yet proven in his career. The righty has an 8.82 ERA in 16 career starts and has won just once. He is 0-2 in two spot starts this season and has allowed 12 earned runs in 6 1/3 innings. He has shown to be more aggressive in his outings out of the 'pen, so the hope is that he can bring that into this start.
away_pitcher_note: Location was a problem for Moehler in his last outing, a loss to the Braves during which he yielded five runs over six innings. The right-hander walked three, and two of those baserunners scored. Moehler has not faced the Pirates yet this year. Lifetime versus the Bucs, he's 3-4 with a 4.54 ERA over 10 games, including seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm continues to be the stabilizer in the rotation. With another stellar outing his last time out, the lefty has gone at least eight innings in four of his starts this season. No other Pittsburgh starter has done so once. Maholm has revamped his preparation routine and it's led to a much-improved efficiency and a tendency to stay lower in the zone with his pitches. When he's getting groundouts, it's a sign that all is right. Maholm was the pitcher in the game between these two clubs that was rained out back in June. The lefty had allowed three runs on five hits in 2 2/3 innings before the game was postponed.
away_pitcher_note: Mussina threw 46 pitches before rain halted play when these two teams tried to wrap up their three-game series on June 26. The Yankees held a 3-1 lead in the top of the third when the umpires called for the tarp. In his most recent start, on Saturday against the Red Sox, Mussina allowed four hits and a walk in six scoreless innings to get his 261st career victory. He struck out five in what became a 2-1 Yankees victory.

home_pitcher_note: Duke had his shortest outing of the season his last time out as he was pulled after allowing six runs (five earned) on seven hits and three walks in 2 1/3 innings against the Brewers. Duke struggled especially with his control, which was surprising considering the lefty had allowed just nine walks in his last 41 2/3 innings. There's little reason to believe, though, this was more than an anomaly, as he had thrown at least six innings in 10 of his last 13 starts before the outing. In one of his best outings of the year, Duke allowed just two runs in 7 2/3 innings in a start against the Astros in early June.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse continued his dominance in a career year when he faced the Cubs on Saturday at Busch Stadium. Though he got the no-decision, Lohse lasted seven innings and gave up only two runs, lowering his ERA to 3.61. In his last nine starts, Lohse is 7-0 and finished June with a perfect record. With the prolonged absences of Chris Carpenter and Adam Wainwright, Lohse has given the Cardinals a needed reliant arm out of the starting rotation.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates recalled Herrera after Friday night's game. The 27-year-old Cuban defector will start for Phil Dumatrait, who was placed on the disabled list with continued shoulder problems. Herrera was signed by the Pirates on Dec. 18, 2006, as a non-drafted free agent from Cuba. He spent the 2001-04 seasons playing for the Cuban national team. He was 3-5 with a 3.43 ERA in 10 starts this season for Double-A Altoona.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has had some fine moments since returning from an early-June elbow injury, but he hasn't quite looked like the same pitcher who was so good in the season's first two months. He's throwing strikes, and he's keeping the ball in the park, definitely two things to like. But he hasn't found the sharpness on his slider that was such a big part of his early success, and he just isn't controlling at-bats and handling hitters the way he was before.

home_pitcher_note: Snell's last start was his first since he was placed on the disabled list with right elbow soreness. Though his efficiency was subpar -- he threw 88 pitches in 3 2/3 innings -- Snell proved that his velocity is once again back. He opened the game with 20 straight fastballs -- a pitch he said he intends to throw often at the beginning of every start from now on -- all registering about three to five mph faster than they were before the injury was discovered. This will be Snell's fourth start of the season against the Cardinals. The righty has allowed 14 runs in the first 15 innings against St. Louis this year.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro finally got a win his last time out, but he's deserved a lot more W's than he's been credited with. He'll try to even his record in the last game of the first half, and he'll be pitching in a park where he turned in one of his best games of the year. Back in April, Pineiro pitched seven exceptional innings against the Pirates at PNC Park. Pineiro hasn't allowed a homer in either of his past two starts, and over his past four games, he has a ground-ball:fly-ball ratio of just under 2.5:1.

home_pitcher_note: The early part of the season was a rough education for Jimenez, who had never started the season in a rotation. But he has learned. In his last seven starts, Jimenez is 3-3 with a 2.28 ERA, with 35 strikeouts in 43 1/3 innings. Jimenez is 3-2 with a 2.67 ERA in nine starts at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Manager John Russell said Maholm will start the first game of the second half because the lefty has been the Pirates' most effective and efficient starter all season. Maholm showed why in his last start on July 10 against the Yankees. He made the Bronx Bombers look like duds in his eight innings, allowing only two runs on seven hits. He had complete control of the strike zone and seemed to drop every curveball and slider in for strikes. The 25-year-old southpaw is 1-1 with a 3.75 ERA against the Rockies in his career. Both decisions were at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: It's been a long time since July 9, the last time Rusch pitched. But it was worth remembering. Rusch, pitching against one of his former clubs, held the Brewers to one run and five hits in six innings for his first win since April 26. The Rockies are hoping Rusch, who began the year in the Padres bullpen, will provide some veteran stability to the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Snell's last outing against the Cardinals was encouraging. His stat line [five innings, five hits, four runs and six strikeouts] wasn't overwhelming, but his approach and variety of pitches were. Snell now believes he's primed to make a strong second-half run and it begins in Colorado, where he's 1-1 with a 4.72 ERA against the Rockies in his career.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had one of his worst outings of the season in his most recent start against the Brewers, giving up seven earned runs in just 3 2/3 innings. However, Mark Redman wasn't much better against the Mets three days later, surrendering five earned runs on eight hits in just 3 1/3 innings. With Kip Wells expected to start on Monday after being on the disabled list since April 29 with a blood clot in his throwing hand, manager Clint Hurdle decided to go with the younger arm in De La Rosa and move Redman to the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: With Phil Dumatrait on the disabled list and Tom Gorzelanny in the Minors, the Pirates have two rotation spots to fill coming out of the All-Star break. This is the first one. While no announcement has been made, the most likely candidate would seem to be Yoslan Herrera, who made his Major League debut on Saturday. It was a rocky one -- six runs on 11 hits in 4 1/3 innings. However, with the lack of Major League-ready options, Herrera will still most likely get a crack at improving those results.

home_pitcher_note: Cook reported feeling fine Tuesday night after throwing 40 pitches in three memorable shutout innings in the All-Star Game at Yankee Stadium, but stay tuned as to whether the Rockies throw him in this game or adjust his schedule. He sparkled in his last start before the break, holding the Mets to one run on six hits in six innings of a game the Rockies eventually lost because of missed opportunities on offense. In that one, Cook worked his sinker well, but also got three strikeouts because his four-seam fastball was accurate and hitters were not ready for it.
away_pitcher_note: Duke has given up 11 runs on 17 hits in his last two starts. He appeared to be in control against the Cardinals on July 11 with two outs in the third, but St. Louis put together a two-out rally, scoring four runs. It was the beginning of the end for Duke, who was pulled after six innings. The lefty is 2-2 with a 2.77 ERA against the Rockies in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez will look to avenge his last outing, which resulted in 10 runs over four innings in a start against the Pirates, after which he was optioned back to Triple-A Round Rock. He is still winless with the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Once again, the Pirates will need a spot starter. With no definitive replacement for Tom Gorzelanny, John Van Benschoten will likely get another chance to pick up his first win as a starter since 2004. Van Benschoten is 1-2 with a 9.77 ERA in seven appearances (three starts) for the Pirates this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Astros recalled Cassel from Triple-A Round Rock following Monday's game to replace the injured Roy Oswalt in the lineup. The righty won his sixth straight outing on July 18, allowing two runs on five hits against Omaha, and he has a 1.92 ERA in 10 starts for the Express. He recorded his first Major League win over six scoreless innings against Pittsburgh in 2007.
away_pitcher_note: A five-run outing over six innings in Colorado bumped Maholm's ERA up over 4.00 after he lowered it in each of his last five starts. Maholm was perfect for three innings, never letting a ball out of the infield.  His next three innings were a different story, allowing eight hits, including seven for extra bases.  He ran into trouble when he started elevating his pitches, and lost the lead on a broken-bat, two-run homer on a first-pitch changeup away. The loss broke a string of nine starts without Maholm suffering defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler continued his consistent performance on the mound with a no-decision against the Cubs in his last start. He allowed one run, a homer, on four hits in seven innings, striking out three. Moehler won his previous start against Pittsburgh despite four earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Snell showed encouraging signs in his first start out of the break as he allowed three earned runs in six innings against the Rockies. Once again, his fastball velocity was consistently in the mid-90s, which, as a result, had Snell saying he felt as good as he has all season. Also, the July 18 start broke a string of four straight starts in which Snell was unable to pitch past the fifth. Snell is 2-3 with a 3.81 ERA in 10 appearances (nine starts) against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Herrera is a long shot to make a third start for the Pirates after yielding 13 runs in six innings during his first two big league starts. Herrera couldn't complete the second inning Saturday night at Coors Field, getting torched for seven runs on eight hits, a wild pitch and a hit batsman in 1 2/3 innings. He had trouble locating his fastball, and when he fell behind in counts, he was forced over the plate, allowing the Rockies to tee off. Herrera jumped from Double-A to the Majors with his July 12 call-up.
away_pitcher_note: Hensley gets the start for Randy Wolf, who was traded to Houston on Tuesday. Hensley has yet to allow a run in five innings this season. Hensley, who made 29 starts for the Padres in 2006, going 11-12 with a 3.71 ERA, posted a 1-1 record with a 3.94 ERA in 16 games, including 10 starts, with Triple-A Portland.

home_pitcher_note: Duke was masterful in the first three innings of his last start, retiring the side in order with ease in each frame. However, after tweaking his delivery motion during the mid-season break, it fell apart beginning in the fourth. As a result, Duke was smashed for nine runs on 10 hits in five total innings. The key will be finding that early-game delivery point and this time maintaining it throughout his start. Duke has not won since June 9. He is 1-1 with a 3.38 ERA in two career starts against San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Baek is coming off one of his best starts since he joined the Padres in a May trade with the Mariners. Baek did the one thing no Padres pitcher did in a four-game series in St. Louis last week -- tame the Cardinals offense. Baek allowed two runs, though only one was earned, in 6 1/3 innings on July 20 at Busch Stadium. He struck out three, allowed six hits and issued one walk. Baek helped his own cause by slugging a two-run home run in the fifth inning, though he eventually received a no-decision when the Cardinals scored three runs in the eighth inning on a Troy Glaus home run.

home_pitcher_note: With the way his first three starts had gone, almost anything would have been a step in the right direction for Van Benschoten. As a result, his five inning, two earned run performance on Monday has to be characterized as such. His aggressiveness in going after hitters is improving, though his efficiency still leaves much to be desired. The right-hander continues to look for his first win as a starter since 2004. Van Benschoten has faced San Diego one other time in his career, allowing three runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Banks isn't approaching Greg Maddux's current stretch of 13 consecutive starts without a victory, though the right-hander has now gone six consecutive starts without a victory after losing 4-3 in Cincinnati on July 21. Banks had trouble with keeping the ball in the ballpark in that start, allowing home runs to Edwin Encarnacion and Ken Griffey Jr. Going into that start, Banks had only allowed five home runs in his previous nine starts for the Padres. He was staked to a 2-0 lead but couldn't hold it in hitter-friendly Great American Ball Park.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm can officially take ownership of the "staff ace" title. In a year where the starting pitching has been dismal, Maholm has shone. He has pitched at least eight innings six times this season, including in three of his last four starts. He's lost just once since mid-May, and the efficiency he has shown with his pitch count continues to be excellent. The sinker and his two breaking pitches are his bread and butter, though his changeup has also complemented them at times as well. Maholm has faced the Padres once and allowed four runs in 7 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy looked to be in line for his eighth victory of the season in his last start, on July 21 in Cincinnati, as the Padres staked him to a 3-0 lead. But Peavy faltered in the sixth inning, allowing two walks and a couple of seeing-eye hits that ultimately led to three runs. Up to that point, Peavy, who allowed three runs in six innings, was pitching well, working fast and working ahead of hitters. Peavy was hurt in the inning when the Padres were unable to complete a double play. He is 2-0 with a 2.77 ERA in two career starts at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: For every step forward, Snell continues to take at least one back. After finally finishing six innings on July 18, Snell lasted just three in his last start. His efficiency is the area of greatest concern as it has been for most of the season. He needed 86 pitches to complete those three innings. He's also got to learn to slow his tempo on the mound. Snell faced Colorado two starts ago, lasting six innings and allowing three earned runs on six hits.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies called up De Los Santos from Triple-A Colorado Springs on Monday for his first Major League action since 2005 and his first start in the Majors since 2000. De Los Santos, 35, was 3-5 with a 4.92 ERA in 17 appearances for Colorado Springs, including 0-4, 6.62 as a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Herrera pick up his first Major League win in his third career appearances. After two horrendous starts, Herrera used his sinker early and often to get into tempo and stopped relying so heavily on his off-speed pitches like he had his previous time out. With the sinker moving and Herrera using both sides of the plate, he limited San Diego to six singles in six scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Rusch has won his past three starts and has become a vital part of the Rockies' recent resurgence. His bread-and-butter pitches -- his changeup and curveball -- weren't working against the Dodgers, but he made enough putouts to help the Rockies win. In five innings he gave up three runs on seven hits and walked two. Rusch was great against Pittsburgh on July 18, when he gave up just two runs on six hits in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After getting off to a promising start this season, Duke is now winless since June 9. He allowed five runs on seven hits in six innings, though only two of those hits were hit on the nose. Regardless, Duke continues to have trouble keeping runners off base and is in a position where he's only pitched past the fifth once in his last six starts. Duke will be facing a Colorado team that he lost to in his first start after the break. Duke started off by retiring the first 10 hitters he face before the Rockies knocked him for nine runs and 10 hits in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: The reasons Cook is having a career year are simple: He's showing batters that he can throw strikes early in counts. That means they don't feel comfortable laying off his sinker, so they're pounding ground ball after ground ball. It happened again Friday night, when he went eight innings, threw 93 pitches and gave up just five hits in a 7-2 victory over the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis did not get a decision in his last start against the Marlins. He gave up six runs on nine hits and three walks over six innings, but did gut it out. Florida had opened a 5-0 lead after three innings and Marquis was able to stay in the game to save the Cubs bullpen. He made some mistakes -- walking the leadoff man in the first and second innings isn't a good idea -- but was aided by a late inning rally from his teammates. He's 2-0 with a no-decision in three starts this year against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens could flip-flop with Paul Maholm and pitch on Saturday, but while management makes that determination, let's slot him in for Friday. Karstens came to Pittsburgh as part of the six-player trade that sent Xavier Nady and Damaso Marte to the Yankees on Saturday. This will be the right-hander's first Major League appearance this season. In 2006-07, Karstens combined to make 15 appearances (nine starts) with New York, going 3-5 with a 5.65 ERA. He was 6-4 with a 3.80 ERA in 12 Triple-A starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a decision in his last start against the Brewers. The lefty gave up three runs on seven hits, including back to back homers by J.J. Hardy and Ryan Braun, over six innings. Lilly was mad at himself for the mistakes. He finished July 1-1 in five starts. He has faced Pittsburgh twice this year, and did not get a decision in either game.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm continued his solid work in his last start against San Diego on July 27. He hurled seven innings and gave up one run on four hits. He recorded nine strikeouts and received a no-decision. Maholm has gone 5-1 in his last 11 starts. He has worked at least six innings in each of his last 15 outings.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano struck out a season-high nine batters in a win over the Brewers in his last start. Big Z threw eight scoreless innings, giving up five hits and two walks. He also hit an RBI single. Zambrano now is batting .349 -- and ranks among the NL leaders with a 2.80 ERA. He is 1-0 in two starts against the Pirates this year, facing them in back-to-back starts in late May. He went 4-1 in July, giving up seven runs over 35 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Snell had arguably his best outing of 2008 against the Rockies at PNC Park his last time out. He struck out eight and walked only one on his way to a quality seven-inning performance. Manager John Russell said he hoped  the start is a turning point for Snell. The right-hander hadn't won a game since June 11. Snell is 1-5 with a 5.26 ERA against the Cubs in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Haren has won each of his past three starts, but his last outing against the Padres on Wednesday did not start well. Haren allowed a pair of first-inning runs as he had trouble keeping his split-finger fastball down. It was a rare early outburst against him as he had allowed a total of one run in the first five innings in his previous seven starts. Haren settled in and allowed just one more run before departing after seven. He gave the team a scare in the fifth when he suffered a cramp in his right hamstring while running the bases, but stayed in the game and appeared fine.
away_pitcher_note: Moans of frustration could be heard from every part of PNC Park when Herrera gave up three first-inning runs in his last start on Tuesday. The Pirates rookie was hit hard, but was never knocked out. He came back to throw a decent five-plus innings, striking one and surrendering only six hits. The outing marked the second consecutive solid start by Herrera. He'll toe the mound for his fifth career Major League start against the Diamondbacks.

home_pitcher_note: Webb was on top of his game in his last start against the Dodgers as he allowed just one run on six hits over eight innings to become the Majors first 15-game winner. After a bit of a lull, Webb is back on a roll having won his last four decisions. He's been particularly tough on the Dodgers in his career having won eight of his last nine starts against them and the only game he didn't win he held them to just one run over eight innings and left with a lead.
away_pitcher_note: Duke is glad to see July over with, finishing the month 0-4 with a 9.51 ERA. He has allowed five runs or more in each of his last five starts and remains winless since June 9. Duke's location has been the problem. The lefty is missing his spots consistently and missing a lot of them up in the strike zone. Duke's last win actually came against Arizona in a start in which he allowed just two runs on five hits in six innings. He is 1-1 with a 5.29 ERA in three career starts against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson won his fifth straight start and the 293rd of his career, as he allowed just one unearned run on five hits over six innings against the Dodgers last Friday at Dodger Stadium. During his five-start win streak, he has allowed just five earned runs in 32 1/3 innings and he has not allowed an earned run in his last 21 innings. The Big Unit has located his pitchers better during the streak thanks to finally feeling locked in with his mechanics.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens picked up a win in his first Major League start this season, going six shutout innings. It wasn't exactly dominant, as he allowed five hits and four walks in the outing. However, Karstens showcased an impressive offspeed repertoire when needed. Whether he relies so heavily on his slider and curveball moving forward remains to be seen. The Pirates acquired Karstens in a deal with the Yankees, and he will remain in the Pirates' rotation after spending the first four months of the season in Triple-A.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton earned his first win on Saturday since joining the Phillies in mid-July. He came over from the West Coast with a reputation as a guy that could carry a team into the late innings, but his previous outing -- July 27 against the Braves -- had been cut short because of a long rain delay. Facing a Cardinals lineup Saturday that featured five hitters batting higher than .300, Blanton posted seven innings, allowing one run on four hits to earn the win. Blanton has never faced the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm's last start was an anomaly from the left-hander's dominant string of performances in recent weeks. He allowed five runs on eight hits in six innings after surrendering more than three runs in a game only once in his previous eight starts. His troubles on Saturday could boil down to one thing: location. Maholm struggled keeping the ball down, and the Cubs thrived off the mistakes. This shouldn't be too much of a setback, however, as Maholm has always shown a knack for bouncing right back.

home_pitcher_note: Myers continued to make strides since his return from a Minor League stint with a six-inning, two-run effort against the Cardinals on Sunday night in which the right-hander allowed four hits, struck out three and did not walk a batter. During the season's first three months, Myers posted a 3-9 record and 5.84 ERA before being optioned to Triple-A Lehigh Valley. In three starts since his return, Myers is 1-0 with a 2.50 ERA. Though the 27-year-old allowed a Major League-leading 24 home runs through the end of June, he has allowed just one home run since his return from the Minors. In seven career appearances against the Pirates, Myers is 2-4 with a 2.92 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Snell exited his last start due to a combination of lower back stiffness, high pitch count and inefficiency. His back tightened in the second and never loosened up, though it is not expected to cost him a start. The right-hander allowed four runs in four innings and has now pitched four or fewer innings eight times this season. On Sunday, he simply never found his fastball and never located his command. Snell is 3-2 with a 4.50 ERA in five career starts against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer's string of five consecutive quality starts and 10 consecutive victories against the Marlins came to an end on Tuesday against Florida. The veteran lefty yielded two runs in five innings, struggled with his command throughout the night, walking three and yielding six hits. In 11 career starts against the Dodgers, Moyer is 3-5 with a 5.19 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Davis has been named the latest in a revolving door of fifth starters for this rotation. He takes the place of Yoslan Herrera, who lasted just 1 1/3 innings in his fourth and likely final start this season. Davis started for Triple-A Indianapolis until being called up in late July to serve in a bullpen role with the Bucs. He pitched seven innings in that role and allowed two runs. In 21 games (20 starts) with Indianapolis, Davis went 6-9 with a 4.41 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez settled down after a shaky start on Wednesday night against the Padres. The righty gave up a home run on the first pitch of the game, then surrendered another just two batters later to put the Mets in an early hole. But he retired the next eight batters he faced and allowed just two more hits through 6 1/3 innings. He exited the game after throwing 102 pitches in just his second game since July 12. Martinez was tagged for three runs (two earned) with three strikeouts and three walks. Despite the loss, the righty said he has been able to make adjustments and improve through his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Duke posted one of his best performances of the season his last time out, though he suffered his sixth straight loss, with Brandon Webb going the distance against him in a 3-1 Arizona win. Duke finished seven innings and allowed just four hits, while striking out a season-high six. The two-run homer he gave up proved to be the difference in the game. The outing was a much-needed step in the right direction for Duke, who had given up at least five runs in each of his last five starts. Duke is 2-0 with a 1.77 ERA in three career starts against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens came four outs away from pitching a perfect game his last time out, but he finished with a two-hit shutout nonetheless. Since coming over to the Pirates, Karstens is 2-0 and has not given up a run in 15 innings. After issuing four walks in his first start, Karstens lived up to his reputation as a strike thrower in his most recent start and finished the game with just one walk. He used all four of his pitches with ease and showed that he is not afraid to alter his approach based on the strengths of the team that he's facing.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez has lost command of his fastball, and that has turned him from a dominating pitcher into an ordinary one. His work against the Brewers in his last outing highlighted the caliber of his recent work. Volquez piled up a high pitch count early. He would have been well over the 100-pitch mark had he lasted longer than five innings. As it was, he threw 96 pitches; 36 of them were balls. In his past four starts, he's given up a combined 19 runs in 21 1/3 innings. That's not the statistical line for success -- no matter how much offensive support a pitcher gets from his teammates.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm held the Phillies scoreless through seven innings on Friday night, scattering five hits in the process. The lefty has been an innings-eater for Pittsburgh -- Maholm has lasted at least six innings in each of his last 17 starts and 19 of his first 23 starts overall. He also struck out 10 batters on Friday night, his highest total of 2008. In 12 career starts against the Reds, Maholm is 2-3 with a 4.28 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Label Fogg's last outing "forgettable," because that's surely about the best thing for Fogg to do with it -- forget about it. He had all sorts of trouble in holding the Astros at bay. He found himself pitching from the stretch in each of his three-plus innings, which speaks to the traffic he put on base. He gave up six runs on eight hits. His was an outing marked by an inability to command the strike zone, a problem that Fogg doesn't have the electric stuff to overcome.

home_pitcher_note: Snell turned in a solid performance on Saturday against the Phillies, despite losing, 4-2. Snell got off to a bad start, giving up two runs in the first inning, which seems to a problem this season. He went five scoreless innings before giving up another run in the seventh. Snell is 3-5 lifetime against Cincinnati, with a 5.87 ERA in nine starts. He's 1-1 against the Reds this season, with a 7.94 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto's outing last Friday proved a mixed bag. He had a stretch here and there where he looked untouchable, as his nine strikeouts demonstrated. But sandwiched around those strikeouts were nine base hits. Not necessarily a bad total had he gone the distance, but nine hits, a walk and an hit batter can be a prescription for trouble. The 22-year-old Cueto had his troubles against the Astros, though he limited them to no big innings. What he also did was showcase the kind of potential Dusty Baker has said he has. Now, if Cueto can show more command of the strike zone, he'll cement his slot in a Reds rotation that remains under construction.

home_pitcher_note: If Pirates manager John Russell wants to stick with Davis, he'll get the go on Friday when the Bucs host the New York Mets. Davis did well in his first start this season for the Pirates, on Sunday at Philadelphia. He surrendered two runs, both unearned, on four hits. Though he took a no-decision, he displayed good velocity on his fastball over six innings and showed a decent slider. Prior to the Sunday's start, Davis had pitched seven innings out of the bullpen, giving up two runs.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey was pulled on Sunday after allowing six runs in 4 2/3 innings against the Marlins, struggling with his command by matching his three strikeouts with three walks and a hit batsman. The first, second and third innings were a setback, but the fourth and fifth were his undoing, as he faced 15 batters who accounted for four of his earned runs. In three appearances against the Marlins this season, Pelfrey has surrendered 15 runs in 12 2/3 innings. Next, he'll take on the Pirates, whom he has never faced.

home_pitcher_note: Duke settled into a rhythm after getting off to a shaky start against the Mets on Monday afternoon. Duke was tagged for five runs (three earned) and gave up two homers, but most of his struggles came in the first three innings, and the lefty kept his team in the game long enough to come away with a no-decision. He gave up eight hits, striking out three, with one walk. Duke remains 2-0 in four career starts against the Mets, and he will get the chance to improve that record on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez sustained a Mets lead through six innings against the Pirates on Monday, holding them to one run and three hits. Four walks opposed to three strikeouts put Martinez in a couple tough spots, but he worked his way out of jams with a timely changeup and a fastball that peaked at 90 mph in the latter innings. He'll face the Pirates again, this time on the road at PNC Park, one of three ballparks where Martinez has yet to allow a home run in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Despite giving up two early home runs against the Reds in his last start, Karstens proved he could bounce back from adversity with a strong seven-inning performance. The outing came four days after his shutout at Arizona. Despite his first loss as a Pirate, manager John Russell liked how the right-hander kept attacking hitters and sticking with stuff. Karstens will go for win No. 3 against a Mets squad he has yet to face in his short career.
away_pitcher_note: Santana picked up his 10th win of the season Tuesday night with a strong performance against Washington. The lefty went seven innings, striking out six and allowing just three runs while walking two. He scattered eight hits over the start, throwing just 94 pitches, 65 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm has taken hold of that "ace" label and run with it. The lefty allowed two runs in eight innings his last time out and has now pitched through the sixth inning in 18 consecutive starts. He's allowed two or fewer runs in seven of his last nine. The consistency of all four of Maholm's pitches continues to improve, and as a result, he's maintaining great efficiency. Not to mention he threw 22 first-pitch strikes in his last start. Maholm is 3-1 with a 2.16 ERA in four career starts against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Maine was in command in his first start back from right rotator cuff soreness. Over five innings, the right-hander struck out six and allowed just one hit and no runs. He walked four before giving way to the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Looper has been brilliant lately, enjoying the finest stretch of his two seasons in the starting rotation. He's pitching deep into games and throwing strikes. He's been occasionally prone to the homer, but everything else is going so well that the solo shots haven't been a problem for the most part. Over his past eight starts, Looper has 29 strikeouts and eight walks.
away_pitcher_note: Snell was good (not great), but with the way things have gone this season, his last start has to at least be a small step in the right direction. The righty gave up five walks and six hits in six innings, but somehow managed to limit the damage to just two runs scored. He would, however, be pegged with his 10th loss of the season because of no run support. The key for Snell remains pounding the strike zone, something that he has looked hesitant doing all year. Snell is winless in four starts against St. Louis this year. He's allowed 19 runs in 19 total innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has clearly regained his form after an injury-hampered June and a slump through much of July. He's allowed eight runs over his past five starts, and his stuff has been very sharp. He's got his slider back, and he's augmenting it with an improved changeup. The right-hander will be pitching on five days' rest thanks to the Cardinals' Monday off-day.
away_pitcher_note: With two starts under his belt, Davis has solidified himself in the rotation, at least for the time being. After allowing two first-inning runs on Friday, Davis settled down and kept the Mets scoreless through the final six frames of his seven-inning start. Davis has now allowed just two earned runs in 13 innings as a starter. The righty doesn't have overpowering stuff, but it continues to be effective because he is consistently throwing down in the strike zone. Davis has never faced St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Bush's performance may have been lost amid the drama of the Brewers' see-saw win Saturday at Dodger Stadium, but he pitched a gem. Matt Kemp doubled leading off the first inning against Bush and Andre Ethier followed with a home run for a quick 2-0 lead, but Bush then blanked the Dodgers on three more hits through the seventh. Left fielder Gabe Kapler tumbled into the stands to deny the Dodgers a home run in Bush's last inning of work, and he was briefly in line for the win when shortstop J.J. Hardy hit a two-run homer in the eighth. Instead, Bush settled for a no-decision and his seventh outing of at least seven innings in his past 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Duke was hit hard for six runs on nine hits in his last start, against the Mets. The lefty still has not won since June 9. He said he has tried a variety of things to shake up this unfortunate streak, but nothing has worked. Opponents swing freely against Duke, and he rarely gets swings and misses. He'll try to go for win No. 5 against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan has been on again, off again all season, and on Sunday in Los Angeles, he was off. He surrendered four runs on nine Dodgers hits, including a trio of home runs that left the Brewers facing deficits of 3-0 and 4-1. Matt Kemp and Manny Ramirez each hit Suppan's first offering for home runs in the first inning. Before that, Suppan had been outstanding in three starts since his dismal July 27 outing against the Astros, going 3-0 in those games with a 2.05 ERA (five earned runs in 22 innings). The Brewers hope Suppan continues his trend as a strong second-half pitcher. In 2007, his first year with Milwaukee, Suppan posted a 5.00 ERA before the All-Star break but lowered it to 4.12 afterward.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny will make his return to the Majors after spending more than a month at Triple-A Indianapolis. The lefty didn't take the demotion well at first, but he rebounded with a 3-1 record and a 2.06 ERA in seven starts as he rebuilt his arm strength. His last start before being sent down came at Milwaukee on July 4, when he gave up eight runs and 11 hits in 4 2/3 innings. Gorzelanny's promotion means that previously scheduled starter Jeff Karstens will start on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Ned Yost said the decision to keep every starter on regular turn, thus allowing for extra days of rest, played a role in the decision to let Sabathia work all nine innings on Monday against Houston. The Astros sent seven men to the plate and drove the lefty's pitch count to 130 before Lance Berkman bounded out with the bases loaded. The workhorse recorded his fifth shutout in nine starts, and he also had two hits and two huge RBIs in the win. "I guess they're going to hitch their wagon to him and ride him on off in the sunset," Astros manager Cecil Cooper said. "He was a horse tonight. Not only on the mound, but swinging the bat."
away_pitcher_note: Maholm continues to be steady and consistent. His last time out, Maholm pitched at least six innings for a 19th consecutive start. Eleven of his 20 starts have lasted at least seven innings. There's no doubt that his confidence level has soared, and he has all four of his pitches working nearly every time out. The only thing to keep an eye on is his innings total, which is already close to matching his previous career high (177 2/3), which was set last year. Maholm is 0-1 against the Brewers this year. He has allowed five earned runs and struck out 11 in 14 1/3 innings against them.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens continues to pitch deep into games, but he also continues to give up runs. His four-run, nine-hit performance against the Mets was good enough to give his team a chance to win, but he was opposed by two-time Cy Young Award winner Johan Santana, who threw a shutout. Pirates manager John Russell continues to praise Karstens for the right-hander's ability to attack the strike zone and go after hitters. He'll try to recapture the magic of his first two Pirates starts against the Cubs, whom Karstens shut out over five innings in his National League debut on Aug. 1.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly had a no-hitter broken up by the leadoff batter in the sixth in his last start and wound up losing a 2-1 decision to the Reds. He only gave up two hits in seven innings and struck out seven. That outing lowered his ERA to 4.25, the lowest it's been after a start all season. The lefty dominated Pittsburgh on Aug. 2, holding the Pirates to one run and six hits in 6 1/3 innings for the win. But he was touched up by them in two previous starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Snell picked up just his third win since mid-April his last time out and finally looked dominant in doing so. The right-hander relied heavily on his changeup and slider to complement his fastball, which he established early. The key for Snell continues to be going aggressively after hitters, which he did successfully on Tuesday. If he does so, Snell can limit his pitch count, which has been on the high end early in games too often this year. Snell is winless in two starts against the Cubs this season. He has allowed seven runs in 10 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Let's see if Zambrano can keep his hitting streak going. He belted his fourth home run of the season in his last start to keep his streak alive at seven games. Big Z also picked up the win against the Reds, giving up one run over seven innings. He was able to slow down his delivery and correct some mechanical flaws that have popped up in the last two starts. He did walk the leadoff batter -- something that really annoys the right-hander. Right now, he's batting .361 and has an ERA of 3.29. That's pretty good.

home_pitcher_note: Duke's winless drought continued in Friday's loss at Milwaukee. It's now at eight straight losses dating to June 9. He tinkered with his throwing motion last week, and despite giving up four runs in six innings to the Brewers, was pleased with his delivery. The left-hander has struggled against the Cubs this season, going 0-2 with a 5.91 ERA in four starts, but then again, he's struggled against just about everybody. Duke has had moderate success against Chicago in 12 career starts with a 4-4 record and a 3.16 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis was cruising in his last start, against the Nationals, throwing five scoreless innings before he got into a mess, giving up an infield single and walking the next two batters. The Cubs eventually lost, 13-5, although he did not factor in the decision. Marquis was working on eight days' rest and would prefer to pitch on a regular routine, like the other starters. This will be a chance for the right-hander to show that's the best scenario.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny has probably seen enough of the Brewers, but the schedule makers aren't giving him a break. His last two big league starts, both 4 2/3-inning clunkers, came at Milwaukee. An eight-run outing at Miller Park on the Fourth of July got Gorzelanny demoted to Triple-A Indianapolis for a month. He returned on Saturday, only to give up six more runs and exit before the end of the fifth once again. This time, he gets the Brewers at PNC Park, where he's 5-1 with an ERA almost five runs lower than his road mark.
away_pitcher_note: Bush is on a roll. He improved to 3-0 with a 2.30 ERA in four August starts with a win over the Pirates at Miller Park on Aug. 22 and has worked at least into the seventh inning in seven of his last eight starts. He's just 2-6 with a 5.76 ERA in 12 appearances, 11 starts, on the road this season, but has allowed three earned runs in 14 innings over his last two starts away from home. Because of two team off-days this week, Bush will be working on two extra days of rest.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm got a no-decision in his last start, when he went toe to toe with CC Sabathia and tossed six innings of two-run ball. He went six for the 20th straight start, a streak not seen in Pittsburgh in 22 years. Nearly as impressive, Ryan Braun and Prince Fielder grounded into a combined three double plays and struck one time each against the lefty. Maholm hasn't beaten the Brewers in three starts this year, but he had one of his best starts of the year at Miller Park on July 5. Even though Pittsburgh lost, 2-1, he held Milwaukee to one run in eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan apparently benefited from his brief stint on the disabled list over the All-Star break. Since missing one start because of a sore right elbow, he has pitched at least six innings in all seven of his starts and at least seven innings five times. That includes Aug. 23 against the Pirates, when Suppan allowed the leadoff man to reach base in each of the first eight innings but escaped with allowing three runs in seven-plus innings of work. He is 4-0 with a 3.09 ERA in five August starts.

home_pitcher_note: After starting the month out 2-0 with 15 scoreless innings, Karstens has dropped each of his last three starts. He has a 6.75 ERA during that span. And most telling may be this: opponents were hitting .143 against Karstens in those first two starts; they have hit .328 against him since. Location was Karstens' biggest problem in his start Monday against the Cubs, as he left most of his off-speed pitches up and over the plate. The Pirates are going to continue to watch Karstens' pitch count as they don't want to overexert him during this final month. This will be Karstens' first career appearance against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia insisted that his workload in a much-debated 130-pitch outing against the Astros on Aug. 18 had little to do with his command issues six days later against the Pirates. Sabathia surrendered only one run in six innings, but he had to work around eight hits in the shortest of his 10 starts for Milwaukee. Sabathia settled for a no-decision in an eventual 4-3, 12-inning win over Pittsburgh. "I think maybe having six days off had more to do with it than anything," Sabathia said. "But I felt I made some pitches when I needed to and I kept us in the game."

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, against the Astros on Thursday, Harang pitched seven innings and gave up three earned runs on seven hits without walking a batter for a quality start. His nine strikeouts tied a season high, but all three runs came on solo home runs, leading to a 3-2 loss. "Those two to [Ty] Wigginton were the only two mistakes I made," Harang said of two of the homers. "Pretty much, I was putting the ball right where I wanted to." Following two rough starts after he came off the disabled list earlier this month due to a sore forearm, Harang has put together back-to-back quality outings and has looked mostly good.
away_pitcher_note: Snell will look to rebound after an outing in which he allowed four runs and walked five in just four innings. Paramount again will be lowering his pitch count, which stood at 95 after just four frames. Snell fell behind in the count often and was unable to entice Chicago to offer at his pitches off the plate. It will be interesting to see if Snell goes back to pitching inside a little more often, which was done with much success two starts again. This will be Snell's fourth start against the Reds. He has given up 12 runs in 17 1/3 innings vs. Cincinnati and is 1-2.

home_pitcher_note: Against the Giants in his last start, Volquez earned his 16th win of the season despite giving up more earned runs (six) in a start than he had all season. In 5 1/3 innings, Volquez gave up eight hits and walked three, but he benefited from heavy run support, which the Reds have provided for Volquez regularly this season. He has faced the Pirates three times this year, earning his first decision against the Bucs the last time he faced them, when he won on Aug. 12, giving up one earned run on five hits and three walks in 6 2/3 innings, while striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf will make his first Major League start -- and first appearance for the Pirates -- when he takes the mound against Cincinnati. Ohlendorf was a September callup by the club and will be a part of a six-man rotation for the Pirates during these last four weeks of the season. The 6-foot-4 right-hander was acquired from the Yankees in late July and was stretched back into being a starter in seven Triple-A games. Ohlendorf went 1-1 with a 6.53 ERA in 31 relief appearances early this season. He finished 4-3 with a 3.47 ERA in seven Triple-A Indianapolis starts.

home_pitcher_note: Fogg posted just his third quality start of the season on Wednesday but had the misfortune of being opposed by Roy Oswalt in a 4-1 loss to the Astros. Fogg, who entered the night 0-6 with a 9.58 ERA in his past 11 games vs. Houston, was much better than history would have suggested. The right-hander gave up two earned runs on six hits, with one walk and two strikeouts. His lone mistake was hanging an 0-1 curveball to Hunter Pence, who launched it for a two-run homer that put Houston ahead for good.
away_pitcher_note: Though he didn't get a win, Gorzelanny showed signs of progress in his last start. The lefty settled down after throwing a 22-pitch first inning in which he allowed three runs. From there, Gorzelanny's efficiency was the best it has been all season. He needed just 75 pitches to finish six more innings and allowed just one walk and one hit after the first. Gorzelanny is 1-1 against Cincinnati this year. He allowed one run in 6 1/3 innings against the Reds in an April start, before allowing six runs in just two-thirds of an inning in a start in Cincinnati in May.

home_pitcher_note: Correia has worked at least six innings in five of his last six starts, although he's only 1-2 in that stretch. He allowed six runs and seven hits over six innings in his most recent outing Saturday at Cincinnati, walking two and striking out two. A five-run first inning by the Reds jarred Correia, who recovered to allow only one hit afterward -- a home run by Edwin Encarnacion, only the second long ball Correia has yielded in seven starts. Correia has no record against Pittsburgh and a 3.00 ERA in three relief appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Duke picked up the loss in his last start, despite making one of his strongest performances in the last two months. It was the second straight start in which Duke employed a slightly different delivery, and afterward, he credited it with his success. Duke is holding his arms higher at the start of his motion, which forces him to stand straighter on the mound. The result? More downward action on his pitches. Still, Duke comes into the start having lost nine straight decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Cain was off his form in his most recent start, last Sunday at Cincinnati, allowing five runs and eight hits in five innings while walking five. Before that, he had posted a 2.13 ERA in a nine-start stretch, which included eight quality starts. Cain lost to the Pirates on May 8, taking a 4-2 lead into the seventh inning before yielding three runs. He's 0-2 lifetime against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm has been the Pirates' most consistent starter this season, but he came up short in his last outing, absorbing an 11-3 loss to the Brewers on Saturday. Maholm (8-8) lasted only 5 1/3 innings for his shortest outing since May 3. He was charged with six runs -- the most he has allowed since May 3 -- on seven hits and a walk, striking out three. He had made 20 consecutive starts where he pitched at least six innings.

home_pitcher_note: After missing three games with left shoulder problems, Sanchez pitched extremely well against the Rockies, giving up three runs on three hits and striking out six in seven innings. However, he received zero run support and was saddled with his sixth straight losing decision. Manager Bruce Bochy lauded Sanchez's use of his fastball and changeup, and Sanchez said he felt no pain during the outing.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens made his sixth start for the Pirates since being acquired in a July 26 trade with the New York Yankees. The right-hander allowed three runs on five hits in 6 1/3 innings of work in a 7-0 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday. Karstens suffered the loss, his fourth in a row, and fell to 2-4 on the season. His pitch location was much better as he tossed 74 of his 110 pitches for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Arias will make a spot start in place of Brandon Backe, who is experiencing soreness in his elbow. Arias, whom the Astros picked up off waivers from the Rockies on July 31, was 1-0 with a 1.52 ERA and one save in eight appearances, including three starts, for Triple-A Round Rock. Arias appeared in 18 career big league games over a two-season span with the Rockies, compiling a 1-0 record and a 3.43 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Snell has now won each of his last two decisions and appears on track to finish the season on a strong note. The right-hander has pitched at least six innings in four of his past five starts after doing so only three times in all his June and July starts combined. Snell again did a better job of attacking the strike zone and getting ahead early, both keys to his recent success. Snell will be making his third start of the season against Houston. Though he didn't factor in either decision, Snell allowed six earned runs in 6 2/3 combined innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf had his best Astros outing in his last start at Wrigley Field on Wednesday, throwing his 12th career complete game and seventh shutout in a 3-0 Houston win. Wolf has allowed one run over his past two outings, spanning 15 innings. The left-hander has not faced the Pirates this year. In his career, he's 5-1 with a 3.61 ERA vs. the Bucs over eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his first Major League start, Ohlendorf didn't factor in the decision despite putting up a respectable performance. He allowed four runs (three earned) on seven hits in six innings. Though his velocity didn't reach the high 90s as anticipated, he was steadily throwing in the mid-90s range and attacked the zone with consistency. You can expect to see that velocity return before the season ends. Ohlendorf has made two career relief appearances against Houston while with the Yankees. In two innings, the righty allowed two hits, one walk and one run. He struck out one.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Moehler had one of his shorter outings since he joined the starting rotation, allowing five runs over 4 2/3 innings in a loss to the Rockies. The right-hander has faced the Pirates twice this year, both as a starter. He earned the win on July 9 in Pittsburgh after yielding four runs over seven innings, and on July 23 at home, he took the loss in his shortest outing of the year, allowing six runs (five earned) in 2 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Staked to a 5-0 lead after an inning and a half against the Reds in his last start, Gorzelanny couldn't take advantage, getting knocked out by the Reds before completing four innings. Although his strikeout-to-walk ratio has shown some slight improvement since he was called up on Aug. 23, Gorzelanny still has more walks than strikeouts for the season (68 to 65). Gorzelanny has just four quality starts in his past 17 outings.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt extended his scoreless-innings streak to 23 1/3 frames with a shutout of the Rockies in his last outing, throwing only the second one-hitter in Coors Field history. Oswalt has won eight of his past nine decisions and hasn't yielded a run since the second inning of his start against the Reds on Aug. 27. The right-hander last faced the Pirates on June 4 at PNC Park, taking the loss after allowing four runs (three earned) on nine hits over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: One-game aberration or full-blown turnaround? This start will go a long way toward proving which phrase best describes Duke, who snapped an 0-9 stretch with a 6.82 ERA in a most emphatic manner on Friday: He throttled the Giants on six hits, all singles, for his second career shutout. Duke recorded 17 groundouts in the victory and had the Giants biting on his sinker, even though they knew it was coming, time and again.

home_pitcher_note: Coming back after his streak of 20 consecutive starts with six or more innings had bitten the dust, Maholm got back in that mode by lasting six full innings against the Giants. Maholm never looked fully comfortable, though, and he was helped by a double play that should have just been a forceout. Maholm said he's not fatigued, despite having thrown a career-high 185 1/3 innings to this point.

Scheduled starter Jeff Karstens will miss this start because of an abscessed tooth on the left side of his mouth The right-hander sat in the Pirates' clubhouse on Friday with a swollen left cheek, which didn't heal enough to allow him to take the mound tonight. Ian Snell will pitch in Karstens' place, but will have had a regular four days of rest because of the Pirates' move to a six-man rotation on Sept. 2.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright is dealing, and it's just like he never left. The right-hander has put to rest the only two lingering questions from his first couple of starts off the disabled list. He's missing bats again, to the tune of 13 strikeouts in his past two outings. And he lasted eight innings on Sunday, his longest start since before he injured his finger. It's a short list of better starters in the NL than a healthy Wainwright.

home_pitcher_note: Davis' bouncing in and out of the starting rotation continues. The right-hander will take the mound on Sunday for Ian Snell, who filled in for an injured Jeff Karstens on Saturday night. The start will be Davis' fourth with the Pirates this season. In those games, he's given up 12 runs in 16 2/3 innings pitched. Manager John Russell said Davis will be limited in his pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro, initially slated for Friday, started the series opener in Pittsburgh. Thompson, announced as Friday's starter on Thursday, will instead pitch the series finale on Sunday. Thompson is 5-2 with a 4.61 ERA this season in 23 games, four of which were starts.

home_pitcher_note: The high-90s velocity that Ohlendorf was said to possess has still not shown itself in a Pirates uniform. That would be OK if he substituted some velocity for command, but that wasn't the case in his most recent outing. Ohlendorf allowed six runs on nine hits against the Astros and was bumped from the game after four innings with his velocity hovering in the mid-90s. It will likely not creep much higher during these final two weeks of the season. Ohlendorf continues to audition for a starting spot and will be making his first career appearance against the Dodgers with this start.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda delivered a gritty performance with little support in his 10th no-decision at San Diego. Lacking a go-to pitch all night, he allowed nine hits and had to pitch out of trouble four of his six innings, but allowed only two runs. He'll be pitching in Pittsburgh for the first time and allowed the Pirates three runs in 6 2/3 innings in a no-decision at home April 14.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens made quite a first impression upon arriving in a trade with the Yankees, throwing 15 shutout innings in his first two starts, the second one a complete game. His five starts since then, however, were mediocre to bleak and he lost all of them. He allowed eight runs in three innings to the Giants in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Derek Lowe expects to be fine for this start against Pittsburgh, although he was driven from last week's outing in San Diego after taking a comebacker off the back of his right knee. He allowed one earned run in 5 1/3 innings to continue his late-season roll, having won his last three decisions and four of his last five. He's allowed five runs in 40 2/3 innings (1.11 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Though Duke started out extremely sharp in his last outing against the Astros, he was undone by some fielding errors and then by his own poor pitch location. Duke came into that start after putting together one of his better stretches this season. He had thrown at least six innings in six consecutive starts, though he lasted just 4 2/3 against Houston. With only two more starts left this season, Duke will look to improve on the results he had against the Dodgers in a start against them back in April. Duke allowed four runs -- three earned -- in six innings in that outing.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley came into Coors Field with an 8.76 ERA in Denver, but he delivered a solid start, allowing two runs over six innings. It wasn't overpowering, as he struck out three and stranded five Rockies in scoring position. He leads club starters in wins, ERA and strikeouts, and has gone 12 straight outings without allowing more than three runs, a time in which he's 7-2 with a 2.52 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm shows no signs of wearing down as the season comes to an end, putting in a performance in his last outing as good as any he's had this season. Though he fell just short of notching his first shutout of the season, Maholm pitched eight strong innings on his way to another dominant victory. He is approaching the 200-inning count rapidly, which may force the Pirates to be more hesitant to extend him in his final two starts. Maholm will get another shot at the Dodgers after losing to L.A. in April, when he allowed six runs (four earned) in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw made all the right adjustments, rebounding not only from four shaky innings in his most recent start, but the kind of Coors Field debut that can leave a 20-year-old pitcher permanently scarred. Instead, he allowed only one run on four hits over six innings. He was able to do it by relying on a curveball in the thin air, and not many can do that. He'll be facing the Pirates for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Snell's roller coaster 2008 season took a dip down in his last start on Saturday against the Cardinals. St. Louis collected six runs on nine hits and chased the Pittsburgh right-hander from the game after only four innings. Snell found trouble in the game after continually missing his spots high and the Cardinals made him pay for it. He is 2-4 with a 4.41 ERA against the Astros in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf had his shortest outing since joining the Astros against the Cubs on Sunday in Milwaukee. After traveling all day from Hurricane-damaged Houston to Milwaukee for the first of two "neutral site" games with the Cubs, Wolf allowed four runs over 2 1/3 innings. Wolf has good career numbers against the Pirates -- 6-1 record, 3.64 ERA over nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: General manager Neal Huntington said Barthmaier's next likely start for the Pirates will come on Saturday. In the right-hander's Major League debut, the Rays gave Barthmaier a rude welcoming. Tampa Bay scored three first-inning runs and knocked the 24-year-old out of the game after seven earned runs and 2 1/3 innings. He'll get a chance to make a better second impression against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler yielded five runs for for the second time this month during his last outing, a five-inning effort against the Cubs at Miller Park. Moehler is 5-4 with a 5.14 ERA over eight career games (five starts) vs. the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf struggled in his three innings against the Dodgers on Monday, surrendering three runs on five hits. His fastball, which was lauded by Pirates management when they received the right-hander in a trade from New York, was met with several thunderous swings from Los Angeles' lineup. Now in three starts with the Pirates, Ohlendorf has given up 11 earned runs in 13 innings pitched. He is 0-1 with a 10.50 ERA against the Astros in his young career.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt saw his franchise-record 32 1/3 consecutive scoreless innings get snapped early in a loss to the Marlins on Tuesday. The 31-year-old threw 29 pitches and gave up four runs in the first inning, which doomed his Astros the rest of the night. Oswalt did end on a good note, giving up just one hit while striking out six in his last four innings, but his struggles against Florida this season continued. In two games against the Marlins in 2008, Oswalt is 0-2 with a 9.90 ERA (11 earned runs in 10 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Bush is the most likely choice to take the injured Ben Sheets' spot because he would be on regular rest. Bush hasn't won this month, but he hasn't pitched poorly. He has not given up more than three runs in any of his past three starts, including his last outing, at Wrigley Field on three days' rest. The right-hander held the Cubs to a pair of solo homers in five innings and would have received the win if Salomon Torres hadn't blown a four-run lead in the ninth. In his last start against Pittsburgh, Bush gave up one run in 6 2/3 innings on Aug. 29 to get his ninth win. He's 2-1 with a 3.71 ERA in four starts against the Pirates this season.
away_pitcher_note: A bad umpiring call worked against Karstens in his last start, though the right-hander can't escape the fact that he allowed 11 hits and needed 91 pitches to finish five innings. Fatigue seems to have set in with Karstens some, and for a pitcher who is not overpowering, that has been just enough to give opponents the edge. Karstens has lost each of his last six starts. One of those losses came against Milwaukee, though it was more a reflection of how good CC Sabathia was than how off Karstens may have been. Karstens allowed three runs on five hits in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia will be working on short rest for the second straight start and could pitch short again in the regular-season finale, if needed, as the Brewers get every last mile out of their second-half rental. He worked on three days' rest in his last outing, at Cincinnati, and surrendered four runs, though three scored unearned after a Prince Fielder error. Sabathia, who is coming up on free agency, isn't worried that some of his postseason suitors will be turned off by his heavy late-season workload. "I'm doing this to get in the playoffs and I really don't care what other teams say or are worried about," he said.
away_pitcher_note: For the ninth time this season, Maholm picked up a no-decision in a start in which he allowed three or fewer runs. In fact in five of those no-decisions, he's given up one or none. Maholm did issue six walks in his last start, though they were a quiet six walks. The seven innings Maholm pitched pushed him over the 200-inning mark, but put him comfortably in position not to exceed the 211-inning maximum set my management. Maholm is still looking for his first win against the Brewers this season. He is 0-2 against them and has allowed 13 runs in 25 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers are rolling the dice to some extent with Gallardo, who has not pitched in a game since he tore the ACL in his right knee on May 1 at Wrigley Field. He underwent surgery and quietly rehabbed all summer, and the Brewers believe he'll be good for about 70 pitches against the Pirates. Gallardo is a fine hitter, but did not pick up a bat until Wednesday, so it will be interesting to see how he approaches his at-bats. He can also expect the Pirates to drop a bunt or two to test his mobility. Left-hander Manny Parra and right-hander Seth McClung will be on high alert in the bullpen should Gallardo need a bailout.
away_pitcher_note: Duke's last start against the Dodgers was eerily similar to ones that preceded it. The left-hander strung together three goose eggs to begin the game, but was hit hard with a four-run inning. He would eventually be taken after five-plus innings, where he allowed 11 hits and five runs. Duke has only one victory in the second half of the 2008 season. He'll look to close the year on a good note against the Brewers, who he is 3-4 with a 5.08 ERA against in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Geer continues to impress the Padres after limiting the Rockies to one run over five innings in his last start on Sept. 17. And that game was played at Coors Field, no less, where the rookie right-hander allowed only a solo home run to Joe Koshansky in the fourth inning. Three walks helped add to Geer's pitch total, though he also struck out five and allowed five hits. Geer didn't get nearly as many fly-ball outs (five) as he did in his last outing (16).
away_pitcher_note: Snell was not his aggressive self in his last start against the Astros. However, the right-hander still managed to limit Houston to only one earned run and three hits. The loss gave him his 12th defeat of the season, which tied his 2007 total. His six victories this season are three fewer than he had the year before and his 5.54 ERA is almost twice as much as last season. Snell will be starting against the Padres for only the second time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: You can't fault Young for trying to make up for lost time as he was sidelined for two months after taking a line drive off the face in May. Young has been especially good since his return from the disabled list and he certainly was good on Sept. 20 against the Nationals when he allowed two hits over seven shutout innings. He even hit his first Major League home run. In his seven starts since returning from the disabled list, Young is 2-2 with a 3.61 ERA, though a rough start in Colorado on Aug. 10, in which he allowed seven runs, skews those statistics some.
away_pitcher_note: Barthmaier, the Pirates' rookie right-hander, made a rocky yet productive second Major League start against the Astros last week. He allowed the first two runners to reach base in each of his three innings. But somehow, he was able to minimize the damage. In his second go-around, Barthmaier appeared more in tune with his surroundings and showed slightly more maturity in difficult situations.

home_pitcher_note: Baek has had an uneven turn as a starter with the Padres since being acquired from the Mariners in May, but the results have been better lately, like his last start on Sept. 21 when he held Washington to one run in seven innings with no walks and five strikeouts. Baek, at the urging of the coaching staff, hastened his tempo, which prevented him from losing focus as he sometimes did on the mound. Consider Baek a lock for the 2009 rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf struggled to gain any momentum in his five innings against the Astros on Sunday. He surrendered four runs on 10 hits, struck out three and walked two. Overall, manager John Russell was encouraged by Ohlendorf's outing, explaining that the right-hander was more aggressive than his previous three starts for the Pirates in September. "It felt like [my command] was a lot better than the last two games," Ohlendorf said. "It felt like I made some steps forward. I'm still not where I want to be. I feel it was an improvement."
