home_pitcher_note:
It was no slam dunk that Wainwright would get the call to start Opening Day for the Cardinals. Kyle Lohse had the most impact for the Cards in 2008, reaching 200 innings with a 3.78 ERA and challenging for an All-Star berth. And of course Chris Carpenter is the leader of the staff and has a Cy Young award on his mantel. But Wainwright has nonetheless earned the assignment with a pair of outstanding seasons.

Wainwright's 2008 was cut short by a finger injury that caused him to miss 2 1/2 months, so he made only 20 starts. Despite that, he was the clear front man on a surprising starting staff. He throws strikes, keeps the ball down, gets groundballs and can miss bats when he needs to.

Wainwright has a full four-pitch arsenal, with a quality fastball, a top-notch curveball, a changeup and a slider that he sometimes throws smaller, like a cutter.
away_pitcher_note:
Maholm begins the season as the Pirates' newfound ace, a label appropriately bestowed upon the left-hander after his breakout season in 2008. Maholm established career highs in starts (31), innings pitched (206 1/3) and strikeouts (139) last year on his way to a team-best nine win season. It was Maholm's efficiency and ability to avoid big innings last year that helped transform the lefty from a relatively unknown middle-of-the-rotation starter to a the Piratesmost dependable arm. At one point last year, Maholm pitched through the sixth inning in 20 consecutive starts.

In his first 19 2/3 innings in Grapefruit League play, Maholm allowed just one earned run and one walk. He had more strikeouts (11) than hits allowed (10).

Maholm made three starts against the Cardinals last season and went 2-1 with a 3.05 ERA. In two career starts at Busch Stadium, he is 1-1 with a 3.55 ERA. He also not alone in the fact that Albert Pujols has given him more fits at the plate than anyone else expected to be in St. Louis' Opening Day lineup. Pujols is 8-for-16 against Maholm with three doubles, one homer and three RBIs. Pujols has also drawn five walks.

home_pitcher_note:
Lohse was a revelation in 2008, signing in March then going on to anchor a Cardinals rotation that exceeded expectations. Before the year was out, he signed a new four-year deal, indicating his and the club's satisfaction with the match.

Lohse threw strikes, kept the ball in the park and totaled 200 innings for his new club. If he even approximates his 2008 performance, it will be a successful season.
away_pitcher_note:
Snell took a step back in 2008 after entering the year fresh off signing a five-year contract with the club. Though he did make 31 starts, he threw 43 2/3 fewer innings than he did in 2007 when he made 32 starts. Those numbers point to Snell biggest culprit last season, which was his inefficiency.

Snell has since admitted that he pressed early while trying to live up to his contract, and with Snell, channeling his mental side could be the biggest hurdle to overcome. With 25 wins combined in 2006 and 2007, Snell has shown he has the stuff. Now he just needs to reclaim it.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer was one of the biggest surprises in the National League in 2008, even if his breakout season was obscured by an even more noteworthy story on the other side of the ball, in Ryan Ludwick. At age 29, he thrived in his first full season as a Major League starter. Wellemeyer had a bit of a rough spring, never really getting going, but he'll have every opportunity to show that his 2008 season was reflective of the quality of pitcher he really is.
away_pitcher_note: Duke arguably has more to prove than any other Pirates starter this year. Memories of his sensational 2005 season seem long gone after the three subpar years that followed. But if anyone looks refreshed as Spring Training comes to a close, it's this left-hander. His results this spring were impressive, and Duke says that his arm strength is as good as it's ever been. If there was good news to come out of 2008, it was that Duke stayed healthy all season. Now, in a year in which his salary jumped to $2.2 million, he has to have the results to accompany that health.

home_pitcher_note: This will quite certainly be the biggest start made anywhere in baseball on the season's fourth day. Most clubs, after all, won't be trotting out a former Cy Young winner in the No. 4 spot in their rotations. But that's the case with the Cardinals and Carpenter, the '05 National League Cy Young and an exceptional pitcher as recently as 2006. He had an outstanding spring, allowing just four earned runs -- all of them in his final start. Assuming Carpenter stays healthy after missing nearly two full years due to elbow and shoulder problems, he's truly a top-flight starter.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf made just five appearances in Pittsburgh last season after coming over in a six-player trade in July. But by the time he pitched for the Pirates, it was obvious arm fatigue had set in. This spring, though, has provided a better glimpse of what the Pirates hope that Ohlendorf is capable of. He has shown no hesitancy to pitch inside, and an adjustment in his delivery has him more consistent. He has a power arm, and the Pirates love the fact that he has walked just two in 22 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto is back for his second season after going 9-14 with a 4.81 ERA in 31 starts during his promising but inconsistent 2008 rookie season. The 23-year-old righty showed signs he will improve in 2009 by posting a 1.57 ERA in five Cactus League games, with six walks and 13 strikeouts over 23 innings. In three starts against the Pirates last season, Cueto was 2-1 with a 4.50 ERA, giving up 18 hits in 16 innings. Pitch conservation will be a big goal for Cueto this season, who was often unable to go deep in games as a rookie.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens earned the rotation's final spot in the last week of Spring Training by beating out fellow right-hander Virgil Vasquez. It was a subpar spring for Karstens, who makes a living on being efficient and having stellar command. He's not going to overpower hitters, but he's on when the groundballs are coming easily. Karstens, who came to Pittsburgh in a July deadline deal with the Yankees, allowed 11 earned runs in his final 13 2/3 spring innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto is back for his second season after going 9-14 with a 4.81 ERA in 31 starts during his promising but inconsistent 2008 rookie season. The 23-year-old righty showed signs he will improve in 2009 by posting a 1.57 ERA in five Cactus League games, with six walks and 13 strikeouts over 23 innings. In three starts against the Pirates last season, Cueto was 2-1 with a 4.50 ERA, giving up 18 hits in 16 innings. Pitch conservation will be a big goal for Cueto this season, who was often unable to go deep in games as a rookie.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm's command wasn't pinpoint sharp as usual in his first start of the season, but he managed through it just fine. Maholm finished 6 2/3 efficient innings and allowed only one earned run, one intentional walk and seven hits. The cold weather affected Maholm's breaking ball early, and he had trouble relying on his breaking pitches until well into his start. If the lefty can find that pitch in his next outing and continues to work the inside part of the plate, he should be back to inducing ground balls with ease. Maholm is 3-3 with a 4.08 ERA in 13 career starts against Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Harang pitched well enough to keep his team in the game, but the Reds notched just three hits in a 2-1 loss to the Mets on Opening Day. The right-hander had a high pitch count of 114 through his five innings while giving up one earned run and seven hits with three walks and two strikeouts. Of those seven hits, two were infield singles, three were bloops and only two were solid hits. One of them was Daniel Murphy's solo home run to right field. Harang is 11-5 with a 4.29 ERA in his career vs. the Pirates. He was 0-2 with a 6.35 ERA against Pittsburgh in three starts last season.
away_pitcher_note: Snell's four-inning outing against the Cardinals on Tuesday was not the way Snell had planned to start the season by any means. He had little command of his pitches and had no success when trying to pitch inside. The start came after Snell missed his final Spring Training tuneup while dealing with a stomach flu, though Snell insisted that the lengthy layoff was not a contributing factor to the struggles. With an unstable bullpen, the Pirates are relying on Snell to be able to consistently pitch deeper into games moving forward. Snell has made 11 career starts against the Reds. He is 4-6 with a 5.21 ERA and has given up 10 homers in those 11 games.

home_pitcher_note: Duke gets the nod to pitch the home opener, and while it just so happened that way because of the rotation order, he certainly deserves the honor after his first start. Duke followed up a great Spring Training with a solid start to the regular season. He limited the Cardinals to one earned run in 6 1/3 innings, largely by establishing his fastball command early and working off of that. He's also showing more confidence in pitching inside and is doing so effectively. Despite having a 1-4 career record in nine career appearances (eight starts) against the Astros, Duke has a respectable 3.81 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler was the surprise of the rotation in '08, logging 11 wins after working himself into the rotation after the season started. Moehler originally was a fill-in for the injured Wandy Rodriguez, but he pitched so well that he maintained his starting job even after Rodriguez returned. Moehler ranked second in wins among Astros pitchers and third in games started. He recorded a five-game winning streak from July 9-Aug. 19, his longest since he won six straight in 2000. The Astros were 16-10 in his 26 starts last year, and he allowed four runs or fewer in 20 of them.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf came out on the wrong end of a pitcher's duel in his first start of the season, despite allowing just two runs in six innings. He kept the Cardinals scoreless through his first six frames. Ohlendorf continues to rely very heavily on his two-seam fastball, which has been a dominant pitch for him through Spring Training and into the season. He's also shown no apprehension in pitching inside. Ohlendorf has made four career appearances (two starts) against the Astros. He is 0-2 with a 9.00 ERA against Houston in those outings.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton will make his second start of the season when he faces the Bucs after the off-day. He yielded three runs on four hits over five innings in his first start against the Cardinals, taking the loss. The lefty did not face the Pirates last year. In his career, he is 10-3 with a 2.71 ERA over 22 games versus Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens' scheduled season debut was rained out Friday in Cincinnati. He was temporarily moved to the bullpen in preparation for his scheduled start. Karstens earned the rotation's final spot in the last week of Spring Training by beating out fellow right-hander Virgil Vasquez. It was a subpar spring for Karstens, who makes a living on being efficient and having stellar command. He's not going to overpower hitters, but he's on when the ground balls are coming easily. Karstens, who came to Pittsburgh in a July deadline deal with the Yankees, allowed 11 earned runs in his final 13 2/3 spring innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ortiz will make his first start of the season when he takes the hill against the Pirates in the series finale. The right-hander threw 73 pitches in a relief appearance on April 8 after Moehler was knocked from the game in the second inning. That outing, during which he allowed three runs on four hits over three innings, marked Ortiz's first in the big leagues since 2007. Ortiz has had success over the Bucs through his career, logging eight wins and one loss and a 3.20 ERA over 14 games (13 starts).

home_pitcher_note: Maholm delivered his second consecutive strong outing on Saturday afternoon, limiting the Reds to just one run on three hits in seven innings. He walked two and struck out three in a 101-pitch effort. Maholm retired the first 11 batters he faced and did not allow a hit until Brandon Phillips' single with two outs in the fourth. The Pirates left-hander was coming off his solid outing on Opening Day when he allowed just one earned run, one intentional walk and seven hits in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: While winning his first two starts, Jurrjens has successfully utilized a bend-but-don't-break approach. Despite issuing eight walks and allowing opponents to compile a .347 on-base percentage in his first 11 innings, the 23-year-old right-hander has allowed just three earned runs. During his five-walk outing against the Nationals on Sunday, he said his control problems were a result of attempting to be too fine with his pitches. He was 1-1 with a 4.35 ERA in two starts against the Pirates last year.

home_pitcher_note: Finally at full strength, Snell allowed just two runs on five hits in six innings in a 2-0 loss at Cincinnati on Sunday. However, he was outdueled by the Reds' Aaron Harang who fired a complete-game, three-hit shutout. Snell's four-inning outing against the Cardinals the previous Tuesday was not the way he had planned to start the season, by any means. That start came after Snell missed his final Spring Training tuneup while dealing with a stomach flu, though he insisted that the lengthy layoff was not a contributing factor to the struggles.
away_pitcher_note: With Tom Glavine's shoulder ailing, Jo-Jo Reyes will be promoted from Triple-A Gwinnett to make his season debut. After going 0-7 with a 7.81 ERA in his final 13 appearances (12 starts) for Atlanta last year, Reyes refined his mechanics during the offseason and proved to be more aggressive in the strike zone during Spring Training.  The 24-year-old southpaw allowed five runs -- four earned -- and seven hits in six innings against Charlotte on April 10.

home_pitcher_note: Duke has been stellar in his two starts this season, the latter of which was a complete-game shutout. In 15 1/3 total innings, he's allowed just one earned run. He's throwing to both sides of the plate with ease and using his sinker and two-seam fastball especially efficiently. There is also a confidence seen in the left-hander as he continues to be able to throw the ball where he wants to, when he wants to. Duke is 2-2 with a 2.76 ERA in five previous starts against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez has encountered his share of early-season misfortune. The Braves squandered a seven-run, seventh-inning lead in his first start and produced just one run while he notched 12 strikeouts during Tuesday night's loss to the Marlins. The 33-year-old right-hander enjoyed a strong March that included an impressive showing for Puerto Rico in the World Baseball Classic. He has allowed 10 earned runs and totaled 12 innings in his past two starts against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: An inability to establish his fastball command early was the ultimate downfall for Ohlendorf in his last start Wednesday, a five-inning outing in which he allowed eight hits and four runs. When Ohlendorf is sharp, he has his fastball sinking with ease and is able to then take advantage of his off-speed pitches to complement that fastball. He did that quite effectively in his first start of the season. Ohlendorf also fell behind too often in his most recent start, which forced him to endure some long counts early. This will be Ohlendorf's first career appearance against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old left-hander will make his first appearance against the Pirates. It comes after his first start, a no-decision against the Braves at Turner Field last Wednesday. Miller got off to a good start in Atlanta, allowing one run through four innings. But he got into trouble in the fifth inning, after being staked to a three-run lead. Miller gave up three runs in the inning, and was lifted before logging the third out. In 4 2/3 innings, he allowed four runs on four hits with two strikeouts. Considering he had been working out of the bullpen until then, pitch count is an issue for him. He threw 79 pitches at Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: If Karstens is going to keep his spot as the team's fifth starter, he's going to have to pitch deeper into games than he was able to in his first start of the season. A 17-day game layoff contributed to some rust in Karstens' first start of the year, but the biggest problem was Karstens' inability to throw strikes as his outing progressed. He walked five in four innings. Karstens isn't one to overpower hitters, making it even more crucial that he establish his fastball command early and stay efficient. Karstens has never faced the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Working into trouble and then getting out of it has pretty much marked Sanchez's first two starts. Still, he's been able to execute when he's had to. In his last outing, at Atlanta on April 16, repeatedly flirted with danger, he turned in a quality start -- two runs in six innings. Still, he gave up eight hits and walked three, while striking out two. The only inning the Venezuelan native retired the side in order was the sixth. In four of the first five innings, he allowed two runners to reach after logging two outs.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm is 3-for-3 in the quality starts category after tossing seven scoreless innings in a win against the Braves on Friday. The lefty did not have his sharpest command, but he battled admirably and used some good defensive work behind him to his benefit. Maholm has quietly put himself among the best left-handed starters in the game as he continues to show he can find a way to keep teams off balance and guessing regardless of whether he has his best stuff. And you know he's on when the ground balls are coming with ease. Maholm is 2-3 with a 4.40 ERA in five career starts against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Nolasco had a frustrating outing. The 26-year-old worked just four innings at Washington, giving up two runs on seven hits with a walk. He didn't have his best stuff, and he was lifted after 87 pitches. Physically, the right-hander is fine. He just was laboring and manager Fredi Gonzalez didn't want to put another stressful inning on him. Nolasco's lone win was on Opening Day against the Nationals. He is 1-2 with a 1.99 ERA in five games against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Correia was rained out of his start Monday, and with Jake Peavy and Chris Young remaining on track, he was moved to Friday and Shawn Hill given an extra day. Correia cut down on his walks in his second start of the season, allowing two runs on five hits and two walks in a start against the Mets last week. Correia left the game after 98 pitches, 65 for strikes. He benefited greatly from two double plays turned behind him and was mostly around the strike zone.
away_pitcher_note: Snell allowed four hits over seven-plus innings in his last start, lifting the Pirates to a 10-0 victory over the Braves. Snell walked three, struck out three and benefited from three double plays in that victory. The big key for the right-hander was getting ahead of hitters and working both sides of the plate. In his career against the Padres, Snell is 1-0  with a 1.69 ERA in four appearances.

home_pitcher_note: In his second start of the season, Hill, who joined the Padres late in Spring Training after being let go by the Washington Nationals, allowed two runs on three hits over five innings, walking one and striking out three. Hill increased his pitch count to 91 and was in line for his second victory of the season before the Phillies tied the game. Hill had good movement on his fastball and managed to thrive at Citizens Bank Park even when getting eight fly-ball outs compared to four ground-ball outs. There's no reason to think that Hill won't be able to exceed 100 pitches in his next start, as he appears fully stretched out.
away_pitcher_note: Duke was around the plate too much in his last start and the Braves made him pay by tagging the lefty for 12 hits and six runs in six innings. Duke isn't a strikeout pitcher and has always been one to give up hits, but the key for him is scattering those hits and keeping them in the ballpark. The more groundball outs he induces, the better his command is. Though the results weren't there in his last start, Duke has had more success using the inside part of the plate this year, and with his sinker. He's 1-2 with a 4.66 ERA in three career starts against San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Peavy allowed more earned runs on one pitch than he had in any one game this season. He served up Edgar Renteria's grand slam against the Giants on Tuesday after allowing three earned runs in each of his first three starts. It's way too early to be concerned about Peavy, who remains the Padres' best pitcher. The Pirates may be just the tonic he needs. He's 5-1 in seven starts against them with a 1.85 ERA, his best against any team outside of the one start (seven shutout innings) he made against the Tampa Bay Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf established his fastball command early in his last start and from there was able to use his offspeed pitches effectively. So far this season, it's been that fastball command that has dictated whether Ohlendorf can keep the opposing offense at bay. Ohlendorf continues to work on his delivery motion, and when he is able to keep his body straight toward the plate during his release, his slider and changeup become more effective. Ohlendorf has made one career start against the Padres. He didn't factor in the decision in that start, allowing one run on five hits and four walks in 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Looper has emerged as an early-season stopper for the Brewers. They had lost three of four games before he took the mound Wednesday in Philadelphia and delivered six shutout innings for his second Brewers win. They key, especially considering Looper did not strike out a single batter, was that he issued only two walks, and both were partly by design. They both went to Phillies slugger Ryan Howard, who grounded into a double play in his first at-bat but entered the night 4-for-5 against looper with four home runs. Looper has walked only three batters in his last two starts, both wins. He has a 3.02 ERA in 29 career appearances against the Pirates, five of them starts.
away_pitcher_note: After a shaky first outing, Karstens rebounded to allow just one run in six innings on Tuesday against the Marlins. He was much more efficient with his pitch count, needing only 87 pitches to go that deep. Karstens isn't going to overpower anyone, which makes it that much more critical that he gets first-pitch strikes and is efficient. It should benefit Karstens, too, that he is now pitching on a normal four-to-five days of rest after having a 17-day layoff prior to his first outing.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start at Philadelphia, Bush was five outs shy of the first Brewers no-hitter in 22 years when Matt Stairs clanked a solo home run off the right-field foul pole. It marked the second time in 10 months and the third time in Bush's career that he took a no-hitter into the eighth inning of a game, and he's not an altogether surprising candidate to end Milwaukee's no-hitter drought, even if he's not exactly a household name outside of Milwaukee. Bush has ranked among the National League's five best pitchers in terms of limiting baserunners (as measured by WHIP; walks plus hits per inning pitched) in two of the last three seasons, including 2008, during which he worked seven no-hit innings against the Blue Jays in June. He's had mixed results in 11 career matchups against the Pirates (10 were starts), going 3-4 with a 4.67 ERA. Two of those wins came last season, when Bush posted a 3.98 ERA against Pittsburgh in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm stumbled a bit in his last outing, allowing four runs on eight hits in six innings. He still managed to get the win and has now pitched at least six innings in 24 of his last 25 starts, dating back to 2008. He continues to be the Pirates' most reliable arm, and when he's sharp, his efficiency is remarkable. He's a groundball pitcher and will mix all of his pitches to both sides of the plate. The fact that he is consistently around the strike zone also keeps him from going into deep counts too frequently.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo gave up a two-run homer to Houston's Carlos Lee and not much else in his last start Friday night in Houston. Gallardo pitched the first complete game of his career, surrendering five hits, four of them singles. He had not pitched more than 6 2/3 innings in any of his three previous starts this season. He struck out four, walked none and threw 106 pitches. After shutting out the Mets for six innings April 18, the game against the Astros represented Gallardo's second strong start in a row.
away_pitcher_note: Snell snapped a streak of 13 scoreless innings in his last outing, one in which he labored through five innings. Reminiscent of a number of 2008 starts in which he fought with his command, Snell walked five and gave up six hits (five for extra bases) in five innings. Snell's pitch count in the first few innings is usually a telling sign of how the rest of the outing is going to go for him. If it gets high early, Snell has a tough time rebounding. He is 4-1 with a 3.60 ERA in six career appearances (five starts) against the Brewers. He is 109 at Miller Park, but has allowed six earned runs in eight innings there.

home_pitcher_note: Duke nearly had his second complete game of the season in his last start, but had to be pulled with one out in the ninth after throwing 114 pitches. Still, it was another gem for the lefty, who has been dominant in three of his four outings this year. Take away one shaky start and Duke has limited opponents to just two earned runs in 23 2/3 innings. He threw first-pitch strikes to 22 of 32 hitters he faced in his last outing, a sure sign of his sharp fastball command. Duke is 2-2 with a 4.05 ERA in five career starts against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo struggled Saturday afternoon while earning his first loss of the season. He allowed nine runs on nine hits, including two home runs, walked three and struck out five in 5 2/3 innings in a loss to Atlanta. He also hit a batter. Arroyo threw 102 pitches, 60 for strikes. The nine hits tied a season-high. Arroyo allowed six of the nine runs in the first two innings before settling down. He pitched three consecutive hitless innings until Yunel Escobar's two-run home run brought an abrupt end to his day.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf has pitched seven innings in each of his last two starts, both wins, and has continued a trend of dominant starting pitching from the Pirates. Ohlendorf can sometimes have the tendency to take too much time and overthink on the mound, which has gotten him into trouble at times. But if he can maintain a quickened tempo, his fastball command and slider are usually quite sharp. In his last outing, Ohlendorf recorded only three outs outside the infield. He has allowed three earned runs in 6 2/3 career innings against Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: Owings earned his first victory as a Red by allowing just one earned run on six hits in seven strong innings Sunday against Atlanta. He walked three and struck out six in a 102-pitch effort. Owings' only run allowed was a solo home run by David Ross. He allowed just three hits and six baserunners through six innings before running out of gas in the seventh. Owings, who was leading Reds pinch-hitters in RBI and pinch-hits, also went 2-for-3 with a double. The outing might've cooled the debate over the Reds' fifth-starter spot for now.

home_pitcher_note: As a pitcher that relies heavily on location, Karstens struggled in his last start against the Brewers on Monday. The right-hander took the mound with a 2-0 lead and served up home runs in each of the first three innings before leaving the game trailing 5-2 in the fifth inning. Karstens worked in the 89-91 mph range with his fastball, but left far too many pitches over the plate and finished with a no-decision. This will be the first time Karstens faces the Reds this season.
away_pitcher_note: A great effort by Johnny Cueto was for naught as the Reds had their hands full with nemesis Roy Oswalt during a 4-1 loss to the Astros on Monday where he got a no-decision. On the heels of his seven scoreless at Chicago on April 22, Cueto allowed one run and seven hits over seven innings vs. Houston. Showing more aggressiveness in the strike zone lately, Cueto allowed no walks in the April 16 game and just one against Houston. He used only 98 pitches in his most recent start. On April 11 vs. the Pirates, Cueto wasn't as effective during a 10-2 loss. He gave up four earned runs and eight hits over six innings with one walk and nine strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm will have another shot at the Brewers after suffering his shortest outing of the season in a no-decision in Milwaukee on Tuesday. The left-hander lasted just 5 1/3 innings and worked in and out of jams the entire night. Maholm gave up seven hits and allowed five earned runs while stranding the bases loaded on two occasions. The Bucs ace benefited from his defense, which turned two double plays in each of the first two innings. Maholm struggled with his location and rarely topped 90 mph with his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo is on a roll. He pitched seven brilliant innings against the Pirates on Wednesday and hit a solo home run for a 1-0 win, and has allowed only two runs in 22 innings over his last three starts. Wednesday's win was filled with hitting milestones: Gallardo became the first pitcher to win a 1-0 game on his own home run since the Dodgers' Odalis Perez in 2002, and with his fourth career home run he set a Brewers record for a pitcher. Both of his home runs this season have won games, including a three-run shot off Randy Johnson on April 8 for a 4-2 Brewers win. But he did throw 116 pitches against the Pirates after working a complete-game in Houston in his previous start, which caused at least mild concern for manager Ken Macha. Since Gallardo missed most of last season with a serious knee injury, the Brewers are worried about wearing him out early this year.

home_pitcher_note: Snell was the tough-luck loser in his last start, allowing just five hits and one run in seven strong innings in a 1-0 setback at Milwaukee on Wednesday. The right-hander appeared to get stronger as the game went on and tallied a Major League season-high 131 pitches. Snell gave up a solo home run to Brewers starter Yovani Gallardo for the game's only run. Working with a fastball in the 87-93 mph range in the early innings, Snell dialed it up to 95 mph late in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan says the only thing that's changed since his ugly outing against the Cubs on April 12 is the result. But those results speak for themselves; in his last three starts he's limited opponents to six runs in 18 1/3 innings for a 2.95 ERA, much better than the 11 runs he allowed in his first 7 2/3 innings and two starts. The Brewers gave Suppan an extra day of rest between those segments, allowing him to throw one extra side session that seems to have made a difference. He didn't face the Pirates when they visited Milwaukee last week but he's 12-3 against them in his career with a 4.20 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Just two starts into his 2009 Cardinals campaign, the rookie right-hander is already making a mighty big impression. After coming up from Triple-A Memphis on April 15 after former Cy Young Award winner Chris Carpenter went on the DL, Boggs made his first start against the Cubs April 26, allowing one unearned run in 5 2/3 innings and getting the nod from manager Tony La Russa to make at least one more start. He closed out the team's 16-7 April by striking out a career-high nine batters over six innings in an April 30 no-decision against Washington in an outing La Russa termed "outstanding."
away_pitcher_note: Duke has now made five starts in 2009 and four of them have been absolutely outstanding. Throw out the six-run outing against Atlanta on April 19 and the left-hander has given up just three earned runs over 30 2/3 innings in those four starts. That's an ERA of 0.88. Duke made three starts against the Brewers in 2008, losing one and finishing with a 5.87 ERA as he allowed 20 hits over 15 1/3 innings. This will be his 13th career start against Milwaukee and he'll look to improve on his 4.70 ERA against the NL Central rivals.

home_pitcher_note: No one is happier to celebrate the merry month of May than Wellemeyer, who rebounded from a 6.14 ERA in six April starts to get the win on May 1 with seven strong innings of work against Washington. Last year, Wellemeyer was the National League's Pitcher of the Month for May with a 4-0 record and 2.19 ERA. The Cards would be happy to see him replicate that stint, but are happy enough to have gotten the quality start and seen his consistency improve in this last outing.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf has four quality starts in five outings this season, a clear sign of how consistent he's been so far. He continues to focus on his early game tempo and rhythm, making sure not to start too slow, which he had been doing early in the season. A poor early tempo often leads to a lack of aggressiveness for Ohlendorf as the outing progresses. Still, he continues to show good control of his sinker and is working his off-speed pitches off of it. Ohlendorf lost in a pitchers' duel to the Cardinals earlier this year when he allowed two earned runs on seven hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Niese, 22, is taking the spot of left-hander Oliver Perez, who was placed on the 15-day disabled list with tendinitis in his right knee. In his first four Triple-A starts for Buffalo this year, Niese produced an 8.44 ERA and an 0-2 record. He allowed three hits, a walk and a run and struck out eight in a six-inning no-decision against Louisville on Friday. He had a 1-1 record and a 7.07 ERA in three starts and 14 innings with the Mets last season, pitching eight scoreless innings against the Braves on Sept. 13. The Mets won that game, 5-0, the only shutout in the team's last six such games not started by Johan Santana. The Pirates have opposed left-handed starters in merely three games this season.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens is a command pitcher, and that command has been shaky at best for him so far this season. His second start of the season was stellar, but his other three have been subpar, with high pitch counts and walks getting him into trouble early. Karstens has only pitched past the fourth inning in one of his four starts this season. The righty has also already given up five homers this season. Karstens took the loss in his only career start against the Mets. He allowed four earned runs on nine hits in six innings in that game.

home_pitcher_note: Maine has won his past two starts after losing his previous two. He walked a career-high six in sixth innings against Atlanta on Monday, but struck out seven and allowed just three hits. On April 27 against Florida, Maine allowed one hit and an unearned run over six innings, striking out four and walking three. He has gone at least five innings in each of his five starts and given up only 20 hits in 27 2/3 innings. Maine is 2-2 with a 2.93 ERA in five career starts against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm got right back on track his last time out and showcased the pitch efficiency that his teammates in Pittsburgh have become so accustomed to. The lefty needed only 98 pitches to finish 7 1/3 innings. He also recorded a season-high seven strikeouts. When he's on, Maholm is around the strike zone and getting groundball outs with ease. And he continues to be the Pirates' most consistent pitcher in being able to finish six innings. Maholm is 3-1 with a 2.25 ERA in five career starts against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez needed just 75 pitches to go 6 1/3 innings in his last start, winning in Atlanta on Tuesday. It was his first victory over the Braves since 2005. He had been 3-15 against them in the regular season and 1-7 at Turner Field. Using his changeup effectively, Hernandez coaxed three double plays. He hadn't got past the fifth inning in his previous three starts after going 6 2/3 innings at Florida in his first outing. Hernandez is 3-4 in his career against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Snell admitted to having nothing in the tank essentially from the get-go in his last start, which lasted only five innings on Tuesday. His 131-pitch outing in his previous appearance could be one explanation for that. Regardless of the reason, Snell has a walk total that is escalating rapidly this season. He has walked at least three in each of his six starts and has 23 in 34 innings. In contrast, the right-hander has only 22 strikeouts. Snell is 0-1 with a 6.55 ERA in five career appearances (four starts) against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Duke wasn't at his sharpest his last time out, but with the way the left-hander has started the season, there's no reason to believe that he won't be just fine when he takes the mound on Tuesday. As has been noted since the start of Spring Training, Duke is very much a different pitcher this season, both mentally and with his command, and he's done a superb job at avoiding the big inning, which constantly plagued him last year. When he's getting groundballs with ease, that's when you know Duke is on.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer's ERA is headed in the right direction. He allowed just two earned runs on four hits in seven innings in a 5-2 victory Thursday afternoon over Pittsburgh, dropping his ERA to 4.75 from a season high of 6.14 just two starts prior. Wellemeyer was the National League's Pitcher of the Month for May in 2008 with a 4-0 record and 2.19 ERA. The Cards would be happy to see him replicate that stint, but are happy enough to have gotten the quality start and seen his consistency improve in his past two outings.

home_pitcher_note: One bad inning did Ohlendorf in his last time out, and again, it has to do with his tempo. The Pirates have been trying to emphasize to Ohlendorf the need to take less time in between pitches and when he does, he seems to be sharp. However, Ohlendorf often falls into a trap, usually early in the game, where his tempo slows. His control suffers as a result. Still, he's been fairly consistent all season and has rebounded from hiccups like he had his last time out pretty well.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro, who entered Friday's game 3-0 with a 2.22 ERA in four career starts vs. Cincinnati, allowed five runs, four earned, on eight hits in six innings. All of the runs and seven of the hits came in the first two innings. Pineiro recovered to retire 11 of the last 12 batters he faced. He struck out three and did not walk a batter in a 96-pitch outing.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens matched his season high with a six-inning outing his last time out. The right-hander's efficiency was much better than it had been in his previous two starts and he was able to not fall behind so often, which had been an issue in April. Karstens also kept the ball in the park, an achievement considering that he had given up five home runs in his first four starts. The right-hander hasn't been dominant at all this season, but he has shown flashes of being a capable fifth starter in the rotation when he establishes his command early. Karstens has never faced the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Boggs will be making his fifth start this season. He allowed two runs  on five hits in 4 1/3 innings Wednesday in a 5-2 win over the Pirates. The rookie right-hander has made a mighty big impression. After coming up from Triple-A Memphis on April 15 after former Cy Young Award winner Chris Carpenter went on the disabled list, Boggs made his first start against the Cubs April 26, allowing one unearned run in 5 2/3 innings. He closed out the team's 16-7 April by striking out a career-high nine batters over six innings in an April 30 no-decision against Washington in an outing La Russa termed "outstanding."

home_pitcher_note: Maholm has not had great results in two out of his last three starts, which is a concern for Pittsburgh considering how consistent the left-hander has been over the past year. However, it was bloop hits on decent pitches that did him in his last time out, on Saturday at Citi Field. Usually depended on to finish at least six innings per start, a 42-pitch fourth inning in his last start did him in and forced him out after five. He allowed seven runs to the Mets, the most Maholm has given up since May 3, 2008. Maholm is 1-2 with a 5.00 ERA in three career starts against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling throughout his career against the Marlins, De La Rosa shined Saturday, when he went eight innings, recorded a career-high 12 strikeouts and allowed two runs on four hits. The left-hander commanded his fastball, a sharp slider and a solid changeup for his best outing of the season. But De La Rosa took the loss as he was outdueled by the Marlins' Josh Johnson. De La Rosa is 2-1 with a 4.97 ERA in six appearances against the Pirates, and 0-1 with a 10.80 ERA in three appearances at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Snell had an encouraging start his last time out, as his fastball velocity returned to the 94-96 mph range after lagging in his previous start. The right-hander seems to be over the effects of his 131-pitch start on April 29, and now all he needs is some run support. Snell has struggled with his walk total all season, but he issued just one across six innings in his last start. Snell is 2-2 with a 4.78 ERA in four appearances (five starts) against the Rockies in his career.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday, Cook posted his fourth consecutive quality start -- defined as six or more innings and three or fewer runs -- by pitching six innings and giving up two runs (one earned) on four hits against the Marlins. The sinkerballer kept the ball down and forced 10 groundouts. In two career appearances -- one start -- at PNC Park, Cook is 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA. Last July 30, Cook gave up four runs in seven innings, inducing 16 ground-ball outs in a 7-4 victory over the Pirates at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Duke pitched a gem in his last start, a 7-1 win over St. Louis on Tuesday. The lefty hurled eight innings, allowing one run on four hits, and notched five strikeouts. Duke was very efficient in tossing 104 pitches -- 67 were strikes. Duke has allowed more than one earned run in a game just twice in his first seven starts and is 2-2 lifetime against the Rockies, with 7.43 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Jimenez spooked the Astros by spending the early innings chucking fastballs, some of which were clocked as high as 99 mph. At times this pitch would buzz by a hitter's chin. More often than not, though, he threw strikes, and that's why he gave up one run on seven hits in seven innings, struck out four and forced 11 groundball outs. It's a minor roll for Jimenez, who has pitched seven innings in each of his last three starts and has held opponents to five runs. Jimenez has never pitched at PNC Park, but is 1-0 with a 2.57 ERA, eight strikeouts and two walks against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Because of the off-day this past Thursday and Saturday's doubleheader against the Phillies, the Nationals need an extra pitcher to start on Monday against the Pirates. MLB.com has learned that left-hander Ross Detwiler will likely make the start for Washington. He is currently with Double-A Harrisburg and was scheduled to start against Reading on Saturday, but he was scratched from that outing. Detwiler, the Nationals' No. 1 pick in the 2007 First-Year Player Draft, is having the best season of his professional career. He is 0-3 with a 2.96 ERA. Even more impressive is that Detwiler has 28 strikeouts over 27 1/3 innings and opponents are hitting .257 against him.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against St. Louis on May 13, Ohlendorf surrendered two hits and one run in six innings as the Bucs won 5-2. Ohlendorf mostly cruised against a Cardinals lineup, the Cards only run off Ohlendorf came on a Skip Schumaker home run. Ohlendorf who has relied on his sinker -- mixed things up with a four seam fastball, slider and a very effective changeup. This will be Ohlendorf's first appearance against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Last Wednesday, Martis improved his record to 5-0 against the Giants, the team that signed him as a Minor League free agent in 2004 then traded him to Washington two years later. Martis pitched seven innings, allowing one run on just two hits. He walked four and struck out two.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' No. 5 starter is coming off of his most encouraging two-start stretch of the year. He didn't get a win in either case, but the right-hander went six innings each against the Mets and Cardinals, allowing five runs over the 12 innings (3.75 ERA). Perhaps more importantly, he didn't walk a batter in either outing. He has never faced Washington in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Manny Acta has a policy of having his young starters leave games on a positive note. In this case, on Friday against the Phillies, left-hander John Lannan left the game with a 4-2 lead after 5 2/3 innings. Right-hander Garrett Mock entered the game and gave up an RBI single to Carlos Ruiz, but Ron Villone was able to end the frame by getting Eric Bruntlett to fly out to center fielder Elijah Dukes. Nationals fans were hoping the bullpen could hold the Phillies in the seventh inning, but it didn't happen.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm didn't get the win in his last start, but it was still very encouraging. The lefty tossed seven shutout innings against the Rockies on Friday night, giving up just five hits and a walk while striking out four. It was a nice bounce-back from his previous outing when he got hit hard for seven earned runs in 5 1/3 IP against the Mets, the third time in four starts he'd given up at least four earned runs. He has not fared well against the Nationals in the past, going 0-2 with a 6.12 ERA over four starts. The Nats have hit .343 off of him in those outings.

home_pitcher_note: With Daniel Cabrera out of the rotation, right-hander Craig Stammen will get the start against the Pirates on Thursday. It will be his Major League debut. Stammen, one of the team's top pitching prospects, was 4-2 with a 1.80 ERA with Triple-A Syracuse. Stammen, 25, has been impressive because he developed a two-seam fastball during Spring Training.
away_pitcher_note: An hour and 37 minute rain delay put an early end to Snell's last start against Colorado on May 16. Snell received a no-decision after two rather ineffective innings -- he gave up two runs in the first on Ryan Spilborghs' double and one more in the second on Clint Barmes' solo homer. Snell is 1-1 in his career against the Nationals with a 3.86 ERA in seven appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Against the Blue Jays in his last outing, Floyd endured yet another rocky start, surrendering six runs in just five innings. The right-hander has not won a game since April 19 -- a span of five starts. During that time, he has posted a 9.95 ERA, while allowing 43 hits in just 25 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Duke had been charged with no more than one run in five of his previous seven starts entering his last outing against Colorado on May 17. He tossed seven innings and allowed four runs on six hits. Duke, who left the game trailing 4-1, got the win, as Pittsburgh rallied for an 11-4 victory, upping his record to 5-3. To his credit, Duke didn't let the one bad inning shake him, and he kept his team in the game. Duke has no record in his career against the White Sox, with a 6.75 ERA in two appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Richard tossed his best outing of the year against the Blue Jays in his last start -- no small feat given that the Jays are one of the top offensive teams in baseball. The southpaw reeled off seven strong innings, allowing two runs (one earned) on three hits. He walked three, struck out three and exhausted 94 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Manager John Russell may have described it best when he characterized Ohlendorf's last start as uneven. It featured three straight innings in which he faced the minimum, but it also included a five-run inning by Washington's offense. Ohlendorf never got his off-speed pitches in sync and left too many balls out over the plate. While he has been fairly consistent all season, he still needs to improve his efforts in getting ahead of hitters and in quickening his pace early in the start. Ohlendorf has made one career appearance against the White Sox and it wasn't pretty. The righty allowed five earned runs on five hits in two innings of relief.

home_pitcher_note: After watching his personal-best five-game winning streak come to an end last Wednesday in Cleveland, Buehrle returned to his winning ways with a stellar effort on five days rest against the Twins at home on Tuesday. The left-hander allowed one earned run on eight hits over seven innings, striking out three and not issuing a walk. He threw 62 of his 101 pitches for strikes and pitched out of two scoring threats posed by the Twins, limiting Minnesota to just one unearned run. Buehrle has a 3-0 career record against the Pirates with a 1.96 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Karsten's last start featured five solid innings and one forgettable sixth inning, in which Karstens allowed three runs on four hits. He continues to work through some mechanical adjustments and is throwing three bullpen sessions in between starts (as opposed to the normal one) to help him expedite the process. Still, it seems that he can't stay away from having one bad inning in which his pitches are consistently up in the zone. Karstens' only career appearance against the White Sox resulted in a loss after the righty allowed three runs on five hits in 3 1/3 innings of relief.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster ran into a hot pitcher in his last outing, having to face St. Louis' Chris Carpenter. Dempster notched another quality start, his fifth, but came up short. He gave up two runs on six hits over seven innings. He walked two, but both were intentional. He'll be happy to face someone other than St. Louis. Dempster has been unable to beat the Cardinals in three starts this year. He's 2-0 at home so far. Against the Pirates, he's 4-7 in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Usually a model of efficiency, Maholm faced a patient Nationals lineup his last time out, and the left-hander had to throw a lot more early pitches than he is used to. As a result, Maholm had to come out after throwing 114 pitches in only six innings. Still, the outing was the third quality start for the left-hander in his last four outings, even though he is just 0-1 in those starts. Maholm is certainly familiar with the Cubs, having made eight starts against them in his career. In those eight games, he is 4-1 but with a 6.32 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: With Rich Harden going on the DL, Marshall stayed in the rotation. In his last start Thursday against the Cardinals, Marshall gave up three runs, two earned, on four hits over five innings. Marshall is 2-0 with one save and a 4.71 ERA in eight games against the Pirates. Last season, he was 1-0 with a 2.70 ERA in four appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Snell was in line to earn his first victory since April 18 in his last start until the bullpen squandered away the lead in the eighth. Though he struggled with his efficiency early -- something that still happens to the right-hander more often than the Pirates would like -- Snell settled in and looked stronger as the game progressed. He retired eight of the last nine hitters he faced and came out after having struck out six in six innings. He gave up three runs on four hits and a walk. Snell is 1-5 with a 5.93 ERA in 11 appearances (nine starts) against the Cubs.
summary: 2009-05-26 - Pittsburgh Pirates @ Chicago Cubs (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano returned from the disabled list on Friday after straining his left hamstring and pitched into the fifth inning before taking the loss in a 4-0 defeat to the Padres. Zambrano was wild in the first inning, when he walked two, hit a batter and threw 31 pitches. He wound up throwing 4 2/3 innings, though, and allowed three runs on three hits and four walks, striking out seven. Zambrano said he was rushing in that first inning and had trouble with his arm slot. Cubs manager Lou Piniella said, "He'll be much sharper next time out."
away_pitcher_note: Duke deserved much better than a loss in his last start, one in which he was masterfully efficient in an eight-inning effort. Duke needed just 88 pitches, but the two runs he allowed on six hits were enough to do him in, with no offensive support to help him. The lefty has pitched at least seven innings in five of his past six starts and continues to be the Pirates' most consistent and dominant starter. He has also already matched his win total from last year. Duke is 4-5 with a 3.07 ERA in 13 career starts against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf had nothing to hang his head about after his last outing, a 7 2/3-inning start in which he allowed three earned runs on six hits. The start was the longest of Ohlendorf's career, and it was also the first start this season in which he had surpassed the 100-pitch plateau. The right-hander threw 114 pitches in all. The key for Ohlendorf, as always, was keeping his pitches down and maintaining a quicker tempo on the mound. Ohlendorf is still looking for his first career win against the Astros. He is 0-3 with an 8.44 ERA in five appearances (three starts) against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Moehler had his first shaky outing since returning from the disabled list, giving up six runs on nine hits over five innings against the Rangers in a losing effort. He had allowed five runs in three previous starts since recovering from a sprained right knee. Moehler has faced the Pirates once already this season, taking the loss after giving up five runs on seven hits in 2 1/3 innings. Last season, he was 2-1 with a 9.39 ERA in four starts against Pittsburgh. In his career against the Pirates, Moehler is 5-6 with a 6.37 ERA in 15 appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens allowed three two-out runs in his last start, which lasted 5 1/3 innings. He hasn't won since his second start of the season and has yet to pitch past the sixth in any of his eight outings this year. His starts haven't been bad, per se, but they've all pretty much been mediocre, leaving the Pirates still looking for more out of their fifth starter. On a positive note, after walking 13 in his first four starts, Karstens has issued only three free passes in his four starts since. He allowed three runs on four hits and five walks in his start against the Astros earlier this year.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez threw only 78 pitches in a rain-shortened outing in Cincinnati in his last start, so it's safe to say he'll be well-rested for the finale in Pittsburgh. Rodriguez allowed six runs -- all unearned -- in a defensively sloppy loss to the Reds. He last faced the Pirates in 2008, logging one win after holding the Pirates scoreless over six frames. In his career, Rodriguez is 3-3 with a 4.96 ERA over nine game.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm was nowhere near his usually efficient form, needing 93 pitches to finish only four innings. His night would end there, too, as he allowed seven runs for the second time this season. He is now winless in his last six starts and has seen his ERA swell from 2.03 to 4.41 in that span. He struggled to throw his breaking ball for strikes last time out and left too many pitches up, rarely something he struggles with. Maholm is 5-3 with a 4.91 in nine career starts against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton is still winless at home after giving up five runs on eight hits and walking one in five innings pitched against the Rangers on Sunday. Hampton won his only start against the Pirates this year, throwing six innings of shutout ball and striking out eight in the Astros 4-1 win on April 15. He is 11-3 with a 2.57 ERA versus Pittsburgh in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Snell has to be glad to see the calendar page turn to June after he finished May with an 0-3 record and a 7.50 ERA. He gave up at least three runs in each of his six starts during the month. Snell has been especially hurt by two-out hits all season. Of the 32 runs he's allowed this year, 18 have come with two outs. Snell lost his May 10 start to the Mets -- six innings, three earned runs, six hits and five strikeouts -- in a game where Snell claimed New York was stealing the catcher's signs.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez threw his first nine-inning complete game since May 7 of last year, holding the Nationals to a lone run on nine hits in a 6-1 win. Hernandez is scheduled to make his next start June 1 in Pittsburgh. Hernandez has started against the Pirates just twice in the last three seasons, with little success. He is 0-1 with a 6.30 ERA, allowing seven runs on 17 hits in 10 innings. Hernandez has also struggled mightily in June since 2006, compiling a 4-9 mark with a 6.73 ERA in 17 starts during the month -- his highest ERA of any month during that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Duke deserved better than a no-decision in his last start, a seven-inning outing in which he allowed two runs. Duke's efficiency continues to be great, as has his ability to avoid the big inning. In his 10 starts this season, Duke has finished at least seven innings in seven of them. He's allowed two earned runs or fewer in seven starts as well. Duke is 2-1 with a 3.62 ERA in five career starts against New York.
away_pitcher_note: Santana struggled at times Wednesday against Washington, walking six batters and throwing 120 pitches in just six innings. That was still enough to pick up his seventh win of the season, though, as he limited the damage to three runs on three hits. Santana faces a Pirates' team he dominated in two starts last season, going 1-0 with a 1.23 ERA. He allowed just five hits and two runs while striking out 14 in 14 and 2/3 innings against Pittsburgh and tossed one of his three complete games of the season at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note:
Ohlendorf wasn't able to string together two straight solid starts, as he lasted just 5+ innings and gave up four runs in a loss to Houston.
Ohlendorf's 97 pitches were the second most of the season, and his three walks tied for a season high. Ohlendorf has two appearances against the Mets in his career, although neither have been starts. He has struggled in those two games, however, as he surrendered 10 runs in only 1 2/3 innings. The Mets are hitting .615 against Ohlendorf in his career, which is the highest batting average for any team against the right-hander.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey continued his run of excellent outings, overcoming some personal demons against the Marlins by allowing just one run on five hits in 7 2/3 innings on Friday. It was Pelfrey's longest start of the season, and the first in which he had given up fewer than two runs. Pelfrey faces a Pirates team against which he has never yielded an earned run. That comprises only one career start, however, when Pelfrey pitched seven shutout innings en route to a 2-1 victory last August.

He has struggled in those two games, however, as he surrendered 10 runs in only 1 2/3 innings. The Mets are hitting .615 against Ohlendorf in his career, which is the highest batting average for any team against the right-hander.

That comprises only one career start, however, when Pelfrey pitched seven shutout innings en route to a 2-1 victory last August.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton has to be pleased about making his second consecutive start against the Pirates. He has won his past eight decisions against them -- having not lost to the Bucs in more than nine years -- and is 2-0 with an 0.69 ERA against them this season. His most recent start was in Pittsburgh Sunday, when he allowed one run on three hits in seven innings. Hampton is 0-2 with a 5.74 ERA at Minute Maid Park this season.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens had one of his best starts of the season in his last game, when he went seven innings and gave up just two runs against Houston. The seven innings were the most he's pitched since a complete-game shutout against Arizona last August. After struggling with his command early in the season, Karstens has just four walks in his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Start No. 12 was a lucky one for Oswalt, who finally captured his second win of the season. Oswalt bounced back from his uncharacteristically wild outing against the Reds to hold Colorado to one run on six hits in his last start, striking out eight and walking two over seven innings. Oswalt was 2-1 with a 1.71 ERA in three starts against the Pirates last season. In his career, Oswalt is 13-6 with a 2.40 ERA over 24 starts against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: It will be back-to-back starts against the Astros for Maholm, who lost to Houston in his last start despite allowing only two runs -- one earned -- in seven innings. Though Maholm is now winless in his last seven starts, that outing last Sunday seemed to get Maholm back on track after his previous start, which lasted but four innings. There are still some consistency issues with Maholm's fastball, but nothing that he feels can't be fixed before his next start. He is now 5-4 with a 4.50 ERA in 10 career starts against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino justified his spot in the starting rotation, at least for the time being, by holding the Rockies to five hits and two runs and striking out a career-high seven batters in six innings in his previous start Tuesday. Despite giving the Astros their fourth quality start in five games, Paulino took a no-decision. The Astros have scored just 12 runs in his seven starts. Paulino's only career outing against the Pirates came in 2007 when he threw one inning in relief.
away_pitcher_note: Snell's struggles continued in his last start, when he gave up five runs in six innings while tying a season high with five walks. All of the runs came before the fourth inning, however, as he rebounded in the last three frames to take a no-decision. Despite the turnaround, Snell remained winless in his past eight outings. Since pitching seven shutout innings on April 18, Snell has given up 29 runs in 42 innings. He is 2-5 in 13 career appearances against the Astros, including 12 starts. He has yet to face Houston this season.

home_pitcher_note: Since tossing eight scoreless innings against the Blue Jays on May 22, Kawakami has once again proven to be mediocre.   After surrendering a leadoff homer to Alfonso Soriano on Tuesday night, he pitched effectively before allowing the Cubs to produce a two-run sixth inning. The 33-year-old right-hander hadn't allowed a homer in his previous six starts. The Braves will continue to monitor his shoulder which has fatigued while he's adapted to the schedule of a five-man rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Duke stretched his streak of pitching at least seven innings to five straight starts as he gave up just one run in seven innings in his last start on Tuesday. He threw only 90 pitches as he outdueled the Mets' Johan Santana. Duke has won three of his last four decisions, with the only loss coming when he pitched eight innings and surrendered only two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe earned a no-decision on Wednesday against the Cubs despite pitching at least seven innings for the fourth straight game. The big right-hander allowed two runs on five hits and retired 11 of the last 13 hitters he faced. Wednesday was the third time this season Lowe allowed three earned runs or fewer and failed to earn a victory. He has enjoyed much success against the Pirates in his career, winning all six games he has started against Pittsburgh and posting a 2.72 ERA.
away_pitcher_note:
Despite being handed four first-inning runs, Ohlendorf wasn't able to earn the win in his last start. He lasted only 4 1/3 innings as he gave up five earned runs on nine hits against the Mets. The no decision kept Ohlendorf winless in his last three starts. The right-hander is facing the Braves for the first time in his career.
He's 2-3 with a 5.12 ERA on the road this season, giving up 31 hits in 31 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: While allowing nine earned runs during his past two starts, Jurrjens has encountered the first rough stretch of the season. He had allowed three earned runs or less during his 10 starts preceding this mini-slump. The 23-year-old right-hander surrendered a season-high nine hits, but still worked seven innings against the Brewers on Friday night.  The outing resulted in his first loss since April 27. One of his tough-luck losses occurred on April 17, when he limited the Pirates to one run and four hits in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The recently acquired right-hander is making his 2009 Major League debut after going 7-2 with a 2.26 ERA (18 earned runs in 71 2/3 innings) in 11 starts for the Triple-A Gwinnett Braves. Morton was 4-8 with a 6.15 ERA in 16 appearances, 15 starts for Atlanta in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez encountered some bad luck on Saturday, when he limited the Brewers to two runs over six innings and found himself on the wrong end of a shutout. He is 1-3 with a 4.18 ERA in six home starts and 3-1 with a 2.87 ERA in six road starts. The 33-year-old right-hander, who ranks among the National League leaders in strikeouts, has won just once while allowing two earned runs or fewer during each of his past four starts at Turner Field. He notched his first win of the season on April 19, when he scattered five hits over six scoreless innings against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm, who lost to the Astros two starts ago despite allowing only two runs (one earned) in seven innings, was just little less impressive outing in his last start against Houston. The left-hander went seven innings again this time, giving up four runs and striking out four. The biggest difference, though, was that he earned the win, his first in his last eight starts. Maholm won his first outing against the Braves this season, throwing seven innings of shutout ball and giving up four hits. He is 1-1 in his career against Atlanta with a 1.80 ERA over three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Snell pitched well in six innings against the Astros in his last start, scattering eight hits and giving up three runs but receiving a no-decision. Snell is now winless in his past nine outings. He has faced the Tigers once in his career, giving up four runs on seven hits in a loss during the 2006 season.
away_pitcher_note: Most expect a 20-year-old breaking into a Major League rotation to have his ups and downs, and after being up for all of May -- when he went 5-0 with a 1.50 ERA -- Porcello has slowed down a bit, although not much. In his last two starts, Porcello is 0-1, having allowed seven earned runs in 9 1/3 innings. Tigers manager Jim Leyland cited some control problems in his most recent outing, but the rookie has still been impressive 11 starts into his career.

home_pitcher_note: After finishing at least seven innings in five consecutive starts, Duke lasted only six in most recent. The six runs allowed matched a season high for the lefty and his 11 hits allowed was just one shy of the most he's allowed this year. Duke also served up three homers in his last start after only giving up four in his previous 11 outings this year. Until Monday's outing, Duke had not given up multiple home runs in any game this season. This will mark Duke's first career appearance against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga might be more frustrated with his game right now than at any other point in this sophomore slump of his. He's seemingly turning a corner, as his three straight quality starts suggest, but his early-inning struggles and hit totals are baffling him -- including a bases-loaded escape with a run allowed in a 33-pitch opening inning Monday afternoon against the White Sox. If he can get command back on his sinker and avoid the untimely sliders that spin a lot and stay flat, it should make a difference in his mix of pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf is looking to break a four-start winless streak, including back-to-back no-decisions. In his last start, Tuesday night in Atlanta, he pitched six strong innings -- he said it was as well as he threw all year -- and left with the lead, but got a no-decision when the bullpen could not hold the lead in a 4-3 loss. He credited improved balance after having worked with pitching coach Joe Kerrigan. Ohlendorf has no record against Detroit and has only faced them once, last April 29, as a member of the Yankees. He threw 3 1/3 shutout innings, allowing one hit, walking one and striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: Willis hasn't won in four starts since his 6 1/3-scoreless-inning victory against the Rangers on May 19, but his ability to compete even in the toughest of situations has earned him a spot in Detroit's rotation over a struggling Jeremy Bonderman. He overcame five walks and five hits over five innings -- and a sore knee he injured trying to make a sliding tag at the plate -- to keep the Tigers in their game against the White Sox in his last start on Tuesday. By starting Sunday's series finale at Pittsburgh, Willis gets the upshot of helping his own cause by batting for the first time in his Tigers tenure.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins is scheduled to make his return from the disabled list and his return to the rotation in the series opener against the Pirates at the Metrodome. The left-hander, who went on the DL with an inflamed nerve in his left elbow, pitched seven scoreless innings in the second of two rehab starts for Class A Fort Myers. This will mark Perkins' first career start against Pittsburgh. The lefty is 2-0 with a 4.26 ERA in three career Interleague starts.
away_pitcher_note: After a stretch of up-and-down results, Maholm steadied himself in his most recent outing. He limited the Braves to one unearned run on four hits in seven innings on Thursday. Though he's not known for being an overpowering pitcher, Maholm also finished the game with eight strikeouts, a new season high. Efficiency and first-pitch strikes continue to be the key for Maholm, who has just one win in his last nine starts. This will be Maholm's second career start against Minnesota. He did not factor in the decision of his 2006 start against the Twins in which he allowed three runs on five hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano wasn't lights-out in his last start against the A's on Wednesday, but he was effective enough. He delivered his second straight quality start, giving up three runs on five hits over his six innings while striking out seven. It still wasn't enough to earn him a "W," but the Twins have been pleased by the fact that Liriano has limited the big inning in each of his last two starts after going just four innings in each of his previous three. The left-hander will try to continue the success in his next start against the Pirates. Liriano has faced Pittsburgh just once in his career, allowing two runs over seven innings while earning the win in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Though his record doesn't show it, Snell has actually pitched decently in his last two starts. After struggling with his efficiency through much of the first two months of the season, Snell has pitched at least six innings in each of his last three games. His last two outings have each been quality starts. Still, Snell hasn't picked up a win since April 18, which could be weighing on his psyche just a bit. Snell lost to the Twins back in 2006, allowing three earned runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The right-handed sinkerball pitcher has quietly become one of the most effective starters for the Twins this season. Blackburn was cruising through his last start against the A's, throwing seven scoreless innings while allowing just three hits, before finding trouble in the eighth. He gave up three runs in the inning and erased what had been a 3-0 Twins lead. He's still managed to deliver quality starts in nine of his 13 outings, five of which he's allowed one earned run or none. He'll next face the Pirates for the first time in his career. Blackburn is 2-0 with a 4.34 ERA in three career Interleague starts.
away_pitcher_note: For the fifth time this season, Duke finished eight innings his last time out. Only four of his 13 starts this year have lasted fewer than six innings. The only concern for Duke may be that he has given up five homers in his last two starts after allowing just four in his first 11 games of the season. This will be Duke's first career start against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis wasn't as dominant as he had shown all season against the Mariners in his last start, but he found a way. In seven innings, Marquis had only one 1-2-3 inning but through guts and guile, he found a way to escape unscathed in every inning but one. In all, Marquis surrendered just an earned run on seven hits but got the no-decision as the Rockies scored twice in the eighth for a 5-3 victory. Marquis' next start will be against the Pirates. He owns an 8-6 career record against the Bucs with a 3.83 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf earned his first win since May 18 in his last start. The right-hander threw six innings and gave up only one run on two hits against the Tigers. The last time Ohlendorf gave up just one run was May 13 against the Cardinals. Ohlendorf has yet to face the Rockies in his career. He is 2-3 with a 5.02 ERA in six road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel silenced all the naysayers with a win against the Mariners at Coors Field, a place he had yet to conquer. Hammel kept his fastball down in the zone in 5 1/3 innings, allowing just an earned run on five hits with no walks and a season-high six strikeouts. Four of the six strikeouts came on curveballs. Hammel's start was cut short because of a 55-minute rain delay in the sixth inning. In Hammel's only career appearance against the Pirates, he picked up the loss in relief by giving up a solo home run in 1 2/3 innings as a member of the Tampa Bay Rays in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Morton makes his first start since suffering from a strain in his left hamstring June 10 against the Braves. He lasted just one inning in that start, surrendering one hit and no runs on 13 pitches. It was his first start of the season. Morton has never pitched against Rockies, but he has been more impressive on the road than at home in his short career. Three of Morton's four career victories have come in opposing ballparks.

home_pitcher_note: After picking up his first wins of the season in consecutive stats to begin June, De La Rosa took a major step backward in his last outing. He gave up seven runs to the Rays in 2 1/3 innings, his shortest effort of 2009. De La Rosa had trouble with his command, leaving the ball up and over the middle of the plate, a dangerous way to pitch at Coors Field. The Rays pounced for five extra-base hits. De La Rosa pitched a gem at Pittsburgh on May 15, striking out 10 and walking none in seven innings of one-run ball. He owns a 3.66 ERA in seven career appearances (19 2/3 innings) against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm was rocked for eight runs on 14 hits in five innings in his most recent start. Despite getting ahead of each of the first nine hitters he faced, the lefty had problems getting the ball down consistently, which the Twins took advantage of. Maholm's results have been to both extremes this season. He's now allowed seven or more runs in three starts, but has allowed one or fewer six different times. Maholm pitched seven scoreless innings against the Rockies earlier this season. He is 1-2 with a 3.60 ERA in four career starts against Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Snell finally snapped a 10-game winless streak in his last start, which also marked his third straight quality outing. Snell was inefficient early, a trend that has plagued him for much of the season, but dominated in his last three innings of the six-inning outing. His challenge is to figure out a way to start out stronger, since he tends to get better as the game progresses. This will be Snell's second career appearance against the Indians. He picked up a win against them in 2006 when he allowed two earned runs on five walks and four hits.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Huff's first career appearance against the Pirates. After making four starts in the Majors before notching his first win, he won his next two starts in succession on June 7 against the White Sox and June 12 against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Duke took the loss in his last start despite allowing only three runs in six innings. He struggled to get ahead of hitters, though, and wasn't at his sharpest with his fastball command. On the positive side, he was able to get some big outs when he really needed them. Duke has allowed six homers in his last three starts after allowing just four through his first 11 outings. The lefty has made one career start against Cleveland, that coming in 2006. He allowed three runs on four hits and six walks in the seven-inning loss.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano was pushed back several days in the rotation because of soreness in his right shoulder, but the injury is not considered to be serious. Pavano wanted some time to get straightened out on the side after giving up 15 runs over 9 2/3 innings over his last two starts. He gave up nine runs on 11 hits in 4 2/3 innings in a loss to the Royals on June 10 and surrendered six runs on nine hits in five innings in a no-decision against the Brewers on June 15. Pavano is 3-4 with a 4.69 ERA in 10 career starts against the Pirates and 1-0 with a 1.98 ERA in two starts at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf had flat pitches and left the ball up in his last start. It cost him. Ohlendorf served up two home runs as part of a six-run, nine-hit, five-inning outing against the Rockies at Coors Field. Ohlendorf picked up his third loss in four decisions after winning five of six. Ohlendorf is 0-1 with a 3.86 ERA in two relief appearances against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Lee finally received the run support he has craved all season but still could not earn a victory, as the Indians collapsed down the stretch in an 8-7 defeat in 10 innings against the Cubs. Lee lasted seven innings, allowing three runs on six hits while striking out five and walking three. He left with nobody out and one man on in the eighth inning with a 7-2 lead that the bullpen was unable to hold. Lee, who entered Friday's game with the seventh-best ERA in the American League at 2.88, had been receiving some of the worst run support in the league. The 4.73 runs he received per start ranked second-worst out of 49 pitchers in the AL with at least 60 innings pitched this season. Lee has never faced the Pirates in his eight-year career.

home_pitcher_note: Vasquez has been recalled from Triple-A Indianapolis and will be making his debut for the Pirates on Friday. Officially, Vasquez takes the rotation spot left vacant when Ian Snell was optioned to the Minors. After losing out on the battle for the rotation's fifth spot in Spring Training, Vasquez went to Indianapolis, where he went 5-2 with a 4.18 ERA in 14 appearances.
