Vasquez hasn't pitched in the Majors since 2007, when he made five appearances (three starts) for the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Meche is coming off a drubbing from the Cardinals, who rang up nine earned runs against him in 3 1/3 innings. Of course five of those runs were knocked in by the destructive force known as Albert Pujols. This episode inflated Meche's ERA from 3.31 to 4.11. In his previous start, Meche gutted his way to 132 pitches to shut out the D-backs, but he insisted that any idea that it adversely affected him against the Cardinals was "stupid." He said he felt great. In his previous six starts, had given up just seven earned runs for an ERA of 1.69.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm still doesn't have the feel of his sinker and it might have cost him in his last start. He gave up five runs on eight hits with four walks and seven strikeouts in five innings. In his last two starts, he's given up 13 runs in 10 innings. Maholm hasn't been able to throw his sinker down-and-away to force right-handed hitters into ground-ball outs. Instead, it's been down-and-in. He's made one career start against the Indians and went 5 1/3 innings, allowing one run on four hits with seven strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Chen was called up from Triple-A Omaha to take the spot in the rotation vacated when Kyle Davies was sent to Omaha after his last start. Chen, a left-hander, was signed last spring after pitching for his native Panama in the World Baseball Classic. He missed the entire 2008 season after undergoing Tommy John elbow reconstruction surgery. But he has 10 years in the Majors, starting with the Braves in 1998, and the Royals will be his 10th club. He has a composite record of 35-37 with a 4.63 ERA in 242 games (112 starts). For Omaha, he was 4-2 in 14 games with a 3.40 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Originally scheduled to pitch on Friday, Morton was pushed back to Sunday in order to give his nagging left hamstring a few extra days to recover. Morton has already missed a start due to the injury and was limited to just one inning in one of the two starts he has made since joining the Pirates. Morton threw 88 pitches in five innings his last time out, showing a nasty sinking fastball in the process. Morton has never faced the Royals, but he is 0-1 with a 4.91 ERA in two career Interleague starts.
away_pitcher_note: For the first time in five starts, Greinke notched a victory and it came as he went eight innings to beat the Astros, 2-1. Looking more like the pitcher who started out with an 8-1 record this season, Greinke allowed only a first-inning run, pitched out of a few jams, struck out five and walked none. One thing that seemed to help was resuming his inside attack; he said he worked inside to every batter and only two of those pitches resulted in base hits. Greinke was used as the No. 8 hitter at Houston (he went 0-for-3) and he gets another chance to swing at Pittsburgh. Now he's just 3-for-15 at bat in his career but loves to hit.

home_pitcher_note: Duke wasn't at his most efficient in his last start, but he sailed to his eighth season win nonetheless by allowing just one run on five hits in six innings. Duke has been the most consistent member of the rotation all season, pitching through the sixth in all but one of his 15 starts this season. He continues to have success pounding the inside of the plate and has been doing that to get ahead of hitters all year. Duke has made 14 career starts against the Cubs and is 4-5 with a 3.03 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Harden lost his third straight decision in his last start against the Tigers. He gave up four runs, two earned, on four hits and four walks over 5 1/3 innings. Harden hasn't looked sharp, although he says he's fine. He threw 109 pitches in the short outing. The right-hander has never faced the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf got a no-decision in his last start, when he pitched seven innings and surrendered two runs on five hits. It was his longest outing since he threw 7 2/3 innings on May 23. Ohlendorf has lost three of his past four decisions. Despite playing in the same division as the Cubs, the right-hander hasn't faced them in his career. Ohlendorf is 4-2 at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly gave up a season high in hits and runs in his last start, against the Tigers, serving up six runs on 10 hits over six innings. The 10 hits Lilly allowed matched his career high -- or low, depending on how you look at it. He was glad to see Interleague Play end. Lilly was 0-1 with two no-decisions against American League teams and has not faced the Pirates yet this season.

home_pitcher_note: Vasquez stepped into the rotation for recently demoted Ian Snell and performed admirably in his debut for the Pirates. After not pitching in the Majors since 2007, Vasquez allowed only two runs on four hits in six innings to earn his first big league win his last time out. Though he's not one to overpower hitters, Vasquez also finished the outing with seven strikeouts. He's a command pitcher with an above-average fastball and has improved the use of his off-speed pitches during his Minor League stint this season.
away_pitcher_note: After not getting a win in his first seven starts, Randy Wells now has two "W's" in back-to-back starts. He beat the White Sox in his last outing, striking out six over seven innings. He gave up five hits, including solo homers to Jermaine Dye and Jim Thome. It's the first time he's given up two home runs in a start. He's gone at least six innings in all of his starts except two and has kept the walks to a minimum.

home_pitcher_note: After laboring through much of June, Maholm closed it out with a bang in his final start of the month. Not only did Maholm snap a personal two-game losing streak, but he did it with the benefit of his sinker, a pitch that had eluded him at times this month. Maholm was also notably efficient, as he typically is when he's at his sharpest. Maholm is 3-2 with a 3.65 ERA in six career starts against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: It all fell apart for Redding in a hurry on Saturday against the Yankees. After giving up two hits in the first five innings, Redding allowed four runs on four hits on four consecutive pitches in the sixth, leading to a 5-0 Yankees' win. Redding is 2-2 with a 3.79 ERA in 11 career starts against the Pirates, including an 0-1 mark with a 6.38 ERA in five starts at PNC Park. Pirates shortstop Jack Wilson owns a .385 career average against Redding in 26 at-bats. Redding is glad to finish June -- historically his worst month -- and enter July, when he's 9-11 with a 4.91 ERA in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad pitched a workmanlike six innings while getting a no-decision against the Rays on Saturday. The 22-year-old right-hander gave up just two runs on five hits in six innings, walking three and striking out five, but he ran his pitch count up and finished throwing 116 (71 for strikes). Since going on a career-long four-game losing streak, Volstad has given up five runs in 12 innings. This will be the Palm Beach Gardens, Fla., native's first time facing the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Morton has been battling a nagging left hamstring strain that has kept him from making starts with any regularity. The hope now, though, is that the injury is behind him. Showcasing his nasty sinking fastball, Morton breezed through the first three innings of his last start, only to allow six hits and three runs in his final two innings. The Pirates continue to be cautious with pushing him too deep into games because of the hamstring injury. Morton made three starts against the Marlins last year, during which he allowed 10 earned runs in 15 innings, walking nine and striking out 10.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a start in which he yielded just one run on one hit in seven innings, Miller surrendered a season-high five runs in a loss to the Rays on Sunday. The 23-year-old needed only 12 pitches to get through the first inning but he struggled while giving up two runs in the second and then allowed a solo homer to B.J. Upton in the third. After settling down a bit, he left the game with two on and one out in the seventh, and the Rays tacked on two more with Tim Wood on the mound. Miller gave up eight hits while walking one, striking out four and throwing 101 pitches (59 for strikes). Since coming off the disabled list in mid-May, he's 2-3 with a 3.91 ERA. The only time Miller has ever faced the Pirates -- on April 20 -- he ended up being put on the shelf with a strained right oblique muscle.
away_pitcher_note: Duke essentially made two mistakes in his last start, but it was enough to send him to a sixth loss. Two two-strike curveballs that Duke wanted to bounce in the dirt were left high enough for contact, and both ended up being driven for RBI hits. With only one run of support from his offense, that made the difference. In fact, in Duke's six losses this season, the Pirates have scored just five runs for him. They've averaged eight runs a game when he's won. Duke is winless in four career starts against the Marlins. In a combined 19 innings, the left-hander has allowed 12 earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco picked up his fifth win of the season after throwing eight innings in which he held Washington to two runs on four hits while striking out eight and walking none. The Nationals hit several balls hard off Nolasco early, including a Ryan Zimmerman solo homer in the second, but the right-hander settled into a groove shortly after. After a rocky second inning, Nolasco got stronger as the game went on, allowing just one runner to reach base and retiring 10 in a row between the fourth and seventh innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf had what he described as his most complete performance of the season his last time out on Tuesday, when he tossed seven scoreless innings against the Cubs and struck out a career-best eight. He was able to rely heavily on his slider, a pitch that Ohlendorf has tended to overthrow at times this season. That slider helped the effectiveness of his fastball, which in turn kept Ohlendorf more efficient than he has been most of the year. One of Ohlendorf's best starts this season came against the Marlins back on April 20 when he pitched seven shutout innings and allowed two hits.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton returned from the disabled list in his previous start Tuesday at San Diego and pitched well, holding the Padres to four hits and one run in six innings. This will be his fourth start this year against Pittsburgh, a team he has dominated in 2009 and in his career. He's 3-0 with a 0.90 ERA in three starts against the Pirates this year and 13-3 with a 2.44 ERA in his career. His .813 winning percentage against the Pirates his best against any team with more than one decision.
away_pitcher_note: Vasquez is 2-for-2 in the quality starts department since being called up to join the rotation in what was Ian Snell's spot. Vasquez finished six innings in his last start but allowed three runs to score on two home runs. Though he did have seven strikeouts in first start for the Pirates, Vasquez is not overpowering, relying mainly on his fastball but also on an improving changeup. This will be Vasquez's first career start against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler has won three of his past four starts, going 3-0 with a 3.13 ERA. In his previous start Wednesday in San Diego, he went six innings and held the Padres to four hits and one run, while walking four batters and striking out a season-high eight. He's 6-6 with a 5.66 ERA in 16 career games against the Pirates, including 13 starts. He threw a complete game against Pittsburgh on May 29, holding the Pirates to seven hits and one run at PNC Park.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm continues to battle problems with his sinker, a pitch that has always been his most reliable. The left-hander has had games where the pitch has worked effectively, but more often than not these last two months, it's been a major struggle. Maholm was knocked out after 4 1/3 innings in his last start and allowed six runs on 11 hits. In the past two months, five of Maholm's starts have not gone past the fifth. He had only three starts of five or fewer innings all of last year. Maholm is 6-4 with a 4.57 ERA in 11 career starts against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander won his second consecutive decision Thursday by holding San Diego to seven hits and one run while striking out five batters. Rodriguez is 3-4 with a 5.37 ERA in 10 career starts against the Pirates, but was roughed up by Pittsburgh in his only appearance against it this year. That came on May 30 in Pittsburgh when he gave up nine hits and five runs in 4 2/3 innings. Rodriguez is 25-20 with a 3.91 ERA in 65 career games (63 starts) at Minute Maid Park.
away_pitcher_note: Despite enduring two rain delays in his last start, Morton showed how effective he can be when he's finally healthy and able to pitch on normal rest. The lingering hamstring injury appears to be in the past, and Morton showcased exceptional movement on his pitches in a one-hit, six-inning shutout of the Marlins. He did walk four, however, while at times losing his control for stretches. Morton has made one career start against the Astros, that coming last season. Morton allowed six runs on eight hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing against the Mets and two-time Cy Young Award-winner Johan Santana, Blanton looked like the better pitcher. He tossed seven innings of shutout ball, allowing just four hits and striking out five. His fastball was consistently around 88-91 mph, although he reached the mid-90s during some crucial at-bats. He also benefited from some quality defense behind him. Still, Blanton has rebounded from early season struggles by going 3-1 with a 2.63 ERA over his past eight starts. In his lone career start against Pittsburgh, he threw seven scoreless innings and struck out seven, receiving a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: It wasn't his sharpest of outings, but Duke still managed to make another quality start his last time out. His two-strike wild pitch actually ended up being his biggest mistake, as it allowed what turned out to be the winning run to score. Duke continues to get no support in his losses, though. In his seven losses, he's been provided a total of eight runs of support. He's made quality starts in five of those seven losses. Duke is 1-2 with a 5.40 ERA in three career starts against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels was given a hefty dose of run support in his last outing -- a 22-1 Phillies victory of the Reds -- but he also made the most of the opportunity. After struggling all season with high pitch counts and short outings, he only needed 92 pitches to get through seven innings against Cincinnati, allowing no walks and just three hits. But the key for him going forward will be consistency and finding similar results in tighter games. Hamels won his only career start against the Pirates, but allowed three runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf's biggest problem continues to be his start-to-start consistency. Without having an explanation, Ohlendorf has fared very well at times, only to follow his strong outings with a subpar start. Lately, it has been much of the same for the right-hander. Without his slider being overly effective, Ohlendorf was hit for nine hits and five runs in his last start. That came just after a start in which he notched a career-high eight strikeouts in seven shutout innings. This will be Ohlendorf's first career start against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Happ had good command in his last start on Tuesday, striking out a career-high seven and walking none. He threw 105 pitches in seven innings and felt fresh enough to last longer. Despite pitching well, he received a no-decision because he allowed two home runs to Reds second baseman Brandon Phillips -- the second of which barely cleared the left-field wall. Although he does not have overpowering stuff, the 26-year-old left-hander has turned into the Phillies' most consistent starter, last losing in his big league debut in 2007. Happ has never faced the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Vasquez looked good in stretches in his last outing -- one in which he allowed four runs in six innings -- but also labored at times. This was his third start since being moved into the rotation and, surprisingly, it's been walks that have been hurting the right-hander. Usually one to go right at hitters, Vasquez admitted he's been timid at times, which has contributed to his eight walks in 18 innings so far. This will be Vasquez's first career start against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm rebounded from one of his worst starts of the season to have a stellar performance in what was his final start of the first half. He was poised to pitch well past the sixth until the Pirates had to pull him for a pinch hitter. Still, he allowed just two runs on six hits. Maholm hasn't been as consistent from start-to-start as he'd like, but when he's been on, he's been dominant. Of the 56 runs he has allowed this season, half of them have been confined to four starts. In his other 14 starts, Maholm has allowed a total of just 28.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum carried a no-hit bid into the seventh inning Thursday against the Padres. He allowed three runs on three hits (and four walks) in 6 2/3 frames, ending his scoreless streak at 29 innings. Lincecum is 4-0 over his past four starts and has whiffed eight or more batters in six straight starts. The Giants' ace lost in his only career appearance against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Morton blamed his struggles last time out on both poor pitch selection and poor location. He made it through the Astros' order once without being hurt, but he would eventually be chased after allowing 10 hits and five runs in only four innings. When he's on, Morton has movement to his pitches that is better than anyone on the staff. Still, there are some growing pains to be expected as Morton continues to try and harness some of that movement.
away_pitcher_note: Giants manager Bruce Bochy planned to shift his rotation after the All-Star break, and he's done just that. With Randy Johnson on the DL (strained throwing shoulder), Zito slides into the No. 2 role, in between All-Star hurlers Tim Lincecum and Matt Cain. Maybe that will force Zito to pick up his game. Sunday against the light-hitting San Diego Padres, the lefty allowed nine earned runs on 10 hits over 4 1/3 innings. He hasn't pitched past the sixth inning in six of his last eight starts. Zito lost his lone start against the Pirates in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Duke threw his sixth career complete game in his last outing, with eight strong innings against the Phillies on July 10 -- but he still lost, 3-2, a running theme in Duke's season. Duke has lost four of his last five starts, with the Pirates scoring just seven runs in those four losses. In his eight losses this season, the Pirates have managed just 10 runs -- only eight while he has been in the game. Duke is 0-5 in his last seven road starts. It was Duke's third complete game this year, making him the first Pirates lefty since Denny Neagle in 1995 to throw three complete games in a season.
away_pitcher_note: Cain will begin the season's second half pitching out of the third slot in the rotation. He will have eight days of rest after he was hit by a line drive in his right (throwing) elbow on July 11. That play resulted in his shortest career start (1 2/3 innings) and forced Cain to cede his spot on the active All-Star roster. Cain's elbow was still sore as he headed to St. Louis, but X-rays ruled out a fracture, and he's expected to regain full strength in his arm simply by resting it. The right-hander will take his 1.17 ERA for July into his start against the Pirates. He went 0-1 with a 6.23 ERA in outings against Pittsburgh last season.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf stumbled a bit going into the All-Star break, as he allowed eight runs in his last 10 2/3 innings (two starts). The right-hander is going through his first full season as a big league starter, which could be one reason for his inconsistencies this year. Though often able to keep the Pirates in the game, Ohlendorf still hasn't been able to pitch past the sixth all that often this year, something the Pirates would like to see more of in the second half.
away_pitcher_note: Dave Bush, who continues to feel discomfort in his injured right triceps, won't come off the DL to make this start, so manager Ken Macha said Burns would continue to start in Bush's spot. Burns beat the Dodgers in his last start, on July 11, allowing three earned runs in five innings and striking out seven. He has alternated wins and losses in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: It remains to be seen whether Vasquez will make this start, or if he will lose his spot in the rotation. Jeff Karstens, who is pitching out of the bullpen, and Tom Gorzelanny, who is dominating in the Minors, would both be candidates to take Vasquez's spot. After making two quality starts fresh off of being called up, Vasquez has pitched poorly his last two times out. He's combined to allow nine runs in just 7 1/3 innings, including five in 1 1/3 innings in his last start. The walk have been quickly piling up, too, which is quite unusual for Vasquez.
away_pitcher_note: Looper wasn't perfect in his most recent start, but he was good enough to earn his eighth win of the season. He gave up three earned runs in 5 1/3 innings of work against the Reds. While he allowed five walks and seven hits, his offense came through with nine runs in the victory. Looper also added a career-high three hits and an RBI single to help pace the offense. Looper received a no-decision against the Pirates on April 27 in a 10-5 win by the Brewers. In that start, he allowed two earned runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm had his longest outing of the season in his last start, throwing eight innings and surrendering one unearned run to get a no-decision against the Giants. The lefty has pitched at least six innings in all but six starts this season. Maholm has faced Milwaukee twice this season, coming in consecutive starts and both ending in a no-decision. His five career losses to the Brewers are the most against one team. Maholm is 2-5 with a 4.38 ERA in 12 career starts against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Brewers manager Ken Macha had no complaints about Suppan's start against the Reds on Friday, when he gave up no earned runs in six innings. His defense committed two costly errors, however, which led to three unearned runs in a 4-0 loss. Although Suppan has posted nine quality starts this season, he hasn't earned a victory since June 12, a string of six starts. Suppan will look to end that streak against the Pirates, against whom he is 1-0 this season; he beat Pittsburgh in an 8-5 win on May 5.

home_pitcher_note: Haren logged another outstanding outing his last time out against the Cardinals as he allowed just one run over eight innings. The right-hander has now recorded quality starts in 17 of his 18 outings this year and leads the Majors in ERA. Haren was selected to his third straight All-Star Game and tossed a scoreless inning of relief in the Midsummer Classic. Though many thought he should have gotten the start in the game, it went to the Giants' Tim Lincecum instead. He has allowed a total of three earned runs in his last four starts and just one run in his last two (17 innings).
away_pitcher_note: Morton won his first home game as a Pirate as he tied a career-high by throwing seven shutout innings. He got stronger as the game wore on as he gave up just three hits. Morton has one career start against Arizona, throwing seven shutout innings in a win on Aug. 7 last season. This will be Morton's fifth road start of the season, compared to just two at home. The righty is 1-1 with a 3.94 away from PNC Park this year.

home_pitcher_note: Petit had probably his best outing of the year in his last start against the Cardinals at Busch Stadium. The right-hander allowed just two runs on three hits over six innings. Walks wound up costing Petit. He walked four in the game, but the crucial two came back-to-back with two outs in the fifth to load the bases for St. Louis pitcher Joel Pineiro. Pineiro hit a slider into left for a two-run double that proved to be the difference in the 2-1 Cardinals win. Petit is filling in Brandon Webb's spot in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Duke lost at home for just the second time in his last seven decisions at PNC Park. And it was all the result of one inning-long hiccup. Duke kept the Giants off the scoreboard in six of the seven frames he pitched, but San Fransisco's four-run sixth was enough to do the lefty in. His pitches started elevating, and Duke allowed four consecutive doubles. Though he continues to pitch well, Duke has now lost four straight starts and hasn't won on the road since April 25. Duke is 1-2 with a 4.50 ERA in four career starts against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Even though Davis has struggled in his last two starts -- 13 earned run given up in six innings -- manager A.J. Hinch believes he will bounce back. After all, in four previous outings before his mini-slump, Davis had a 1.32 ERA in 27 1/3 innings. Despite his record, Davis has pitched well this season and for him to continue to be effective he must be able to jam right-handed hitters with his two-seam fastball instead of throwing them in the dirt -- which is what happened in his last start. He's 6-6 with a 5.22 ERA against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf has not been able to finish six innings in any of his last six starts, though he's not pitched too poorly in his most recent two. Still in his first full season as a Major League starter, Ohlendorf continues to work toward increasing his stamina late in games. His changeup continues to develop as well, though it's still not reliable 100 percent of the time. The Pirates still believe there is a little more velocity in his arm, though it's questionable whether or not anyone will see that the rest of this season.

home_pitcher_note: With the All-Star break looming, manager A.J. Hinch saw the perfect opportunity to avoid overusing Max Scherzer by pushing the youngster to the back of the rotation after the break. He wanted to get Scherzer into the 180-innings range by the end of the season. After a 13-day layoff, Scherzer's first start after the break was not a happy one. It was an uneven performance that he labored through. He threw 61 of 95 pitches in the first two innings and yielded four runs on seven hits -- albeit with six strikeouts -- in four innings. He received a no-decision as the Diamondbacks rallied for a 6-5 win. Scherzer said he needs to throw first pitch strikes if he's going to bounce back from this performance.
away_pitcher_note: Vasquez rebounded from a tumultuous outing against the Phillies and pitched a career-long 6 2/3 innings in his first start back after the break. After nitpicking with his pitches too much to be successful earlier this month, Vasquez got back to pounding the zone and went to a three-ball count just once. Of the 29 hitters he faced, he threw two or fewer pitches to 13 of them. Vasquez allowed only two runs, both coming on two-out RBI singles.  This will be Vasquez's first career start against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: The reigning National League Cy Young Award winner and two-time All-Star is 0-1 in his first two second-half starts despite pitching capably. Lincecum received no decision in the first game following the All-Star break, allowing one run and five hits while striking out 10 in seven innings at Pittsburgh on July 17. He followed that with a five-inning effort -- his shortest of the year since a three-inning cameo on Opening Day -- last Wednesday at Atlanta. Lincecum yielded four runs in that one, but struck out nine, proving that his arm and stuff remained sound.
away_pitcher_note: It was not a pretty sight the last time Maholm took the mound, as he squandered an early lead and was chased after 4 2/3 innings. Maholm allowed seven runs for the fourth time this season. Maholm has just not had the same consistency that he did a year ago, especially when it comes to keeping his sinking fastball down. It's been up too often, which is evident in Maholm's numbers. Maholm is 1-0 with a 2.31 ERA in five career starts against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Zito came through in his last start with one of his biggest wins as a Giant. He limited Atlanta to one run and three hits in seven innings last Thursday in a 5-1 triumph. That snapped a personal two-game losing streak for Zito, who endured a tough-luck loss to Pittsburgh on July 18 when he worked 6 1/3 innings in a 2-0 Pirates win. Zito is 71-37 with a 3.45 ERA in his career after the All-Star break. He's also 2-4 with a 4.45 ERA in nine starts at home this year.
away_pitcher_note: Staked to an early lead in his last start, Morton couldn't hold it. He fell behind hitters consistently and still showed a bit of struggle in harnessing what can be electric movement of his pitches. Morton admitted afterward to not feeling sharp from the get-go, and it was evident as he labored to locate through the 4 2/3-inning start. That start came on the heels of Morton throwing seven scoreless innings against the Giants. Now almost two months since being put in the rotation, Morton is still searching for that start-to-start consistency.

home_pitcher_note: Cain made his best run at the Cy Young Award in his last start with an impressive win over the Rockies. Cain threw 117 pitches in seven innings and yielded an earned run on three hits with five strikeouts. The victory vaulted the Giants into a tie with the Rockies at the time for the National League's Wild Card lead. Cain ended July with a 3-0 record and a 1.23 ERA. Cain's best month, career-wise has been in August where he's 9-6 with a 2.85 ERA. His next opponent is the Pirates and against them on July 19, Cain went seven and gave up an earned run on five hits with eight strikeouts for his 11th win.
away_pitcher_note: Duke wasn't at his sharpest in his last start, one in which he allowed 10 hits in six innings. However, as he's shown a knack for doing all season, he limited the damage -- this time to three runs. The consistency shown by Duke early in the season has taken a bit of a hit, but there's no reason to expect anything less than a six-inning start from the lefty each time out. He is just 1-5 on the road since the end of April and has a 2-2 record and 4.06 ERA in six career starts against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf kept his pitch count low -- something he's struggled to do all year -- in his last start, but without his command, it didn't matter all that much. Ohlendorf struggled with his location in allowing six hits (five for extra bases) and two earned runs in six innings. Still, he showed impressive poise in getting out of a number of jams. Ohlendorf is still looking for some consistency with his pitches, especially his slider, as it has been rare that he has command of all his pitches on the same night.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan's ERA continued to creep lower with his eight-inning, one-run outing on Sunday against the Padres. He was unable to earn the victory, as closer Mike MacDougal blew the save in the ninth. Lannan needed just 81 pitches to get through eight innings before the Nationals opted to use a pinch-hitter for him. His accuracy was there again, walking just one batter, and throwing more than 72 percent of his pitches for strikes. Lannan has walked four batters in his past five starts combined.

home_pitcher_note: Whether Vasquez is still in the rotation when his turn comes around remains to be seen. The righty was knocked out of his last start after only three innings. He allowed four runs on six hits and two walks. It was the second time in three starts that Vasquez was not able to pitch more than three innings. He has lost five straight and shown very little consistency with his command. The Pirates could decide to move Jeff Karstens from the bullpen back into the rotation. Otherwise Ian Snell or Tom Gorzelanny, both in Triple-A, could get a sniff.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen had one of his worst outings of the season on Monday, giving up five runs in 4 2/3 innings against the Brewers. However, he ended up with no decision, thanks to outfielder Josh Willingham, who hit two grand slams.

home_pitcher_note: A couple of wacky defensive sequences hurt Maholm in his last start despite the fact that he didn't pitch that poorly. He was up in the strike zone a little too much early, which did cost him a few early runs. He did find a way to settle into his rhythm late, though, and threw four scoreless innings to end the six-inning start. He also closed out his start by getting plenty of groundballs, a sign that he's on top of his command. Maholm is 0-2 with a 5.23 ERA in five career starts against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Balester had one of his best outings of his career on Tuesday, lasting six innings and giving up two runs on five hits against the Brewers. In the second inning, he gave up an RBI single to J.J. Hardy that tied the score at 1-1. In the sixth inning, Ryan Braun hit a solo homer, but the Nationals already had a comfortable lead.

home_pitcher_note: Morton took the tough-luck loss in his last start despite allowing just two earned runs in six innings. On an encouraging note, he was more aggressive with his fastball for much of the night and maintained his velocity through his 107-pitch effort. The consistency is still a work in progress for Morton, but the Pirates continue to be enthralled by the movement of his pitches. This will be Morton's first career start against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Mock started for the Nationals on Wednesday and lasted five-plus innings and gave up four runs on eight hits. For weeks, the Nationals would often talk about how Mock dominated the Minor Leagues as a starter for Triple-A Syracuse. He was 5-1 with a 2.65 ERA there. But that success hasn't transferred to the big league level in three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Duke allowed just six hits over seven shutout innings against the San Francisco Giants Wednesday afternoon but still came away with a no-decision. A lack of offensive support has been a continued theme for the lefty: He's received nine total runs in his nine losses this season. Duke finished July with a 3.67 ERA but exited the month with a 1-3 record in five starts. He won in his last outing against the Arizona Diamondbacks, yielding three runs over 6 1/3 innings on July 24.
away_pitcher_note: Petit had his finest outing of the season last Wednesday against the Phillies at Chase Field. The right-hander handled the NL's best lineup and made it look easy. Philadelphia managed just two hits against him through the first six innings and he retired 13 in a row before allowing two hits to open the seventh. Petit does not have overpowering stuff, so he needs to hit his spots and keep the ball down. When he does that, he can have some success; when he doesn't, it can be ugly as his 6.75 ERA can attest.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf closed out July by earning a victory against the Nationals in his last start. He gave up two runs on six hits in 6 1/3 innings. The right-hander has been solid at PNC Park this season, going 7-2 in 11 starts while posting a 3.34 ERA. Ohlendorf has pitched against Arizona once this season, on July 25. He took the loss despite surrendering three runs - two earned - in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Davis did not pitch particularly well in his last start against the Mets on Friday, but he did get the job done. The left-hander allowed four hits and walked six in six innings, but managed to allow just two runs. That can be typical of Davis, who tends to allow a lot of baserunners, but more often than not pitches his way out of trouble. At the end of one of his outings, it is not uncommon to look at the final score and wonder how exactly he got there. Davis does not give into hitters, which contributes to the walk total, but he also can try to be too fine at times, which compounds the problem.

home_pitcher_note: Hart, who was one of the acquisitions in the Pirates' trade with the Cubs on July 30, makes his Pittsburgh debut. It will be the fifth game and first start of his career at PNC Park, where he is 1-0 with a 9.00 ERA. Hart hasn't faced Arizona this season, but the right-hander has won his last three starts overall, giving up six runs in 17 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer had a disastrous fourth inning against the Mets in his last outing on Saturday night and it prevented him from getting a win. Following his best start of the year, the right-hander held the Mets scoreless through the first three innings. But in the fourth, he wound up allowing five hits and four runs. Even more damaging to his chances for a win was the fact that he threw a whopping 38 pitches in the inning, which caused manager A.J. Hinch to take him out. In his start before that, Scherzer tossed seven scoreless innings allowing five hits and no walks while striking out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm gave up only one run through six innings in his last start before surrendering three in the seventh. But manager John Russell thought the left-hander improved as the game went on. The big hit against Maholm was a two-run home run that put him behind. It was just the eighth long ball the pitcher has given up this season.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter is quietly putting together a pretty strong case for his second NL Cy Young Award. The 2005 winner leads the NL with a 2.10 ERA and has 10 wins despite missing five weeks with a strained oblique in April and May. Carpenter was dominant once again on Saturday against Houston, giving up just one run in the 27th complete game of his career. He struck out five in going at least eight innings for the third time in his past four starts. Carpenter, who hasn't given up more than three runs since June 30, has dominated Pittsburgh over his career. He is 10-1 with a 2.06 ERA in 12 career starts against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Morton was on his way to a victory in his last start by throwing five shutout innings, but the right-hander gave up four runs in the sixth and was handed defeat. The big hit off Morton was a three-run home run by Adam Dunn, and the pitcher has now given up a home run in three consecutive starts. Morton has faced the Cardinals twice in his career, although he hasn't yet seen them this season. In those two starts, Morton has given up 12 runs in five innings, going 0-2.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright was a tough-luck loser yet again on Sunday, when he gave up two runs in seven innings but lost to the Astros, 2-0. The durable righty, who has gone at least six innings in 21 straight starts, has thrown at least 111 pitches in nine starts this season and has gone over the 120-pitch mark three times. Wainwright gave up eight hits to the Astros but was happy with his stuff. Both of the runs that he gave up were preventable, with one scoring on a two-out hit and the other coming after an infield single started the inning. The righty's fastball had good life and his curveball had good break, both good signs as the Cardinals gear up for the stretch run.

home_pitcher_note: The long ball hurt Duke in his last start, when he gave up three in a loss to the D-backs. The three home runs tied a season-high for him as the lefty has lost five of his last six decisions. Facing the Cardinals has been nothing new for Duke this season; this will be his fourth start against them. He is 2-1 with a 2.75 ERA against St. Louis in 2009, although he hasn't faced the division foe since May 12.
away_pitcher_note: In his first August start after a sparkling July, Pineiro had his worst outing of the year. Pitching at Citi Field, the same ballpark in which he authored a two-hit shutout on June 23, Pineiro was lit up by the Mets for seven runs on 11 hits in five innings. August has traditionally given Pineiro trouble -- it's the only month in which he has a career ERA over 5.00. Pineiro is 3-2 with a 5.66 ERA in seven career starts versus the Pirates and 2-2 with a 5.87 ERA at PNC Park, where he gave up 11 hits in a loss earlier this year. The Pittsburgh lineup has success in limited experience against Pineiro, hitting a collective .355 in 31 at-bats.

home_pitcher_note: The start became available because the Rockies are resting right-hander Aaron Cook, who is recovering from a hyperextended right big toe. He has been pushed to Saturday. Chacin, 21, called up from Double-A Tulsa on July 24, has pitched well in four relief appearances, including two innings on Saturday in his last appearance. Chacin showed a good fastball and changeup, plus beyond-his-years mound presence during Spring Training. He's also developed a slider that he has used at the Major League level. This will be his first regular-season start. The Rockies considered going with veteran Josh Fogg, but manager Jim Tracy said it was more important to have Fogg ready in case Chacin struggles. Chacin will be limited to around 75 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf left his last start with a one-run lead but was handed a no-decision as the Diamondbacks rallied late. Ohlendorf gave up just one run on four hits in six innings, with manager John Russell saying after the game that the next step for Ohlendorf is to get a little more efficient so he can pitch deeper into games. The righty has one start against the Rockies this season and took a defeat by giving up six runs on nine hits in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez won his third straight decision in his last start to even his record. He threw 6 2/3 innings and yielded two runs on four hits with six strikeouts to defeat the Cubs. However, he did issue five walks. Even with the command issues, Jimenez throws at least five pitches and he was able to control a two-seam fastball and, later, the curveball to cruise to victory. Jimenez has tossed at least six innings in 19 consecutive starts and has thrown more than 100 pitches in 21 of his 23 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hart's first start with the Pirates ended in a no-decision, though the right-hander pitched well enough to earn his new manager's praise afterward. Hart allowed three runs on nine hits in six innings. Pittsburgh is looking to Hart to stabilize a spot in the rotation that has been in shaky all season. He showcased solid fastball command with velocity in the 92-95 range in his last start. This will be Hart's first career start against the Rockies. He has pitched one inning of relief against Colorado and allowed two runs in it.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis has been stuck on 12 wins for nearly a month now, but of the three starts he's had for win No. 13, his last start was easily the worst. The first-time All-Star lacked sharpness as he surrendered five runs on eights with a season-high five walks to take the loss Saturday against the Cubs. Marquis had been pitching with a blister problem as recently as July 19 against the Padres. Coincidentally, that was when he picked up his 12th win. In his three starts since then, he's 0-2 with a 4.74 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm is now 0-2 in his last five starts after a no-decision in his last start, one in which Maholm allowed four runs in seven innings. Maholm has now allowed at least four runs in each of his last four starts. He was hurt by two home runs in his last start. It was the second time in his last four starts that Maholm had allowed two runs in a game. He is 1-3 with a 4.50 ERA in five career starts against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Wells had the roughest start of his rookie season in his last start, snapping a four-game winning streak by allowing career highs of seven runs and five earned runs in his 5 1/3 innings at Coors Field. His slider was ineffective, and he relied on four-seam fastballs and cutters -- with poor results. Wells' big struggle was with his command, as he walked two but found too much of the plate in yielding eight hits. Perhaps most frustrating for Wells was his inability to adapt during the game and his difficulty bearing down and offering shutdown innings. As a result, he let the Rockies resume their attack every time the Cubs staged a minor comeback.
away_pitcher_note: Morton dropped his third straight decision in his last start despite not pitching too poorly against a hot Cardinals lineup. Morton limited St. Louis to one run on seven singles in five innings. His start was cut short, though, because of a quickly escalating pitch count. Morton need 93 pitches to get through five innings. The right-hander continues to struggle with his pitch-to-pitch and inning-to-inning consistency. But being that he has never pitched a full season in the Majors before, that is a somewhat expected growing pain. Morton has made one career start against the Cubs and lasted only 2 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny had a strong first outing for the Cubs after a July 30 trade from Pittsburgh, pitching 7 1/3 innings of one-run, three-hit ball against the Reds. His second time out couldn't have been much different as he was touched for six runs on six hits in 1 1/3 innings. He left the game after suffering a contusion on his right foot when it was struck by a hard-hit ball in the second inning, but X-rays showed no fracture and he is expected to make his next start. His two-out, two-run homer allowed to Troy Tulowitzki could be forgiven as the shortstop had a career night, hitting for the cycle and driving in seven, but Gorzelanny gave up four consecutive hits in the second, all of whom scored.
away_pitcher_note: In his fourth go at getting his 10th win of the year, Duke was denied the victory by his own defense and bullpen. Duke left his last start after 7 1/3 innings, having given up one earned run and one unearned one. He left a runner on base who would eventually score as Duke watched from the bench, which charged Duke with two earned runs allowed in the start. He has pitched at least six innings in 16 of his last 17 starts. Duke is 3-3 with a 3.19 ERA in six career starts at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Harden did not get a decision in his last start vs. the Phillies. He retired the first 16 batters he faced before walking Carlos Ruiz with one out in the sixth. One batter later, Jimmy Rollins spoiled Harden's no-hit bid with a two-run homer. That was one of two hits off Harden in his seven innings of work. He also struck out six. Harden has a 1.95 ERA in his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf was nothing short of efficient in his last start as he gave up three runs on six hits in six-plus innings for the win against the Rockies on Tuesday. Ohlendorf is in the midst of a second-half surge as he's 3-1 with a 3.07 ERA in five starts -- the last four of which have been a quality start -- since the All-Star break. If there's anything that could derail him, it might be his ribs. Ohlendorf fielded a ground ball in the sixth inning against the Rockies and had his wind knocked out. He stayed in the ballgame and said he was a little sore postgame.

home_pitcher_note: It was only the sixth start of Hart's young career, but it was easily the worst. Hart surrendered five earned runs on eight hits in 5 1/3 innings in a 8-0 loss to the Rockies Wednesday. In his previous five starts, he had not given up more than three runs. Hart's problem was when he got ahead of hitters with two strikes, he couldn't put them away especially with his slider. Hart will be making his first career start against the Brewers but has a career 3.52 ERA in five relief appearances facing the Brew Crew.
away_pitcher_note: Villanueva pitched a solid 5 2/3 innings in his last start, a no-decision against San Diego on Wednesday. The right-hander held the Padres to two runs on five hits, walking two and striking out four. He threw 91 pitches, the most he's thrown as a starter this season. Villanueva has faced the Pirates 13 times in his career, owning a 2-1 record with a 2.10 ERA. He has started against Pittsburgh once in his career, giving up two runs and walking three in a 7-4 loss on September 10, 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf was scheduled to start on Sunday, but his start got rained out before it began. The righty was nothing short of efficient in his previous start, when he gave up three runs on six hits in six-plus innings for the win against the Rockies on Tuesday. Ohlendorf is in the midst of a second-half surge, as he's 3-1 with a 3.07 ERA in five outings -- the past four of which have been quality starts -- since the All-Star break. If there's anything that could derail him, it might be his ribs. Ohlendorf fielded a ground ball in the sixth inning against the Rockies and had his wind knocked out. He stayed in the ballgame and said he was a little sore postgame.
away_pitcher_note: Parra took advantage of an early nine-run lead on Thursday to earn his eighth win of the season despite not lasting through the sixth inning. Parra held San Diego scoreless for the first four innings, but the Padres made him pay in the fifth and sixth, scoring all six runs in those two innings. Parra threw 104 pitches in 5 2/3 innings, allowing six runs on 13 hits, and he struck out seven. Parra's only start against the Pirates came on May 20, 2008, when he allowed four hits in 5 2/3 shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm struggled in his last start against the Rockies on Thursday as he surrenderd seven runs -- six earned -- on 11 hits, which includes two home runs, in 6 1/3 innings. Even though he was sharper than his past four starts, Maholm either left pitches out over the plate or couldn't finish off hitters. In a broader view, Maholm is 0-3 with a 7.42 ERA in his last five outings. Career-wise, Maholm is 2-5 with a 4.91 ERA against his next opponent, the Milwaukee Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo got a bunch of run support -- eight first-inning runs -- in his last start, against the Astros, to earn his 11th win of the season. The Brewers' ace allowed two runs on three hits in six innings, throwing 105 pitches. In his last start against the Pirates, on April 29, Gallardo became just the third pitcher in Major League history to win, 1-0, while recording at least 10 strikeouts and hitting a home run. He tossed eight scoreless innings, holding Pittsburgh to two hits while striking out 11.

home_pitcher_note: The Cubs chased Morton before the right-hander could record an out in the second in his last start, but not before Morton had given up 10 runs to what had been a slumping Chicago offense. His problems were evident early: Morton fell behind consistently and never established his fastball command, a priority he had set coming into the start. He continues to show deceptive movement on his pitches, but without the command to go with it, that movement has proved to be as troublesome as it has been beneficial.
away_pitcher_note: Owings, who has been on the DL since July 27 with right shoulder stiffness, will replace Johnny Cueto in the rotation for Friday's game against the Pirates. In his last start, Owings only pitched three innings before leaving the game with his shoulder injury. Owings lost to the Pirates on May 2 in a 8-6 loss. He gave up five runs and nine hits over 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Duke can't seem to buy run support from his teammates, and his last start was no different. In Duke's 11 losses this year, the Pirates have scored a total of 14 runs, 10 while he was on the mound. The left-hander has been sitting on nine wins since July 24 and looks to match his career-high total of 10 wins, achieved in 2006. Though he is 0-2 in his past four starts, Duke has pitched at least seven innings in three of those games. He is 2-3 with a 3.48 ERA in six career starts against Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: Lehr wasn't perfect but he kept the Reds in the game. He gave up three runs on six hits in six innings. He left with a 4-3 lead but his bullpen couldn't hold the lead for him in a 5-4 loss. Lehr gave up two runs in the fourth but settled down and only allowed one more before he exited after the sixth. Lehr will look to keep his record perfect against the Pirates, who he has never faced in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Hart shows flashes of above-average command at times, but he is still too frequently leaving pitches up. And it's costing him. Despite being staked to an early five-run lead in his last start, Hart immediately allowed the Brewers to chip away as he surrendered two homers in the final two innings of his six-inning start. Before that start, Hart had given up just seven homers in 77 2/3 career innings. He's been plagued, too, by running up a high pitch count early. In four appearances (one start) against Cincinnati, Hart has allowed three earned runs in 11 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey was cruising through the Giants' order through five innings his last time out and had a 5-1 lead entering the sixth. But he fell apart in the sixth and gave up four runs to lose the lead and a shot at beating Giants starter Tim Lincecum. Bailey left with one out in the sixth, having surrendered five runs and seven hits while striking out four. He will look to get his first win since July 27 against the Pirates. Bailey has not faced the Pirates this season.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf might be pitching as well as he has at any point this season. Now four starts into using a tweaked delivery motion, Ohlendorf is showing that his improved velocity and sustained command are no flukes. He has now won three straight and has allowed three or fewer runs in nine of his last 10 starts. Ohlendorf did not factor in the decision in his July 11 start against the Phillies. He allowed three earned runs on five hits and four walks in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton allowed 10 hits and three runs in eight innings Thursday in a 12-3 victory over the D-backs. Blanton is 8-6 with a 3.86 ERA, and has been one of the team's best starters this season. He worked quickly and efficiently against Arizona, not walking a single batter. "It's a young, aggressive team," Blanton said. "Just because somebody is aggressive it doesn't mean you throw more balls. You still come right at them. Go at them and make your defense do some work. Just keep attacking the zone." He's been doing that to everybody most of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Despite being hit by line drives to his left tricep and left shin, Maholm tossed 7 2/3 innings his last time out and allowed just one run on seven hits. Though he had some nice bruises to show from the knocks, he is not expected to be affected by either injury in his next start. Maholm snapped a six-start winless streak with the victory and also found good feel with his sinker again. His bread-and-butter pitch helped him induce 15 groundball outs. Maholm is 3-1 with a 3.71 ERA in five career starts against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: This season has been a struggle for Hamels. He is is 7-8 with the fifth-highest ERA (4.72) in the National League. He allowed 10 hits and four runs just five innings Friday in a 4-2 loss to the Mets at Citi Field. "I've always been a step ahead, and right now I'm neck-and-neck," Hamels said. "I might have a good game or a good inning, but you really have to put it together, pitch by pitch, inning by inning, to make it a good game. And then you have to back it up with another good game and another good game. Like what our other four starters are doing. For some odd reason, I'm the one that's bringing them down. I don't like that fact at all."

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Morton did a terrific job at bouncing back from a horrific start that saw him allow 10 earned runs in one inning. He snapped a personal four-game losing streak in an outing during which he allowed just two runs in 6 1/3 innings. For all of the questions about how strong Morton is mentally, that bounce-back outing should have put some of those concerns to rest. Morton relied heavily on his two-seam fastball and changeup in his last outing, and while he was more efficient than he has been, there is still work to do in that area. Morton faced the Phillies once in 2008 and took a loss after allowing five runs in two innings.
away_pitcher_note: Happ is 10-2 with a 2.59 ERA following a 4-1 victory Saturday over the Mets. He could become the first Phillies rookie to win 11 games since Bob Walk in 1980. No Phillies rookie has had a lower ERA since Eppa Rixey's 2.50 ERA in 1912. "J.A. does not pitch like he's a young pitcher," Brad Lidge said. "Honestly, he's pitching like he's one of the best pitchers in the National League. I know he's a rookie, but it is what it is. He's pitching like one of the best guys in the National League." Happ's ERA is the lowest for any rookie pitcher anywhere since Hideo Nomo in 1995, when he had a 2.54 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: If the Brewers are going to try to climb back into postseason contention, they are going to need Parra to turn his recent woes around. After seeing a four-game winning streak snapped Aug. 18, Parra got hammered Aug. 23 at Washington, allowing eight runs, five of them earned, on eight hits in just 3 1/3 innings. It could have been worse for his ERA, as he gave up three long home runs and was hit hard in the first inning, but all three runs were unearned due to an error.
away_pitcher_note: With the run support he has been begging for lately, Duke finally succeeded in getting his 10th win of the season in his fifth try. As Duke's ERA reflects, the left-hander has been wonderfully consistent all season for the Pirates, but has had no consistent support from his offense in the process. Duke has pitched at least seven innings, as he did in his last start, in 16 of his 25 starts this season. Duke is 3-4 with a 4.70 ERA in 12 previous starts against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo inched closer to reaching the 200-strikeout plateau in his last start Aug. 24 against Washington, as he got the win with five innings of four-hit one-run ball, striking out eight while walking four to raise his season total to 179. The right-hander, who has become the most reliable young starter in the Brewers rotation after missing most of 2008 with knee injuries, looked like he might be en route to another low-scoring loss before the team exploded for six sixth-inning runs to get him the victory.
away_pitcher_note: In four starts since being traded to the Pirates, Hart has still yet to show great command. Granted, he has kept Pittsburgh in each game he has started, but none of those starts have been especially sharp. Getting his command back is the main focus moving forward, especially when it comes to being able to put away hitters after he gets ahead of them. Hart has made six appearances against the Brewers in his career, though only one has come as a starter. In all, he is 1-0 with a 4.61 ERA in 13 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his return from the disabled list, Suppan slogged through 4 1/3 innings against the Reds on Tuesday with 90 pitches and was charged with four runs on nine hits and five walks, though one of the walks was intentional. The good news was that the rib-cage injury that sidelined him nearly a month was a non-issue. The bad news was that Suppan remained winless in the Majors since June 12. He pitched at least six innings in three of his nine starts since then, but in the other six he's allowed 32 earned runs and 50 hits in 29 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf left in line for his fourth straight win, only to have the bullpen blow the lead late in his last start. Pitching against a tough left-handed-heavy Phillies lineup, Ohlendorf allowed just two solo homers in 6 1/3 innings. Not usual for the righty, most of his outs were recorded via fly ball, a result of the Phillies not biting at his sinker all that much. Ohlendorf has beaten the Brewers in each of his two career starts against them. In 12 innings against Milwaukee, Ohlendorf has allowed just three earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: On Wednesday vs. the Brewers, Wells pitched five innings, allowing three earned runs and seven hits with three walks and two strikeouts during his first big league start since July 21, 2008, with the Rockies. Wells had runners on base in each of his first four innings, but kept putting zeroes on the board until the fifth when he gave up three runs on two home runs.
away_pitcher_note: McCutchen will be summoned from Triple-A Indianapolis to make his Major League debut and start the first game of the Pirates' doubleheader against the Reds. Just last week, McCutchen had committed to play for Team USA in the upcoming World Cup tournament. However, the Pirates' need for an extra starter for the final month and McCutchen's deserving credentials prompted management to change its mind and invite the righty to the big leagues for the season's final five weeks. Since the All-Star break, McCutchen, whom the Pirates acquired in a six-player deal with the Yankees last summer, has gone 5-1 with a 1.90 ERA in eight Triple-A starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto will be activated from the disabled list to make the start. He's been out with right shoulder inflammation. In his last start on Aug. 15, a 10-6 loss the Nationals, Cueto gave up seven earned runs and eight hits over 2 2/3 innings. His record is 0-6 with a 10.64 ERA over his last eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm has had an up-and-down season, but he might be saving his best for last. In his last two starts, a win against the Brewers and a no-decision against the Phillies, he's looked more like the head of the rotation who earned the Opening Day start than he has in a while. He gave up just two runs in 14 2/3 over those two starts. An even better sign is that he induced 25 ground-ball outs, showing perhaps that he's got his sinker working better than he has since the beginning of the season.

home_pitcher_note: During a game in which the Reds needed to save a worn bullpen, Lehr came through by working 7 2/3 innings in an 8-5 win over the Brewers on Thursday. Lehr gave up five earned runs and seven hits with three walks and seven strikeouts, but he became extremely stingy after trailing, 4-0, in the first inning. Lehr allowed just one more run and four hits the rest of the day. The biggest adjustment Lehr made was getting his pitches down in the strike zone after leaving everything up in the first.
away_pitcher_note: Morton has struggled to find a level of consistency since coming to the Pirates from the Braves in the June trade for Nate McLouth. If his last two starts are any indication, he might be starting to figure some things out. Even though his command has still been spotty (seven walks in those two starts), he's given up just four runs over 12 1/3 innings, a 2.92 ERA. Take out the one disastrous one-inning, 10-run outing and Morton had a 3.47 ERA in August. His one win of the month came against the Reds, when he allowed two earned runs over 6 1/3 inning.

home_pitcher_note: Over his past two starts, Bailey has allowed one run in 15 innings. The 23-year-old right-hander is coming off of the best big league start of his young career, a 4-2 win over the Dodgers on Friday in which he pitched a career-high eight scoreless innings with seven hits -- all singles -- one walk and a career-high seven strikeouts. Bailey's fastball velocity was high throughout the game; his 115th and final pitch was a 97 mph fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Duke had his worst outing of the season in his last start, though the numbers look like he was hit much worse than he actually was. Yes, the left-hander gave up a season-high seven runs on 11 hits, but he was largely hurt by a number of ground balls that snuck through the infield. That's not to say he didn't also make mistakes, as he was taken deep twice. Without his sinking fastball to rely on, he was simply up in the zone all too often. Duke is 3-3 with a 3.32 ERA in seven career starts against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Hart certainly wasn't helped by his defense in his last start, though that's not to say he still didn't labor. The right-hander needed 118 pitches to get through six innings and is now 1-3 since being traded to the Pirates. In fact, he's been hardly the same pitcher for Pittsburgh as he was with the Cubs. After going 3-1 with a 2.86 ERA in four starts with Chicago, Hart's ERA with the Pirates sits at 6.04. This will be Hart's first career start against the Cardinals. In two relief appearances, Hart has allowed one run in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright has been all but automatic lately, and he shows no signs of slowing down. He has lasted at least six innings in 26 straight starts, and he's allowed two or fewer earned runs in each of his last 13. He's emerged as a very real candidate for National League Cy Young honors, and he's been a critical part of the Redbirds' run to a huge lead in the NL Central. Pittsburgh hasn't always been a friendly park for him, but the way he's rolling lately, it's hard to see him being tripped up.

home_pitcher_note: One bases-loaded walk to the pitcher ultimately did Ohlendorf in during his last start, a loss to the Brewers. Not only did that walk push across a run, but it helped extend what was a three-run inning for Milwaukee. In all, Ohlendorf allowed four runs on five hits in six innings. Take away that one frame, and the right-hander was impressive. His efficiency was exceptional early, and his fastball velocity continues to sit in the mid-90s. Ohlendorf is 1-2 with a 4.00 ERA in three career starts against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Boggs is coming off of one of his best starts of the year, and as a reward it appears that he'll get another one. His story tends to be pretty consistent from start to start: he gives up a lot of baserunners, runs up some high pitch counts but ultimately tends to avoid too much trouble. If he can improve his efficiency -- as he did to some extent in his last outing -- he can be pretty effective.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm gave up three early runs, and that was the difference in a 6-3 loss to the Reds in Game 2 of a doubleheader Monday. Maholm threw 43 pitches in the first inning and only made one mistake after that marathon frame. His final line was four runs and nine hits over five innings, including a homer to Brandon Phillips. Maholm will look to get back on the winning track against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Last time out, Pineiro did two things on consecutive batters that he often doesn't do in an entire game: Issued a walk and allowed a homer. That put him in a hole, but after that he was fine, and the Cardinals dug out. As a result, St. Louis has now won 10 straight starts by the right-hander, and he's been especially good at home. He keeps doing the same thing: Throwing strikes and keeping the ball on the ground. And it keeps working.

home_pitcher_note: McCutchen made his Major League debut last Monday and fared pretty well. After allowing a leadoff homer, McCutchen settled in to finish six innings. He allowed three runs and five hits. With the Pirates now going with a six-man rotation for the rest of the season, McCutchen will be a mainstay among the starters. He's not going to overwhelm anyone with his fastball, which is in the 90- to 93-mph range, but he's a guy with above-average command.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly picked up his 10th win in his last start, against the Astros. The lefty threw eight scoreless innings, giving up four hits and striking out five. With the win, he's posted seven straight 10-win seasons. Over his past 86 innings, Lilly has walked 12 and struck out 71. In his past four starts, he's given up four earned runs over 27 1/3 innings for a 1.32 ERA. The only thing wrong with his win over the Astros was an ill-advised attempt to steal second and his head-first slide into the base. He won't be doing that again.

home_pitcher_note: Duke looked as if he was in line for a win entering the sixth inning with a 3-2 lead on Wednesday against the Reds, but fielding woes and a home run by Drew Stubbs turned that chance at a win into a loss. Duke pitched six innings and gave up five runs, three of which were earned in a 5-3 loss. He has lost three of his past four decisions. Duke will look to get back on the winning track against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster was a hard-luck loser in his last start, on Thursday against the White Sox. For the second time this season, all three runs he gave up in a game were unearned, although he also allowed nine hits. Dempster did pitch seven innings, his seventh consecutive outing in which he lasted at least six frames. In his one start against the Pirates this season, Dempster was roughed up for six earned runs in four innings, although five of Pittsburgh's starting position players in that game have since been traded.

home_pitcher_note: The command that Hart showed while with the Cubs earlier this season continues to come only in short spurts here with Pittsburgh. Hart was chased after allowing seven runs (five earned) in 5 2/3 innings his last time out. After going 3-1 with a 2.60 ERA in four starts with the Cubs, Hart has gone 1-4 with a 6.35 ERA in six starts with Pittsburgh. He's had little consistency with his command and has given up six home runs.
away_pitcher_note: While Zambrano hasn't won a game since July 22 at Philadelphia and has spent a session on the disabled list with muscle spasms in his back since that victory, he showed in his last start he may be rounding back into form. He was 0-2 in two starts since coming off the disabled list before he pitched six innings of three-hit baseball and yielded only a solo home run in a no-decision against the Mets at Citi Field on Sept. 4. He has faced the Pirates only once this season. He gave up two runs, one of which was earned, on seven hits over 6 1/3 innings in a no-decision on May 27 in Chicago. He's 6-1 lifetime at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Norris, who was coming off three poor starts, showed the kind of poise and fastball command that made him one of the organization's top-rated prospects by holding the Phillies to six hits and two runs in six innings last Sunday. He was the first Astros rookie to win his first three starts before falling on hard times; Norris had gone 0-3 with a 13.11 ERA in three starts prior to Sunday. This will be his eighth Major League start and first appearance against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Morton was pushed back three days in order to give his tender groin a little more time to heal. It also gave the right-hander a chance to have an extra side session with pitching coach Joe Kerrigan. Morton's season could be defined simply by the word inconsistency. He has shown flashes of being able to command the exceptional movement he has on his pitcheS, But there have only been flashes of that. Morton is 0-1 with a 9.90 ERA in two previous starts against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler held the Phillies to three runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings in his previous start Monday at Minute Maid Park. He had not allowed more than three earned runs in any of his last four starts, going 1-1 with a 3.57 ERA in those starts. The Astros are 3-1 in his last four starts. Moehler is 1-2 with a 5.09 ERA in three starts this year against Pittsburgh and 6-7 with a 4.67 ERA in 17 career games, including 14 starts, against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf pushed his ERA below 4.00 for the first time since May 13 after making his best outing of his young career in his last start. Ohlendorf pitched a career-high eight innings and struck out a career-high 11 in the outing, though he was denied a win because of no run support. The right-hander allowed just one unearned run. Simply put, things have just clicked for Ohlendorf since the All-Star break. He has a 2.70 ERA in the second half and has been benefiting tremendously from a much-improved slider.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino is coming off a pair of quality starts in which he lost both games because the Astros didn't score a run while he was in the game. He held the Cubs to four hits and two runs on a two-run homer to Derrek Lee in six innings Sept. 2 at Wrigley Field and gave up four hits and two runs on a pair of solo homers in six innings Tuesday against Atlanta. In his past two starts, he's allowed four earned runs and struck out 13 in 12 innings, but is riding a career-long four-game losing streak. In his only appearance against the Pirates this year, he pitched 1 2/3 innings in relief June 7 and allowed three hits, one run and struck out four.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm wasn't at his sharpest in his last start, but he battled well. His sinker has been more consistent over his past four outings than at times earlier in the season, which continues to be the biggest key for the left-hander. While Maholm still has an outside chance at reaching the 10-win mark before the end of the season, his primary objective over these next few weeks is just to find the consistency that will allow him to end the season on a high note. Maholm is 7-4 with a 4.44 ERA in 12 career starts against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Jon Garland starts for the Dodgers for the first time against a team other than his most recent employer. Garland, 1-0 in two starts against the D-backs since they traded him to the Dodgers at the Aug. 31 deadline, will try to stay unbeaten for his new club.
away_pitcher_note: Take away two misplaced pitches to Derrek Lee and McCutchen's outing really wasn't all that bad. Three of the four runs he allowed came on Lee's two first-pitch homers, one a misplaced fastball and the other a poorly located changeup. McCutchen, in just his second Major League start, finished seven innings in all, allowing nine hits and striking out five. He's a command pitcher who lives on his ability to establish his 90-93 mph fastball early and then use his changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf will return after missing one start because of a hyperextended left elbow suffered while swinging a bat in batting practice. Wolf is on a five-game win streak with quality starts in 13 of his past 14 outings. His .228 opponents batting average is seventh-lowest in the league. He's 7-1 lifetime against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: For the first time this season, Duke's ERA has climbed over 4.00. It was the result of a rough outing last Tuesday against the Cubs, who chased Duke from the start after scoring eight times in four innings. Duke had some bad luck with ground balls finding holes. But he was also up in the strikezone way too often to have any sustained success. That outing was the second time in Duke's last three starts that the left-hander wasn't able to pitch past the fourth. Duke is 1-3 with a 7.53 ERA in six career starts against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: In his second start back from a concussion, Kuroda stepped up with a masterpiece. He allowed three hits over eight innings, retiring 19 consecutive batters at one point and looked much like the prime-time starter he became down the stretch last season. He didn't have much of a splitter but didn't need it, relying on a sinker and cutter to shut down the Giants. Against the Pirates last year, he was 1-0 in two starts with a 2.08 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: There may still be the potential, but the Pirates have not seen what they were looking for when the club dealt for Hart at the Trade Deadline. With another six walks, a career-high, in his last start, Hart continues to have obvious problems with his command. Hart is 1-5 with a 6.46 ERA in seven starts since joining the club. He has walked 18 in 39 innings. Hart's only previous appearances against the Dodgers have come in relief. In 3 1/3 total innings against L.A., Hart has allowed one run on six hits.

home_pitcher_note: Morton had a decent start his most recent time out, though there still has been no sort of consistency shown from the right-hander this season. The movement on his pitches remains extremely intriguing. But with often minimal command of that movement, Morton has been hit quite hard. He has, however, made three quality starts in his past four outings after his disastrous start in Chicago on Aug. 14, when he allowed 10 runs in one inning. This will be Morton's second career start against the Padres. He won his first by allowing one run in 5 1/3 innings against San Diego last season.
away_pitcher_note: Another strong start for Stauffer, who lowered his ERA to 3.31 by allowing one run over six innings to the red-hot Rockies on Sept. 12. The right-hander took a shutout into the sixth inning before allowing a solo home run to Troy Tulowitzki. Stauffer, who has allowed three earned runs in his last three starts, spanning 19 1/3 innings, got 10 ground ball outs to overcome four walks. He also struck out three, but was at his best when he was able to get ahead in the count and get the Rockies to beat the ball into the ground.

home_pitcher_note: This could very well be Ohlendorf's last start of the season as he is about 10 innings away from the maximum innings count that the Pirates have set. The Pirates will surely miss Ohlendorf once he is shut town, as he has been the horse in the rotation since the All-Star Break. In his 10 starts since the break, Ohlendorf has a 3.00 ERA and has limited opponents to a .234 batting average. Ohlendorf is 1-0 with a 3.09 ERA in two career starts against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Richard got a no-decision in his last start against the Rockies on Sept. 13, allowing three runs on three hits and three walks in five innings. Richard, obtained in the July 31 deal with the White Sox for Jake Peavy, has shown that he can be wild in the strike zone at times. He's also shown the ability to get a lot of ground balls. Against the Rockies, he struck out eight, including the last five batters he faced. But manager Bud Black opted for a pinch-hitter in the bottom of the fifth inning as the Padres turned a 3-1 deficit into a 7-3 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm pitched phenomenally in his last start to break the Pirates out of a losing funk and earn his first win since Aug. 19. The lefty didn't allow a run in eight innings. Maholm, who has endured his fair share of ups and downs, has a chance to reach the 10-win mark if he can finish the season strong. The Pirates haven't had three 10-game winners on their staff since 2003. The key for Maholm continues to be how well he has a feel for his sinker pitch, which, when on, can be devastating.
away_pitcher_note: Correia made his team-high 30th start of the season against Arizona on Sept. 14 and pitched well, allowing a two-run single to the opposing pitcher, Billy Buckner, and little else. "Hanging slider," Correia said. "Those pitchers are tough sometimes. We knew he was a good hitter, but you don't get scouting reports on them. It was just a slider that stayed up." Correia didn't allow another run, as he struck out seven in 6 1/3 innings with two walks.

home_pitcher_note: McCutchen is still looking for his first Major League win after falling up short in each of his first three starts. As a pitcher who lives and dies off his command, McCutchen was bothered by an inability to get ahead in the count his last time out. He fell behind 15 of 23 hitters he faced and wasn't able to incorporate his changeup with much success because of the struggles with the fastball. McCutchen ended up allowing four runs in five innings and needed 84 pitches to get that deep into the game.
