away_pitcher_note: Another strong start for the left-hander LeBlanc, who has shined in three starts since being promoted from Triple-A Portland. LeBlanc, who allowed one run on three hits over six innings against Arizona on Sept. 15, didn't back down after he allowed a solo home run to Eric Byrnes in the third inning. He worked a scoreless sixth inning, getting Stephen Drew, Justin Upton and Montero in order to finish strong. LeBlanc, who has allowed three earned runs in 19 innings in three starts since returning from Triple-A Portland, has impressed his manager with the way he's aggressively gone after hitters. "It was more fastballs again. He located it and threw some [changeups]. It comes down to fastball command," Black said. "He had some funky swings against him."

home_pitcher_note: The bullpen blew what should have been an 11th win of the season for Duke in his start on Tuesday. The left-hander, who entered that start just 1-5 with a 6.81 ERA since the beginning of August, broke out of the funk with one of his more dominant starts of the season. Duke limited a hot-hitting Dodgers team to just two runs on four hits in 7 1/3 innings. He struck out 10. Duke is 3-4 with a 3.47 ERA in eight career outings against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto was scratched from Thursday's scheduled start against the Marlins due to flu-like  symptoms. Cueto will be making his 28th start of the season, fourth since being reinstated  from the disabled list on Aug. 31. Cueto was placed on the DL on Aug. 20 with inflammation in his right shoulder. His most recent start came on Sept. 12 against the Cubs at Wrigley Field. Cueto allowed three runs on four hits in 5 1/3 innings but was the victim of a blown save in the 7-5 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Though Hart couldn't snap a personal five-game losing streak in his last outing, he did make significant strides forward with his command and delivery adjustment. Hart allowed a two-run homer in the sixth, but otherwise kept the Dodgers off the scoreboard. After walking six in his previous start, Hart cut down that total to just one. Hart is nearing an innings mark where the Pirates will cut him off, but he will at least make this next scheduled start. Hart has made five previous appearances (two starts) in his career against the Reds. He is 1-1 with a 3.38 ERA in 16 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey pitched outstanding Friday against the Marlins, allowing just three hits in seven innings. He walked two and had eight strikeouts. The Reds bullpen, however, could not secure him a victory as Florida rallied for four runs in the ninth off closer Francisco Cordero and won 4-3, denying Bailey his sixth victory. It was Bailey's seventh quality start of the season and fourth in his past six outings. His eight strikeouts matched a career high. In six starts since August 23, Bailey is 3-1 with a 1.83 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Morton showed some improved command in his last start, a sign that maybe he's beginning to figure out how to use the movement he can get on his pitches to his benefit. The consistency of his command has been the biggest problem for Morton all season, but after allowing an early run and getting out of an early jam, Morton found just that against the Padres. He matched his career high with seven innings and has now allowed three or fewer runs in four of his past five starts. Morton is 1-1 with a 6.35 ERA in two previous starts against Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo was perfect through three innings Saturday against Florida, but a couple of costly mistakes led to a loss, most notably a changeup to pinch-hitter Ross Gload that resulted in a two-run home run in the eighth, which lifted the Marlins to a 3-2 victory. Arroyo allowed three runs on six hits. He walked one and struck out six but allowed two home runs. Despite the loss, Arroyo extended his streak of consecutive quality starts to 11.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens gets the nod to make the start in place of Ross Ohlendorf, who has been shut down for the season. Karstens has stretched his arm out some, but it's unlikely that he'll be able to go more than four innings at best since he has been in the bullpen for months. The Pirates plan to piggyback a handful of relievers to get through this game since they don't have a true starter available. Karstens is 0-1 in two appearances (one start) against the Dodgers. He allowed six runs (three earned) in 5 1/3 innings in those games.
away_pitcher_note: Garland has been a standout addition to the Dodgers' rotation since he was acquired from the Diamondbacks at the end of August. Garland is 3-0 with a 2.33 ERA in his four starts with the Dodgers, and his most recent outing against the Dodgers was his best of the bunch. Garland allowed one run in the first inning but then held the Giants scoreless en route to an eight-inning, one-run, seven-hit stat line. Garland is 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA in his career against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm wasn't at his best in his most recent outing, allowing nine hits (five for extra bases) and three walks in six innings. To his credit, though, only two earned runs scored. As it usually is when Maholm labors, the culprit was an elevated sinker. Maholm never found rhythm with the pitch, nor was he able to throw his breaking pitch for a strike. With two more starts remaining, Maholm is still gunning for a possible 10-win season. He is 0-3 with a 6.00 ERA in five career starts against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf might be on a short leash, having been yanked in his most recent start after allowing a single leading off the seventh inning. But he's also been the Dodgers' most consistent starter this year. The Dodgers are 21-11 in his starts and with six innings he surpassed 200 innings for the first time since 2003. He's 6-0 with a 2.41 ERA in his last eight starts, all quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: McCutchen hasn't been great in any of his four starts with the Pirates, though to his credit he hasn't been knocked out early either. He's still trying to get his footing in the Majors, which is likely a large reason why McCutchen still struggles in the early innings before settling in. He has allowed at least one homer in each of his four starts and admitted after his last outing to being a little anxious early.
away_pitcher_note: The Dodgers welcome the 21-year-old southpaw back into the rotation after losing him to a shoulder injury Sept. 6 when he collided with an outfield wall while shagging flies, two days after his most recent start. Coming off a 45-pitch simulated game Sept. 18 and two hitless innings of work on Sept. 22, they think he's ready to move back into what is, for now, a six-man rotation. But he'll likely be limited to 70 pitches in this first start back. A healthy Kershaw would be a virtual lock for one of the four spots in the postseason rotation so the Dodgers hope to get two starts from him before then. He leads the team's starters in ERA and strikeouts with 171 in 161 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Duke opened PNC Park in April and he'll close the Pirates' home schedule as well with this start. It's been a decent season for Duke, who has taken significant strides since last season, though his record does not reflect that. He has, however, hit a rut during these last two months and has gone 1-6 since the start of August. He's not getting hit all that hard, but with the Pirates' offense struggling mightily he has to be close to perfect these days to get a win. Duke is 1-3 with a 6.64 ERA in seven previous starts against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda continued to look strong in his comeback from a concussion sustained when he was hit in the head by a line drive. In his fourth start back and his first career start against Washington, he held the Nationals to just four hits and two unearned runs in six strong innings, walking two and fanning six, making a strong bid to stay in Dodgers manager Joe Torre's postseason rotation plans as he continues to try to figure out how to cut his six-man rotation to four.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster did not get a decision in his last start, but did post his seventh quality start in his last 11 outings. He has thrown six or more innings in 26 of his 29 starts. Dempster is trying to finish with 200 innings this year, and will make two more starts -- this one vs. the Pirates and in the season finale Oct. 4. His next win will be No. 87, and he would be the second active pitcher with 87 wins and 87 saves. John Smoltz has 213 wins and 154 saves.
away_pitcher_note: Hart did not look good in his last start, one in which he lasted just 4 1/3 innings and gave up eight runs on eight hits and three walks. It was a step backward for the righty, who, in his previous outing, finally found some consistency with his command and new delivery' motion. This time he pitched with hardly any fastball command and never found any rhythm with his slider. This might be Hart's last start of the season and it's one from which he'd like to salvage something positive. Since coming to the Pirates, he is 1-6 with a 6.93 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly was given a few extra days this week because of tendinitis in his left shoulder. He should've gotten the win in his last outing against the Cardinals. The lefty gave up two runs on five hits over 7 2/3 innings, striking out six. He did not walk a batter, the 10th start this year in which he has done that. Lilly did notch career strikeout No. 1,300, but he'd rather have the "W." The lefty was pulled in the eighth after throwing 110 pitches so he didn't have to face Albert Pujols. St. Louis won on a walk-off homer by Matt Holliday. Lilly has faced the Brewers once this year, July 5, and won.
away_pitcher_note: His line may not be overly impressive, but Morton actually pitched quite well his last time out. He allowed four runs on four two-out hits in the third inning, but otherwise dominated. Manager John Russell lauded Morton's improved aggressiveness afterward. Morton has seemed to find some control of the movement he has on his pitches, and the result of that is improved efficiency. This will be Morton's first start at Wrigley Field since a disastrous outing there in August when he allowed 10 runs in just one inning.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano was masterful in his last outing, throwing a two-hit shutout against the Giants, who were battling to stay alive in the NL Wild Card race. Zambrano fanned eight in his first shutout since his no-hitter last September 2008. Big Z gave up two singles, and he also drove in two runs. With a win against the Pirates, Zambrano has a chance to finish the season with double-digit wins for the seventh straight year. Zambrano now has made 237 starts for the Cubs, passing Dick Ellsworth for 13th on the team's all-time list.
away_pitcher_note: As he did on Friday, Karstens will lead a parade of bullpen arms to help the Pirates get through this game. The Pirates need Karstens to start in place of Ross Ohlendorf, who has been shut down because of a high innings total. The right-hander allowed one run on three hits in three innings of relief in his last spot start. The Pirates would ideally like to get four innings out of Karstens, with five innings being a bonus. He'll be followed by various relievers who can give the Pirates multiple innings.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Samardzija's third Major League start. In his last outing, Sept. 23 against Milwaukee, the right-hander took the loss, but pitched well. He gave up three runs on five hits over five innings and appeared to have better command of his pitches. It was a big improvement over his first big league start Aug. 12 against the Phillies, when he lasted 3 1/3 innings. Samardzija will be pitching in Mexico this winter to add a few innings.
away_pitcher_note: If it weren't for some stellar defensive plays made behind him on Saturday, Maholm's last start likely would have turned out much worse than it did. As it was, the lefty battled again without his bread-and-butter sinker and allowed three runs on seven hits and three walks. Maholm lost his chance at going for a 10-win season when the Pirates bullpen blew a save in the start, though he can salvage a .500 record with a win in this, his final start of the year. Maholm is 4-1 but with a 7.06 ERA in nine starts against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Lehr will fill in for Matt Maloney, who had to be replaced due to a blister on his left middle finger. Lehr is 1-1 with an 8.18 ERA in 11 innings over two starts against the Pirates this year. He's made five starts each at home and on the road this season, faring considerably better at Great American Ballpark. He's 2-0 with a 4.35 ERA at home, compared to 3-2 with a 6.67 ERA on the road.
away_pitcher_note: McCutchen made the best start of his young career in his last outing, though the right-hander is still looking for his first Major League win. Showing an aggressiveness and command of the strike zone that he did not have in his four previous starts, McCutchen limited Los Angeles to just two runs as he pitched into the seventh. And for the first time, he did not allow a home run in his start. McCutchen made his Major League debut in a start against the Reds back on Aug. 31. He allowed three runs on five hits and two walks in six innings. McCutchen, who did not factor in the decision, also struck out five.

home_pitcher_note: During a 3-2 loss to the Astros, Cueto gave up three earned runs and six hits over 7 1/3 innings with five walks and five strikeouts. One rough inning cost Cueto when he started the third by allowing back-to-back singles and a walk to load the bases. That led to a pair of runs and a 2-0 deficit.
away_pitcher_note: Duke was sensational in his last start, which was marred only by manager John Russell's questionable decision to remove the left-hander with one out left to get in the ninth. Duke allowed one run in those 8 2/3 innings and threw 74 of his 103 pitches for strikes against the National League's best hitting team. Duke has already set a career high in wins and now enters his last start of the season trying to get back-to-back victories for the first time since early June. Duke is 3-5 with a 3.93 ERA in nine starts against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Over seven superb innings, Bailey gave up one earned run on seven hits with one walk and seven strikeouts in his last outing. He also improved to 5-1 with a 1.89 ERA over his last eight starts. The most impressive moment came during a fifth inning, bases-loaded situation against Albert Pujols. He did a fine job of damage control when he got Pujols to hit a sacrifice fly and Matt Holliday to ground out to end the threat.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates had to scratch Kevin Hart from this outing because of a mild rib cage strain. That means Jeff Karstens will make his third spot start in the last two weeks. Karstens will be pitching on only three days' rest, but that isn't a large concern given that he only threw 61 pitches in his outing on Wednesday. He will likely only be able to give the Pirates three or four innings at most on Sunday, but with the number of relievers the Pirates have right now, it won't be a problem covering the rest of the outing for him.

summary: 2010-03-02 - State College of Florida, Manatee-Sarasota @ Pittsburgh Pirates (Completed Early)

home_pitcher_note: Happ has allowed six runs over 16 1/3 innings this Spring Training for a 3.31 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm, making his final start before the regular season, has allowed 19 hits and 11 runs -- nine earned -- this spring.

home_pitcher_note: For the second time in his career, Duke has earned the nod as an Opening Day starter. He first did so in 2007 and responded with seven strong innings, in which he allowed two runs in a no-decision. The left-hander will certainly be looking to emulate the start he had to last year's season. Duke posted a 2.43 ERA last April and followed with a 2.98 mark in May. Though he stumbled a bit at the end of the year, Duke doesn't believe his strong start to '09 was a fluke. The Pirates have said that they may be a little more cautious with Duke's early workload than they were last year, so that's something to keep an eye on as the season gets underway. The lefty is 2-3 with a 5.68 ERA in eight career starts against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: The surprise choice for Opening Day starter is Vicente Padilla, chosen as much for the way he stepped up late in the season, when the Dodgers took him off the scrap heap after his release by Texas, as anything. When he's right, he can be tough to hit, as he showed against the Cardinals and Phillies in the playoffs. He's admitted to some forearm tightness this spring, and he takes heat treatment before he pitches, not unusual for pitchers. He's 18-5 on the road over the past two seasons. This is his first Opening Day start, although he has won at least 14 games in four different seasons.

home_pitcher_note: At this time last season, Ohlendorf was in the process of establishing himself as a capable Major League starter. With that accomplished through his '09 results, Ohlendorf now takes his spot near the top of the Pirates' rotation. No one finished last season stronger than Ohlendorf, who posted a 2.43 ERA during his 11 post-All-Star Game starts. That ERA was almost two runs lower than it was in the first half of the season. Ohlendorf has really focused on developing his changeup this spring, but overall his Grapefruit League results weren't that good. Command was his biggest problem. This will be Ohlendorf's second career start against the Dodgers. His first lasted only three innings.
away_pitcher_note: It's still a bit puzzling why Joe Torre didn't select Clayton Kershaw as his Opening Day starter, as most opponents would say he's the one pitcher on the Dodgers team they don't want to face. After all, Torre had him start Game 1 of the NL Championship Series last year. You can't tell by his statistics that he just turned 22. Opposing batters hit .200 against Kershaw in 2009, lowest in the Major Leagues. His 2.79 ERA was fifth lowest in the league. Kershaw has dominating stuff, but he prefers to adhere to a regular routine and the juggling of starters coming into the season didn't allow that coming into this race.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm slots into the third spot in the Pirates' rotation because of the club's need to split up its two left-handed starters. The lefty may not have had the most dominant numbers of any Pittsburgh pitcher last season, but he has largely been a model of consistency over the past two years. He is at 100 percent health again, with no reason to be concerned that his left knee will bother him as it did at times in 2009. Maholm is still looking for his first career win over the Dodgers, however. Heading into the start, he is 0-3 with a 5.59 ERA in six starts against the Los Angeles club.
away_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley once was viewed as a potential ace of the staff. Eight months ago he was an All-Star. Now the Dodgers want to take the pressure off and get him back on track after he struggled down the stretch and was dropped from the rotation in the postseason. So far, so good in Spring Training, as he looks like he might have ironed out the mechanical flaw he believes set in motion his late-season fade. Scouts say Billingsley tends to overuse his cutter and it's taken a foot off his fastball. The Dodgers believe he's throwing as well as he did over the first half last season.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff earlier in the decade. He seems to be completely over any health issues and has a good feel for pitching and how to manage a game. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and change. Lopez appeared in seven games (five starts) for the Phillies last year and also started 18 games for Triple-A Lehigh Valley.
away_pitcher_note: Though Morton pitched much of the 2008 and 2009 seasons in the big leagues, he has never been on a Major League Opening Day roster until now. This is the start of a critical season for the right-hander, too. Everyone loves the movement on his pitches, but questions about Morton's mental fortitude remain. And the Pirates really need him to help stabilize the back end of the rotation. Morton's ERA last season is a bit deceptive and certainly skewed by a disastrous one-inning outing against the Cubs in which he gave up 10 runs. Take away that start and Morton posted a 3.90 ERA in 17 games. He is 1-0 with a 3.09 ERA in two previous starts against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Haren was dominant on Opening Day against the Padres as he allowed just three hits and one run over seven innings. Haren was aggressive in the strike zone as evidenced by throwing first-pitch strikes to 20 of the 24 hitters he faced. Haren only went to three balls on one of those 24 hitters. The lone run off him came in the seventh when Chase Headley singled home Adrian Gonzalez, who had doubled earlier in the inning. Since coming over to the D-backs in an eight-player deal with the A's in December 2007, Haren is 31-18. He throws a fastball, cut fastball, curve and split.
away_pitcher_note: Duke battled without his best stuff or command on Opening Day, but he battled admirably. After allowing two first-inning runs, Duke stranded six baserunners through the first five innings. Manager John Russell took a gamble pinch-hitting for Duke in the bottom of the fifth, and it paid off, solidifying a first career Opening Day win for the left-hander. Still, it meant that Duke's outing lasted only 79 pitches (54 strikes).  Though Duke wasn't at his sharpest on Monday, he continues to be one of the Pirates' best when it comes to efficiency and finding a way to pitch deep into a ballgame. Duke is 2-3 with a 5.09 ERA in six career starts against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson made his first start in an Arizona uniform on Tuesday night against the Padres at Chase Field. The Padres did a nice job of making him work hard and running up his pitch count. The right-hander threw 94 pitches in just five innings. Over that span he allowed five hits and three runs. He almost got out of a first-and-second jam in the second, but Evereth Cabrera laced a two-out, two-run double to left-center. Jackson was acquired by Arizona in a three-team trade during the Winter Meetings that sent Max Scherzer and Daniel Schlereth to the Tigers. The D-backs are his third team in three years. He pitched for Tampa Bay in 2008 before being dealt to the Tigers before last year. Jackson throws a fastball, curve, slider and change.
away_pitcher_note: McCutchen arrived at Spring Training dueling against Kevin Hart for the fifth start in the Pirates' rotation, and he won it with an impressive spring. More than anything, the Pirates love the way McCutchen is consistently around the strike zone, which was something Hart didn't show. This is the first time McCutchen has been on an Opening Day roster, but he did get a taste of the big leagues last year as a late-season callup. In six starts with Pittsburgh, McCutchen went 1-2 with a 4.21 ERA. He pitched at least six innings in all but one of those starts. He has never pitched against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Barry Zito hopes to continue establishing a new trend when he faces the Pittsburgh Pirates. Known for his subpar first-half pitching, Zito blanked Houston for six innings in his season debut last Tuesday. Zito typically performs well against Pittsburgh with little to show for it, having posted an 0-3 record with a 3.13 ERA in four starts against the Pirates. This will be Zito's first start of the season at AT&T Park, where he finished 6-6 with a 3.92 ERA last year.
away_pitcher_note: Burres has been called up from Triple-A Indianapolis to make an emergency start for Ross Ohlendorf, who has been scratched due to back spasms. Burres had already been scheduled to make his first start of the season on Monday. Though this will be Burres' debut for the Pirates, he has made 41 Major League starts, including two last season with the Blue Jays. The left-hander is 13-19 with a 5.85 ERA in those previous big league starts. This will be Burres' first career start against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Cain sustained a strong 6 2/3-inning effort in his 2010 debut last Wednesday at Houston, but surrendered three of the four runs he allowed in his final inning. The Giants scored six runs in the final two innings to win, 10-4, though Cain emerged with no decision. Cain didn't issue a walk, which reflects his annual goal of improving his control. Cain excelled against Pittsburgh last year, posting a 1-0 record with a 0.56 ERA in two starts. Since this is Cain's first start at AT&T Park this season, it's worth noting that he compiled identical 7-4 records home and away a year ago. His ERA was slightly lower at home (2.72, compared to 3.09 on the road).
away_pitcher_note: Despite allowing four runs in six innings, Maholm left the mound after his first start of the season feeling good about the big picture. Things finally clicked with his curveball and changeup after the lefty struggled with both pitches all spring. Maholm's outing largely came down to two unexecuted pitches, and he was kicking himself afterward about the pitch selection of both. In each case, Maholm said, he chose to throw a pitch that his mind told him not to. Maholm is 1-1 with a 2.85 ERA in six career starts against San Francisco.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez received the distinction of pitching the Giants' home opener last Friday and had decent stuff, striking out six in 4 1/3 innings. But he wasn't consistent with his fastball, which prevented him from getting ahead on the count to most hitters. That, in turn, shortened his outing, though San Francisco proceeded to outlast Atlanta, 5-4, in 13 innings. Sanchez did not face the Pirates last season and is 0-1 with a 14.04 ERA in four lifetime appearances against them.
away_pitcher_note: Morton said he learned a valuable lesson while being hit hard in his first start of the season Friday in Arizona: Don't be afraid to rely on the fastball to get ahead of hitters and gain the advantage. Morton did that while striking out five in the first two innings, then absorbed a six-run third in which four of the D-backs' six hits came either on the first pitch or when ahead in the count. The 26-year-old righty has fared well in three career starts against the Giants, holding them to five earned runs in 19 innings (2.37 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Duke had a fantastic sinker working in his last start and with a complimentary changeup also going for him, the D-backs could do little against the lefty. Wins were hard to come by for Duke last season, so getting off to a 2-0 start in the first week of the season sure has to feel good. Duke has so far looked like he belongs at the top of the Pirates' rotation, and in fact gave the team its first quality start with his seven-inning gem on Saturday. Duke has made 10 previous starts against the Reds, going 3-6 with a 4.37 ERA against the division rival.
away_pitcher_note: Leake's professional debut came at the Major League level and he did not disappoint. The 5-foot-10 right-hander gave up one earned run and four hits with five strikeouts in 6 1/3 innings. The only downside was the seven walks he allowed. As a batter, Leake also collected the first two hits of his big league career. He became the 21st drafted player since the Draft began in 1965 to bypass the Minor Leagues and go straight to the Majors. His cap from the game was donated to the Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown and the lineup card was autographed and given to the Reds Hall of Fame.

home_pitcher_note: Daniel McCutchen will make Saturday night's start against the Reds after being recalled from Triple-A Indianapolis earlier in the afternoon. McCutchen is stepping in for Ross Ohlendorf, who has now missed two scheduled starts because of back spasms. McCutchen, who opened the season in the Pirates' rotation, had a forgettable first of the season. He allowed nine earned runs on six hits and three walks in 3 1/3 innings against Arizona last Sunday. The right-hander made two starts against the Reds last season and allowed a combined four runs in 12 1/3 innings. McCutchen's only Major League win came against Cincinnati in his final start of 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto's first two starts were shortened by high pitch counts and one long inning. During a no-decision on Monday, won by the Reds over Florida in 10 innings, 6-5, Cueto threw 110 pitches in five innings and left with a 5-4 lead. He allowed four earned runs on nine hits with one walk and two strikeouts. There was a particularly rough 33-pitch bottom of the third inning, when Florida scored three runs that included four hits, a walk, a wild pitch and a balk.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm faced a patient Giants offense in his last start, which resulted in an elevated pitch count early. Maholm lasted just five innings as a result, but he battled admirably. The lefty made some critical pitches when he needed to in order to limit San Francisco to three runs and set the Pirates up for a late-inning win. Neither of Maholm's first two starts has been superb, but he's kept the club in both despite less-than-stellar stuff. He is also looking to maintain a more consistent arm slot moving forward. Maholm is plenty familiar with Cincinnati, which he has faced more often than any other team in his career. In 15 starts against the Reds, Maholm is 4-4 with a 4.04 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo did not figure in the decision during a 10-8 win over the Marlins in 11 innings on Tuesday. He gave up five earned runs and six hits with one walk and three strikeouts in six innings and was unable to take advantage of a 6-1 lead through four innings. Things got tough for Arroyo in the Marlins' fifth inning when he faced eight batters and allowed four runs. He lacked some zip on his fastball and dealt with the wind in his face much of the night. A bruised left calf, caused by a line drive in his first outing, was bothering him a little but Arroyo declined to make that an excuse for his lackluster night.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has not gotten off to the start he had envisioned. He was able to log six innings in his most recent start, but the six runs he allowed off three home runs cost Morton the chance to take a step forward. Pinpointing one problem with the right-hander is a bit hard. He has been hurt when behind in the count, so first-pitch strikes are definitely a must. His execution must also improve. Morton is going to rely heavily on a fastball-curveball mix, but too often those pitches are drifting back over the plate. Morton is 0-2 with a 2.77 ERA in two previous starts against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Dave Bush's turn would come up next when the Brewers open a three-game series at PNC Park on Tuesday, though manager Ken Macha won't announce his rotation for the series until Saturday. Bush is still searching for his first win of 2010, though he's coming off a no-decision in a decent enough outing at Chicago on Wednesday. He'll need to repeat his performance against the Cubs -- seven hits and no walks in six innings -- and he needs to remain around the plate. Against Chicago, Bush threw 56 of 77 pitches for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Zach Duke should be sitting on three wins right now if not for a poor night from the Pirates' bullpen after his last start. Duke threw 90 pitches in his last outing before being pulled after allowing a leadoff walk in the eighth. That runner eventually scored, as did another two, which took Duke out of line for the win. Regardless of his record, though, the Pirates have to like what they're seeing from the lefty so far. His sinker has been devastating, and Duke has had a nice changeup to go along with it. He's been pretty efficient and, to this point, the only reliable starter the Pirates have. In 13 career starts against the Brewers, Duke is 3-5 with a 5.38 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo may be the Brewers' staff ace, but he's still searching for consistency, not to mention his first 2010 victory. The right-hander thought he took a positive step forward in his last outing, on Friday, when he allowed two runs on six hits and four walks in six innings against Washington. For Gallardo to succeed, the Brewers need the strikeout artist who 204 hitters in 184 2/3 innings last year, not the guy who's given up a home run in each of his three outings and walked eight hitters in 15 innings. Gallardo, however, believes he's on the verge of becoming his old self. To do that, he'll have to avoid big innings, keep the ball inside PNC Park and attack the Pirates hitters.

home_pitcher_note: McCutchen is guaranteed at least one more start with Ross Ohlendorf on the mend from back spasms. However, McCutchen is going to soon have to start proving that he belongs in the rotation to stay. He has combined for just 7 1/3 innings in his first two starts of the year, with 12 runs scoring against him. Granted, the results were much improved his last time out -- four innings, three earned runs, four hits, three walks -- but they aren't good enough for what the Pirates need from a fifth starter in their rotation. Surprisingly, control and efficiency have been issues for McCutchen, who has always been known to be a strike thrower. This will be McCutchen's first career appearance against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: There's not a lot of mystery when it comes to what Wolf needs to do to be successful. When the veteran southpaw commands his fastball, pounding the strike zone and challenging and getting ahead opposing hitters, he gives his team a chance to win. When he doesn't, Wolf falls behind hitters, goes deeper than he wants to into counts and gives the advantage to the hitter. Fastball command was the issue in Wolf's last start, on Saturday in Washington, where he lasted only five innings, throwing 100 pitches. There's significant pressure on Wolf to start justifying Milwaukee's investment of $29.75 million for a three-year free-agent contract this past offseason, but there's also ample time for Wolf to turn his first season with the Brewers around.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt has quality starts in each of his first three outings of the season, allowing 17 hits and striking out 17 batters in 19 innings. He lost his first two decisions before throwing seven scoreless innings Saturday in Chicago to beat the Cubs and move past Larry Dierker into second place on the club's all-time wins list with 138. He's six shy of tying Joe Niekro for first. Oswalt is 13-7 with a 2.62 ERA in 26 career games against the Pirates, including 25 starts. He lost his only start against them last year, giving up nine hits and six runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm found an effective mix of fastballs, curves and sliders his last time out on the way to sealing his first win of the season. The lefty was also able to finish 6 2/3 innings, which was longer than either of his previous two starts had lasted. It's rare when Maholm isn't able to keep his team in the game with a quality start, and the Pirates need that consistency given some of the struggles in the rest of the rotation. The other good news is that the left-hander continues to pitch with good health, a benefit that he did not enjoy through all of 2009. Maholm is 8-4 with a 4.01 ERA in 13 career starts against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez, who led the Astros in wins last year with a career-high 14, is searching for his first this season. He lost his first two starts to the Giants and Cardinals but regrouped and pitched well against the Cubs on Sunday at Wrigley Field. He went seven innings and allowed two runs on six hits, striking out three batters and getting a no-decision.  Rodriguez is 4-4 with a 4.60 ERA in 11 career starts against the Pirates. He faced them twice last year and was 1-1 with a 3.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: It looks like Jakubauskas will get the call from Triple-A to make the spot start for the Pirates on Saturday. The right-hander has made two Minor League starts this season and was kept from making his next scheduled one on Thursday to get him ready for Saturday. In 10 innings, Jakubauskas has allowed five earned runs on 10 hits. He's walked four and struck out eight. Jakubauskas has Major League experience, all of that coming last season with the Mariners. In 35 appearances (eight starts) with Seattle last year, Jakubauskas went 6-7 with a 5.32 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Myers is still searching for his first win with the Astros. He's pitched into the sixth inning in all three starts this year and threw seven innings in his previous two starts, April 14 at St. Louis and April 20 against Florida. In those two games, he allowed 12 hits, six runs (five earned) and struck out nine batters in 14 innings. Myers has made eight career appearances against the Pirates, including seven starts, and is 3-4 with a 2.64 ERA. He's allowed 41 hits and struck out 42 in 47 2/3 innings. He last faced Pittsburgh in 2008, going 1-1 with a 3.55 ERA in two starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates continue to rave about Morton's potential, but potential has not come close to translating into results for the right-hander this season. An already bad start to the season got worse for Morton on Tuesday, when he was pulled after allowing the first five hitters in the second inning to reach base. Morton was charged with six runs (five earned) on six hits and three walks in one inning. He pegged a lack of aggressiveness as the main problem afterward, and it's obvious that Morton needs to trust his fastball more than he has so far. More bad news for Morton: He is winless with a 7.88 ERA in three previous starts against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: It's a rematch of Wednesday at PNC Park, where Gallardo was not his sharpest but nonetheless pitched five scoreless innings in the fourth double-digit strikeout game of his career. The first inning was a harbinger of Gallardo's night, when he needed 26 pitches to get through five batters despite the fact that none of them put a ball in play. Gallardo walked two of them and struck out the other three. In all, he notched 10 strikeouts and earned his first win this season. He improved to 4-2 against the Pirates with a 2.66 ERA in nine games, including eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Duke will get another shot at the Brewers, who knocked him around in his last start. Duke's first three outings of the year were strong, but he worked behind in the count too often in his last start and that hurt him. Duke served up three homers and walked four while allowing six earned runs in five innings. His usual bread-and-butter sinker was also not so sharp. The Pirates are pretty confident this was just a hiccup for Duke, who has been the staff's most reliable pitcher since the start of 2009. Still, he hasn't beaten the Brewers since 2006 and has a career 5.73 ERA against Milwaukee (14 starts).

home_pitcher_note: Last time out, Wolf benefited from the Brewers' historic offensive performance, as they put up 20 runs against the Pirates at PNC Park. Lost in all the offense for Milwaukee was the fact that Wolf had his best outing as a Brewer. The lefty pitched six strong innings, scattering six hits, and did not allow a run. For good measure, Wolf added a pair of hits and scored twice in three at-bats. Thanks in part to Wolf's strong performance, the Brewers notched the first 20-0 result in Major League Baseball since 1900 and the largest margin of victory in a shutout in club history.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' need for a spot starter leads them back to Triple-A, where this time the club will pluck Karstens. Though Karstens started the 2009 season in the Pirates' rotation, the organization had him lined up to be a reliever this season. All the fluctuation in the big-league rotation, though, forced Karstens into Indianapolis' rotation recently. He has made five appearances (one start) so far this season. In 16 innings, the right-hander has allowed 13 earned runs on 21 hits. He's walked two and struck out five.

home_pitcher_note: After two poor outings by veteran right-hander Jeff Suppan to begin the season, Narveson will be given his shot at the fifth-starter role on Wednesday against the Pirates. Narveson gets the opportunity based on his performance last September and in Spring Training this year, Brewers manager Ken Macha said. In five Cactus League games, Narveson pitched 13 scoreless innings, allowing 10 hits. Last season, Narveson went 2-0 with a 3.83 ERA in 21 games (four starts) with Milwaukee, including a 1-0 record with a 3.38 ERA as a starter. He was named Brewers Pitcher of the Month for September/October last season after finishing the season 1-0 with a 2.73 ERA in 29 2/3 innings over his final nine appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm hasn't necessarily added to the Pirates' starting pitching woes, but he hasn't been dominant to this point either. Maholm gave the Pirates a much-needed seven-inning start on Friday, though he took the lost by giving up four earned runs on seven hits. Maholm has lasted at least six innings in three of his four starts this year, which is particularly significant given the burden the bullpen has carried so far this year. The Pirates will continue to rely on the lefty to pitch deep and keep any deficits manageable. Maholm is 3-5 with a 4.58 ERA in 14 career starts against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw put on an escape act in Washington in his last start. He allowed eight hits and three walks in six innings, wiggling out of enough jams for the Nationals to strand eight runners, six in scoring position. The 18 walks in 23 innings are a troublesome sign for the left-hander, but he is keeping his club in the game as the Dodgers were able to pull out a win from his last start in the 13th inning. Kershaw didn't make it out of the fifth inning in his first start of the season in Pittsburgh, but after the first three batters scored on Garrett Jones' first-inning homer, he didn't allow a run.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates have named Burres their spot starter for Thursday. The Pirates continue to try to bridge the gap to Ross Ohlendorf's return to the rotation, and they are hopeful that Burres can get the job done. Burres was called up on Sunday to provide reinforcement to an overworked bullpen and pitched 1 2/3 innings in Sunday's game. He allowed two earned runs on three hits and three walks in that outing. This is already Burres' second stint with the big league club this season. He allowed six runs on eight hits in a four-inning start against the Giants on April 12. Burres has never faced the Dodgers before.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley came up with the rebound effort the Dodgers were counting on after the serious meeting he had with manager Joe Torre and pitching coach Rick Honeycutt in the wake of his three-inning start in Cincinnati. Sticking with just a fastball and curve, Billingsley said he tried to simplify his pitching approach and the hardball style really suited him, as he shook off a first-inning run and allowed the Nationals nothing further in six innings. It was the closest Billingsley has looked to the first-half All-Star he was a year ago.
away_pitcher_note: Morton has been nothing close to the reliable arm that the Pirates expected to have this season. He has not pitched a full four innings in three of his four outings and has allowed at least five runs per start. Morton has had a hard time pinpointing the issues, too. In some cases, pitch selection has been a problem. In other starts, it's been fastball command or a hesitancy to be aggressive enough with his fastball. You have to wonder if the terrible season start is starting to have an effect on Morton's mental fortitude, particularly given his lack of big league experience.  This will be Morton's first career appearance against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Rookie reliever Carlos Monasterios is scheduled to make his starting debut. Monasterios has six strikeouts and three walks in 10 2/3 innings over seven appearances, although he's allowed the only two runners he's inherited to score and hasn't been relied on in magnified spots. Manager Joe Torre said he hoped Monasterios could throw 70 to 75 pitches. If Monasterios struggles, Ramon Ortiz (0-1, 6.39 ERA), who was also a candidate to start the game, could work in long relief.
away_pitcher_note: Command has been a serious issue for Duke in his last two starts, both of which were losses to Milwaukee. Typically efficient and in the strike zone, Duke walked eight in nine total innings against the Brewers. His last outing lasted a season-short four innings. And altogether, Duke has allowed 15 runs in his last nine innings. For Duke to get back on track, it will start with getting ahead in counts and regaining dominance with his sinker. Duke was sharp early in the season, so the hope is that this two-game stretch has been nothing more than a hiccup. He is 3-3 with a 5.50 ERA in nine career starts against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda has been the most consistent starter in the Dodgers' rotation this year, an interesting achievement after one month, considering that he was coming off an injury-plagued season that relegated him to fourth on the depth chart at the start of the year. He's proven to be healthy and effective so far. In his latest start against the Mets last week, he delivered another quality outing of six innings with two runs allowed and pitched out of two jams, but the Dodgers scored nothing against Johan Santana in support of Kuroda. He's 2-1 with a 2.74 ERA in four career starts against the Pirates and 1-0 with a 3.00 ERA in two starts against Pittsburgh at home.
away_pitcher_note: Called up from Triple-A to plug a rotation vacancy, Karstens is here to stay for the time being. His 6 2/3-inning outing on Tuesday was enough to earn Karstens another start for a Pirates team that has been looking for anyone to seize the opportunity to claim a rotation spot. Karstens allowed just two hits and never labored much in the 101-pitch effort against the Brewers. The start came after he moved from a relief role to a starting one in Triple-A because that club was running out of starting options.

home_pitcher_note: The common theme throughout Maholm's five starts this year has been the left-hander's ability to battle. He has yet to give the Pirates a dominant start, though neither has Maholm struggled enough to keep the team out of striking distance. In a season where Pittsburgh starters have struggled immensely, Maholm's ability to go at least six innings in all but one of his starts has been huge. Maholm has been the Pirates' most consistent starter since the start of 2008. Though Maholm is 4-1 in nine career appearances against the Cubs, Maholm's ERA versus Chicago is 7.06.
away_pitcher_note: It may be better for Dempster to be on the road. So far, the right-hander is 1-0 with a 1.32 ERA in two road starts compared to 1-1 with a 3.68 ERA in three games at Wrigley Field. In his last outing at home against the Nationals, Dempster took the loss as he served up three runs on four hits over eight innings. Two of those hits were home runs. Last year against the Pirates, he was 2-0 with a 4.66 ERA in three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Morton's last outing was certainly a step in the right direction, though the right-hander remains winless in five starts this season. He allowed six runs (three earned) in six innings last Friday in what was just his second start to go past the four-inning mark this year. Morton has to start keeping balls in the park -- he has allowed seven homers in 19 innings -- and he has to continue to stay aggressive and trust his abilities if Morton is going to turn things around. His numbers obviously haven't been good, but the Pirates don't have the starting pitching depth to replace him in the rotation. Morton is 1-2 with a 10.22 ERA in three career starts against the Cubs. That ERA is bloated, however, by the one-inning start last August in which he gave up 10 earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: In Lilly's last start, some of the D-backs players said it seemed as if the lefty's velocity was down. It was only his second start since coming off the disabled list and Lou Piniella said he expects the velocity to improve as Lilly builds up arm strength. In that last start, Lilly gave up six runs on seven hits over five innings. He didn't look as sharp as he did in his season debut on April 24 against the Brewers, when Lilly threw six scoreless innings. Last year, Lilly was 1-2 with a 3.60 ERA in three starts against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: This will be the last time the Pirates need to find someone to fill Ross Ohlendorf's spot in the rotation, and left-hander Brian Burres gets the call. Burres stepped into Ohlendorf's vacant rotation spot last Thursday and provided the Pirates with 5 1/3 scoreless innings. Burres wasn't dominant in the outing, but he made quality pitches when he needed to. In his previous start, Burres was knocked around for six earned runs in just four innings.  Burres' only previous appearance against the Cubs came in relief. In that outing, the left-hander allowed one run on three hits in an inning of work.
away_pitcher_note: Wells is coming off a win over the D-backs in which the right-hander gave up five runs on eight hits over six-plus innings. He has not walked a batter in his last two starts, both wins, while striking out 14 in that stretch. In his last start, Wells said he was forced to make some pitches he didn't want to because of the wind at Wrigley. It was blowing out at 18 mph during the game. "I made some mistakes and they made me pay," said Wells, who served up one home run. So far, he's posted better numbers away from Wrigley, compiling a 1.42 ERA in three road starts compared to a 6.57 ERA in two games at home.

home_pitcher_note: Duke has lost each of his past three starts, none of which have been reminiscent of his first three this season. After allowing five earned runs in his first three starts, Duke has given up 18 earned runs in his last 15 outings. His start on Saturday was a step forward -- there were more first-pitch strikes and better overall fastball command -- but Duke isn't as consistently sharp as he needs to be. He hung a slider that Andre Ethier sent over the wall for a three-run homer, and Duke skirted out of other trouble all night. Duke is 4-5 with a 3.73 ERA in 13 career starts against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter will look to stay unbeaten in his seventh start this season. In his six previous starts, Carpenter has been extremely consistent with four victories and two no-decisions. In 38 innings, Carpenter has only allowed 27 hits and 15 runs (12 earned). He has struck out 39 and walked 13, good for an impressive 3-to-1 ratio. A 17-game winner last season, Carpenter has continued to pitch well in 2010 thanks to terrific control. Plus, he has been locating all of his pitches with very few mistakes. That has added up to a terrific month of April and early May for the veteran right-hander.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens remains the fifth starter for now, though the rotation spot is likely to remain in flux from week to week. After a strong start against Milwaukee, Karstens came out a bit flat in his outing against Milwaukee on Sunday. Too many balls were elevated, and Karstens gave up six runs and 11 hits in five innings. The Pirates aren't expecting great things from the right-hander -- who is in the rotation largely because of a lack of other options -- but they would love to see Karstens provide some stability in the back of the rotation if he can. Karstens allowed three runs in six innings and took the loss in his only previous start against St. Louis.

Maholm picked up his second win of the season in a gutsy start against the Cubs on Tuesday. It was clear Maholm was having issues with his sinker from the start as Chicago teed off and hit a number of deep fly balls. But only two went out of the park -- both were solo shots -- and Maholm otherwise kept the Cubs off the scoreboard. As has become expected from the Pirates' most consistent pitcher, Maholm found a way to make the big pitches when he needed to most. He has given the Pirates at least six innings in five of his six starts, which is more than any other pitcher on the staff can say. In 10 career starts against St. Louis, Maholm is 3-3 with a 3.09 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals wasted a signature outing by Wainwright in a 2-1, 10-inning loss to the Phillies on Wednesday. Wainwright received a no-decision, allowing one run, four hits and two walks in eight innings. Wainwright, entered the game with a 2.13 ERA that shrank to 1.96.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf pitched four shutout innings for Double-A Altoona on Wednesday night in a rehab start. Ohlendorf, who has been sidelined with back spasms since his April 7 start, threw 59 pitches (41 strikes) in the outing. He gave up three hits, one walk and struck out six. Wednesday's outing marked Ohlendorf's second Minor League rehab start. His first came in extended spring training last Friday.
away_pitcher_note: In a 5-4 loss where he got a no decision against the Mets on Tuesday, Arroyo pitched well for seven innings but was trailing by a 4-2 score when he exited. He allowed four earned runs on seven hits with two walks and three strikeouts. Against the Pirates at PNC Park on April 18, Arroyo and the Reds were 5-3 losers. A five-run bottom of the fourth inning was all Pittsburgh needed to derail an otherwise well-pitched game by Arroyo.

home_pitcher_note: After opening the season with five straight losses, Morton finally put things together last Wednesday and walked away with win No. 1. Morton pitched into the seventh for the first time this season and refused to let one bad inning snowball into a terrible one. The two runs he allowed both came in the fourth. Otherwise, four of Morton's six innings were of the 1-2-3 variety. And he needed more than 12 pitches only in the fourth. Morton's success hinged largely on his focus to maintain an aggressiveness from start to finish. In three career starts against the Reds, Morton is 1-2 with a 5.89 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto is starting to show improvement over his last couple of starts and will try to keep moving forward. Being prone to an extended inning is still his main shortcoming. During Wednesday's 5-4 Reds win in extra innings, Cueto pitched six innings for a no-decision and gave up three earned runs and seven hits with two walks and a season-high eight strikeouts. But there was a 36-pitch top of the third inning where he walked .162 hitter Alex Cora to force home a run. "In all reality that's two innings," manager Dusty Baker said. "Instead of him going six, he could have gone seven or eight." However, Baker has been very impressed lately with Cueto's dedication to conditioning and running and believes it will pay off.

home_pitcher_note: Duke's last start was marred by two errors behind him, which led to three unearned runs. Those would be the only runs that would score while Duke was on the mound in his 6 1/3-inning performance. Duke struck out a season-high seven and even kept nemesis Albert Pujols off the bases. Though Duke wasn't rewarded with a win, it was a step forward for the left-hander, who hadn't pitched into the seventh since April 16. Duke rediscovered his fastball command and did a much better job of executing his sinker. Duke allowed one run in seven innings against the Reds back in April. He is 3-6 with a 4.04 ERA in 11 career starts against Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey is coming off one of his poorer outings of the season -- a 14-7 Reds loss to the Cubs on Friday. In his four-plus innings, he was charged with seven earned runs with five hits and five walks. In that short amount of time, he threw 94 pitches. Bailey did a pretty good job of throwing strike one but lacked finishing pitches and couldn't get the outs. "I just couldn't put them away," Bailey said. "Before you know it, you're 3-2."

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny took the loss in his last start against the Reds, giving up three runs on nine hits over six innings. The final score was 14-2, as the Reds took advantage of two Cubs errors. Gorzelanny now has four quality starts and one win to show for it. He'll be facing his former team for the third time in his career. So far, the lefty is 1-1 with a 1.69 ERA against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Burres' last start earned him the opportunity to make another. The Pirates had to open up a spot in the rotation for Ross Ohlendorf, but Burres turned out to not be the one to give up that spot. The left-hander has pitched 12 1/3 combined scoreless innings in his last two starts - both Pirates wins -- after stepping into the rotation as a spot starter. Burres will continue to have to prove that he deserves to keep the rotation spot, though one bad start won't necessarily mean he's gone. Burres' last start -- which spanned seven scoreless innings -- came against the Cubs, who he is now slated to face again.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster was vying for his fifth straight quality start in his last outing against the Reds. He'd thrown 111 pitches over 6 1/3 innings and had a one-run lead. But Joey Votto hit his 112th pitch for a three-run homer and Dempster took the loss. He struck out seven over seven innings. Dempster faced the Pirates May 4 in Pittsburgh and lost, but didn't get much run support.
away_pitcher_note: The Maholm that showed up on Sunday was certainly not the Maholm that the Pirates are accustomed to seeing. In what was his shortest start since September 2007, Maholm was chased after just 3 1/3 innings. He had problems locating his sinker down, and those were only further exacerbated by a 54-pitch fourth inning. Maholm, who started off the afternoon with two clean innings, never found his command again. Still, the Pirates have no reason not to expect Maholm to bounce back. He had gone at least six innings in six of his other seven starts this year and has been as consistent a starter as the club has had these last few seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly was cruising through the first five innings of his last start against the Marlins and did not give up a hit until Chris Coghlan doubled with one out in the sixth. There's one other pitch Lilly would like to have back and that was the first one to Ronny Paulino with a man on and one out in the seventh. Paulino homered to help lead Florida to a 4-2 win. Lilly struck out one in seven innings and looked better than he did in his two previous outings.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf threw four innings in his return off the disabled list last Monday in what was viewed as a very successful return. After missing just over a month of action, Ohlendorf allowed one earned run on three hits and four walks in the outing. He did need 84 pitches to get that deep in the game, but part of that can be attributed to rustiness. Too, the game wasn't so much about results as it was Ohlendorf's ability to get through an outing healthy. The Pirates are hopeful that his return will better stabilize the rotation, and he shouldn't be on any sort of a pitch count in this next start.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed four runs in six innings in his last start last week against the Rockies. It wasn't great. It wasn't bad. But he kept the Phillies close. He had suffered four bad starts and two good starts to start the season. This one was somewhere in the middle, so maybe it is a sign that Kendrick can be a little more consistent on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Morton's last start was another encouraging one for the right-hander even though it ended up in the loss column. Morton continues to appear back on the right track now with two consecutive quality starts. He's pitching aggressively and not falling victim to big innings as he was earlier in the season. Two solid starts in a row should also be a boost mentally for Morton, who has talked about that mental side often being the hardest to overcome. Morton is 0-1 with a 7.88 ERA in two career starts against Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay grinded through 6 1/3 innings Wednesday in a loss to the Rockies at Coors Field. Phillies manager Charlie Manuel said Halladay had difficulty gripping the ball, although Halladay wouldn't use it as an excuse. But after he allowed a two-run double to Brad Hawpe to tie the game, Manuel pulled him. He had thrown 121 pitches. Manuel would have liked to pitch Halladay longer, but he knows he needs him later in the season, too.
away_pitcher_note: Duke's fastball command left him again on Wednesday, and as has become the story of his season, he couldn't pitch through it. The left-hander lasted just five innings and gave up five runs in a loss to the Reds. He remains winless since April 10, when Duke moved to 2-0 to start the season. Half of his eight starts haven't gone more than five innings, and Duke has shown that if he doesn't have a sinker to rely on, he can't be all that effective. Duke is 1-3 with a 4.78 ERA in four career starts against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Burres had a 13 scoreless innings streak snapped his last time out and labored through his four-inning start. The left-hander scattered seven hits and allowed six runs (five earned) in what was his fourth start with Pittsburgh. To this point, only two of those starts have extended past the fourth inning. Burres' spot in the rotation is by no means secure. The club is likely to give him at least one more chance to prove that he belongs in the rotation, but the leash probably won't be much longer. Burres' only previous appearance against the Brewers came in relief. He allowed two runs on three hits in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf minced no words after his last start, a loss to the Phillies in which he surrendered six runs in five innings. "It's kind of embarrassing the way I pitched," Wolf said. "I couldn't execute anything. I was behind everybody. ... There's no excuses other than I was terrible today." He's allowed at least one home run in each of his past four starts and has had trouble with left-handed hitters. Last year with the Dodgers, he limited left-handed batters to a .159 average and surrendered only four extra-base hits in 185 plate appearances. This year, left-handers are batting .302 against Wolf, with 10 extra-base hits in 60 plate appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm wasn't sensational, but he got the job done his last time out. Despite allowing a number of deep fly-ball outs, the left-hander worked his way through six innings, limiting the Cubs to two runs on eight hits. He struck out four and didn't walk a batter. Maholm's season has been very much up and down, though he's still managed to pitch at least six innings in six of his eight starts. Maholm allowed four runs on seven hits in seven innings against the Brewers back on April 28. He is 3-5 with a 4.63 ERA in 15 career starts against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers considered giving Narveson an extra day's rest after he threw 130 pitches in Saturday's loss to the Phillies, the most pitches for any Major League pitcher this season. Narveson was given extra treatment and conditioning before being cleared to make his scheduled start on Thursday. Narveson had allowed only two runs on Saturday, but was already nearing 110 pitches when he went out for the sixth inning and surrendered a two-run homer to Shane Victorino. When he struck Chase Utley with pitch No. 130, Macha was forced to tap the bullpen. Before Saturday, Narveson had topped 100 pitches once in eight big league starts.

home_pitcher_note: The bullpen took away what should have been Ohlendorf's first win of the season on Sunday. Ohlendorf was quite efficient, needing only 69 pitches to get through six innings. However, manager John Russell pulled the right-hander when he issued a four-pitch walk to lead off the seventh. Ohlendorf said he could have gone longer, but the six-inning start was still the longest of his three this year. He limited Chicago to one run on four hits and three walks. Ohlendorf allowed three runs on eight hits in six innings against the Braves last year in his first career start against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: The month of May couldn't be going much better for Hudson. The right-hander has accumulated three wins with a dominating 1.63 ERA in 27 2/3 innings. In his most recent effort on Sunday against the D-backs, the 34-year-old produced a pitching masterpiece, allowing one run and three hits while striking out six. After walking six batters against Washington on May 11, Hudson maintained his control on Sunday afternoon -- surrendering just one base on balls. Even Hudson's bat has been sizzling more than usual lately. In May, Hudson has been hitting .364, (4-for-11), with two doubles.

home_pitcher_note: Just as Morton looked to be finding a groove, the right-hander took a step back in his outing on Monday. Yes, he was pitching against a potent Phillies lineup in a hitter-friendly park, but that doesn't excuse Morton from still serving up too many hittable pitches. The right-hander continues to have a hard time getting out of jams and has been prone to giving up a big inning in most of his losses this year. Half of his eight starts have now ended in four or fewer innings. Morton, who was drafted by the Braves in 2002, will be making his second career start against his former team. His first, which came last June, lasted just one inning due to a tight hamstring.
away_pitcher_note: With Lowe no longer relying as much on his sinker, the quality starts are beginning to pile up. In his last two starts, the 36-year-old has pitched 13 innings with a 3.46 ERA. During his first seven, he worked 38 innings with a 6.46 ERA. But after surrendering seven runs in five innings during a May 8 start against Philadelphia, the righty knew he needed to switch up his pitching. He completed an effective six innings of two-run ball in his next start against Milwaukee and followed that with three runs in seven innings against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Duke shook off a six-game winless streak to pick up his third of the season in a solid six-inning effort against the Phillies on Tuesday. Pitching against one of the league's more formidable lineups and in one of the more hitter-friendly parks, Duke limited Philadelphia to one run and came up with some big pitches when he needed to late in his outing. The left-hander found his sinker to be a reliable pitch throughout the night and likely would have pitched deeper if he hadn't needed 45 pitches to get through the fifth and sixth. Duke is 2-3 with a 4.43 ERA in seven career starts against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Medlen's matchup with Johan Santana on Tuesday may have looked like a mismatch on paper, but the 24-year-old righty more than held his own, completing 6 1/3 innings of two-run, two-hit ball. Although Medlen has started just two games this season as a fill-in starter for the injured Jair Jurrjens -- who will be out until late June -- he has continued to excel in his transition from the bullpen. Manager Bobby Cox has been cautious while stretching Medlen out, as he hurled 88 pitches against the Phillies on May 8 before throwing 90 on Tuesday night. Still, even in limited action -- including his time as a reliever -- Medlen hasn't surrendered more than two runs in an outing this year.

home_pitcher_note: The Reds are 2-7 in Harang's starts as their Opening Day pitcher has struggled most of the season. He gave up three runs in the first inning at Atlanta on Wednesday and only escaped another loss when the Reds rallied to tie the game in the ninth inning before losing, 5-4. Harang allowed eight hits and four earned runs in six innings, striking out four and walking one. It was the fifth straight start ij which he pitched at least six innings, and he went 2-2 in those starts. He was 0-3 with an 8.31 ERA in his first four starts. Harang hasn't faced the Pirates this season.
away_pitcher_note: Burres bounced back from a rough four-inning outing in Chicago to limit the Brewers to three runs off seven hits Wednesday at PNC Park in just his fifth start and ninth appearance of the season, a 6-4 Pirates win. The southpaw connected for strikes on 55 of his 74 pitches over six innings, keeping his fastball low and retiring eight of the first 10 batters he faced. Jeff Clement pinch-hit for him with the bases loaded in sixth, marking a no-decision for Burres. The 29-year-old tossed a perfect ninth in the Pirates' 9-0 home loss to the Reds on May 11, the only time he has faced Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Leake, the seventh overall pick in the First-Year Player Draft a year ago, is bidding to become the first Reds pitcher to start his career 5-0 as a starter since Santo Alcala did it in 1976. It looked like Leake would get his fifth victory Thursday in Atlanta. But the Reds couldn't hold a six-run lead in the ninth inning, losing on a pinch-hit grand slam. The former Arizona State standout allowed one earned run and five hits over six innings, striking out six and walking one. He also had two hits, including a double, and is batting .353. Leake didn't pitch in the first series against the Pirates this season, but has gone at least six innings in all eight of his starts. Only once has he allowed more than three runs.
away_pitcher_note: Despite feeling the best he has all season, Maholm was saddled with a 4-3 loss to the Brewers in his last start on May 20. Maholm could not hold an early three-run lead and lost his rhythm after a 40-minute delay due to an injury to umpire John Hirschbeck. Maholm allowed four runs on four hits and recorded a season-high seven strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo has not lost a decision since April 23 at San Diego and is 4-0 with a 3.22 ERA in his last five starts. He's won three starts in a row, beginning with a May 10 win against Ross Ohlendorf and the Pirates. In that outing, the right-hander pitched seven scoreless innings before allowing a solo home run in the eighth -- the only blemish in a 2-1 Reds win. After beginning his career in Pittsburgh and spending three seasons there, Arroyo has posted a 5-4 record with a 3.34 ERA against his former club.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf got hit hard early Friday by the Braves. Making just his fifth start of the season after missing a month with back spasms, the right-hander was knocked out in the fourth after surrendering an RBI double to Jason Heyward off the right-field wall at PNC Park that gave Atlanta a six-run lead en route to a 7-0 win. Heyward took Ohlendorf deep for a two-run homer an inning earlier, with both hits coming off sliders. The outing -- which lasted just 3 2/3 innings -- lifted Ohlendorf's ERA from 3.00 to 5.30. The 27-year-old is 1-1 with a 3.78 ERA in three career starts against the Reds, the most recent of which came May 10 at PNC Park, a 2-1 Cincinnati win.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto's last time out against the Pirates resulted in the best start of his young career. He allowed just one hit and tossed his first complete game and first shutout in a 9-0 win on May 11 in Pittsburgh. He struck out eight and walked none, finishing with 102 pitches. He is now 4-0 in his last five starts with a 2.18 ERA. However, after allowing two runs in six innings in his last outing on Saturday in Cleveland, he left after 93 pitches because of a blister on his right index finger. The blister is not expected to impact his start.
away_pitcher_note: Morton's record took a beating in Pittsburgh's 4-2 home loss to Atlanta Saturday, but he lowered his ERA from 9.68 to 8.71 after settling down in the fourth through sixth innings. He faced the minimum three batters in each of those frames after surrendering three runs (two earned) in the first three innings, putting behind a rough outing in Philadelphia that saw him give up six earned runs over four innings in a 12-2 loss. Morton has made quality starts in four of his last five outings, going exactly six innings in each despite picking up the win just once. The third of those starts came in a May 11 home loss to the Reds, when he gave up three earned runs off seven hits while striking out four and walking two. Morton is 1-3 with a 5.55 ERA in four career starts against Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Three weeks ago, on May 7, Lowe surrendered more runs in a game than he had since Aug. 18 of last season. The righty sinkerballer conceded seven runs and 11 hits against the Phillies and decided it was time for a change in his pitching approach. Since then, in his past three starts, the 36-year-old has averaged six innings, five hits surrendered and an overall ERA of 3.50.  Lowe is still struggling at times with high pitch counts -- throwing 99 pitches in five innings during his latest outing against the Pirates -- and has yet to complete more than seven innings in a start this season.
away_pitcher_note: Duke had another terrific outing Sunday, giving up no earned runs over seven innings while striking out five and walking none in the Pirates' 3-2, 10-inning win over the Braves. That came on the heels of going stride-for-stride with Roy Halladay in a win over Philadelphia. Over his past two outings, the southpaw is 1-1 with a 0.69 ERA. Duke is 1-0 lifetime with a 4.00 ERA in four starts at Turner Field, though his most recent outing in Atlanta, last June 8, did not go smoothly. The 27-year-old was taken deep three times, giving up six earned runs on 11 hits and getting the no-decision in a 7-6 Pittsburgh loss.

home_pitcher_note: Making just his third start of the season Sunday in Pittsburgh, Medlen pitched strongly before running into trouble in the sixth inning, giving up two earned runs and walking away with a no-decision in the Braves' 3-2, 10-inning loss. Medlen struck out two and walked none, giving up seven hits and hitting one batter. The right-hander got the win in relief against the Pirates last June 8 at Turner Field, tossing three shutout innings and allowing just one hit while striking out three. The 24-year-old is 1-0 with a 2.08 ERA against the Pirates in his two career starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Burres' wildness caught up to him against the Reds on Monday, when he allowed four walks, five hits and five runs (four earned) in a 7-5 loss at Cincinnati. On the season, he's struck out 23 and walked 21 -- not a great ratio -- and his ineffectiveness led him to walk the first two batters of what would become a five-run inning that knocked him out of the game in the fourth. Afterward, Burres said he lost the feel of the ball, and, considering he was doing all he could just to get the ball across the plate, he knew he was in trouble with his first pitch of the fourth inning.

home_pitcher_note: After another misfortunate start against the Marlins on May 25, Kenshin Kawakami became the first Braves starter to lose his first seven decisions to start a season since 1985. Recently, however, it's been more tough luck than anything. Against the Diamondbacks on May 14 and against the Marlins on Tuesday, the righty was afforded little run support. And in his best chance for a win, against the Reds on May 19, the Braves bullpen faltered. The 34-year-old has an ERA of 3.31 in his past three starts and hasn't surrendered more than five runs in an outing this year.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Maholm was fantastic, allowing just six hits and no runs in seven innings against the Reds in a game the Pirates eventually won, 2-1. Maholm left with the lead, but Pittsburgh's bullpen couldn't hold it and he got the no-decision. Afterward, he called himself effectively wild, but he was also efficient, tallying 89 pitches in seven innings. Against the Braves, Maholm has performed quite well in his career. He's only 1-1 in four starts, but he's allowed only four runs in 27 innings (a 1.33 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Since Ohlendorf has been back from the disabled list at the beginning of May, he's had mixed results. He's coming off a solid performance Wednesday vs. Cincinnati when he allowed three runs on eight hits in six innings but took the loss, and against Chicago on May 16, he pitched six innings and gave up four hits and two runs. But he's also had a couple of rough outings as well. Ohlendorf hasn't won a decision this calendar year (0-3 in the regular season and 0-3 in Spring Training), so he'll look for a change of pace vs. the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note:
Wells threw 16 pitches to six batters in the first inning of his last start on Friday against 
the Cardinals and was pulled before he retired anyone. All six Redbirds got hits. It was an 
"embarrassing" outing, Wells said. He was assigned to the bullpen on Saturday as a backup. So far, he's 1-2 with a 6.00 ERA at home and 2-1 with a 3.68 ERA on the road. He faced the 
Pirates on May 6, and was roughed up, giving up seven runs (six earned) on five hits in two 
innings. Pittsburgh scored five runs in the first.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens, who has made six appearances in long relief this year, will be making just his fourth start of the season after Charlie Morton was placed on the 15-day disabled list Friday with right shoulder fatigue. The right-hander's last start came in Milwaukee on April 27, when he gave up two earned runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings while striking out four and walking four. He recorded a no-decision in the Pirates' 7-3 win. Karstens has made four career appearances against the Cubs, starting three times and going 2-1 with a 5.06 ERA. He has given up nine earned runs off 19 hits in those four games while striking out eight and walking six.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly threw seven shutout innings in his last start against the Dodgers, giving up three hits and striking out five. But he did not get a decision as the lefty exited when the game was tied. The Dodgers felt Lilly tried to get an edge by positioning himself in front of the rubber a little bit and even asked the first-base umpire about it. But no fine was levied and there was no penalty. Expect the umpires -- and the Pirates -- to watch Lilly's footwork very closely in this game.

home_pitcher_note: Duke has lost five of his past six decisions after winning his first two, with the Pirates giving him little run support. He allowed just one earned run in his previous two starts, getting a win and a no-decision, before allowing 12 hits and seven runs over 5 1/3 innings in a loss Friday in Atlanta. Although Duke is 1-2 at home, he has a 3.57 ERA in his six starts at PNC Park this year, and he is the all-time wins leader there with a 27-26 record. Duke will be facing the Cubs for the first time this season. He has allowed 85 hits in 63 2/3 innings, including seven homers, while striking out 40 and walking 23.
away_pitcher_note:
This will be Zambrano's first start since April 20. The right-hander moved to the bullpen to 
make room in the rotation for Ted Lilly and also to give the team a potent setup pitcher. He was effective until May 14 against the Pirates, when he gave up three runs on four hits over one inning. Zambrano then said he wasn't comfortable in the role and wanted to go back to the rotation. Since that game against the Pirates, he has given up one hit over 4 1/3 scoreless innings. Big Z tuned up with a 73-pitch simulated game last Monday. In four starts, Zambrano was 1-2 with a 7.45 ERA.
