He's made 13 relief outings, including Saturday, when he needed just two pitches to get a double play and end the eighth against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Duke has lost five of his past six decisions after winning his first two, with the Pirates giving him little run support. He allowed just one earned run in his previous two starts, getting a win and a no-decision, before allowing 12 hits and seven runs over 5 1/3 innings in a loss Friday in Atlanta. Although Duke is 1-2 at home, he has a 3.57 ERA in his six starts at PNC Park this year, and he is the all-time wins leader there with a 27-26 record. Duke will be facing the Cubs for the first time this season. He has allowed 85 hits in 63 2/3 innings, including seven homers, while striking out 40 and walking 23.
away_pitcher_note: A high pitch count limited Sanchez to only five innings in his last outing against Arizona, but the left-hander still was effective. Sanchez allowed just two hits -- one a solo home run -- and struck out seven. After struggling against Pittsburgh the first four times of his career, Sanchez turned in a gem of an outing against the Pirates his last time out. On April 14, Sanchez tossed eight innings of shutout ball, holding the Bucs to three hits while striking out a career-high 11.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm was effective on Sunday in Atlanta, limiting the Braves to just two earned runs on 10 hits while striking out five and walking three. He left after six, trailing 2-0 before the Pirates' comeback went for naught in a 5-2 loss. Maholm's first start of the year came in San Francisco, when he gave up three earned runs on eight hits over five innings while walking three and striking out three. He took a no-decision in the 6-5 Pittsburgh win. In seven career starts against the Giants, Maholm is 1-1 with a 3.13 ERA, giving up 16 earned runs and 44 hits over 46 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer pitched well in his past two starts, earning the win on Tuesday against Washington and giving up only two runs in his last outing against the D-backs, a no-decision. Of course, Wellemeyer's success in those outings should come as no surprise. Both came at AT&T Park, where the right-hander has shined this season. If history is any case, however, the stars certainly do not appear to align with him for his next outing. Wellemeyer is going on the road -- where he is 0-3 with a 9.35 ERA this season -- to PNC Park, where he is 0-2 with a 6.95 ERA in eight career outings (four starts).

home_pitcher_note: Relying more on his changeup against a struggling Cubs lineup on Memorial Day, Ohlendorf pitched his best game of the season, going for season highs of 103 pitches and 67 strikes over seven innings of one-run, three-hit ball. Ohlendorf also stuck out a season-high six batters while walking a season-low two. A defensive gaffe in the outfield eventually resulted in Chicago's lone run and ruined Ohlendorf's shot at his first win of the season in the 2-1 Pirates win. The outing marked his second consecutive quality start, though the first went for naught with the Pittsburgh bats lifeless in a 4-0 loss at Cincinnati May 26. The right-hander now appears fully recovered from the back spasms that kept him out for more than a month after his first start of the season, April 7. Ohlendorf's seventh start of the season will mark the first time in his young career that he has faced the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: The uncharacteristic struggles of Lincecum continued in his last start, a highly anticipated duel between Colorado's Ubaldo Jimenez, as the right-hander was saddled with his second consecutive loss. Lincecum failed to make it out of the sixth inning for the third straight outing, throwing 121 pitches (73 strikes) in 5 2/3 innings. He allowed four runs (thee earned) on six hits, and also walked five batters (two intentionally) for the fourth consecutive game. Lincecum has faced Pittsburgh three times in his career, posting a 1-1 record with 2.86 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: A rainout between these two clubs Wednesday forced them to play on an off-day, and the Pirates are taking it as an opportunity to start the newly acquired Eveland without mixing up the rotation too much. Eveland threw two innings in an extended Spring Training game Thursday in Bradenton, Fla., and will look to erase any lingering memory of his last three starts with the Blue Jays, when he went just a combined 9 1/3 innings, giving up 17 earned runs off 23 hits while walking 10 and striking out just five. Eveland has pitched just 2 2/3 innings in three appearances against the Cubs, giving up two runs on two hits while striking out three and walking two.
away_pitcher_note: Silva is 7-0 in 10 starts for the Cubs after a win over the Cardinals on Saturday. He's the first pitcher in Cubs history to go 7-0 (or better) in his first 10 starts for the team.  The last Major League player to do that for any team was CC Sabathia for the Brewers in 2008 (8-0). Silva is coming off a win over the Cardinals in which he threw seven shutout innings, giving up two hits and striking out a career-high 11 batters.

home_pitcher_note: The Nationals have decided that Strasburg will make his Major League debut on June 8 against the Pirates -- provided that a rainout or injury doesn't stand in the way. Strasburg, 21, will become the fourth first-round Draft pick -- third baseman Ryan Zimmerman and pitchers Ross Detwiler and Drew Storen are the others -- in Nationals history to reach the big leagues. Strasburg, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2009 First-Year Player Draft, has been dominant in the Minors, going a combined 8-2 with a 1.30 ERA and 65 strikeouts in 55 1/3 innings for Double-A Harrisburg and Triple-A Syracuse.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens is the man called upon to face the highly touted Stephen Strasburg in the rookie's debut, though Wednesday's rainout against the Cubs made this more a matter of circumstance, since Zach Duke's start was pushed back to Friday. Regardless, Karstens hopes to be up for the challenge, though he has struggled against Washington in the past. In three appearances (one start) against the Nationals, Karstens has a no-decision and a 9.35 ERA over 8 2/3 innings pitched. He has given up nine runs on 15 hits while striking out six and walking three. But Pirates manager John Russell mentioned Karstens' performances in pressure situations when announcing him for Tuesday, citing his April 27 outing against the Brewers, when he pitched 6 2/3 innings and gave up just two earned runs to help the Pirates snap a 22-game skid at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: The last thing Lannan was seen throwing was a shaving-cream pie in the face of Stephen Strasburg, during the postgame interviews following Strasburg's debut on Tuesday night. There might be fewer people in the stands and fewer laptops in the press box, but Lannan is the one who will try to give the Nationals their back-to-back wins since May 22-23, when they took two straight Interleague games from the Orioles. After a rough start to the season, Lannan has seen his ERA steadily shrink from 6.51 to 4.79 across his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates promoted Lincoln to make his MLB debut. The Bucs' first pick -- and the fourth selection overall -- in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, the 25-year-old Texan right-hander sat out the 2007 season following Tommy John surgery. Lincoln is 6-2 with a 3.16 ERA in 11 starts for Triple-A Indianapolis this season. He has a 55-14 strikeout-to-walk ratio in 68 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: This past Friday, Hernandez gave the Nationals another quality start by allowing just two runs in his six innings against the Reds. He has not win a game in more than a month. His last victory came in on May 4 against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: The long ball did in Duke in his last outing, when the southpaw gave up three home runs in a two-inning span to take the 6-4 loss. He gave up 10 hits and struck out five, and he has not won a game since out-dueling Philadelphia's Roy Halladay in a 2-1 win on May 18. Duke has given up 10 home runs on the season. In four career starts against the Nationals, Duke is 1-1 with a 5.11 ERA, giving up 29 hits in 24 2/3 innings while striking out eight and walking 11. His last start in Washington came May 1, 2008, when he recorded a no-decision in a seven-inning performance. He gave up two runs off five hits in a 3-2 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander will welcome the Pirates for Game 1 of a three-game series that kicks off a nine-game homestand of Interleague Play for the Tigers. Verlander is fresh off his sixth victory of the season, in which he pitched seven-plus innings and allowed only five hits and two earned runs as the Tigers beat the Royals, 4-2. Interleague Play has been kind to Verlander. In 13 career starts, he is 9-1 with a 2.90 ERA to go along with 89 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Another stellar outing once again did not result in a win for Ohlendorf, who was aided by tremendous fielding in his last outing, a 6-5, 10-inning home loss to the Giants on Sunday. Ohlendorf went six innings, giving up three runs on eight hits while striking out two and walking three. He added a single off Tim Lincecum in the fifth. In two career appearances (one start) against the Tigers, Ohlendorf is 1-0 with a 0.96 ERA, having surrendered just one run on three hits in 9 1/3 innings. The right-hander has stuck out seven and walked just three.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman is coming off a rough outing against the Royals in which he picked up his fourth loss of the season. Coming into his last start, Bonderman had only given up four runs in his last 21 innings, but that all changed against the Royals. Bonderman was hit hard for five runs in the first two innings and ended up giving up seven on the day. He lasted 5 2/3 innings, while giving up 11 hits with a walk and two strikeouts. Bonderman will look to rebound against the Pirates in game two of a three-game series. Bonderman is 7-7 in 21 starts in Interleague Play with a 5.38 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Make it three quality starts in a row for Maholm, who continues to be the Pirates' steadiest rotation presence. The left-hander picked up his team-leading fourth win on Saturday with a strong 6 1/3-inning performance in which he kept the Giants to six hits and two runs. Maholm seems to have found better efficiency as of late, too, evidenced by the mere 86 pitches he needed in his last start. Maholm has pitched at least six innings in 10 of his 12 starts this year as well.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga will be making his first start at Comerica Park since his bid for a perfect game a week and a half earlier set up a surge of national publicity and made him a name in Detroit. He got back to some sense of normalcy in his last start Tuesday at Chicago, where he gave up two runs over five innings against the White Sox. The Tigers aren't expecting complete games from him, let alone perfect games, but the more innings they can get out of him, the better. He owns a 4-3 record and 5.12 ERA in nine career Interleague starts but was roughed up was four runs on eight hits in two innings against the Pirates last June in Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens put up a good effort on Tuesday, especially considering it came in one of the most hyped games (Stephen Strasburg's debut) in recent memory. Karstens actually took a lead into the sixth inning, before two Washington home runs sunk him. Still, the outing earned Karstens a stay in the Pirates' rotation for the time being. The right-hander has been a fairly stable presence in the Pirates' rotation when called upon to start this season. As a starter, Karstens is 1-2 with a 4.40 ERA in five games. He has, however, allowed six home runs in 28 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lincoln will make his home debut in this game, as the Pirates open up the home portion of their Interleague schedule. The former first-round pick made his Major League debut on Wednesday and allowed five earned runs on seven hits and two walks in six innings. Though his line didn't stand out, the performance was largely viewed as a success. Lincoln effectively used his changeup, which was a pitch he really focused on developing in Triple-A earlier this season. With what Lincoln has done in the Minors over the past two years, he's given the Pirates no reason not to believe that he won't make the rotation better.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia continued his run of quality starts, notching his seventh in eight tries, this time against the Detroit Tigers. He went seven innings and gave up solo home runs to Brennan Boesch and Miguel Cabrera. Of his seven quality starts, two have come against the Tigers, and the rest have come against the likes of the Rays, Yankees, Twins and Rangers. Garcia danced in and out of trouble in the game, allowing two hits in three different innings, but only allowing three runs on the evening. Lifetime against the Pirates, Garcia is 2-0 with 12 innings in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: After being the team's most consistent starter during the first half of 2009, Duke cannot seem to find that key to consistency this year. Duke has won just once in his last 11 games and has been pegged with the loss in each of his last three starts. His problems largely stem from one bad inning, and Duke has yet to be able to rely on his best pitch -- the sinker -- to get him out of jams consistently. The good news is that Duke does seem to have a string of good innings (even dominance) in most of his starts. Now, if he can keep from hitting a wall in the middle innings, he'd be on the right track. Duke is 0-1 with a 4.95 ERA in three career starts against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: John Danks pitched extremely well in his last start, allowing only a single hit to the Detroit Tigers en rout to earning his fifth victory of the season. The southpaw rebounded from a disastrous past two starts, in which he gave up 12 earned runs in just 9 1/3 innings. Danks did not allow a runner into scoring position in the entirety of his seven innings pitched. He also fanned four and walked four. Danks has not started a game against the Pirates in his career, but in all Interleague games, he is 3-2 with a 2.58 ERA in 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Though Ohlendorf gave up six runs in six innings his last time out, there were some positives to be cited afterward. The velocity on the right-hander's fastball and slider were both up. He also had a pretty effective sinker working for him most of the night. That was the good news. On the other end, Ohlendorf remains winless in eight season starts and struggled to close innings out in his last start. All six runs scored against him came with two down, and it was mostly a result of leaving pitches up. Ohlendorf still hasn't found the type of groove he did late last season. He is 0-1 with a 7.45 ERA in two career appearances (one start) against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander bounced back from consecutive rough starts against Texas and Cleveland at U.S. Cellular Field by shutting out the Cubs over 6 2/3 innings during Saturday's 2-1 victory at Wrigley Field. Buehrle struck out a season-high seven, his biggest total since Sept. 5, 2008 against the Angels, and didn't issue a walk. He also allowed no earned runs for the fourth time this season, after accomplishing the same feat just five times in 2009. Buehrle is tied with Mike Mussina for the all-time Interleague victory lead at 21.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm made a bunch of critical pitches with runners on base in his last outing, and he managed to get himself out of almost every jam. Though Detroit had runners swarming the bases all throughout Maholm's six-inning, 104-pitch effort, the left-hander allowed just one run and stranded eight. There's no question that Maholm has been the Pirates' best pitcher this season. He's gone at least six innings in all but two of his 13 starts. And five of his last six starts have been quality ones. The Pirates are 7-6 when Maholm starts, which is better than the team's record with any other starter. Maholm allowed one run in 5 1/3 innings against the Indians in a start against Cleveland in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona fired his fifth career complete game Saturday night, yielding one run on three hits and facing just one batter over the minimum in the Indians' 7-1 victory against the Nationals at Progressive Field. The 26-year-old right-hander struck out seven and did not walk a batter in his 106-pitch outing. He has logged 10 quality starts in 13 outings this season, allowing three or fewer earned runs in all but two appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens deserved to win his second game of the year on Sunday after making his strongest performance to date this season. Through seven innings, he limited Detroit to one solo homer and three singles. He was charged with one more run after giving up a leadoff hit in the eighth, but that would be it. The key for Karstens was terrific fastball command. That helped him through the outing even though he had trouble throwing his breaking pitches for strikes. Karstens has become a pretty stable presence in the rotation, and he'll likely stay in it as long as he continues to give Pittsburgh these types of starts. Karstens pitched 1 1/3 scoreless innings against Cleveland in a relief appearance last year.
away_pitcher_note: Huff worked five solid innings of two-run ball Sunday before coming undone in his matchup against Stephen Strasburg. The Nationals tagged Huff for four runs in the sixth, sending the 25-year-old left-hander to his seventh loss in eight decisions. He scattered six hits over 5 2/3 innings with three walks and four strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Lincoln has two Major League starts under his belt and is still looking for that first big league win. He has finished six innings in each of his first two appearances, allowing five runs in both. Lincoln showed his last time out that he still has things left to learn. He fell behind too often and didn't always pick the right place to throw his breaking ball. All three of the walks Lincoln issued came back to hurt him. Still, the Pirates love his mentality and competitiveness, and that should carry him through this learning curve.
away_pitcher_note: The Mets tagged Masterson for seven runs on 10 hits over seven innings Tuesday in the Indians' 7-6 loss at Progressive Field. The 25-year-old right-hander yielded just one extra-base hit but was done in by three Tribe errors, one of which came in a five-run fifth for the Mets. Masterson walked two and struck out two in the 104-pitch outing.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter won his first two starts but had to come out of his last start against the Marlins on Wednesday when he strained his right hip flexor. The Rangers don't think it's serious and they still expect Hunter to make that start. He pitched 2 1/3 innings against the Marlins. Hunter started the season on the disabled list and had to make six starts at Triple-A Oklahoma City. He is 11-8 with a 4.81 ERA in 25 Major League starts over the past three seasons, including 8-4 with a 3.87 ERA in 14 starts at the Ballpark. This will be his first start ever against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Now nine starts into the season, Ohlendorf is still in search of that first season win. His outings haven't been terrible, but they've certainly not been up to par with what the Pirates were expecting out of the right-hander at the start of the year. He's been average, at best, and continues to struggle pitching out of the stretch. Batters are hitting .310 off of him with runners on base, compared to .243 in the same situations last year. In his last start, Ohlendorf was especially plagued by command issues with his breaking pitches. The Austin, Texas, native will be making his first career appearance against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Nippert will be making his second start. He was called out of the bullpen after 22 relief appearances when Derek Holland and Rich Harden went on the disabled list. The Rangers could also go with Matt Harrison, but Nippert made the last start in this spot, pitching three innings and giving up three runs on Thursday against the Marlins. He is now 6-8 with a 5.81 ERA in 22 career Major League starts. He is 6-6 with a 5.25 ERA in 82 relief appearances. He has a career 4.53 ERA at the Ballpark in Arlington.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm was charged with four runs his last time out, though his performance was much more dominant than that would suggest. The left-hander breezed through six scoreless innings before an array of singles just squeaked through during a four-run seventh. Still, with the Pirates' offense struggling, it was enough to send Maholm to his first loss since May 20. He continues to be the most consistent starter Pittsburgh has, having gone at least six innings in his past seven starts. The loss snapped a streak of four straight quality starts, too. This will be Maholm's first career start against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman is 3-1 with a 3.71 ERA in four starts in June after going 1-3 with a 6.97 ERA in five starts in May. He won his last start by holding the Astros to three runs in seven innings in a 9-3 victory on Friday in Houston. He is now 3-1 with a 3.44 ERA in six starts against National League teams over the past two years. He is 2-2 with a 4.58 ERA in seven starts at home this season. Opponents are hitting .300 off him.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens would like just one pitch back from his last start. Until allowing a three-run homer to Austin Kearns in the sixth, Karstens was rolling through Cleveland's batting order with ease. Kearns would be the last hitter Karstens faced in his 5 1/3-inning effort. The fact that he threw just 68 pitches is evidence of how efficient he was before getting into some sixth-inning trouble. Karstens has now made four straight starts and appears to be sticking in the rotation for the time being. He continues to consistently give the Pirates a chance to win, and has come up with some big performances when the Pirates needed it most. This will be Karstens' first career appearance against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets has struggled since the calendar turned to June, losing all four of his starts in the month. In his latest outing on Saturday in St. Louis, Sheets gave up four earned runs on four walks and six hits while striking out two over seven innings. He hasn't earned a victory since defeating Tampa Bay on May 8. Like the rest of his teammates, Sheets has fared much better at home this season. He's 2-2 with a 2.79 ERA in seven home starts in 2010, compared to 0-5 with a 6.95 ERA in eight road outings. In 22 career starts against the Pirates, the 31-year-old righty is 8-8 with a 2.92 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lincoln will get a fourth crack at his first Major League win in this start. He hasn't had a terrific outing yet, but he's had three suitable ones. Lincoln has pitched six innings in all of his starts since being called up, and he did so last time after enduring a 32-pitch first. Lincoln's fastball command was a bit shaky against the Indians on Sunday, but he is showing more aggressiveness, perhaps a sign that he's not giving hitters too much credit anymore. The key now for Lincoln is to be able to preserve leads when they're given to him. This will be Lincoln's first career appearance against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old right-hander is making his case to become an All-Star in his second big league season. Cahill has won his last five decisions and hasn't lost since May 16 against the Angels. His 3.21 ERA is the lowest among current A's starters. In his last outing on Sunday in St. Louis, Cahill went six innings, allowing two earned runs on four hits. He struck out seven batters to set a new season high and tie his career high. Sunday's start marked the second time all season that he hadn't walked a batter. Cahill is 3-0 with a 1.75 ERA in four home starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: His 2010 line with the Pirates isn't pretty -- 0-2, 13.50 ERA in three starts and four appearances -- but there's a belief he's improved lately in Indianapolis. He's 4-5 with a 3.86 ERA in 10 starts at Triple-A, and even though his last start on June 21 was a loss, he still went seven innings and allowed two earned runs. McCutchen has never pitched in an interleague game. His last appearance with the Pirates was one inning of scoreless relief April 24. He was optioned to Triple-A the next day.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez threw a gem in his latest start against the Reds in Oakland on Monday, but the bullpen faltered down the stretch in a 6-4 loss. Gonzalez threw seven innings, allowing an unearned run on four hits and a walk while striking out a season-high nine. Gonzalez said they key to his success was trusting his curveball and changeup, which he threw for strikes all night. In seven home starts this season, Gonzalez is 4-2 with a 2.47 ERA. Gonzalez has been particularly tough on lefties this season, limiting them to a .145 batting average, while righties are hitting .261 off him.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf remains winless through 10 starts this season, largely hurt by one or two big innings per outing. The right-hander continues to feel uncomfortable pitching out of the stretch, which explains why he is having issues closing out innings with runners on base. Opponents are also having remarkable success against him as the game progresses. Ohlendorf has held opponents to a .203 batting average his first time through the order. The second and third times through the order, opponents are batting .341. Ohlendorf has made one previous appearance against Oakland, that coming in 2008. Ohlendorf pitched 1 2/3 innings in relief and allowed one earned run on two hits and three walks.

home_pitcher_note: Wells is looking for his first win since April 30. The right-hander is coming off a loss to Seattle in which he gave up six runs on 10 hits over six innings. He has gone winless in May and June, serving up 20 earned runs in 61 1/3 innings in those two months so far. He's 0-1 in two starts against the Pirates, including a loss May 6 when he gave up six earned runs on five hits in two innings.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm would like to forget absolutely everything from his last outing, one which lasted a career-short one inning. The left-hander was missing with all his pitches, and when he wasn't walking hitters, the pitches were right down the middle. He faced just 15 hitters. Four of them walked and seven got hits. Still, the outing was an anomaly for Maholm, who has been the Pirates' most consistent starter all year. Prior to Wednesday, he hadn't allowed more than four runs in any of his first 14 starts this year. Maholm is 6-1 with a 6.29 ERA in 11 career starts against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a decision in his last start June 24 against the Mariners. He gave up one run on five hits over six innings. He has only one win in his last 11 starts. The lefty is 0-2 with a 4.35 ERA in three games against the Pirates this season.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens battled through 5 1/3 innings in his last start, but was denied a third win when the Pirates' bullpen couldn't a two-run lead. Karstens wasn't lights out, but given that he was facing baseball's hottest team at the time, he did well in limiting Texas to two earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny will replace Carlos Zambrano in the Cubs rotation. Gorzelanny began the season in the rotation but was moved when Zambrano didn't like his relief role. Gorzelanny has made six relief appearances, including last Friday when he went 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lincoln's outing Friday was his fourth start of the season. His performance -- six innings, three earned runs, eight hits -- was similar to his others and only lowered his ERA from 6.50 to 6.00. Lincoln threw 107 pitches, 63 of them for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: McCutchen is plugging the rotation vacancy left by Zach Duke. The righty remains winless this year and has only pitched past the fourth in one of four starts. His rotation spot remains tenuous, and unless he dazzles, he's likely to go back to Triple-A when Duke returns.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels had his worst start in nearly a year on Saturday against the Blue Jays, allowing six runs in five innings, including three homers, against the team that leads the Majors in homers. But Hamels has pitched well since April. He hopes to get back on track.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf hasn't won in 11 starts this year, though he did not allow an earned run in his last outing. If Ohlendorf can pitch better out of the stretch and avoid being plagued by the big innings, he should be on his way to a victory soon.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer became just the 40th pitcher in baseball history to throw 4,000 or more innings in a career in his last start Sunday against the Jays. He also allowed the 506th homer of his career, an all-time record.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday, Maholm became the first Pittsburgh starter to finish eight innings this season, and he did it bouncing back from a career-worst one-inning start. Maholm's sinker and changeup in the game were as good as the pitches have been for the lefty at any point this year.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick is 1-1 with a 6.04 ERA in his last four starts. J.A. Happ is getting closer to rejoining the team, so Kendrick will need to show something Saturday to convince the Phillies to keep him in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: A pair of two-out solo homers stung Karstens in his last outing, but the right-hander continues to be a reliable piece of Pittsburgh's rotation. He has allowed two earned runs or fewer in six of his nine starts and has pitched into the sixth all but once.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton is showing signs of improvement. He is 2-0 with a 3.80 ERA in his last three starts after carrying a 1-5 record and a 7.28 ERA through his first eight starts. Blanton credits a mechanical adjustments for the improvement.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez won his second consecutive start after losing six of his previous seven decisions. He pitched seven innings and gave up just one run. Rodriguez also executed a suicide squeeze to give the Astros a 2-1 lead over the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: It took Lincoln five starts, but he doesn't have to worry about getting that first big-league win any longer. And if Lincoln pitches with as nasty a curve as he did Wednesday, there are a lot more coming. The key for Lincoln is not to be hesitant to attack the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler was in line for his second consecutive win after allowing one run in 5 2/3 innings on Thursday in San Diego, but the Padres rallied against the Houston bullpen to send the game into extra innings.
away_pitcher_note: McCutchen gave up just one earned run in his last outing on Thursday against the Phillies. He got ahead of 12 of the 23 batters he faced, earning his first win of the season, his first since last Oct. 2.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt retired the first 11 batters he faced on Friday in San Diego en route to tossing seven scoreless innings, but his counterpart, Mat Latos, did Oswalt one better with eight shutout frames.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf recorded his first win of the season Friday by shutting down the Phillies for seven innings. The right-hander struck out eight and flashed command of his fastball that hadn't been seen all season. Ohlendorf has lost both starts of his career at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: On the disabled list since May 16 due to inflammation of the lining around his heart, Davis is finally making his return. The veteran left-hander made three rehab starts. In his last one, he pitched seven innings, and allowed just one run on six hits.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' ace suffered his second awful outing in his last three starts, getting chased in the fourth inning Saturday against the Phillies after giving up seven earned runs on 10 hits. Maholm has given up at least four earned runs in three of his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bush has put together four consecutive quality starts, including a no-decision against the Giants this week in which he allowed only one run on five hits in six innings. One of his best outings of the year came against the Pirates on April 20, when he tossed seven scoreless.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens has pitched six innings in each of his past two starts, though his last outing was not one his sharpest. He allowed more than four runs for only the second time in 10 starts this year. Fourteen of the 31 runs Karstens has allowed starting have come off homers.

home_pitcher_note: A Craig Counsell error cost Wolf a chance to win his last start against the Giants, but he had his best curveball of the year. A follow-up effort in the final game before the break could give the Brewers' big offseason pickup something to build upon in the second half.
away_pitcher_note: Lincoln never settled in comfortably his last time out, and an inability to establish his fastball command compromised his ability to be successful with his secondary pitches. Lincoln is at his best when he's aggressive and using both sides of the plate effectively.

home_pitcher_note: Duke will look to get back on track after a rocky stretch of outings and a visit to the disabled list while nursing a muscle strain in his pitching elbow. After two effective rehab outings, Duke will make his first start in a month.
away_pitcher_note: Myers had one of the most consistent first halves in baseball, pitching at least six innings in all 18 of his starts. He closed off the first half with a dominating eight-inning win against the Cardinals in which he gave up just five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf has quietly been a very effective pitcher over the last three starts, and doing his work without much offensive support. He's only allowed two earned runs in his past 20 innings (0.90 ERA), but the Pirates have scored only four runs in those three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Norris closed the first half by losing to the Cardinals but he was still impressive in the  outing. His only major mistake was giving up a three-run homer to Matt Holliday. He retired 18 of 19 Cardinals hitters during that start.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm deserved a better fate after a fine outing in his last start before the All-Star break. Maholm held the Brewers in check before a rare bullpen lapse led to a 5-4 extra-inning loss.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt threw a one-hit shutout in his last start in front of a number of scouts. The win put him one win behind Joe Niekro for the most wins in Astros history. Oswalt said he feels the best he has in his entire career.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens will rematch with Milwaukee, who tagged him for a loss in his last outing. Back-to-back Brewers homers hurt the cause, but the real surprise was a career-high six walks for a pitcher with just 16 walks headed in.
away_pitcher_note: Capuano, who won 18 games for the Brewers in 2005, gets a spot start in place of Doug Davis, who had to go back on the DL. Coming back from Tommy John surgery, Capuano was called up from the Minors to start at Florida on June 3 and has made seven relief appearances since.

home_pitcher_note: Lincoln allowed two home runs against Milwaukee on July 11 in his last start, but kept his team in the game and left in line for a win that never came. His moment of truth came when he walked Ryan Braun and Prince Fielder to lead off the sixth, but kept runs off the board.
away_pitcher_note: Bush has six straight quality starts, but the Brewers are just 3-3 in those games because of a lack of offensive support. Bush lost, 2-1, in Atlanta on Thursday, with both of the Braves runs coming on homers. He has allowed 13 home runs this season.

home_pitcher_note: Duke's first start off the DL was a successful one, given that he showed some of the better command he's had in months. He was limited to just 78 pitches in the outing because of the month-long layoff, but Duke should be free to go as deep as he can from here on out.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf is 5-4 on the road, winning his last three decisions. Only seven of the 21 homers he's allowed have come on the road. This will be Wolf's fifth start against the Pirates. He's 1-1 at Pittsburgh and has two no-decisions at home.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf's last start was entirely forgettable as he lasted a career-low 1 1/3 innings. Other than an easy 15-pitch first, there were few positives. Ohlendorf's lost his fastball command, had suspect control and struggled to find a good tempo in the 46-pitch effort.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo, an All-Star pick, is coming off the DL after straining his left oblique against the Cardinals on July 4 and leaving in the third inning. He is 2-0 against the Pirates this season and struck out 10 over five scoreless innings at Pittsburgh on April 21.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm gave the Bucs their first complete game of the season and the fourth of his career in his last outing. He faced only two hitters over the minimum and allowed just three hits in the shutout. He cited mixing pitches and speeds as the biggest factor in his success.
away_pitcher_note: Correia picked up his sixth win of the season on Sunday against Arizona when he gave up three runs on six hits over six innings and tied his career high with nine strikeouts. He beat the Braves in the Padres' home opener in April, allowing two runs in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens retired the first 12 batters he faced Monday on 29 pitches before surrendering a first-pitch home run to Prince Fielder in the fifth. A Rickie Weeks long ball did him in, though Karsten's efficiency was eye-opening: 53 of his 66 pitches went for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Latos will be reinstated from the disabled list (strained left oblique) for this start against the Pirates. Latos, who leads the Padres with 10 victories, will be making his first start since July 8. He's had two bullpen sessions since that last start in Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Lincoln will forget all about his last outing, which lasted 2 1/3 innings and saw a nine-run lead almost disintegrate as he gave up seven runs. The righty never found any rhythm with his curveball, and he starting leaving pitches up when he got the lead and relaxed.
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc has lost eight games this season, the last coming in Atlanta on this road trip, though his ERA is 3.28. His fastball command wasn't as sharp against the Braves, though his changeup has been good. He's struggled away from PETCO Park (4.78).

home_pitcher_note: After giving up 10 hits and 14 runs (11 earned) in his first two starts after returning from a left middle finger injury, De La Rosa found his form against the Marlins on Thursday. De La Rosa gave up two runs on three hits and struck out eight in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Duke gave the Bucs his second consecutive strong start since returning from the DL with a strained flexor pronator, going six innings and giving up just three runs on six hits for his first win since out-dueling Roy Halladay on May 18 and giving a taxed bullpen a rest.

home_pitcher_note: Cook was hit hard by the Phillies on Friday, giving up five runs on nine hits while walking three in 4 1/3 innings. The 31-year-old has a 5.67 ERA in eight career games (five starts) against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf followed his worst start of the season by tossing his fourth quality start in his past five outings, fanning six Brewers over six frames Thursday. His only mistake was a Prince Fielder solo homer, and it was the difference in a 3-2 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez will try to rebound after what was one of his poorer outings in what has otherwise been a magical season. On Saturday against the Phillies, the righty lasted just two innings, surrendering six earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: A four-run second inning handed Maholm the loss Friday vs. the Padres. Maholm has been mired in a good-start, bad-start routine going back to June 23 at Texas. Two of his last six outings have lasted fewer than four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter thrives when he pitches within the division, and he's pretty tough at home too. He'll be kicking off an important six-game homestand in which the Cardinals theoretically will have a chance to make some serious headway in the standings.
away_pitcher_note: After starting with four perfect innings during his last outing, Karstens pitched four more strong innings against the Padres Saturday, striking out four. But his third time around resulted in a three-run (one earned) sixth. Karstens has not recorded

home_pitcher_note: The pressure may be building on Suppan. Either he or Blake Hawksworth will be bumped from the rotation when Kyle Lohse comes back from a forearm injury, and recent actions seem to indicate the staff has more faith in Hawksworth.
away_pitcher_note: McCutchen is expected to be recalled from Triple-A on Saturday to make the start that evening. This will be McCutchen's third stint in the Pirates' rotation, the most recent of which came to an end just before the All-Star break.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright is coming off a rare iffy start, but he's coming home, where he's been dominant. Wainwright is 10-0 with a ridiculous 1.22 ERA at Busch Stadium. In his last five home starts, he's pitched 35 1/3 innings and allowed one earned run.
away_pitcher_note: Duke continues to look like a different pitcher since coming off the DL. In those last three starts, he has rediscovered his sinker and efficiency, and the confidence is building as a result. Duke said he feels as good now as he has all season.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf lasted just four batters in his last start, exiting after being struck in the head by a line drive. He suffered a bad contusion and abrasion but is hopeful he won't have to miss his next start. He'll be evaluated in the coming days.
away_pitcher_note: Wood finally got big league win No. 1, and some run support to beat the Brewers on Wednesday. It was a five-inning start and he used only 82 pitches. Wood said he "had some trouble getting the curveball at first and then finally found it."

home_pitcher_note: Maholm allowed a season-worst eight earned runs and 11 hits in the most recent outing of an up-and-down stretch. The lefty threw a season-high 120 pitches in just 5 1/3 innings and has now not finished six innings in three of his last seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Leake is pitching on eight days' rest after the Reds skipped his turn in an effort to limit his innings total in his rookie season. There was talk of lowering his pitch count from 100 to 90, but that remains in flux.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens was terrific in his last start, a scoreless duel with Chris Carpenter. He tossed six scoreless innings and was taken out with a pitch count of 69 for a pinch-hitter. Karstens threw a first-pitch strike to 19 of 22 hitters.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto is coming off his worst start since mid-June, giving up for four runs on 10 hits in a 6-4 loss Friday. Still, the no-decision kept Cueto's unbeaten streak at seven straight starts, a stretch that's seen him go 4-0 with a 1.55 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates acquired McDonald on July 31 and inserted him into the rotation. McDonald started in Triple-A this season, but made only one start with LA this year. He has pitched just 2 2/3 innings since July 19, which could affect how deep he can go.
away_pitcher_note: Francis' solid outing on July 30 was lost in a 17-2 win against the Cub, but he recorded one of his most efficient outings of the year. The lefty needed just 88 pitches to work through six innings, allowing two runs for the win.

home_pitcher_note: Duke wasn't hit all that hard in his last start, but the Cardinals found enough holes to chase him after five innings. Duke has given up at least six earned runs in five different starts this year. He is the first Pirates pitcher to lose 10 games.
away_pitcher_note:
Hammel had a particularly efficient start spoiled by a three-run homer allowed by a reliever on Saturday against the Cubs. Hammel needed just
83 pitches for 7 1/3 innings, taking the no-decision while striking out five and walking none.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf labored through his last start, needing 95 pitches to finish just the first four innings. Though he limited the damage (three runs), Ohlendorf walked four and went to a three-ball count eight times to the first 18 hitters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa earned his first win since returning from the disabled list in early July in an 8-7 win against the Cubs on Sunday. De La Rosa struck out five and allowed three runs in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm leads the club with seven wins, having snapped a two-game losing skid in his last outing. Maholm has been up-and-down lately, though his most recent start was an encouraging six-inning step in the right direction.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers had two big relief performances for the Rockies in early July before going to Triple-A Colorado Springs to stretch out as a starter. With Aaron Cook on the disabled list with a sprained right big toe, Rogers gets his shot.

home_pitcher_note: LeBlanc has won just once since June 12, as he's been plagued by home runs over the past month or so. He didn't allow any in his last start, vs. the Dodgers, the first time in seven starts he hadn't allowed a long ball. He has a 2.67 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens succeed at damage control, though he labored in his last start. In five innings, the right-hander allowed nine hits, two walks and three runs. Most of his issues were related to issues with his command, particularly with his slider.

home_pitcher_note: Correia helped the Padres gain a split of a four-game series against the Dodgers last week by tossing 5 2/3 scoreless innings. He was able to bury his fastball down in the zone, something he hasn't always done this season.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald struck out a career-high eight in a career-best six-inning start in his Pirates debut. He pitched with a changeup that was better than it has been all season, and that complemented a wicked curveball and low-to-mid 90s fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Garland was the tough-luck loser in his last start, against Arizona, allowing two runs over seven innings. He got 11 groundouts and pitched well enough for his 11th victory, but Daniel Hudson outpitched him.
away_pitcher_note: Duke grinded through 100 pitches over six innings Friday, giving up 10 hits but keeping the Rockies at bay with five strikeouts and no walks, allowing just three runs. Carlos Gonzalez's first-inning homer was the 17th Duke's given up this season.

home_pitcher_note: Extending his franchise record streak to 23 straight starts of six innings or more to open the season on Saturday, Myers needed just 78 pitches as he went six innings while giving up four runs on seven hits, walking one and striking out two batters.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf turned in one of his most efficient performances of the season Saturday against the Rockies, striking out six over six-plus innings and allowing just four hits. Bullpen gaffes, however, kept him from winning his second game.

home_pitcher_note: Norris worked 6 2/3 innings in his previous start, Monday against Atlanta, allowing seven hits and four runs en route to a no-decision. He's pitched at least six innings in six of his last seven starts after doing it only once in his first 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm's inconsistency continued Sunday against the Rockies, as the southpaw gave up eight runs (six earned) in just 2 2/3 innings. Since his shutout on July 18, Maholm has gone 1-3 with a 9.90 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Happ makes his fourth start for the Astros since coming from the Phillies in the trade for Roy Oswalt. He's allowed four hits and one earned run in 12 innings at Minute Maid Park and was rocked for seven runs in one inning in his only road start.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens is 0-6 in his past nine starts despite allowing more than three runs only twice over that stretch. The biggest issue is run support, as the Bucs have scored just 14 runs when Karstens has been on the mound in those outings.

home_pitcher_note: Efficiency issues and an inability to put away hitters got McDonald in trouble in his last start. He went to seven three-ball counts, four coming after he got ahead 1-2 or 0-2. McDonald is stretched out now, meaning he has no pitch limitations.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad has won two of his past three starts, with a no-decision. He worked five innings in beating Washington his last time out. He last threw as many as six innings on July 25.

home_pitcher_note: Since coming off the disabled list, Zach Duke has notched four quality starts in six outings. The wins, though, aren't falling as easily. The good news for Duke is that his next start will come at home, where the Bucs have given him good run support.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco blanked the Nationals for six innings on Thursday, allowing six hits with one walk and eight strikeouts. He's won four of his past five decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf threw 6 2/3 shutout innings in his last start, but he didn't factor in the decision after the bullpen allowed the Astros to pull ahead in a 4-1 loss. Ohlendorf fanned seven batters against two walks and four hits.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson said he feels fine physically after his shortest outing of the season, Friday at Cincinnati. He lasted just 3 2/3 innings in a 7-2 loss to the Reds, allowing a season-high six runs and a career-high 10 hits.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm was solid in his most recent appearance, a 3-2 loss to the Astros. He threw 6 2/3 innings, allowing nine hits but only three runs. He fanned four and ceded only one walk. Still, he was saddled with the loss, dropping his record to 7-11.
away_pitcher_note: Sean West has been placed on the DL with right knee inflammation, so Sanabia has been recalled from Triple-A New Orleans for this one. Sanabia, who also pitched at Double-A Jacksonville this year, is a 6-1 with a 1.92 ERA in the Minors in 2010.

home_pitcher_note: One bad inning did Karstens in his last time out, and that kept him winless since June 19. During that 10-start span, however, the right-hander has not pitched that poorly. He continues to be the least supported pitcher in the Pirates' rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey pitched well enough to earn a win against the Phillies but didn't receive any run support in a 3-1 loss. He gave up three runs on seven hits over seven innings and fell to 1-5 over his past nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald's next start comes at PNC Park, where he has dominated. In 17 1/3 innings there, McDonald is 2-0 with 20 strikeouts. He has allowed just three earned runs there. If McDonald has his curveball and changeup both working, he's tough to beat.
away_pitcher_note: Niese gave up just one run over seven innings but couldn't get his first win since July 27. The Mets offense gave him only one run over those seven innings, in which he gave up seven hits. Niese has a 1.29 ERA over his past three starts.
summary: 2010-08-21 - New York Mets @ Pittsburgh Pirates (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Duke was again stung by the big inning as he lost his 12th game. In eight of those losses, he's allowed four or more runs in one inning. This last time it was a result of pitches falling flat, though pitch selection has also sometimes been an issue.
away_pitcher_note: Santana allowed four runs over eight innings in a 4-3 loss to the Astros on Tuesday night. He went the distance, but a go-ahead solo homer by Hunter Pence in the bottom of the eighth proved to be the difference.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf has a 2.35 ERA over his last 10 starts, though minimal run support has him 1-4 during that span. He lasted a career-long eight innings in his last start and continues to offer quality starts. Now he just needs some help from the offense.
away_pitcher_note: Whatever Lohse does, it'll be easy to improve on his last start. Coming back from a two-month DL stint, Lohse was rocked for seven runs in three innings on six hits and two walks. A night against the Bucs' meager offense might help.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm breezed through five innings but never got out of the sixth on Thursday. A string of six hits, a walk and a hit batter led to four runs, which sent Maholm to loss No. 12. He has not pitched six innings in five of his last 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright will shoot for sole possession of the Major League lead in wins, 18, against the Bucs. He was effective, if unlucky in his last start, allowing three runs in seven innings and fanning seven while falling to the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: McCutchen will start in place of scheduled starter Jeff Karstens who was scratched because of arm fatigue. In his last nine relief appearances McCutchen has posted a 1.74 ERA and has eight strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook has gone at least six innings in each of his four starts with the Redbirds, but he's only earned one victory. He took a hard-luck defeat in his most recent, allowing three runs in six innings while striking out seven Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson should be fresh. He threw only 64 pitches against the Padres in his last start and was pulled after three-plus innings. Manager Ken Macha made the early move to avoid letting the Padres get a mid-inning lead to their outstanding bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Command issues plagued McDonald in his last start, as he walked five batters in five innings. He never got a reliable breaking pitch working, which allowed the Mets to sit on his fastball. Efficiency is always key for McDonald to have success.

home_pitcher_note: Capuano is replacing fellow lefty Manny Parra in the rotation and will get a good, long look over the final month-plus of the season. Capuano, a pending free agent, returned this season from his second Tommy John surgery.
away_pitcher_note: Duke had one of his best starts of the season last time out, outdueling Johan Santana to ensure he didn't go winless in August. Two things continue to be key for the lefty: the sinker has to be working, and he has to avoid big innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bush was in line for a win against the Dodgers on Tuesday before he surrendered a two-out, three-run homer to the No. 8 hitter, Rod Barajas. "I made one bad pitch and it turns the whole game around," Bush said.
away_pitcher_note: Morton returns to the Pirates for his first Major League start since May 27. In 14 starts at Triple-A since then, Morton went 4-4 with a 3.83 ERA, striking out 53 batters and walking 30 in 80 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano is coming off one of his best outings, having given up one run on five hits over 7 1/3 innings vs. the Nats. But he's also been dealing with personal matters and flew to Venezuela after that game to see a nephew who is seriously ill.
away_pitcher_note: Winless in his last four starts, Maholm is looking for his third victory in as many starts against the Cubs this season. In his last start at Wrigley Field, on June 28, Maholm held the Cubs to one run on seven hits in eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster wasn't happy about being pulled after 79 pitches in his last start, vs. the Nats. But it worked, as a pinch-hitter got on and the Cubs won. Dempster is 4-0 with a 1.31 ERA in five starts in August.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens had his last start skipped because of arm fatigue, but he's expected to not miss any more time. Karstens has already exceeded his 2009 innings total, so the Pirates are going to watch his workload during this final month.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny wasn't happy with his last start and for good reason. He gave up six runs on seven hits to the Reds, including two of three homers that night by Jay Bruce. The lefty will be happy to turn the calendar. He was 1-3 with a 5.46 ERA in August.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald appeared headed for his third win with the Pirates in his last until things imploded for him in the seventh. His defense hurt him, and by the time McDonald's outing ended, he was charged with six earned runs on seven hits in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Duke left his last start in line for a win, but the bullpen couldn't hold a lead and give Duke what would have been his seventh season victory. Regardless, the outing wasn't Duke's sharpest. He gave up nine hits in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Fresh off signing a one-year contract extension that will keep him with the Nats through the end of 2011, Hernandez tries to rebound from back-to-back rough outings in which he allowed 18 hits and 12 runs combined over 10 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm's inconsistent results don't appear to be ending. He lasted only 3 1/3 innings in his last start, marking the fourth time that he hasn't finished four innings this season. He hadn't had a start that short in either of the past two years.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan was dominant in his last start, throwing 7 2/3 innings of one run ball against the Cardinals to even his record at 6-6 for the season. He posted a 3.25 ERA in six starts in August, winning four and losing one.

home_pitcher_note: Morton's return from the Minors did not go as planned. He lasted just 3 1/3 innings (eight runs) and didn't pitch aggressively enough. The Pirates want Morton to rely less on his offspeed pitches and go after hitters with more fastballs.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis earned his first win of the season, allowing three runs and seven hits in a victory over Florida on Monday. Marquis (1-7) pitched out of three two-out jams, including a bases-loaded threat in the third.

home_pitcher_note: Jeff Karstens (shoulder soreness) has been scratched, giving Burres his first start for the Bucs since May 29. Since being recalled on Aug. 23, Burres has pitched exclusively out of the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson brushed off two shaky starts and regained his dominant form while allowing one hit in seven scoreless innings against the Mets on Wednesday night. He has allowed one or no earned runs in six of his past eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Competing without his best command, McDonald was able to limit Chicago to three runs in five innings. Keeping the Cubs to 1-for-9 with runners in scoring position helped, but McDonald labored too much to be able to pitch deep.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has allowed one earned run or fewer in six of his past nine starts. But he has surrendered three earned runs or more in two of his past three outings. He hasn't allowed an earned run in his past three starts (22 innings) against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Duke enjoyed five solid innings in his last start. His sinker worked and he mixed his pitches well. Then, the wheels came off in the sixth. Duke held on for the win -- thanks to the offense -- but Duke's middle-inning issues are a concerning trend.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe tested his sore right elbow Sunday morning and came away confident that he will be able to make this start against the Pirates. He will be pitching for the first time since allowing the Marlins five earned runs in three innings on Aug. 29.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey was having a terrific duel with Chris Carpenter and the Cardinals Sunday until one critical mistake ruined him. He shook off catcher Ryan Hanigan and threw a fastball that tailed over the plate to Matt Holliday, who crushed a three-run homer.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm's inconsistencies continued in his last start. The lefty gave up five runs in the fourth inning, marking the ninth time in Maholm's last 15 starts that he has allowed an opponent to score at least four runs in a single frame.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez made the second of his two starts for Class A Dayton on Monday, throwing six-plus innings with three runs (two earned), three walks, 10 strikeouts and two home runs. He believed he had his mechanics right again and was throwing strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Morton did better relying on his fastball, but only with limited success. Hurt by his defense and some seeing-eye singles, Morton lasted only 3 2/3 innings. His velocity crept up late, but Morton hasn't finished four innings in half of his 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto was pitching with a heavy heart after his uncle passed away last week. He lost because of a three-run first inning, but was praised for pitching well and going six innings while preserving the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Burres earned himself a stay in the rotation after dominating the Braves in a spot start on Monday. Burres, who allowed just one run on five hits and no walks in six innings, keeps the rotation slot that had belonged to Jeff Karstens.

home_pitcher_note: Gee's big league debut was sparkling, earning him at least one more start. Though concerns about Gee's innings total may limit him down the stretch, the Mets are eager to see how Gee will fare vs. Pittsburgh with his modest-but-effective repertoire.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald has pitched better at home than on the road, but he made some mechanical changes in his last start that he hopes will translate to success regardless of venue. If McDonald can pound the lower part of the strike zone, he can roll.

home_pitcher_note: Though Dickey allowed another two-out homer last Wednesday in Washington, that did not prevent him from recording his career-high 10th victory. The Pirates, whom he last faced in relief two seasons ago, are all that stands between Dickey and No. 11.
away_pitcher_note: Duke lasted a career-short one inning in his last start, exiting after facing only 11 hitters. He never established command of his fastball and fooled no one in Atlanta's lineup. Opponents are now hitting .320 off the lefty this year.

home_pitcher_note: Mejia's second big league start was more forgettable than the first, but that won't stop the Mets from salivating over his upper-90s fastball and much-improved changeup and curve. His next foe is the Pirates, a team Mejia has not faced in relief.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm allowed three runs, all in the third inning, and six hits in seven innings against the Reds on Friday. He earned a no-decision when the Pirates rallied for two runs in the ninth to tie the score before losing in the 12th.

home_pitcher_note: Though Pelfrey entered last Saturday's play with an 0-2 record and a 10.28 ERA over his previous two starts, he submitted seven innings of two-run ball against the Phillies. Next up are the Pirates, a team he beat handily in Pittsburgh last month.
away_pitcher_note: Morton had his finest outing of the season Saturday at Cincinnati, going 6 1/3 innings and giving up three runs and six hits. He walked one and struck out two in a no-decision. Morton was efficient, needing just 69 pitches to complete his outing.

home_pitcher_note: Burres has been one of the Pirates' best pitchers since taking Jeff Karstens' spot in the rotation. In his last two starts, the lefty has combined to allow just two runs on nine hits in 13 innings. He has struck out nine and walked one.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy has pitched 14 scoreless innings over his last two starts, allowing just two hits each game but leaving with a no-decision as the D-backs lost both games following his departure.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald takes a string of 17 scoreless innings into his next start. The righty has been terrific lately and has lowered his ERA with Pittsburgh to 3.49. McDonald has also been efficient. He needed just 100 pitches to finish eight innings on Monday.
away_pitcher_note: After an outstanding first 12 starts after being called up from Double-A Mobile, Enright has struggled mightily in his last two. In those two outings, he has allowed 11 runs over nine innings. Last time out he gave up five runs in three innings.

home_pitcher_note: There's a chance Duke won't still be in the rotation, but if he is, it can't get any worse for the lefty. He's not fooling anyone (opponents are batting .326 against him) and has lasted a combined 4 1/3 innings in his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson limited Cincinnati to four hits and a walk in eight shutout innings. He led Arizona to a 3-1 victory over the NL Central-leading Reds on Tuesday. Hudson, 24, has gone at least seven innings in eight of his starts with the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: For the sixth time this season, Maholm made a start that lasted fewer than four innings. This time, though, it wasn't his entire fault. Two errors behind him led to five unearned runs in seven-run fourth that knocked Maholm out.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook is coming off his best start as a Cardinal, and his best start for anyone in a long time. His peripherals have been strong throughout his St. Louis tenure, so it should be no surprise that he finally got more zeroes on the scoreboard.

home_pitcher_note: For Morton, progress is coming in baby steps. He lasted only five innings in his last start, but he did push his ERA to its lowest point of the season. Morton is hoping that some delivery tweaks will make his pitches more deception.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse appears to be rounding into form, and he's won back-to-back starts for the first time since his first two starts of the 2009 season. In his most recent, he allowed three runs on seven hits in five innings to down the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Burres has gone 3-for-3 in the quality start department since being reinserted into the rotation. He's walked just one in 20 innings and allowed four earned runs on 16 hits during that same span. He's become one of the club's most reliable arms.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan pitched well in his first start since Sept. 1 on Saturday, yielding one run in five innings to the Padres in a no-decision. He hurled 5 1/3 shutout innings in his only other start against the Pirates this year, on July 31.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald's scoreless inning streak was snapped at 20 in his last start, which was a battle throughout. Though McDonald picked up the win, he needed 101 pitches to go five innings. This will be his final start at home, where he is 4-1 with a 2.40 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Myers will try to improve on his club-record string of working at least six innings in 31 straight starts. He is one of six Major League pitchers since 1920 to go six or more innings in their first 31 appearances. His ERA is third-best in the NL.

home_pitcher_note: Duke is the all-time wins leader at PNC Park with 30 and he's making his final start of the season there. Over two-thirds of his 44 career victories have come at home. His most recent outing was solid (three runs, six hits, a season-high 7 2/3 IP).
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander has won seven of his past eight decisions, posting a 3.52 ERA over that span, and the Astros are 10-1 in his last 11 starts. In his last outing at Washington on Monday, Norris allowed two runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm has an outside shot at a 10-win season after snapping a six-game losing skid on Tuesday. He pitched seven innings for just the third time since the All-Star break and would like nothing more than to finish an up-and-down season on a high note.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander has been on a roll for the past several weeks. He came from the Phillies in the Roy Oswalt deal and is on a three-game winning streak and hasn't lost in six starts. He gave up no earned runs and just three hits in six innings at DC.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse had been showing signs of progress, but he got knocked around in Pittsburgh in his last start. He has at most two more games to secure some kind of good feeling going into the offseason as he tries to salvage a frustrating year.
away_pitcher_note: Morton picked up his first win since May 5 in his last start, finally putting a bright spot on a tumultuous season. He allowed a season-low two runs in six innings, but more importantly, he did so being aggressive and trusting his abilities.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan will try to end his season on a high note as makes his final start. Suppan has pitched well down the stretch, going 1-0 with a 2.38 ERA over his last three starts. Last time out, he beat the Pirates for just his second win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Burres lasted 2 1/3 innings against the Cardinals in his last start. Little went right. He struggled locating pitches down, which was the result of his arm and body not being in sync. Burres had allowed just four runs in his previous 20 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Walters will make his second September appearance. In his last outing, he was cuffed around for seven hits and five runs in four innings during a loss to Pittsburgh on Sept. 22, though he did strike out a season-best six batters.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald was wild in his last start on Friday against Houston. He tossed 80 pitches in four innings of work, his shortest outing since joining the Pirates on July 31. He was tagged for three runs on five hits and received a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad is finishing the season on a high note, not allowing a run in his past two starts. He has tossed 15 2/3 scoreless innings, allowing 11 hits over that span. This will be his 30th and final start and he's thrown 169 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Duke's looking to close an up-and-down season on a high note. Opponents continue to hit over .300 against him, though Duke limited damage in his last two starts. He's pitched into the seventh in consecutive outings for the first time since April.

home_pitcher_note: The 28-year-old right-hander will make his fifth start, and he seeks to get back on track after going through a roughing outing in Milwaukee, where he allowed six runs and gave up four homers in two-plus innings.
away_pitcher_note: Probable starter Paul Maholm was scratched Thursday night due to left knee irritation, which thrusts McCutchen into starting duty. McCutchen has pitched out of the bullpen all month and will be limited in his pitch count. He last pitched on Sept. 24.

Morton has one more outing to put it all together. He's had some bright moments this final month, though the consistency of execution still isn't there. Morton needs to stay aggressive and show more belief in his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez wraps up the year by making his 32nd start, the most of any Marlin this year. The right-hander, however, hasn't had much luck of late, having dropped three straight decisions. At home he is 4-4 with a 2.73 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Burres has a chance to be the only Pirates starter to finish the year with a winning record, though he'll have to win this last start to do so. The Pirates have won four of the five starts he has made since being reinserted into the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Dempster's first Opening Day assignment with the Cubs, the third of his career. He did so twice for the Marlins. The right-hander was 15-12 last season with a 3.85 ERA, totaling 200 innings for the third straight year.
away_pitcher_note: The newest member of the Pirates' rotation, Correia will be making the first Opening Day start of his career. Wrigley Field hasn't been kind to Correia in the past, but he did toss six shutout innings his last start there.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano held the franchise record for Opening Day starts, getting the assignment six years in a row. But he's been bumped to No. 2 this season. Zambrano is eager to put last season behind him after spending part of the year in the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm will start the home opener, but first he has this matchup against the Cubs. Despite his high ERA at Wrigley Field, Maholm has won five of seven starts there. No one in the rotation has as many career starts as Maholm.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired from the Rays in an eight-player deal, Garza is the newest member of the Cubs rotation. This will be his first season in the NL and he's spent a lot of time working on his bunting. Garza was 15-10 with a 3.91 ERA for the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates can only hope that Ohlendorf's spring troubles don't bleed into the season. Health is the first key. Ohlendorf must also show better efficiency and find a way to stop himself from overthrowing.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse was one of the best stories of spring, going all of the Grapefruit League season without issuing a walk. If he's back in form after struggling due to injury for more than a year and a half, it will be an enormous boost for St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Back in the rotation after a dismal 2010 season, Morton is eager to seize the second chance. He was the Pirates' best pitcher all spring and will bring a changed arm angle and revitalized sinker to the mound with him now.

home_pitcher_note: McClellan finally won the job he's coveted for years, earning a spot in the Cardinals rotation with a superb spring. It remains to be seen how he'll hold up over a full season, but he pitched lights-out in the Grapefruit League.
away_pitcher_note: A left side injury cost McDonald two weeks of spring games, but the right-hander still hopes to be ready for this first start. McDonald likely won't be able to throw more than 100 pitches given his light spring workload.

home_pitcher_note: The bell rang, and Carpenter came out looking like himself. Carpenter had some iffy results during Grapefruit League play, but was sharp on Opening Day. The Cardinals have won Carpenter's last 13 starts against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: In terrible conditions, Correia provided the Pirates a strong six-inning start in his club debut on Opening Day. The Cubs did not have an extra-base hit off the right-hander, who threw 61 of his 92 pitches for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm gets the opportunity to start in the Pirates' home opener for the first time in his career. His season got off to a stellar start with 6 2/3 scoreless innings at Wrigley Field in his season debut.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers showed an electric fastball and the fearlessness necessary for success. But he didn't execute with consistency, and never was able to grab a role. Rogers learned a changeup this winter, however, and earned the fifth spot on the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough spring, Ohlendorf was pleased with his season debut. A tweaked delivery motion seemed to help, and Ohlendorf also benefited from taking less time between pitches and not getting as distracted with runners on.
away_pitcher_note: Despite a blood blister that caused him to leave his first start early, De La Rosa is expected to get the nod against the Pirates, a team he is 3-2 with a 4.06 ERA against in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Morton went 2-12 with a 7.57 ERA in 2010 but had a strong debut on Monday against the Cardinals, allowing one run on three hits over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: With Rockies ace Ubaldo Jimenez placed on the 15-day DL with a cut cuticle on his pitching thumb, the Rockies recalled Reynolds from Triple-A Colorado Springs to make his first Major League start since 2008.

home_pitcher_note: After missing time with a strained oblique, McDonald was fine in his first start on Tuesday. He allowed two runs on four hits over 4 2/3 innings, with four strikeouts and four walks, and 51 of his 87 pitches went for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin aims for a repeat of his first start, when he threw seven scoreless innings in a 3-0 win over the Dodgers. Chacin's only outing against Pittsburgh came in 2009, when he gave up four runs, while walking six in 2 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Correia was needed to pitch in relief on Saturday, but that shouldn't affect his ability to go deep in his next start. He's been the team's most consistent pitcher to this point and outdueled Chris Carpenter in his previous game.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum is still a work in progress after pitching six innings against the Braves on Sunday for his first Brewers win. He's trying to hone his command after missing his next-to-last spring start with a stiff shoulder.

home_pitcher_note: Correia was needed to pitch in relief on Saturday, but that shouldn't affect his ability to go deep on Wednesday. He's been the team's most consistent pitcher to this point and outdueled Chris Carpenter in his start last week.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum is still a work in progress after pitching six innings against the Braves on Sunday for his first Brewers win. He's trying to hone his command after missing his next-to-last spring start with a stiff shoulder.

home_pitcher_note: Hurt by his defense and Colorado's Troy Tulowitzki, Maholm lost his first decision of the year. Still, he's pitching inside and down in the zone effectively and consistently. Both are essential for Maholm to have success.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf hasn't been blessed with stellar defensive help in his two starts, but he has not put up zeroes, either. In 10 innings, he's already allowed 19 hits and four home runs, two in each outing.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo threw 94 pitches over six innings before coming out of Saturday's start at Arizona. He was fatigued from the effects of mono but says he's getting much stronger.
away_pitcher_note: Though Morton is in a much better place than he was a year ago, he is still battling a mechanical issue that is leading to too many walks. If Morton can limit the walks and have success with his sinker, he'll be tough to beat.

home_pitcher_note: Leake allowed a five-run sixth and blew a 5-0 lead on Sunday at Arizona. The first four singles against him were not hit that hard. But he missed his fastball location to Ryan Roberts, who clobbered a three-run homer.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald shook off a 38-pitch first inning and managed to go 6 2/3 innings deep in his previous start. His pitch count won't be an issue anymore, and McDonald finally seems to have made up for the time he missed this spring.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez was pushed back to Sunday's start with a stiff neck. Volquez has a 27.00 ERA in the first inning through three starts, and his ERA is 1.29 for the other innings.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens steps into the rotation to fill in for an injured Ross Ohlendorf. He's plenty stretched out, having thrown 67 pitches in relief on April 8, and he has made the jump from reliever to starter effectively in the past.

home_pitcher_note: Wood rebounded after giving up six runs in five innings vs. Arizona with a one-run performance in San Diego in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Correia suffered his first loss largely due to a hanging curveball to Prince Fielder. Fielder blasted a three-run homer after Correia pitched five no-hit frames. Other than that, Correia has been strong so far this year.

home_pitcher_note: History nearly was made the last time Johnson pitched. The Florida ace had his no-hit bid thwarted by Atlanta's Freddie Freeman with one out double in the eighth. Twice this year he has not given up a hit through six.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm again deserved better than a loss in his last start. After allowing two runs in a 28-pitch first, Maholm cruised through six scoreless innings. Two of his starts have been strong, but he has no win to show for it.

home_pitcher_note: Impressive in his first two starts, Nolasco struggled in a no-decision at Atlanta in his last outing. He went five innings, giving up five runs with four strikeouts. Nolasco is 3-3 (2.11 ERA) lifetime in 8 games, 6 starts vs. Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Morton was terrific in his last start. He notched his second career complete game and threw 81 of 110 pitches for strikes. He did it, too, relaying mostly on a sinker that is more deceptive thanks to a change in his arm angle.
