home_pitcher_note: Roughed up in Atlanta, Volstad will look to close the Marlins' nine-game road trip on a high note. The righty exited after 4 2/3 innings Tuesday at Atlanta, giving up five runs on eight hits. Lifetime, Volstad is 2-0 with a 5.11 ERA at Philadelphia.
away_pitcher_note: James McDonald again battled a mechanical issue in his last start that has caused him to leave too many pitches up in the zone this season. He has had strong stretches in between, but big innings have been plaguing him.

home_pitcher_note: After considering several options, the Bucs will start Karstens on Friday in their opener vs. the Nationals. The righty allowed five runs over 4 1/3 innings in Sunday's start against the Reds while filling in for an injured Ross Ohlendorf.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez allowed one run on six hits with three strikeouts and no walks in seven innings to pick up his second win on Sunday against the Brewers. Hernandez will face the Bucs for the 17th time in his career. He is 5-5 with a 5.52 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: After considering several options, the Bucs will start Karstens on Friday in their opener vs. the Nationals. The righty allowed five runs over 4 1/3 innings in Sunday's start against the Reds while filling in for an injured Ross Ohlendorf.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez allowed one run on six hits with three strikeouts and no walks in seven innings to pick up his second win on Sunday against the Brewers. Hernandez will face the Bucs for the 17th time in his career. He is 5-5 with a 5.52 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Correia is coming off one of his best outings of the season. The 30-year-old threw a complete game on Monday against the Reds, holding them to three runs to earn his third win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis entered Sunday's game against the Brewers with four consecutive quality starts at Nationals Park without a win to show for it. Marquis pitched seven-plus innings, allowing two runs on seven hits with four K's and one walk for his first win.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm had been throwing well without much to show for it. But the lefty struggled to pitch out of jams in his latest outing, surrendering six runs over 3 2/3 innings. Maholm, 0-4 with a 6.26 ERA in seven starts vs. the Nats, will try to rebound.
away_pitcher_note: Because of a rainout, Lannan is pitching with his normal rest. Lannan tossed five-plus innings during an 8-6 win over the Cards in Game 1 of a day-night twin bill Wednesday, allowing two runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: After throwing a complete game against the Reds on April 15, Morton struggled mightily against the Marlins in his latest start. The 27-year-old allowed six runs on 10 hits over five innings to earn his first loss of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Cain struggled through his first bad start of the season in his last outing, giving up six runs on nine hits in 4 2/3 innings. He allowed three runs and 14 hits over his first 19 innings of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Despite working on his mechanics, McDonald's early struggles continued in his last outing. The right-hander gave up eight runs on six hits over just three innings in a loss to the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner's 2 2/3-inning effort against Atlanta last Friday matched the shortest of his career. He also endured that fate last Aug. 25 against Cincinnati. This will be Bumgarner's first career assignment against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Karstens' third spot start for Ross Ohlendorf. Karstens was strong in his last outing, giving the Pirates six efficient innings in a win over Washington. The only concern is that Karstens tends to tire when his pitch count gets near 75.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong will be making his first Major League start since September 2004, when he allowed six runs in 1 1/3 innings for Pittsburgh. After leaving the Pirates in 2006, he toiled in Japan and Triple-A until earning a job with the Giants this season.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin, whose start Wednesday was rained out, has shown no signs of a sophomore slump after setting franchise rookie records in 2010 for strikeouts (138) and ERA by a starter (3.28). He is 3-1 with a 2.67 ERA and 18 strikeouts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Correia was doomed by a high fastball to Michael Morse in his last start, though the Nats peppered him for 11 hits in 4 2/3 innings. Morse hit a three-run homer, and Correia was unable to finish six innings for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel turned in his best outing of '11, allowing one run on seven hits in 6 2/3 frames Saturday. What may have been most impressive about Hammel was how he continually pitched himself out of jams. Eight Marlins reached base, but just one scored.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm has had most of his problems in the first two innings this year, though he's often gotten stronger as his starts get deeper. He's no longer winless, and Maholm was especially impressive pitching inside last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez continues to look for his first win after allowing three runs on one hit and four walks over five innings against the Marlins. He struck out seven in a no-decision and has yet to work more than six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Morton did a much better job mixing his pitches in his last start Tuesday after relying too heavily on his sinker in his previous one. The Giants tallied just one run and four hits off him in six-plus innings, though the bullpen cost Morton a win.

home_pitcher_note: After winning his first four starts with the Padres, Harang suffered his first loss in his last start to the Braves, allowing eight earned runs over six frames. He's throwing his slider and changeup more, and velocity on his fastball has been better.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates hope that McDonald is on track after a stellar six-plus-inning start on Wednesday. He finally found his curveball and fastball command, and his delivery looked much smoother. He still needs to get the walk total down.

home_pitcher_note: Latos hasn't won a game this season and has dropped his past nine starts, dating back to September. He improved in his last start against the Braves, allowing one earned run over five innings, but he is still trying to regain his 2010 form.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens deserved better in his last start, which was marred by four errors. He has been strong through the sixth in his last two starts, but has stumbled in the seventh both times. Extending himself longer is the next goal.

home_pitcher_note: Richard won his first start on April 2 and has gone winless in his last five outings (two losses, three no-decisions). He held the Dodgers to two runs in 5 2/3 innings in his last start. He allowed a season-high eight hits but got eight groundouts.
away_pitcher_note: Correia had a terrific April, becoming the first Pirates pitcher since '03 to win four games in the month. He has emerged as the team's most reliable starter and has thrown at least six innings in all but one of his six starts.

home_pitcher_note: A four-run second stung Maholm in his last outing, which was otherwise impressive. He went seven innings deep for the third time in four starts, and did not allow a run after the second. He has been hurt by lack of run support.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is coming off his best start of the season, even though he didn't get a win after the Astros blew a save in the ninth. The lefty tossed eight scoreless innings Saturday against Milwaukee and struck out six.

home_pitcher_note: Morton threw just 56 of his 104 pitches for strikes, but he skirted trouble to pick up a win his last time out. It was yet another sign of growth for the righty, who let such trouble frequently snowball on him last year.
away_pitcher_note: Norris hasn't allowed an earned run in three of his past four starts. He had electric stuff in his previous start Sunday against the Brewers, striking out 11 batters in 7 2/3 scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: With two strong starts in a row, McDonald seems to have found his way. He's pitching aggressively, establishing fastball command early and finding his curve to be effective again. He's allowed only two runs in his past 12 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Happ is coming off a win over the Reds on Tuesday in which he said he had his best stuff of the season. He allowed eight hits and four runs in 6 1/3 innings, which isn't a quality start, but he was ahead in the count and limited his walks.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens has made four spot starts for Ross Ohlendorf, and the most recent was his shortest. He didn't have good command and was especially hurt by two home runs. Karstens had gone at least six innings in his two previous outings.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley is coming off one of his better starts, holding the Cubs to one run over seven innings in a tough loss. Billingsley is 4-0 lifetime against Pittsburgh and 2-0 at PNC Park. He's pitched into the sixth in each of his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: In a homecoming to San Diego, Correia became the first National League pitcher to win five games. Oddly enough, Correia is still seeking his first win at home. He has gone at least six innings in six of seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: It's been a bit of a struggle so far for the left-handed Lilly, whose ERA is approaching 5.00. Opponents are hitting .318 and even left-handers are batting .303 with only one strikeout. Lilly is 5-4 lifetime against the Pirates and 3-3 at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm has pitched seven innings in four of his last five starts, but the team is giving him no run support. The offense has scored 11 runs with Maholm on the mound this year, a large reason why the club is 1-7 in his starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda's velocity was down a bit and his pitches were up a bit, leading to a pair of home runs by the Mets on Friday. Kuroda has already allowed seven homers this season after averaging 13 allowed his first three seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Scripting one of the best comeback stories of the year, Morton has been terrific so far this season. The command of his sinker is only getting better, evidenced by the decreasing walk totals. He's also been mighty efficient.
away_pitcher_note: The 1-2 record doesn't show it, but the Dodgers are getting more than they should from a fifth starter in Garland. His ERA is 3.66 and opponents are batting only .237 after he missed his first two turns with a strained oblique muscle.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo took a no-hitter into the eighth inning on Saturday to snap a streak of five consecutive subpar starts and will try to stay on track against the Pirates. He's 6-2 against them, with a 2.15 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald matched his career high with eight strikeouts in his past start, which, like the previous two, lasted six innings. McDonald has been as reliable as anyone in the rotation lately. Watch out if he has his curve working.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson is still winless in five starts since pitching seven scoreless innings against the Cubs in a home victory on April 9. He did pitch well against the Cardinals on Sunday, allowing only two earned runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens is doing everything asked as he fills in for Ross Ohlendorf. He lasted just 5 2/3 innings his last time out, but pitched well after first-inning trouble. Pittsburgh has won three of the five games he has started.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke dazzled in the early innings of his winning Miller Park debut before running out of steam in the fifth and sixth. The Brewers figure those late innings will improve as Grienke gains arm strength.
away_pitcher_note: Correia's next start is on the road, and that's a good thing, as he's won all five starts away from PNC Park. Correia has a 1.56 ERA on the road and has pitched at least six innings in all but one of his eight season starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates handed Lannan one of his four losses on the season in late April, when he allowed four earned runs in 5 2/3 innings. Lannan last won on April 20 in St. Louis and took a no-decision in his previous start.
away_pitcher_note: Until Maholm gets some run support, his record will continue to be deceiving. The Pirates have scored one run or less in all five of Maholm's losses, and the bullpen has cost him wins twice. He has a 5.19 ERA on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann enters the Tuesday matinee with Pittsburgh off a career game, as he struck out 11 Braves in 6 1/3 innings. He did allow three runs and took a no-decision, as the Nats lost in 10. The 24-year-old righty has never faced the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Morton's last start was brief, as rain stopped the game after two innings. Morton allowed one run, but only one ball was hit hard off him. Though Morton's away ERA is higher than at home, three of his wins have been on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo did not factor into the decision in his start last Friday, allowing four runs (three earned) on six hits in six innings. He did not give up a hit his first time through the order against St. Louis but struggled his second time around.
away_pitcher_note: Morton's last start was brief, as rain stopped the game after two innings. Morton allowed one run, but only one ball was hit hard off him. Though Morton's away ERA is higher than at home, three of his wins have been on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto has yet to surrender an earned run in 13 2/3 innings this season. He was particularly strong in his most recent start, going deeper than any Reds pitcher this season (7 2/3 innings) while allowing three unearned runs on three hits.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald's undoing in his last start in Milwaukee on Friday was the bottom of the order -- eighth hitter Jonathan Lucroy homered and pitcher Yovani Gallardo delivered two hits and scored twice in a 5-2 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens threw an economical 69 pitches and allowed two runs in five innings on two solo homers, but he was lifted for a pinch hitter as an offense-starved Pittsburgh fell to Milwaukee in his last start, 8-2.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling in his first four starts, Penny has won four of his last five, with three scoreless outings. An improved sinker pitch has led to at least 11 ground-ball outs in each of his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Correia is trying to snap a personal two-game losing streak. The right-hander has struggled in those two starts, giving up 10 earned runs in his last 10 1/3 innings after winning his two starts before that.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer has at least one more chance, possibly two, to become the first Tigers pitcher since Vern Kennedy in 1938 to own a 7-0 record by the end of May. He went 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA in three Interleague starts last year.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm gave up three runs on four hits in 6 1/3 innings in Monday's tough-luck loss to Washington. The Pirates aren't giving him much support, having scored only 14 runs in his nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello has quietly become one of the American League's stingiest pitchers since starting his season with back-to-back rough outings. He's allowed just seven runs on 29 hits over 31 2/3 innings over his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Morton's former teammates in Atlanta won't recognize the right-hander, who has remade himself since last season. The Braves can expect to see a heavy dose of sinkers from Morton, who is coming off his second career shutout.
away_pitcher_note: Through no fault of his own, Jurrjens suffered his first loss of the season Thursday in Arizona. Jurrjens gave up two runs on eight hits in 6 2/3 innings, but received no support. He's 1-3 with 3.13 ERA in four career starts vs. Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: It took McDonald 30 pitches to become aggressive in his last start. Once he did, he was terrific. He showcased his best fastball of the year in the 6 2/3-inning outing and showed how good he can be when he doesn't nibble.
away_pitcher_note: The Braves plan to call up the left-handed Minor from Triple-A Gwinnett for Wednesday's start in place of Tim Hudson. Minor is also scheduled to start against San Diego on May 31, when the Braves will need a fifth starter after a slew of off-days.

home_pitcher_note: The Red Sox had the edge in Davis' last start as he fell behind hitters. He served up eight hits and walked three over 3 2/3 innings. The good news is he's healthy -- just looking for that first "W."
away_pitcher_note: Correia heads back on the road, where he is 5-1 with a 2.79 ERA. He's finished at least six innings in eight of 10 starts and beat the Cubs in Chicago on Opening Day. Correia allowed two earned runs in six hits that day.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Wells' first start since April 4. He's been on the DL with a strained right forearm since then and has made two Minor League rehab starts. In his last outing, he threw 68 pitches over four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ignore Maholm's record because it has everything to do with run support. Maholm continues to be competitive each time he takes the mound, but the Pirates have scored just 13 runs in the 61 2/3 innings he has been on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster posted his fourth quality start in his last five games against the Mets, giving up one run on seven hits over seven innings. He's doing better at home, picking up back-to-back wins for the first time since July 15-Aug. 4, 2010.
away_pitcher_note: All questions about whether Karstens will stay in the rotation have ceased. In his best start yet, Karstens allowed the Tigers just three hits and one run in six innings on Friday. He retired the first 14 hitters and threw only 75 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Recovering from a four-run first inning Wednesday, Gee bounced back to retire 15 of the next 16 batters for a rain-shortened six-inning win. In his only career meeting against the Pirates, Gee pitched six shutout innings last September.
away_pitcher_note: Morton battled against a left-handed heavy Braves lineup in his last start, and it was a reminder that he can't rely as heavily on his sinker against lefties. Still, Morton completed seven innings for the fifth time this year.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey is the probable, but not definite, starter after leaving his last start against the Cubs after 2 2/3 innings with a partial tear of the plantar fascia of his right foot. Dickey's fitness will be determined by his bullpen session Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: After a 27-pitch first on Wednesday, McDonald settled in and retired 17 of the final 20 hitters he faced. He's had a habit of laboring through the first, though McDonald has lasted six innings in five of his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Capuano rebounded from his four-homer outing against the Yankees with six strong innings at home against the Phillies. Capuano gave up two runs (one earned) and struck out eight, tying his season high. He is 3-6 with a 6.46 ERA against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Correia became the league's first seven-game winner on Friday, and he has to be glad his next start is also on the road. Correia, now 6-1 away from home, has lasted at least six innings in nine of his 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey pitched 7 2/3 innings, but settled for a no-decision after the bullpen allowed the Phillies to rally on Saturday. Pelfrey tied a season high with 116 pitches. He struck out six, also a season high, and walked two.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm needed just 91 pitches to hurl his third career shutout, on Saturday against the Cubs. He allowed three baserunners and finally got run support. Despite his record, Maholm has allowed two or fewer runs in seven of 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: After a nine-day layoff between starts, Karstens battled through five innings in his last one against the Cubs on Sunday. He allowed just two earned runs in the outing, and he's now given up two or fewer earned runs in six of his eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels earned his win at Citi Field on Saturday, allowing two runs and striking out 10 in seven innings in a 5-2 victory against the Mets. The Phillies have won nine of Hamels' last 10 starts. He has allowed three earned runs or fewer in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Morton pitched well in his last outing against the Mets, but fell victim to a string of well-placed ground balls and two passed balls. He gave up 11 singles and three runs, but he did not allow an extra-base hit and two of the runs came unearned.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies scheduled Kendrick to make a spot start after optioning right-hander Vance Worley on Monday. Kendrick is no stranger to starting, but he is not stretched out. He said he thinks he could throw at least 65 pitches against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald allowed one run in the first inning against the Mets on Tuesday, but did not allow another in his six innings. He has now gone three straight starts in which he has pitched at least six innings and given up two earned runs or fewer.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay struggled Monday in his start against the Nationals. He allowed 10 hits, four runs and three home runs in seven innings. The three homers against Washington were one short of his career-high four, which he set last season against Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Correia notched his eighth win of the season Wednesday night against the Mets by giving up two runs in six innings. Correia is sporting a 3.40 ERA and has won his last three starts. He is 4-8 with a 4.80 ERA against Arizona lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: After holding opponents to three runs or less in six consecutive starts, Hudson has hit bumps in his past two starts, allowing five and four runs, respectively.

home_pitcher_note: The wheels fell off in the sixth inning of Malholm's last outing against the Mets on June 2. He allowed four runs in the frame, three earned, to finish with six earned runs in 5 2/3 IP. Current D-Backs are 10-for-44 against him without a homer.
away_pitcher_note: In his third start for the D-backs, Duke returns to Pittsburgh, where he spent the first six seasons of his career. In two starts for Arizona, Duke is 1-1 with a 3.00 ERA. He allowed four runs on 10 hits to the Nationals in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens continues to hold down the rotation's fifth spot as well as the Pirates could want. He lasted a season-high seven innings in his last start and threw more pitches (97) than he had in an outing since June 1, 2010.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday, Collmenter picked up where he left off before allowing two earned runs in back-to-back starts, blanking the Nationals over seven innings. The right-hander allowed only three hits, struck out five and lowered his ERA to 1.25 on the season.

home_pitcher_note: Against the Phillies on Saturday, Morton pitched seven innings, giving up two runs on six hits while striking out five batters. He has not surrendered more than two earned runs in a game since May 1.
away_pitcher_note: Gee extended his season-long unbeaten streak to eight on Saturday with six shutout innings against Atlanta. It was his second start of the year in which he didn't allow a run. He allowed three runs in seven innings in a May 30 win against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald lost his ability to repeat his delivery beginning in the fourth inning of his last start. His command evaporated as a result. McDonald ended up walking five in four innings and ended his outing with 12 straight balls.
away_pitcher_note: In his second start since partially tearing the plantar fascia in his right foot, Dickey threw eight innings against the Braves on Sunday, allowing one run on a solo homer. He gave up three runs in 7 2/3 innings his last start against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Correia left too many pitches up on Tuesday and was hurt as a result. He's still looking for more success at home, where he is 1-3 with a 5.76 ERA. Correia faced the Mets on June 1 and earned a win with six strong innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his first game against his old teammates in Milwaukee, Capuano held the Brewers to one run -- a Prince Fielder homer -- in six innings. He did not fare so well in his previous start against the Pirates, allowing five runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm pitched six innings Wednesday against the D-backs and gave up just one single and no runs. However, he came away with a no-decision. Maholm has allowed three earned runs or less in 10 of his 13 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey submitted one of his best starts of the season Wednesday against the Brewers, holding them to two runs in six efficient innings. But his previous start against the Pirates was ugly: 10 hits and seven runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Norris has won his past two starts and didn't allow a hit until the seventh inning in his last start Wednesday against St. Louis. In his past four starts, he's 2-1 with a 3.12 ERA. The Astros are 3-1 in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens has thrown a season-high seven innings in each of his past two starts. On Thursday, he blanked the D-backs, retiring 13 consecutive batters between the third and seventh innings.

home_pitcher_note: Happ already has eight losses this season. His previous high for losses was just four. He's lost his last four decisions and four of his last five starts. He had a 3.09 ERA in his previous six starts before getting roughed up Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Morton's command was absent in his last start, which lasted a season-short four-plus innings. He never established an off-speed pitch, which hurt his fastball. Morton is continuing to learn how to attack left-handed heavy lineups.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles, the 20-year-old prospect, makes his fourth Major League start and second at Minute Maid Park. He's had two quality starts, including Saturday, when he allowed eight hits and two runs in 6 1/3 innings against Braves.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald wasn't his sharpest on Saturday against the Mets, but he turned eight hits and three walks into just two runs. His efficiency was better, which is key as he tries to pitch deeper into games. He hasn't had a seven-inning start this year.

home_pitcher_note: As poor as the Indians' offense has been over the past few weeks, Tomlin has not helped his own cause, giving up six earned runs in each of his last three starts. After starting the year 6-1, he is now 7-4.
away_pitcher_note: Correia must be glad his next start is on the road, where he is 7-1 with a 2.42 ERA. Correia allowed two hits in his first six innings on Sunday before unraveling late. Still, his eight wins leads a Pirates staff that has 22.

home_pitcher_note: The Indians have won just two of their last 11 games, and both wins were by a score of 1-0, with Carrasco getting the start. Carrasco has won five of his last six starts and allowed two runs or fewer in four of them.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm hasn't allowed a run in three of his last four starts, including Monday's vs. the Mets. His record continues to be deceiving because of a lack of run support and blown saves, but he's been as consistent as anyone on the staff.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson won his first five starts of the season, but a slumping Cleveland offense has not helped him win any more games. He has given up more than three earned runs just three times this season.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens has allowed just one run in his last 20 2/3 innings over his last three starts, including none in his last two. Karstens surrendered just three hits in 6 2/3 innings on Tuesday against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Morton needed 109 pitches to get through five innings against Houston on Wednesday but still grabbed his seventh win of the season. The Astros stranded 14 men on base and left the bases loaded twice against Morton.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta pitched a quality start his last time out against the Blue Jays but still took the loss to drop to 8-4 on the season. He allowed three earned runs on nine hits while striking out five over 6 2/3 innings. He leads the O's with 69 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Though the numbers might not indicate it, McDonald has labored his last three times out. Escalating pitch counts have hindered McDonald from being able to pitch deep, and he's only thrown more than six innings once in 14 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie left his last start in Toronto with back spasms but still pitched five scoreless innings against the Blue Jays prior to his exit. He is the unquestioned ace and leader of the staff.

home_pitcher_note: Correia is looking to reverse his results at home, where he hasn't been as dominant as he has been on the road. With only one home win this year, Correia is also hoping to see improvements in his ability to pitch from the stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Britton felt he had some of the best stuff of the season on Friday, a result of extra rest. The 23-year-old lefty was charged with four runs -- only one earned -- on five hits over five innings in Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm allowed four earned runs for the second time in his last nine starts and struggled especially against Cleveland's left-handed hitters. The Pirates have scored one or fewer runs in seven of his 15 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lester misfired on Saturday against the Brewers in his first crack at 10 wins. Still, he completed eight innings and struck out eight for a second straight outing.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens had his scoreless innings streak snapped at 15 2/3 on Sunday, but that was the only earned run he allowed in seven innings. Karstens has been efficient lately, lasting at least seven innings in three of his past four games.
away_pitcher_note: The 44-year-old's knuckleball has been difficult to hit over his past six starts, when Wakefield has gone 4-1. The Pirates have won both games they played against Mets' knuckler R.A. Dickey this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates' decision to skip Charlie Morton in the rotation means McDonald will close out the homestand. McDonald has been inefficient and is still trying to avoid being knocked around the second and third times through a lineup.
away_pitcher_note: Miller was sharp in his Red Sox debut against the Padres on Monday, but one bad pitch ruined his scoreless outing, in which the lefty allowed three runs and struck out six. Miller is 1-1 with a 5.56 ERA against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes allowed four runs in 5 1/3 innings during his most recent outing against Atlanta. The four runs came on a pair of homers, which marked the second consecutive start Reyes surrendered two long balls. Reyes is now 3-2 in his past five outings.
away_pitcher_note: Seven of Correia's nine wins have come on the road, where he has a 2.34 ERA. Overall, he has pitched at least six innings in 12 of 16 outings, and the Pirates are 10-6 in his starts. He is 2-1 against the American League in 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Morrow threw seven strong innings but got a no-decision in a 5-4 win over St. Louis on Friday. Morrow has not allowed an earned run in two of his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm gave up six hits and three walks Friday, but he limited the damage to one run in 5 1/3 innings. He has held his ERA well below four since the start of May, and he has allowed one run or fewer in three of his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cecil makes his first start since being recalled from Triple-A Las Vegas on Tuesday. The 24-year-old made 12 starts for Las Vegas, going 8-2 with a 5.26 ERA. He began the season with the Blue Jays, going 1-2 with a 6.86 ERA before being sent down.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens entered uncharted waters when he eclipsed the 100-pitch mark in his last start. He ended up throwing 109, and perhaps that was too many. Two of the last four hitters he faced in his 6 2/3-inning start hit home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny will face his former team, the Pittsburgh Pirates. In his last start, Saturday against the White Sox, the right-hander gave up one run on seven hits in seven innings of work, yet still took the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Morton returns to the rotation after a 10-day layoff that was designed to help him rebuild arm strength. The Pirates believe his recent dip in results is the byproduct of how many innings he has already thrown.

home_pitcher_note: While nine of Hernandez's 11 starts against the Pirates have taken place at PNC Park, he'll face them at home this time around. Getting the win Sunday against the White Sox, the right-hander tossed 6 2/3 innings, giving up one run on eight hits.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald was noticeably more aggressive in his last start than he had been recently, but efficiency remains an issue for the righty. He has to do a better job of keeping his pitch count down early if he wants to pitch deeper.

home_pitcher_note: In four career starts against the Pirates at Nationals Park, Lannan is 0-1 with a 5.14 ERA. In his last start, Monday against the Angels, Lannan took a no-decision, going 5 2/3 innings, while giving up three runs on 11 hits.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates are expected to recall Brad Lincoln from Triple-A Indianapolis to start the finale. Lincoln, the fourth overall pick in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, is 6-7 with a 4.14 ERA for Indianapolis and hasn't pitched for Pittsburgh this year.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis hasn't lost since May 25, but has received three straight no-decisions, despite tossing eight scoreless frames against Seattle on June 23.
away_pitcher_note: Correia battled through his last outing, but the offense helped him become the third National League pitcher to reach 10 wins. Eight of those have come on the road, so Correia will have no issue staying away from home.

home_pitcher_note: Whether because of no run support or blown saves, Maholm continues to get little help. He allowed two or fewer runs in four of his six June starts, but ended the month 2-2. After his last start, he was leading the team in innings pitched.
away_pitcher_note: Myers delivered a quality start, but still took the loss in his last outing, falling, 3-2, to Texas. Myers leads the Majors in home runs allowed with 22 and has allowed at least one home run in each of his past eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: He's not flashy, but Karstens continues to get the job done almost every time. He went at least 6 2/3 innings in all six June starts and did not lose a decision. He's working quick, too, which is a sign of confidence.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez snapped the Astros' five-game losing skid by throwing seven shutout innings against the Rangers on Thursday. The southpaw is 5-1 in his last nine starts with a 1.77 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Morton had a 10-day layoff before his most recent start and the rest made a difference. He showed a fluid delivery and sharper sinker. He threw 88 pitches but should be clear to go past the 100-pitch mark.
away_pitcher_note: Norris had a one-hitter through the first six innings in his last outing before a Red Sox explosion. The Astros led, 5-1, before Boston scored six runs in the seventh inning, three of which were charged to Norris.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald has not allowed more than three earned runs in a start since May 13, and has lowered his ERA from 6.20 to 4.40 since. In his last start, against the Nationals on Saturday, he allowed two runs in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez threw seven shutout innings against the White Sox in his last start, giving up two hits and striking out three. He also was efficient, throwing 75 pitches. If Lopez can get ground-ball outs, he's effective.

home_pitcher_note: Correia picked up his 11th win Sunday and is tied for the most victories in the Major Leagues. He accounts for 25 percent of the Pirates' 44 wins.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster skipped a turn Monday against the Nationals because of discomfort in his stomach and core. He threw on Thursday, and is good to go. This will be his last start before the break and a chance to enter the second half on a positive note.

home_pitcher_note: After a string of hard-luck losses to begin the season, Maholm has won four of his last six decisions. Against Houston on Monday, he allowed three runs (one earned) in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first Major League start since May 19, 2010, Ortiz gave up three runs (two earned) on seven hits and struck out seven over six innings. He is the 10th different starter Cubs have used this season.

home_pitcher_note: Myers lasted 4 1/3 innings and gave up six runs -- five earned -- on four hits and four walks in a loss to the Marlins. Logan Morrison's bases-clearing triple in the fifth chased Myers from the game. He is 6-5 with a 3.14 ERA against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens, who began the season as the Pirates' long reliever, leads off the second half for the Bucs with a team-low ERA of 2.55, good enough for sixth-best in the National League.

home_pitcher_note: Norris faced the Pirates in his last start before the All-Star break and went seven innings, allowing just two runs on seven hits in the Astros' 8-2 win. He struck out three batters and walked two. Norris is 3-4 with a 3.74 ERA against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm matched a season-high with eight strikeouts on Sunday against Chicago. He has allowed two earned runs or less in six of his last seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struggled with his command by walking a season-high five batters and hitting another in a loss to the Marlins. The southpaw went 5 1/3 innings and gave up five runs on five hits. The Astros have won seven of his last 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Correia pledged to make changes during the All-Star break after allowing five runs in 3 2/3 innings on Saturday against the Cubs. An All-Star appearance may give him less time to work on mechanics, though.

home_pitcher_note: Morton hasn't pitched six innings in a start since throwing seven frames on June 4. After allowing one run in 5 2/3 innings on July 1, Morton surrendered five runs in 5 1/3 innings against Houston in his most recent outing.
away_pitcher_note: Willis made his first big league start in more than a year on July 10 at Milwaukee. The high-kicking soutpaw looked pretty sharp, allowing two earned on four hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald has allowed three runs or fewer in each of his last 10 starts. He has allowed exactly three runs in four of his last seven trips to the hill, including his most recent outing against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Leake has been solid since a brief stint with Triple-A in late May. In nine starts since, the righty is 5-2 with a 3.39 ERA. Most recently, though, he lasted just 5 1/3 and gave up five earned against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens' 83-pitch shutout against the Astros in his last outing marked the least amount of pitches thrown in a shutout since Aaron Cook threw 79 in a start for the Rockies in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto has gone four outings without a victory, though all have been quality starts. The right-hander has logged at least seven innings in eight of his last nine trips to the hill and sports a 2.01 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm continues to be a rock the Bucs' rotation. He has allowed more than two earned runs in just two of his last eight starts and has a 1.93 in 11 season starts at PNC Park. The lefty has not faced the Cardinals yet this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals have won Carpenter's last five starts, and he has a 1.66 ERA in that span. He gets the ball in the opener of a pivotal series in a park where he's had considerable success.

home_pitcher_note: Correia's ERA has steadily climbed since mid-June, but the right-hander is, for the most part, still pitching deep. He has lasted six innings in five of his last seven outings. Just two of Correia's wins have come at home.

away_pitcher_note: Lee returned to Philadelphia to help the Phillies form one of baseball's most formidable rotations. He lived up to the hype, finishing third in NL Cy Young Award voting.

home_pitcher_note: None of the Pirates are as glad for Spring Training to be over than McDonald, who gets to push the reset button after a shaky preseason. He won't miss injured Phils Ryan Howard and Chase Utley, who have a combined .555 average against him.
away_pitcher_note: Roy Oswalt and Joe Blanton suffered injuries last season, but Worley picked up the slack. He finished third in NL Rookie of the Year Award voting, proving to be a valuable piece of the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw gets a do-over of his Opening Day start. After lasting only three innings in San Diego on Thursday before leaving with the flu, he takes the ball in the home opener and the 50th anniversary of Dodger Stadium's debut.
away_pitcher_note: Who better to pitch the Pirates' first away game than Correia, whose road getaway in '11 (5-0, 1.56 ERA) was compelling enough to land him on the All-Star team. It was all downhill from there, but now he gets to try to regain the fans' confidence.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start of the season, Billingsley responded to Don Mattingly's challenge to step up with 8 1/3 scoreless and 11 strikeouts. He is using his cutter to pitch to the right side of the plate and the slider to the left side of the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard gave the Pirates everything they could have hoped for in his Opening Day assignment, but they didn't give him any offensive support. He doesn't throw as hard as he did in his Baltimore days, but is becoming the prototypical wily left-hander.

home_pitcher_note: Chris Capuano cruised through four innings against the Padres, then couldn't throw a strike, walking a total of five and not getting out of the fifth inning. He said he will attack the strike zone more aggressively next time.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Clint Hurdle expects Karstens to "run with this opportunity" to be in the season-opening rotation, and he got off to a fast start with six innings of five-hit ball Saturday. When he keeps the ball down, the righty is very tough.

home_pitcher_note: After being staked to a six-run lead in his first start, against the D-backs, Cain let up five runs in the fourth and sixth innings in a game the Giants went on to lose. He gave up six hits (two homers) and two walks while striking out four.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald hopes to build on a rarity for him: two straight solid starts, albeit the first of those wasin Spring Training. But he was tough on Sunday against the Phillies, escaping multiple jams to hold them to two runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Zito threw a shutout at Coors Field in his 2012 debut, using pinpoint control and a crafty mix of four pitches to keep the Rockies off-balance.  Zito pitched backward, setting up hitters with his curve and changeup and spotting his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Morton merges into the rotation after a couple rehab outings that completed his gradual comeback from hip surgery in October. Morton opened the season on the disabled, and he threw 98 pitches in a Monday rehab start.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Vogelsong's first regular-season appearance. His progress has been delayed by back pain that bothered him as spring began. Vogelsong also made his first two starts of 2011 against the Bucs and Mets (his next opponent).
away_pitcher_note: The 2011 road warrior (10-3, 2.64) continued to be one Tuesday in L.A., allowing a run in six efficient innings. A former Giants pitcher (2003-08), Correia knows AT&T Park well, but he was primarily a reliever then. This will be his 28th start there.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders was impressive in his first start of the year, as he tossed seven shutout innings against the Padres at Petco Park. The left-hander allowed four hits and walked two while striking out four. Saunders did not face the Pirates in 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Veteran lefty signed to set a pace for a young staff certainly has, but only in hard-luck losses. Seeks to avoid a repeat of last season's 0-4 start.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy beat the Padres in his last start allowing just one run on five hits over six innings. One of his finest starts of 2011 came against the Pirates when he fanned 12 and allowed one hit in eight shutout innings.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens has endured rough first innings in both of his starts before settling down, and it upset him enough to make a point of changing his mindset.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson suffered through a miserable start on Friday against the Rockies. He had trouble finding his release point and couldn't get in rhythm, allowing six runs in 3 2/3 innings. Last year in two starts vs. the Pirates, Hudson was 0-1 with 3.00 ERA
away_pitcher_note: Two straight solid starts to begin the season is a welcome novelty for McDonald, still considered the difference-maker for the Pirates staff.

home_pitcher_note: Morton was workmanlike in first start of the season, on Saturday, needing 71 pitches to get through five innings against the Giants. He is 2-5 in nine starts vs. the Cards.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn has allowed one run in his two starts and has proven plenty capable of holding down Chris Carpenter's spot. There is room for Lynn to improve the quality of his offspeed pitches. Doing so would increase the effectiveness of his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett returns from the 15-day disabled list to replace Kevin Correia, who experienced discomfort in his left side.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook recorded 16 of his 21 outs Sunday via a ground ball, a terrific sign for the sinker-baller. He was more efficient in his second outing than his first, allowing him to finish seven frames. Westbrook is 2-0 for the first time since '06.

home_pitcher_note: Making his first career appearance against the Cardinals is an opportunity for Bedard to end his streak of tough-luck defeats, as the Cards are vulnerable vs. lefties.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse would have been the NL's second three-game winner had the bullpen not lost a lead in his start on Tuesday. Lohse showcased terrific fastball command in the outing and has pitched ahead in the count consistently all year.

home_pitcher_note: Correia was scratched from his start Saturday, but he insists his left side is fine. In his last outing on April 14 in a 4-1 victory over the Giants, he allowed one run on three hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer tossed seven innings Tuesday, allowing just two unearned runs on six hits to pick up his first win of the season. At 49 years of age, he became the oldest pitcher in Major League history to record a victory.

home_pitcher_note: Correia was scratched from his start Saturday, but he insists his left side is fine. In his last outing on April 14 in a 4-1 victory over the Giants, he allowed one run on three hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer tossed seven innings Tuesday, allowing just two unearned runs on six hits to pick up his first win of the season. At 49 years of age, he became the oldest pitcher in Major League history to record a victory.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald was removed after allowing one run and three hits in four innings on Wednesday against the Diamondbacks.
away_pitcher_note: In his second start at Coors Field since suffering a broken neck and fractured skull last Aug. 5, Nicasio picked up his first win of the year Wednesday. The right-hander tossed 6 1/3 innings, allowing four runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Charlie Morton pitched well in a losing effort against the Cardinals on Friday, allowing just one earned run on four hits in five innings of work. He struck out six and walked three, though he needed 93 pitches to get through his five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Dominant through five innings on Friday vs. the Brewers, a rough sixth kept Chacin from getting his first win of the season. The right-hander retired the first 10 batters he faced, and allowed three runs on four hits over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson was charged with two runs on five hits in seven strong innings for the win against the D-backs in his last outing. He credits an improved command of his fastball and breaking pitches for his success. He retired the last 13 batters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: A.J. Burnett's Pirates debut was not only a best-case scenario, but a scenario no one could've envisioned after his rocky rehab outings. But the veteran got it all together to blank St. Louis on three hits through seven, with seven strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado impressed when he pitched into the sixth inning after imploding with two outs in a five-run second inning against the D-backs on Sunday. He has continued to find success despite struggling to command his curve.
away_pitcher_note: In 24 innings, the lefty has allowed seven runs -- and received three runs of support. In 2011, Bedard also had an 0-4 record, but with an ERA of 7.71. His changes of speed and command have played well against NL lineups more used to fastball diets.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson will be making his season debut. The veteran hurler has been encouraged with the relief he has experienced since undergoing back surgery in November. He has posted a 2.85 ERA in 11 career starts against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Three days after being scratched from a start with left-side discomfort, Correia made a miraculous recovery to pitch four-hit ball for six innings vs. the Rockies. His history in Turner Field is short (three starts, 16 innings) and sweet (2.25 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Minor has completed at least six innings in three consecutive starts and showed increased confidence since the start of Spring Training. The lefty has limited opponents to a .208 batting average in his past three starts.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald has battled inconsistency in the past, but will try to continue the best stretch of his young career. He has as many strikeouts (14) as hits allowed in 22 2/3 innings, and he is developing the confidence to pitch aggressively.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright showed signs of getting back on track in his last outing. He allowed one run and struck out seven in six innings. Now he just needs run support. In Wainwright's four starts, the Cards have not scored a run while he's been on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Morton's delayed season -- he remained in extended spring camp until April 14, recovering from hip surgery -- is in full swing largely due to the effectiveness of his breaking stuff, which he has been able to set up with inside fastballs.

home_pitcher_note: In the rotation because of an injury to Chris Carpenter, Lynn became the Majors' first four-game winner his last time out. He has fooled hitters with his use of three fastballs and two off-speed pitches. He maintains velocity deep into outings, too.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett will make his first Busch Stadium appearance since 2005. He owns a 2.08 ERA in three starts there. The Cards were foils for his stellar Bucs debut on April 21, when he blanked them on three hits through seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook, thriving with his sinker, has gone at least 6 2/3 innings in each of his first four starts for the first time in his career. Asked if Friday's win over Milwaukee was the best start he's ever had to date, Westbrook said, "Without a doubt."
away_pitcher_note: Getting some runs on Saturday in Atlanta turned Bedard into the best 1-4 pitcher in baseball. The veteran's moxie is beginning to show through, and his ability to vary his approach the second and third times through a lineup confounds batters.

home_pitcher_note: Correia comes off an odd game against the Braves in which he walked five without recording a strikeout. Still, it was his fourth start without yielding more than two earned runs, so he's been giving the Bucs consistent outings.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto racked up 120 pitches over seven frames vs. Houston last time out, in part because his throwing more than 50 pitches over the first two. But he settled down and retired 10 of his final 11 batters, including the last seven.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald has taken his game to a new level, pitching one-hit ball for seven innings in one start, then coming back with a 10-strikeout effort. It's all about confidence and pacing: He's been working faster and maintaining his focus.
away_pitcher_note: Leake hasn't been very good lately with 16 runs (13 earned) allowed over 15 2/3 innings in his last three starts. With Aroldis Chapman potentially waiting in the wings, a good start could help Leake significantly.

home_pitcher_note: Morton is coming off his worst start of 2012, giving up five earned runs in 4 1/3 innings of a 10-7 loss at St. Louis on Tuesday. He gave up a three-run homer to David Freese in the fifth that broke a 2-2 tie. Morton struck out five and walked two.
away_pitcher_note: Latos is 2-8 with a 5.73 ERA and 14 homers allowed lifetime in April since 2010. The good news is he's been much better in the other months. In 12 career May starts, he is 7-3 with a 2.41 ERA and five homers allowed.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett is coming off the worst outing of his career. He gave up 12 earned runs in 2 2/3 innings in a 12-3 loss on Wednesday. He allowed just two earned runs over 13 innings during his first two starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson allowed four earned runs in six innings against the D-backs on Wednesday. He allowed eight hits, walked two batters and struck out three in the game. Jackson picked up his third no-decison of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard fanned 11 in five innings in St. Louis. The lefty struck out seven in a row at one point. He gave up two runs in the first, then shut the Cards down on two hits over his final four frames. He has won two in a row after losing four straight.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler allowed a run in 6 1/3 innings against the Diamondbacks on Thursday. Since he was picked over John Lannan to be the fifth starter at the end of Spring Training, Detwiler has been almost unhittable.

home_pitcher_note: Correia makes his 15th PNC Park start as a Pirate, still looking for third win at home. Dating to 2011, has won one of his last nine starts. Location spoiled the good stuff in his last two starts (eight runs in 11 1/3 innings vs. Reds and Braves.)
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg lasted six innings against the Phillies on Friday, allowing three hits and three earned runs -- all coming on homers -- while striking out four and walking one in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald turned a corner by perfectly adopting the approach the Bucs want all their pitchers to follow: Get quick outs if possible but, once you get two strikes on a batter, try to finish him off. He's finished off 25 in his last 21 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Norris will be making his seventh start of the season, and first against the Pirates. He's 4-4 in eight starts against the Pirates. Norris didn't allow an earned run in six innings in his last start Saturday vs. the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Morton spent time between starts trying to re-discover the hard sinker that has right-handed hitters pounding the ball into the ground, rather than hitting it out of the park. Has already allowed four homers to them, compared to one all last year.
away_pitcher_note: Happ allowed four walks and two homers, tying his season highs in both categories, in his previous start Sunday vs. the Cardinals. He's delivered quality starts for the Astros in four of his six starts (team is 3-3).

home_pitcher_note: The current king of misleading stats. Remove the 2 2/3-inning (12 earned runs) start in St. Louis, and Burnett's ERA is 1.71 for three other starts. Last time out, had his best curve in a while and relied on it almost exclusively, fanning 10 Nats.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is coming off his worst outing of the season stat-wise, but he still didn't pitch poorly. Rodriguez was the first Astros starter to work into the ninth, but he was done in by three homers Monday against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez turned in perhaps his best performance of the season Tuesday in Houston, going seven innings while allowing no earned runs on five hits. He struck out eight and walked two, but got a no-decision when the Marlins blew a 2-0 lead in a 3-2 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Lincoln makes his first start, subbing for Erik Bedard (back spasms), after excelling in scattered relief chores. His ERA is third-best among NL relievers. Lincoln made 17 starts for the Bucs in 2010-11 (5.54 ERA in them), but is more confident now.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson had arguably his best outing of the year his last time out, a seven-inning, two-run effort against Houston in which he fanned six and walked two. He is 2-0 with a 1.64 ERA in his career against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Correia hopes to stay away from that one inning that seems to hurt him every start, spoiling good overall efforts. Has lacked a put-away pitch, but competes well. Even he may be buying into that "road killer" rep; he's lost four of 17 road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez picked up his fourth win in five decisions by striking out nine in five innings in a win at Cincinnati. Gonzalez threw 115 pitches and walked four in his shortest outing since going 3 2/3 innings April 7 at Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard gets his Mulligan against Washington, the team he was facing last week when ousted after an inning with back spasms. The Pirates will keep a close eye on the lefty to make sure he doesn't alter his normal delivery to favor his back.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann picked up his second win of the season by going seven innings and striking out nine in a 2-1 victory at Cincinnati. He lowered his ERA to 2.14 and has allowed just 37 hits in 46 1/3 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald will try to extend a stretch of domination that has seen him ring up almost twice as many strikeouts (33) as hits allowed (18) in his last four starts, covering 29 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Few pitchers in recent years have dominated Interleague Play like Verlander, 15-2 with a 2.94 ERA for his career against the National League. He won all three of his Interleague starts last year, allowing two runs on 15 hits over 24 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Morton was solid in his last start, holding the Braves to a pair of runs (one earned) over six innings to snap a two-start losing streak. The righty will try to carry his success into Interleague Play, where he is 1-2 with a 7.50 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly was removed from his start against Chicago after five innings and only 69 pitches as manager Jim Leyland didn't like how the lefty was leaving the ball up. He allowed two two-run homers in just his second non-quality start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett threw eight strong innings and came away with a no-decision for the second straight start. The righty held the Astros to two runs on six hits in a game the Bucs won in extra innings. He is 4-2 with a 6.33 ERA in eight starts vs. the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer struggled in his last outing, allowing six runs (five earned) on eight hits against the White Sox. The righty worked just four-plus innings, throwing 99 pitches. He has a 3.98 ERA in four career outings (three starts) against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Correia had a tough time against the Marlins, allowing six runs on eight hits over 3 2/3 innings. The right-hander will look to bounce back against the Tigers in Interleague Play, where he is 5-5 with a 3.87 ERA over 86 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard recovered in fine style from his brief bout with back spasms, keeping Washington down until allowing consecutive homers with two outs in the sixth. Most of his 44 strikeouts in 41 innings have come on breaking balls.
away_pitcher_note: Santana has five straight quality starts, but has wound up with no-decisions in four of those. The lefty has rung up more strikeouts (46) than he's allowed hits (37), and he's held the opposition to two runs or fewer in five of his eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: It has been a bona fide breakthrough season thus far for the lanky right-hander, who has flirted with no-hitters twice in his last five starts and has 44 punchouts in his last 34 2/3 innings. He has been flourishing with a true 12-to-6 curve ball.
away_pitcher_note: Dickey had his fifth consecutive quality start last time out, marking his 19th quality start in 20 outings dating back to last year. Dickey took the loss in his only start in '11 at PNC Park, despite holding the Bucs to one earned run over eight.

home_pitcher_note: In an on-and-off season, Morton should be on again after yielding four runs in six innings by Detroit. Not coincidentally, he has struggled to find consistency with his bread-and-butter sinker.
away_pitcher_note: Among the lowlights of Niese's worst start of the season were a career-high four homers and eight total runs against the Blue Jays, increasing the left-hander's ERA from 3.40 to 4.85. Niese is 1-0 with a 2.45 ERA in two career starts vs. the Bucs.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett showed his veteran wiles by winning a start Saturday in Detroit in which he had two strikeouts, his fewest in a winning start of six-plus innings since April 11, 2010. But when the hook is biting, still has days when he's a power pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster is trying to end a 16-game winless streak. He had command issues in his last start, and has given up four runs in each of his last two outings. The Cubs have scored three or fewer runs in six of his seven starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Correia showed the strain of the top-shelf opposition he's been drawing after being the victim Sunday of Max Scherzer's 15-strikeout gem. He depends on control, which he had against the Tigers after a pair of uncharacteristic wild outings.
away_pitcher_note: This will be a homecoming for Maholm, who pitched for six-plus years with the Pirates before signing this offseason with the Cubs. His four-game win streak was snapped in his last start by the White Sox. He could use some run support.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty keeps giving the Bucs everything they could have hoped for, having put up zeros in 33 of his 46 innings and averaging more than a strikeout an inning. Yet he comes off his two poorest starts, allowing four runs to both the Nats and Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Garza is coming off his shortest outing, in which he lasted three innings against the Astros, allowing two homers and giving up seven runs, the most by a Cubs starter this year. He had given up three HRs over 45 1/3 innings in his other seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Bucs' most consistent starter has held opponents to a .184 average in his last six starts (41 2/3 innings), a span in which he has a 52-12 strikeout-walk ratio.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo has five quality starts out of his nine games this season. During a 6 2/3-innings no-decision vs. the Braves on Wednesday, he threw first-pitch strikes to 17 of his 26 batters faced. His only bad pitch resulted in a solo homer by Dan Uggla.

home_pitcher_note: Morton's inconsistencies are reflected in the Pirates having gone 2-6 in his first eight starts. He's dealing with the awareness that when he can't keep his sinker down, his stuff isn't good enough to keep hitters in the park.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey has notched seven quality starts out of his nine games this season and has been quite effective of late. "The thing for him that's coming along is he's throwing everything for strikes," catcher Devin Mesoraco said.

home_pitcher_note: Two starts removed from being the National League's most efficient hurler, Burnett needed 105 pitches in 5 1/3 innings of his most recent start but still gutted out a victory over the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto has given up more than three earned runs in a start twice, but it's happened in two of his past three starts. He gave up five over 4 2/3 innings in a loss Friday. Cueto said his breaking ball was lacking and opened up too much in his delivery.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf has remained winless since April 30, when a Brewers lead slipped away in the sixth inning Sunday. But he's been effective at home, with a 3.60 ERA in five Miller Park starts this season after logging a 3.56 ERA there in 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Not even the Pirates' road king has been exempt from the club's recent woes in Miller Park, where Correia has one win in 11 career games. Two of the losses came last season, when otherwise he was 10-1 on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum threw a career-high 119 pitches in a Memorial Day win over the Dodgers that marked his best start of the season. He'll look to avoid the sort of drop-off he endured soon after a 116-pitch outing last August.
away_pitcher_note: Maybe what the Pirates' deference to the Brewers needs: A fresh face. Bedard has never faced Milwaukee. He rebounded from his two poorest starts of the season to blank the Cubs through six on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old frustrated the Dodgers over seven innings in his first Major League start, and he should be particularly tough on opponents the first time they see him because of his deceptive delivery.
away_pitcher_note: J-Mac hasn't had trouble coming up with an encore; in fact, he's had eight straight of them, lowering his ERA each time, from 3.86 to the current figure. He's the toughest Major League righty to homer off of (two in 65 1/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Bailey was sensational in his last start, throwing a complete game four-hitter against the same Pirates he'll face Tuesday. He threw 77 strikes, a season-high. His ERA dropped steadily in May and is now down to 3.73.
away_pitcher_note: One of the season's fun stats just grows in popularity with every Burnett outing: Take away that 12-run hiccup in St. Louis, and his ERA for his other seven starts is 1.52. He has allowed a total of eight runs in those other starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto has been up and down in his last four starts, going seven innings in two and not making it through the fifth inning in the other two. His ERA, which was 1.12 on May 9, is now up to 2.54, the highest it's been in 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Lincoln makes his second start, filling in for Charlie Morton -- who's on the DL -- three weeks after going six solid innings in the first, a 3-2 victory in Miami. He has been valuable in any role, including long and short relief.

home_pitcher_note: After a shaky start against the Rockies, Leake bounced back with a strong seven-inning outing in Houston, throwing 108 pitches and giving up just one run. He hasn't given up more than three earned runs since May 11.
away_pitcher_note: Correia fell one out shy of his seventh quality start of the season in his last outing, but gladly traded that gold star for a win. He has won only one of those six quality efforts, and the frustration was getting to him.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard allowed five earned runs in five innings on Saturday in Milwaukee in a 5-1 loss. Bedard has lost two of his past three decisions after winning two straight.
away_pitcher_note: Since pitching seven scoreless innings in a May 12 win at Chicago, Hochevar has three losses and a 5.72 ERA in his four starts without a victory. His pitch counts have soared -- 104 and then 90 in his last two outings of just 4 2/3 frames.

home_pitcher_note: MacDonald pitched six strong innings on Sunday in Milwaukee. He allowed only one earned run on four hits. His control was exceptional, with just one walk and eight strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: On his second recall from Triple-A, Mazzaro is coming off six shutout innings in a 2-0 win over the A's on Sunday. He gave up four hits and three walks but kept working out of trouble, pulled after he reached 97 pitches. He also won May 15 at Texas.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett allowed just five hits on Tuesday, but an elevated pitch-count forced him to exit after five innings. Burnett gave up three earned runs, walked four and struck out eight. He threw 100 pitches, 57 strikes.
away_pitcher_note: In his first six starts, Chen was 0-4; in his last six starts, he's 5-1. He was superb at changing speeds in his last start, a 1-0 win over the Twins. This will be his fourth career start at PNC Park; he lost the other three.

home_pitcher_note: Chen was stellar in his last outing, allowing only one run in seven innings Wednesday at Boston. Chen's fastball command has been critical to the rookie's hot start.
away_pitcher_note: Lincoln was effective for four innings Wednesday before running out of gas. He needed 66 pitches to get through four, allowing five earned runs on six hits. Making just his second start this season, Lincoln's location issues might've been fatigue.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta gets the start, replacing Brian Matusz, Matusz was struck in the face with a ball prior to Tuesday's game.
away_pitcher_note: Correia allowed solo homers to Jay Bruce and Ryan Ludwick Thursday, both on first pitches leading off an inning. Correia finished with three runs allowed on eight hits in five innings, with one walk and four K's over 77 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter will make his second career appearance vs. the Bucs after coming off a solid seven-inning performance against Philly in which he scattered eight hits, three for solo home runs. The O's are 7-4 in Hunter's 11 starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard is starting against Baltimore, the team that drafted him, for just the third time. In both previous outings, he lasted into the seventh inning and struck out seven batters. Matt Wieters homered off him last year.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson took the loss in his last start against the Cardinals on Saturday but also threw his seventh quality start of the season. He allowed one run on five hits while walking none. His lone mistake was a solo shot by Carlos Beltran.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald's command was off in his last start, and he allowed three runs on five hits and two walks in only four innings. Still, McDonald is yet to allow more than three runs in a start during his breakout 2012 season.

home_pitcher_note: Jiménez called his most recent outing his best yet with Cleveland, and for good reason. The righty allowed one run on five hits through seven innings. He set a season-high with seven K's and didn't a walk a batter for the first time this year.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett carried a no-hitter into the sixth inning in his last outing, allowing two runs on five hits in 7 1/2 innings. Removing his disastrous 12-run start May 2 against St. Louis, Burnett has posted a 1.96 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Gomez pitched well in his last start at Cincinnati, but he took the loss when the bullpen let the game get away. After allowing 11 combined earned runs in his previous two starts, Gomez allowed only one against the Reds on six hits in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lincoln said his arm felt fine throwing a season-high 88 pitches in his third start, but his command was off as he took the loss. If he doesn't keep the ball down and stay aggressive, he could go back to the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Correia's dependence on pinpoint control was evident in his last start, when he lacked it and allowed a season-high 10 hits. The righty will be pitching for his second win in 11 starts -- and possibly for his spot in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Diamond saw his streak of four straight quality starts come to an end on Thursday against the Phillies, as he surrendered four runs on five hits over six innings. He was hurt by two homers, including a three-run blast given up to Jim Thome.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard has been much more effective at home, pitching to a 2.45 ERA in six starts compared to a 6.27 ERA away from PNC Park. The left-hander is 2-5 with a 4.13 ERA in 12 career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano gave up just one hit in six innings against the Brewers on Friday, but it was a costly one, as he served up a three-run blast to Ryan Braun in the sixth. He struggled with his control, as he walked four and hit a batter.

home_pitcher_note: The record isn't bad, but in his no-decisions McDonald has been almost as good, with a 2.57 ERA in those five starts. He has allowed four homers in 81 1/3 innings, compared to 24 a year ago in 171 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hendriks, making his first big league start since May 2, had trouble keeping the ball in the park against the Brewers on Saturday. He gave up three homers, including two to Ryan Braun, to get saddled with the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett will seek to win a seventh consecutive start for the first time since 2005. Beginning with a pair of no-decisions, he is 6-0 in his last eight starts with a 2.19 ERA and .218 OBA and 41 strikeouts in 53 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Fister returned Saturday from a three-week stay on the disabled list with a left side strain and looked like he was in midseason form, tossing six scoreless innings with six strikeouts against the Rockies to earn his first win of the year.

home_pitcher_note: His recent starts nearly cost Lincoln his spot in the rotation, but the former No. 1 Draft choice's potential saved it. The Pirates still hope to have him get comfortable as a starter after being an early-season relief hit.
away_pitcher_note: Few, if any, pitchers in baseball have run as hot and cold this season as Scherzer, whose eight scoreless innings with no walks and 12 strikeouts Sunday marked his sixth outing with nine or more strikeouts in 14 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Correia ended a winless year in PNC Park by beating Minnesota on Tuesday, yet needing 97 pitches to get through 5 1/3 innings was short of convincing. The Pirates want to see more before considering his job safe.
away_pitcher_note: After losing three consecutive starts from mid-May into June, Verlander has gotten back rolling with back-to-back wins against the NL. He'll get one more Interleague outing against a Pirates team he nearly no-hit May 18 at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton has allowed a troubling 16 home runs in 41 1/3 innings over his last eight starts. He also has allowed five or more earned runs in six of his last seven starts to give him a 7.44 ERA in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens makes his long-awaited return, from mostly shoulder inflammation and more recently a hip-flexor tweak. This will be his first start since April 17, when he departed after one inning with the shoulder issue.

home_pitcher_note: Worley allowed four hits, two runs, two walks, one home run and struck out two in seven innings Thursday against Colorado. He has a 2.78 ERA this season and a 2.25 ERA in four starts since returning from the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard stopped a three-start slide (14 runs in 14 innings) by hurling four-hit ball for six innings his last time out, but now needs to halt a road skid. He's allowed 16 runs in his last three away starts, covering 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Valdes will start Wednesday's game against the Pirates. It's a bullpen game after the Phillies used Cole Hamels and Cliff Lee in a doubleheader Sunday against the Tampa Bay Rays. It's Valdes' second big league start.
away_pitcher_note: The night the Miami Heat won the NBA title, McDonald was baseball's King James, hurling his first career complete game. He hasn't allowed more than three runs in any of his 14 starts, recording the National League's fourth-lowest ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick has really struggled in his past four starts, carrying an 8.10 ERA in that span. To make matters worse, he has lasted just four innings twice and has pitched six innings just once. He's hoping for better Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett goes for his eighth consecutive winning start, which would match the run Dock Ellis had for the 1974 Pirates. Though comfortable at PNC Park, Burnett has had issues on the road, giving up five homers in 26 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After early-season ups and downs, Wainwright appears to have found his footing. He has a 3.02 ERA over his last eight starts and has allowed two or fewer earned runs in seven of his last 10 outings. He's made three consecutive seven-inning starts.
away_pitcher_note: Save a first-inning, two-run home run from the Tigers' Quintin Berry, Correia had a very good outing. The right-hander allowed just those two runs on six hits over six innings. He also struck out four and walked just one.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn's ERA jumped from 2.42 to 3.23 over his past two starts, neither of which lasted more than 5 1/3 innings. Lynn's results have progressively slipped each month, leaving some to wonder if fatigue is setting in with the first-year starter.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since spending more than two months on the disabled list with shoulder and hip issues, Karstens did not have his best stuff in a loss to the Phillies. He allowed six runs, but said he felt fine health-wise afterward.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook didn't factor into the decision in a wild, and confusing, 10-inning affair in Miami, but he turned in a quality start nonetheless. Westbrook tossed six innings and gave up two runs, both earned, on six hits as he lowered his ERA to 3.77.
away_pitcher_note: Against the Cardinals, Bedard will look to record his 1,000th career strikeout. He finished Tuesday's start against the Phillies -- a 5-4 loss -- two shy of the mark. The left-hander will also try to snap his four-start road losing streak.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald picked up his seventh win of the season in Philadelphia. According to the Elias Sports Bureau, McDonald became the first Pirates pitcher since Todd Richie in 1999 to get a win after allowing a pair of first-inning home runs.
away_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old is coming into his own. He's coming off two of the best career starts, going 1-1 with a 2.03 ERA in a tough-luck loss to the Royals and a win over the Padres in which he allowed one run in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett won his eighth consecutive game and the Pirates won for the 10th consecutive time in games he started with a 5-4 victory over Philadelphia. Burnett worked 6 2/3 innings and struck out seven to notch his ninth win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell is coming off his first career complete game, a six-hit shutout in a 1-0 win over the Padres on Wednesday. He's 1-1 with a 0.56 ERA in last two starts, having allowed eight hits and striking out 16 in 16 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Correia's allowed a homer in five of his six starts in June after giving up a three-run bomb in his most recent appearance. Correia was tagged for five earned runs, the most he'd allowed since May 15, over five innings in a win against the Cards.
away_pitcher_note: The soft-tossing lefty makes his fourth career start and first on the road since his June 17 debut in Arlington. He's given up only 14 hits and walked nine in 20 career innings, allowing one earned run in all starts.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens struck out a season-high seven while allowing two runs over seven innings in his second outing since returning from the DL. Karstens changed speeds effectively, and didn't allow a runner past second base in six of his seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Norris returned from the DL, where he landed June 12 with a sprained ankle, and allowed four runs and seven hits in six innings in his last start Friday against the Cubs. All four of the runs he allowed were via home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard lasted 4 2/3 innings and allowed five runs on eight hits in St. Louis in his previous start. He is much better at home, posting a 2.31 ERA in seven starts at PNC Park and allowing 32 earned runs in 43 2/3 innings on the road.
