away_pitcher_note: Despite a lack of control that led to six walks, Zito held the Reds to one run in six innings his last time out in a 2-1 loss. The only time Zito faced the Pirates this year, he held them to two earned runs in seven innings in the Giants' 4-3 win.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, McDonald shook off a shaky start before picking up a win against Houston. The righty had command issues early, but allowed just two runs in seven innings. He is 4-1 with 1.73 ERA at PNC Park this season.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong's seven-inning, two-run outing last time out gives him 12 straight quality starts and seven straight starts of at least seven innings. He has a 3.54 ERA on the road compared to 1.29 at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett gave up six earned runs his last time out, which equaled the total he had previously allowed at PNC Park all year. The veteran's string of eight straight wins snapped, but Burnett still hasn't lost a game since May 2.
away_pitcher_note: The eight runs Lincecum allowed last Tuesday at Washington, where the heat bothered him, represented a career high. His road ERA swelled to 8.45 in nine starts. The Giants are just 4-13 when he pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke took the loss on Saturday after pitching to only two batters before getting ejected. He came back on Sunday but only lasted three innings and got a no-decision. Greinke allowed five hits and three runs while striking out five and walking two.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald opens up the second half five days after reaching a career zenith with his no-walk, 10-strikeout outing against the Giants. It was his third double-digit strikeout game of the season; his previous career high had been nine.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has allowed five earned runs and nine hits in 15 effective innings since returning from the disabled list, where he spent a month with a groin strain. Current Pirates are 7-for-41 (.171) against Estrada.
away_pitcher_note: Correia last pitched on Independence Day, when he allowed three earned runs in six innings. He gave up two earned on five hits in 5 2/3 innings in his last outing against the Brewers on June 1.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo capped the first half with six consecutive quality starts, a run that dropped his ERA from 4.50 to 3.74. The Brewers have won his last three starts at Miller Park.
away_pitcher_note: After taking losses in two of his first three starts, Burnett won nine of his last 12 decisions heading into the break. He hasn't lost since May 2, which is also the last time he failed to go at least five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Francis pitched well in his last start on a blistering day at Washington, but he saw the two runners who were on base when he departed score because of sloppy defense, taking the loss. He has been the team's most consistent starter.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens had his best outing since being on the disabled list for two months on July 5, pitching eight scoreless innings, allowing four hits and walking just one batter. He also registered a season-high eight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Friedrich outdueled Cliff Lee in his last start, giving up one run in six innings against the Phillies. The win, his first since early June, gave him more than any Rockies pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard is winless in his last five starts, recording four losses and a no-decision since June 8. He gave up four or more runs in each of his last three outings, including when he went just 3 2/3 innings on July 6.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie has struggled mightily at Coors Field this year, with a 9.23 ERA and 12 homers given up. In his last home start, against the Phillies, he gave up four runs in 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald struggled in his last outing, going just 4 2/3 innings and matching a season high with five walks. He surrendered four earned runs on eight hits and struck out two batters after striking out 10 in his prior start.

home_pitcher_note: Correia retired the final 11 batters he faced Saturday and stuck around long enough to procure a win after the Pirates rallied in the top of the seventh. He matched a personal best by winning his fourth straight decision.
away_pitcher_note: It was a baffling last start for Nolasco -- who held Washington hitless for four innings, only to wind up giving up four runs in 5 1/3 frames in a loss. Nolasco is 5-3 (2.10 ERA) lifetime vs. the Pirates, and 2-3 (3.82 ERA) at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett makes only his second career start against his original big-league club, seeking to start a winning streak after his first loss in 13 starts on Sunday. Still, he was sharp, as he struck out seven against zero walks.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano was in jams for most of his last start, but the right-hander induced four double plays to limit the Nationals to three runs on eight hits over six innings. Zambrano earned his first win since June 3.

home_pitcher_note: With a fresh arm after two-plus months on the DL, Karstens has gone seven-plus innings in three straight starts. An off-the-table curve has been his chief weapon, but he has struggled a bit with allowing big innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: After two straight no-decisions, Sanchez opened the road trip with a win at Wrigley Field. He gave up two runs (one earned) while striking out seven in seven innings. On May 14, Sanchez lost to the Pirates in Miami.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard came out of the 11-day layoff surrounding the All-Star break sharp on Tuesday, holding Colorado to two runs in the longest (6 2/3 innings) of his last six starts. Remarkably, a sixth win would match his most since 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija needs to keep his pitch count down. In his last start against the Marlins, he was pulled after throwing 97 pitches over five innings. He has one win in his last eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: After not giving up more than three runs in any of his first 16 starts, McDonald has allowed four-plus in three of the last five. He hasn't had his putaway slider of late, but he has become a fierce competitor who doesn't give in.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm, who pitched seven seasons with the Pirates before signing with the Cubs this offseason, makes his second start in Pittsburgh this year. He took a no-decision on May 26, but is riding a four-game winning streak in which he has an 0.89 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The righty, who could win only on the road last season, has a superior record (4-3) at PNC Park. Correia will try to add on to his career-long streak of five straight wins. But he has needed support for that: He has a 4.05 ERA across the stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster's scoreless-innings streak was snapped in an eight-pitch span in the first inning vs. the Cardinals on Friday as they scored three quick runs. He recovered, and gave up three hits after that. He's 0-1 vs. Pirates this year.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel was hit hard and struggled in his most recent outing, giving up a pair of home runs to D-backs slugger Jason Kubel. He could not command his pitches and was removed after only 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett bounced back from his first loss since early May by shutting down the Marlins on Saturday, allowing one run in 7 2/3 innings to lower his ERA to 3.59.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles, the youngest starting pitcher on any NL roster (21 years old), has been extremely erratic this year. He's 0-2 with a 7.71 ERA in his past two starts, allowing 21 hits and striking out just five in 11 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: All three of Karstens' wins have come in the last month. Since beating St. Louis on June 30, the lefty is undefeated and owns a 1.86 ERA. Karstens has lasted at least seven innings in each start over that time period.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga, who signed a Minor League contract with the Astros on May 21, had a 4.12 ERA in nine starts and 43 2/3 innings at Triple-A Oklahoma City. His last Major League start came on May 16, 2011, with the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez will make the first start for his new ballclub against the one that signed him as an amateur free agent in 1999. As a Major League pitcher, Rodriguez has started 218 games, and all of them have been for the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell hasn't won in four July starts, but it's not because of the way he's pitched. In his past three starts, Harrell is 0-1 with a 1.42 ERA. He's allowed 16 hits and struck out 16 batters in 19 innings in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Over the season's first three months, McDonald allowed six homers. The righty has given up that many already in July, having served up a couple in each of his two most recent starts. McDonald's ERA in July is 5.46.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired from the Red Sox for cash considerations on July 19, Germano will be making his first start for the Cubs in his second appearance for the team. He pitched three innings in relief on July 21. He was starting at Triple-A Pawtucket.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard held the Cubs to one run on two hits during his last start, throwing seven stellar innings without being rewarded with a win. He threw 113 pitches in the outing, his most in a start since August 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Coleman gets the call in place of the departed Ryan Dempster, who was traded to the Rangers earlier on Tuesday. This will be Coleman's first start of the season, after he started 17 times for Chicago last year.
away_pitcher_note: The 13-year veteran just keeps rolling along; a 13th win would match the second-most of his career, with two months of the season to go. His 14 quality starts do not include his May 25 turn vs. the Cubs; he blanked them, but only for 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals roughed up Wood in his last start as he became the first Major League pitcher to give up home runs in five consecutive innings. In his last five starts, Wood is 2-3 with a 7.36 ERA, and he has given up 10 home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens has had a wicked breaking pitch through a recent hot stretch, using it primarily to notch 29 strikeouts in his last 34 innings. Trying to close out another strong July (2-0, 2.67) after posting a 2.06 ERA in five starts in July last season.

home_pitcher_note: Latos' sprained right ankle seemed to be a non-factor Sunday, as he chalked up eight strikeouts in eight innings while allowing just four hits. He made a lone mistake on a two-run home run ball while earning his ninth win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: The Bucs anticipate Rodriguez being calmer and sharper as he makes his second start for them outside of Houston, and Cincinnati is a good place to put that to a test. He is 1-0 there this season, and 4-4 lifetime with a 3.90 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Leake struggled mightily in his most recent outing Monday, making his earliest exit of the season after just 1 2/3 innings. He struggled to find the strike zone, throwing just 25 of his 49 pitches for strikes and walking three batters in the loss.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald has been rising to occasions all season: Against teams with winning records, he is 5-1 with a 2.45 ERA and 44 strikeouts in 40 1/3 innings. That already includes two wins over the Reds, against whom he's allowed one run in 14 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey seemed to be his normal self in the early going on Tuesday against the Padres before getting hit hard in the fourth. The six earned runs given up Tuesday equaled the amount he allowed in his previous five July starts combined.
away_pitcher_note: In the prime of his career, Burnett comes off his best start of the season, the one-hitter over the Cubs. He had never before been 10 wins over .500, and the Bucs are 16-3 in his starts. An off-day allows him to start Sunday on his regular schedule.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard's stuff doesn't square with his numbers, one reason he keeps getting the ball. But the fact is while pitching for a contender, the lefty leads the Majors in losses. Hasn't lasted five innings in half of his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Miley was outstanding in his last start against the Dodgers. He allowed just one run -- a homer by Mark Ellis -- over eight innings while striking out seven and walking one. He tossed six shutout innings against the Phillies on April 23.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens goes after his fifth straight win -- across seven starts -- hoping this start vs. Arizona is healthier than the first: He left an April 17 start in Phoenix with shoulder inflammation that would keep him out for more than two months.
away_pitcher_note: Promoted from Triple-A Reno to start Wednesday, Corbin combined with three relievers to throw a two-hit shutout against the Dodgers. The left-hander lasted six innings, striking out five and walking two.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander ousted from the rotation two weeks ago gets to make a cameo start, in search of a seventh straight victory, no less. He has a 4-2 record at home, with an ERA (3.62) nearly two runs better than on the road (5.34).
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy beat the Phillies on Friday to extend his winning streak to four consecutive starts. He wasn't at his best, but allowed just two runs on seven hits over six innings. He struck out only one and issued two walks.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty makes his first PNC Park start since his July 24 trade from Houston. He comes off a sharp start against the Reds, in which in seven innings he allowed three runs -- two of them on a home run by his pitching opponent (Mat Latos).
away_pitcher_note: Saunders pitched well in his last outing, allowing just two runs over 6 1/3 innings against the Phillies. Unfortunately for him, he faced Roy Halladay, who blanked the D-backs in a 3-0 Arizona loss.

home_pitcher_note: J-Mac hasn't been very effective since the All-Star break. In five starts, he's 1-2 with a 7.76 ERA. Opponents are hitting .315 off him, and have taken him deep six times. He has also issued 20 walks to go with 22 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez allowed four runs and exited after just 1 2/3 innings his last time out due to a blister on his thumb. He said the thumb feels good, and he looks to rebound from his shortest outing of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The ace has won four straight starts. Pitching at PNC Park, he is 7-0 with a 2.00 ERA. He was named the National League Player of the Week after going 2-0 against the Cubs and Reds, posting a 1.02 ERA in 17 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis gave up three runs on four hits after 6 1/3 innings against the New York Mets on Sunday. He retired 14 straight at one point as the Padres hit three home runs in support of his victory.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard has seen mixed results in the second half. In his most recent outing, he was stellar, holding Arizona to two hits over seven innings. He has a 2.38 ERA at PNC Park, where opponents are hitting .192 off him.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf allowed one run in six innings in his last start, a win over the Cubs. He's been a better pitcher at Petco Park (2.61 ERA) than the road (8.34), but he will be pitching in his old confines, PNC Park, where he pitched from 2008-2011.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens has won four straight decisions since he lost the first game in his late-June return to the Pirates rotation. But he has struggled against the Dodgers, going 0-3 with a 5.25 ERA in six outings (five starts).
away_pitcher_note: With a couple of extra days off after getting hit hard by the D-backs, Harang rebounded with a better effort but another loss to Colorado. He pitched better than his line showed, as two of the three runs he was charged with scored off relievers.

home_pitcher_note: This marks Correia's second spot start since being removed from the rotation. The righty is 7-0 with a 4.56 ERA in his last nine outings. He recorded a quality start in L.A. on April 10, allowing one run in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley insists his stint on the DL is not the reason for reeling off four straight wins. But he has been sharper since returning and more aggressive in his approach. He already beat the Pirates this year, and is 6-1 lifetime against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is still looking for his first win in a Pirates uniform. He hasn't pitched poorly in three appearances for Pittsburgh though, as he has posted a 4.74 ERA and managed to last at least six innings in each outing.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw retired 14 straight at one point while defeating the Marlins, then said it was a battle all night. The perfectionist might not repeat as Cy Young winner, but he still ranks among league leaders in just about every key starting stat.

home_pitcher_note: The Bucs adjusted their rotation to keep their ace on his regular fifth-day schedule, and he will try to rebound from his only loss in 11 home starts. Oddly, Burnett matched his season high of 10 K's in that game against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton comes off a peculiar game in Miami, where he coasted through 4 1/3 innings with a one-hitter, then allowed four consecutive hits to the bottom of the batting order. He is still looking for his first win as a Dodger.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook dominated the Phillies for 7 2/3 innings in a 4-1 win at Citizens Bank Park. Westbrook set a career-best five consecutive wins in that game and has a 2.94 ERA in that span.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald's second-half numbers are just not good. In six starts since the All-Star break, McDonald is 1-2 with an 8.71 ERA. Over that stretch, he has given up eight homers, walked 21 batters, and notched 26 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn has posted a 6.55 ERA in his last four starts, while the Cards have gone 1-3. He hasn't looked sharp since the All-Star break, allowing four or more earned runs in three of his six starts. He did that four times in 17 starts in the first half.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard seeks his third straight win, but on the road his ERA (6.75) is more than four runs higher than in PNC Park. One of his three road wins came in Busch Stadium, where in two starts he has fanned 16 in 9 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia will be making his first start since missing more than two months with left shoulder impingement. He posted a 4.08 ERA with 20 strikeouts in four Minor League rehab starts, and had an 11.25 ERA in two starts prior to heading to the DL.
away_pitcher_note: The righty has gone seven-plus innings in five of his last eight starts, but some of his best work has come in later innings after early-game damage. Leadoff men in his 69 innings are hitting .328.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez has struggled in his last three starts, allowing 16 runs in 8 2/3 innings. He thinks he's getting closer to being mechanically sound, though he allowed six runs in 3 2/3 innings in his last start. One saving grace? He has a 3.24 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: After Wandy Rodriguez stepped in to finish off the Pirates 19-inning victory on Sunday, the Bucs needed someone to fill this start. In steps Correia, who pitched two scoreless innings himself in marathon win over the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis struggled in his last start against the Braves, allowing three home runs, two to Chipper Jones. That said, he's held his own and his strikeouts/per nine innings ratio (7.5) is higher than it's been in his 13-year Major League career.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett has already posted the second-most wins of his career, but dismisses the personal side with "the more I win, the closer we get." Matched his season high of 10 strikeouts in last start versus Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Werner will make his first Major League start on Wednesday. The 25-year-old has made two stops in the Padres' Minor League system in 2012, going 5-10 with a 3.70 ERA in 22 games. He tossed a five-hit shutout against Round Rock on Aug. 2.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates welcomed back the first-half McDonald in his last start, when he blanked the Cardinals on two hits for six innings. The seven strikeouts also matched his most since July 7.

Since flirting with a perfect game on Aug. 7, Fiers has pitched seven innings and allowed 12 runs in his last two starts. He gave up two home runs for just the second time this season in a loss on Saturday.

Marcum will make his first start for the Brewers since June 14. Out of action with right elbow tightness, Marcum made his third and final rehab start on Monday, giving up one run on four hits in six innings.

After the bullpen blew leads in three of his previous four starts, Rogers picked up his first career win on Monday. He gave up three runs on five hits and struck out seven on the way to beating the Cubs, 9-5.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett worked what manager Clint Hurdle called a "gritty" outing in his last start, going 6 1/3 innings with 17 combined baserunners (12 hits, 5 walks) while yielding four runs. Burnett got a no-decision, but his 15 wins are 2nd most in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse's .867 winning percentage is tops in the NL, and he's allowed three earned runs in 26 2/3 innings this month. All four of his August starts have gone at least six innings in length, and he's not allowed more than four hits in any of them.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald walked the bases loaded in the first in his last outing against the Padres and gave up three runs in that frame before settling in for five innings of four-run ball. His outing before that was one of his best, six scoreless vs. St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: The Cards' offense bailed Westbrook out on Thursday, when the right-hander did not have his usual sharp sinker. The Bucs have habitually given Westbrook trouble, though he allowed only one earned run against them in an Aug. 18 start.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez again had better stuff than luck in his last outing, which was his third quality start of five since his trade to Pittsburgh, although he has yet to win as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Kelly returns to the starting rotation after stopping the bleeding in the Cardinals' 8-5 win over the Reds on Friday. He is 3-5 with a 3.75 ERA in 12 starts this season after making the first start of his career on June 10.

home_pitcher_note: He gutted through five innings to beat the Pirates on Sunday without his best stuff, and will try to be sharper in the rematch. After being denied in his first six Major League starts, Rogers has two straight wins.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens hopes to not have any residual effect from the strained left-groin that forced him out last Saturday against the Brewers. He did go seven scoreless innings -- the seventh time in his last 10 starts that he'd gone seven-plus.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada's best outings have come at home, where he has a 3.54 ERA in 41 games, including 14 starts. He took a no-decision after allowing three Pirates runs in 5 2/3 innings on July 14 at Miller Park.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett will be trying to bounce back from a rarity for him: failing to hold onto a mid-game lead, as he did in a 4-3 loss to St. Louis. The Bucs have scored a total of eight runs in the right-hander's five losses.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo is on a roll. He has pitched at least seven innings in six straight starts, all wins. He has allowed more than one run only twice in those games, and leads the Majors with 22 quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald hopes to stop a second-half pattern of inconsistency by following up Tuesday's seven scoreless innings of two-hit pitching against the Cardinals. After a volatile period, he has allowed only two homers in last 28 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Locke makes his first start after a pair of impressive relief appearances after first being called up in early August. He has averaged close to a strikeout an inning in the Minors. This could be the start of his tenure as a rotation mainstay.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros will call up Edgar Gonzalez from Triple-A Oklahoma City to start at PNC Park. He was 1-0 with a 0.69 ERA in two starts for the RedHawks this year after pitching for Monterrey in the Mexican League.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran comes off not only his best start with the Pirates, but also since April, when he was still with the Astros. His six shutout innings versus St. Louis helped put his Bucs tenure into a new light: 5 of his 6 starts have been quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old has been up and down this season, but has a couple of good starts under his belt. He's 1-0 with a 3.27 ERA in his last two starts. He lost to the Giants last time out, but allowed three runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Correia returns to the rotation in place of Jeff Karstens (strained hip flexor), seeking his ninth win in his last 12 decisions. He has made only seven appearances (including three starts) since getting pulled from the rotation on July 25.
away_pitcher_note: Abad was moved from the bullpen to the rotation earlier this year, and his first two starts were rough. He's 0-2 with a 7.56 ERA in two starts, at the Mets on Aug. 25 and against the Reds on Aug. 31 in Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett shrugs off the possibility, but he has to win his last five starts, beginning with this one, to reach 20 for the first time in his career. He comes off his first quality start of the last five, but is winless in last three.
away_pitcher_note: Wood is looking for his first win since July 6. He's 0-8 in his last 10 starts, but has not given up more than three earned runs in six of his last seven outings, dating to Aug. 1.

home_pitcher_note: The good McDonald is scheduled to show up, as he has alternated great-ghastly starts for the last month. He was rocked for a career-high four homers in only 2 2/3 innings in last outing, in Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija threw seven innings in his last start, a one-run, seven-hit gem against the Nationals on Sept. 3. He ultimately earned a loss as the Cubs fell, 2-1. With his innings count at 165 2/3, the Cubs could soon shut down Samardzija.

home_pitcher_note: Locke hopes for more consistency in his second start than he had against Houston on Monday, when he started off 18 of 23 batters with strikes but allowed five runs in five innings. Left-handed hitters are 4-for-8 off the southpaw.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin, a 25-year-old rookie, made his second career start on Sept. 4 against the Nationals, when he allowed five runs on eight hits in just one inning. After the game, manager Dale Sveum lamented Rusin's lack of a solid breaking ball.

home_pitcher_note: Latos looked strong again Tuesday, limiting the Phillies to one run on four hits to earn his 12th win of the season. He has held his opponents to two earned runs or fewer in 18 of 28 starts this season and is two wins shy of his career high.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez enters with a string of 13 scoreless innings to validate the Bucs' decision to make him their key Trade Deadline pick up. His five quality starts among seven with the Pirates include an Aug. 3 start in Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Leake had his second shortest outing of the season Wednesday, exiting after 2 1/3 innings as Philly roughed him up for six runs on six hits, including two homers. His two-game winning streak ended, but he hasn't lost in consecutive outings since May.
away_pitcher_note: Correia makes a second straight start on regular rest for the first time in a month. Including intermittent relief work, he has allowed four earned runs in his last 18 2/3 innings. He has also won nine of his last 12 decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey is still in search of his first September win after earning his second consecutive no-decision on Friday. He gave up two runs on five hits in 6 2/3 innings, and had the win in his pocket until closer Aroldis Chapman blew the save in the ninth.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran is out to avoid a fifth straight start without a win for the first time all year (he's 0-2 with two no-decisions in his last four). He has a 4.84 ERA in seven starts since his one-hitter on July 31 in Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: Following a rough outing, Rusin showed an ability to bounce back on Sunday vs. the Pirates, allowing one run on five hits over five innings. The lefty was able to mix up his pitches well and had good command of his offspeed stuff.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald's ERA has been on a steady rise since it stood at 2.37 at the All-Star break. J-Mac had an early-season stretch of eight-plus strikeouts in seven of eight starts, and has hit that figure only once in his last 17 starts.

home_pitcher_note: This would have been Jeff Samardzija's spot, but he was shut down after Saturday's game because he had reached his maximum innings. Berken, acquired off waivers from the Orioles on Friday, was 5-6 with a 3.50 ERA at Triple-A Norfolk.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez can't pitch better than he did on Monday, when he took a one-hitter into the seventh in Cincinnati. The Pirates lost after he got the hook after 89 pitches, and he'll be out to make up for that disappointment.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing one run over five innings on Monday against the Astros, Volstad said he's felt like a different pitcher since returning from Triple-A Iowa on Aug. 4. He has a 4.08 ERA in his past eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Locke makes his seventh big league start, and ninth appearance, still looking for his first win. The Bucs are counting on him using September to stake a claim to a 2013 rotation job.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander has allowed one run over his last 13 2/3 innings. In each of his last two starts, he opened with four hitless innings before giving up a hit in the fifth. Since Aug. 22, he has a 2.43 ERA in 33 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling against the Cubs last year -- posting a 7.11 ERA in four starts -- Correia has held Chicago in check this season. The right-hander is 1-0 with a 2.92 ERA in two starts against the Cubs this season, with the victory coming July 25.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates are winless in Burnett's last five starts, but the righty held the Reds to two runs over six innings and struck out eight his last time out. Burnett held the Brewers to two runs in 6 2/3 innings on Sept. 1, striking out nine.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo has led the way since the Zack Greinke trade, going 7-0 with a 2.98 ERA in nine starts. He leads the Majors with 24 quality starts, and the Brewers are 20-10 when he takes the mound.

home_pitcher_note: McPherson gets his first Major League start in place of righty James McDonald, who was removed from the rotation while the teams was in Chicago. McPherson, the club's No. 10 prospect according to MLB.com, posted a 3.22 ERA in 12 Minor League starts.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada won for the third time in four decisions by outdueling Atlanta's Tim Hudson last Tuesday. He pitched a gem against the Pirates on Sept. 1, striking out 10 batters while allowing only one run in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriquez spun his fifth straight quality start his last time out, lowering his ERA to 1.95 in that span. That stretch began against the Brewers on Aug. 24, when he allowed three runs and walked four in 6 2/3 innings while taking the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers beat the Pirates at PNC Park on Aug. 24, when he struck out 10 batters, allowed three runs in 6 2/3 innings and bunted for his first hit of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez has made three starts for the Astros since they signed him out of the Mexican League, where he was pitching for his native Monterrey. He won two road games before giving up six hits and five runs last Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Locke is winless in nine Major League appearances, including seven starts, and his "show us" rope may be getting shorter -- particularly after his most recent start, when he let a five-run lead over the Cubs turn into a 13-9 loss.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie left-hander is coming off his second career win, throwing 5 1/3 scoreless innings to beat the Phillies on Saturday. He had lost his previous seven decisions since throwing a complete game on June 23 against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Two months after being removed from the rotation to make room for Wandy Rodriguez, Correia is the Bucs' hottest starter (10 wins in last 14 decisions) as he goes for his 12th win, which would tie a career high.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles has had an up-and-down season in his second year in the Majors. The 21-year-old pitched five scoreless innings on Sept. 11, before giving up five hits and four runs in five innings last Sunday in a no-decision against Philly.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett has gone through a strange stretch, with his ERA continuing to go down as his losses go up. He is winless in his last six starts and has dropped four straight decisions; he has not lost five in a row since June 2010.

home_pitcher_note: Mejia has made one start and two relief appearances since joining the Mets earlier this month. He lasted just three innings in his only start, allowing five runs on six hits against the Brewers on Sept. 15.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie righty makes his second start after an encouraging debut Wednesday against the Brewers, holding them to a pair of runs while stretching out to 4 1/3 innings after breaking into the Majors with seven relief appearances.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh hasn't started a game since Sept. 10, but he pitched three innings of relief on Thursday against the Phillies. Since pitching seven innings of shutout ball in his Major League debut on Aug. 23, McHugh has a 6.94 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty responsible for half of the Pirates' wins in the last month finished each of the last two seasons with 11 wins and will try to break through that. He has an ERA of 2.77 while splitting two career starts at Citi Field.

home_pitcher_note: Hefner had a tough outing against the Phillies on Thursday, allowing six consecutive singles to open the game before walking in a run and leaving without recording an out.
away_pitcher_note: Making his ninth start still in search of his first Major League win, Locke will have to solve the long-ball problem: He has given up five homers in his last 15 innings, but he has also struck out 16 in that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey was nearly flawless on Saturday, until he left in the ninth inning with a 4-0 lead but runners on second and third. The Marlins ultimately plated three runs, but New York held on for the win, as Dickey picked up win No. 19 on the season.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran righty makes possibly his last start of the season, still hoping to match his career-high of 12 wins (set in 2009 and tied last season). He has been very sharp in September (2.52 ERA in four starts).

home_pitcher_note: Burnett makes what could be his final start of the season. His turn would come up again for the final game on Wednesday, but manager Clint Hurdle may want to get some others on the mound before the string runs out.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey started Sunday before giving up five runs over 6 2/3 innings in a loss to the Dodgers. Bailey admittedly wasn't feeling his sharpest, especially after the club was coming off a celebration of clinching the division the previous night.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie's search for his first Major League win continues in his first home start after a pair of encouraging starts on the road. McPherson has overall been tougher on left-handed batters (eight hits in 34 at-bats).
away_pitcher_note: Leake finished without a decision Wednesday but lasted six innings. He's given up at least three earned runs in each of his past three outings and is looking to break even for his ninth win of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander anticipated to return as one of the rotation's anchors in 2013 tries to even his overall record in his final start. The former Astros southpaw is already a winner as a Pirate -- 5-4 -- including four consecutive wins.
away_pitcher_note: After losing three straight, Cueto has bounced back to win his past two starts and is one victory away from a 20-win season, which would make him the first Red to reach the plateau since Danny Jackson in 1988.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie lefty hopes to enter the offseason with his first big league win. Otherwise, he'll have the burden of remaining winless after 10 starts, the most at the start of a career by a Pirates pitcher since 1962-65 (Tommie Sisk).
away_pitcher_note: Maholm will make his third start of the year against his former team. He allowed one run and four hits in eight innings at PNC Park on July 24. He has bounced back from two rough starts at the beginning of the month.

home_pitcher_note: In very likely his final start for Pittsburgh, the free-agent-to-be takes his third crack at a 12th win that would tie his career high (also in 2009 and 2011). He blamed poor command for getting knocked around (six runs) in last start.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson has not thrown six or more innings in his last seven starts and has a 4.64 ERA since returning from a trip to the disabled list because of a lower back strain. In his last start Thursday, Hanson got his first win since July 30.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran righty who spent the summer raising fans' hopes gets to lower the 2012 curtain. He's 3 1/3 innings short of 200 innings for the first time since 2009. His current ERA is second lowest of career (3.30 in 2002).
away_pitcher_note: Sheets will be making what he expects to be the final appearance of his injury-plagued career. He is expected to pitch two innings before prospects Julio Teheran and Randall Delgado also make brief appearances.

home_pitcher_note: At 36 and starting his 15th season, Burnett has earned his first Opening Day assignment. He's looking to start this season off on the right foot after ending last year on the wrong one, with only one win in his last nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: It's fitting that Samardzija opens the season in Pittsburgh. That's where he made his last and best start of 2012, a complete game victory on Sept. 8. The right-hander was then shut down because he'd reached his innings limit for the year.

home_pitcher_note: If there is a Pittsburgh pitcher already in midseason form, it is this veteran lefty, after helping pitch the Dominican Republic to the World Baseball Classic title. Rodriguez had a 2.25 ERA in three 2012 starts against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson -- signed to a four-year, $52 million deal -- is one of the more durable pitchers, averaging 199 innings over the last five years.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander is bent on erasing memories of a split '12 season, when he followed up an All-Star caliber first half with a total second-half implosion. Not known for good Aprils (5.71 career ERA), so he'll be challenged.
away_pitcher_note: Wood was inserted into the rotation while the Cubs wait for Matt Garza and Scott Baker to heal. The lefty is 3-4 in seven career games against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke makes his Dodgers debut, which was delayed by a minor elbow ailment that threw him off schedule. The $147 million, former Cy Young winner might be a little short in arm strength, but the 'pen should be rested after a day off Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: The Majors' arguably poorest 2012 starter (8.07 ERA for Rockies and Royals) tries to begin writing his comeback story in familiar territory: The former Giant has made 13 career starts against the Dodgers, five in Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: What can Kershaw do as an encore to his Opening Day shutout and home run? When he's throwing strikes with his curveball, as he did against the Giants, he's pretty much untouchable. He's only 1-1 in six starts against the Pirates lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett, not yet active last season for the Pirates' only West Swing, makes only his second Dodger Stadium start in nine years. In 2010, he was roughed up there for six runs in three innings, but he's 4-3 lifetime against Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Ryu made his Major League debut vs. the Giants, giving up three runs (one earned) on 10 hits with five strikeouts. He used his changeup to induce three double plays and escape trouble. Ryu said he was nervous but should be more comfortable Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: The Bucs' steadiest Spring Training pitcher makes his first regular-season start, hoping to pick up where he left off last season, which he finished by holding Atlanta to two hits for six innings for his first big league win.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill was cruising along in his first start of the year against the Cardinals before hitting a wall in the sixth. Cahill gave up a pair of runs in the sixth on a homer by Matt Holliday and allowed three runs in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: When Rodriguez won his season debut, it gave him six wins in a 35-game stretch dating to August, compared with five combined for other Bucs starters. He was brilliant in that debut, blanking the Cubs on two hits for 6 2/3.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy struggled in his D-backs debut, but after the game went 16 innings, many forgot at the end that he had even started. McCarthy allowed six runs on nine hits in five innings against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald was very encouraging in his first start of the season, allowing the Cubs two hits and one run in seven innings and retiring 13 of the last 14 men he faced. He's still trying to conquer road woes (career 14-20 with 5.30 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Miley struggled a bit during the spring, battling a dead arm for a stretch, but he showed no ill effects in his first start of the regular season. Miley held the Brewers to one run over six innings with eight strikeouts to get the win.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching aggressively without any thoughts of mechanics is paying off for the lefty. Including Spring Training and his first start, has walked three in his last 15 2/3 innings -- the most in-control stretch of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett is very aware of being the Pirates' tone-setter, so it is fitting that he would start the first of 19 against the rival Reds. With his curveball already in midseason form, he has racked up 19 strikeouts in 11 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Leake has generally pitched well at PNC Park, with a 2.68 ERA in six lifetime starts since 2010. But he is little to show for it since his lifetime record there is 0-3.

home_pitcher_note: Locke has extra incentive after the Pirates had considered skipping his start, until a hamstring injury by Wandy Rodriguez kept him in line. He must get ahead of hitters to be effective, which he did not do in his first start.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto was not sharp opposing the Nationals, as he threw 108 pitches over six innings. The killer inning was a 30-pitch second where he gave up three runs and blew a 3-0 lead. But credit to Cueto for hanging in there and getting his team a win.

home_pitcher_note: Irwin will make his big league debut in place of an injured Wandy Rodriguez, after a productive spring with the Pirates. He threw six innings of one-run ball in his only Triple-A start this season.
away_pitcher_note: During Monday's start at St. Louis, Latos lacked command early and was not locating his slider. He made the adjustment and kept the Reds in the game, but was out well before they rallied late for a 13-4 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching at home against St. Louis is about as good as it gets for J-Mac. Last season alone, he was 6-2 at PNC Park with a 2.73 ERA -- less than half what it was on the road (5.95) -- and didn't allow a run to the Cards in two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn struck out 10 Reds batters en route to getting his first win on Tuesday. He corrected some delivery flaws between outings and likely could have pitched deeper had the strikeouts not pushed up his pitch count.

home_pitcher_note: Clint Hurdle was interested in Sanchez's follow-up start to a strong season debut, and he's even more curious to see his rebound from Wednesday's shellacking (nine runs in 3 1/3 innings). The lefty must pitch in to be effective.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook dazzled on Wednesday, pitching his first shutout in seven seasons and throwing just 111 pitches. He's yet to allow an earned run this season and is garnering ground balls with regularity, evidence of a strong sinker.

home_pitcher_note: As steady as he's been, Burnett has one win in his past 12 starts dating back to mid-August. The Cards gave him a hard time last season (16 runs in 15 1/3 innings). His second strikeout of the game will be No. 2,000 of his career.
away_pitcher_note: Miller was brilliant against the Brewers on Friday. Making his third career start, the 22-year-old rookie allowed one hit and struck out eight batters in seven shutout innings as part of a 2-0 win. He threw 113 pitches, with 87 going for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Locke held the Reds to one run over five innings Saturday night in a Pirates victory. Locke gave up four hits with four walks and no strikeouts. He has a 4.09 ERA, 1.55 WHIP and 3/5 K/BB ratio in 11 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran showed some resolve when he allowed the Nationals four runs in the first two innings on Friday and then surrendered just two more baserunners during his six-inning effort. This will be his seventh career start.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez was scratched from an outing Sunday because of a strained left hamstring, but he was able to make it through a bullpen session on Wednesday. Rodriguez left the April 8 game in Arizona after just 2 1/3 innings when he injured his hamstring.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has allowed just two earned runs and seven hits while totaling 13 2/3 innings in his past two starts. As his arm strength has improved the past couple weeks, his cutter, splitter and curveball have been more effective.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald gave up eight runs -- three earned -- in 1 2/3 innings against the Cardinals on Monday. In his previous outing, McDonald allowed four runs in five frames April 9 against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm hasn't allowed a run in his first three starts (20 1/3 innings) this season. The veteran left-hander has posted a 2.51 ERA in his past 21 starts. He compiled a 2.25 ERA in three starts against Pittsburgh last year.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez allowed two runs in the first inning but retired the side in order in the second in his last outing, a rainout against St. Louis on Tuesday. He was pounded for nine runs in 3 1/3 innings by the D-backs on April 10.
away_pitcher_note: Medlen struggled with his mechanics in March and during the first two innings of his season debut.  But the right-hander, who has a 1.05 ERA in his past 15 starts, has allowed just one earned run in his past 17 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old righty, the club's third-round selection in the 2008 First-Year Player Draft, will make his Major League debut. He surrendered 12 runs (10 earned) in two starts at Triple-A this year.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett has featured a devastating curve in the early going, the pitch that has gotten him most of his 35 strikeouts. That's the most for a Pittsburgh pitcher in the season's first three games since Jose DeLeon's 28 in 1985.

home_pitcher_note: He allowed five hits, three runs, two walks and struck out eight in seven innings Thursday against St. Louis, but a lack of run support cost him for the second consecutive start. He hopes to get some help Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: This will be a key start for the lefty, pitching for his spot in the rotation with two veterans (Francisco Liriano, Charlie Morton) weeks from completing rehabs. Two musts for Locke: Get ahead, and keep the ball down.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay allowed two hits, two runs, two walks and struck out six in seven innings on Friday against St. Louis. After a terrible start, Halladay has a 1.80 ERA (three earned runs in 15 innings) in his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty truly has been Wonderful Wandy, having allowed  five hits in 16 innings this season, with a terrific 11-to-1 strikeout-to-walk ratio. He has found Citizens Bank Park a tough house, with a 7.11 ERA in four appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Lee is coming off his least effective start of the season, allowing five runs in five innings against the Cardinals on April 20. He walked three batters, snapping his streak of 20 straight starts with at least six innings and one or fewer walks.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald pitched with more confidence in his last start than at any time since his hot first half of last season. The Pirates have always felt there are "two McDonalds," and the hope is the good one has returned for keeps.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn shut out the Phillies on one hit in seven innings Saturday, his best start of the year. He did not have similar success in a start against the Pirates earlier in April. He gave up four runs in five innings on that night.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez allowed two runs in three innings against Atlanta in a 4-2 win his last time out. Sanchez has struggled over the past two weeks, during which he has allowed 11 runs and 12 hits in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook had a start against Pittsburgh rained out earlier this month, which gives him more time to solve that offense. The Pirates have always given Westbrook fits; he has only one win in 13 appearances against the Bucs.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett has allowed three earned runs or fewer in all five of his starts this season. He's struck out 42 batters in 29 innings. In his last start, against the Phillies on April 22, neither of the runs he allowed came on a hit.

home_pitcher_note: Miller allowed two runs in six innings against Pittsburgh earlier in April but was outpitched by A.J. Burnett. He's made three straight quality starts and continues to have hitters fooled by the late life on his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Locke had the best outing of his career, throwing six scoreless innings in a 2-0 win over the Phillies. Locke impressed manager Clint Hurdle after the youngster battled through jams in both the second and fourth innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo threw only 58 of 108 pitches for strikes in his last start, and Brewers manager Ron Roenicke described his top starter as "out of whack." Gallardo still pitched into the seventh inning for his second straight win.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is coming off a no-decision last time out vs. the Phils. The left-hander allowed nine hits and three runs, including a pair of homers, in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada has authored four consecutive quality starts, including a loss to the Padres in which he allowed only one earned run in 6 1/3 innings. "It was probably the best I've felt all year," Estrada said.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald has been extra stingy over his last two outings, allowing just seven hits and four runs in 11 innings. The right-hander has struggled in his career vs. the Brewers, though, posting a 6.98 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Burgos was briefly in line for his second win in as many big league starts, but it was snatched away in the seventh inning on Friday in Los Angeles. He still managed to deliver his second quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Gomez emerges from the bullpen to make his first start of the season, but hardly his first in the Majors: He made 38 starts for the Indians over the last three seasons, posting a 5.32 ERA while averaging 5 1/3 innings per outing.

home_pitcher_note: Even without his main weapon, the curve, Burnett fanned six his last time out to retain the NL lead with 48 strikeouts. Before and since joining the Bucs, he's enjoyed pitching at PNC Park, with a career ERA of 2.98 in 23 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler wasn't sharp in his last outing, allowing four runs (three earned) in five innings against the Reds. Manager Davey Johnson said he would like Detwiler to start using all of his arsenal of pitches.

home_pitcher_note: The young lefty's light went on two starts ago, and he brings a 13-inning shutout streak into this start. While he posted those zeros on the road, his track record is to be sharper at home, so hopes are high that he can keep it going.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg is winless in five straight starts despite allowing three or fewer runs four times, and whiffing 33 in 30 1/3 innings. There was some talk of forearm tightness after his last start, but the ace says he is good to go.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez aims to rebound from "one of those games," when he allowed seven runs on three homers Monday in Milwaukee. He could not control his pitches, and without blow-away stuff, he needs to work ahead in the count to survive.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez has a 7.36 ERA (18 ER in 22 innings) in his last four starts but is 2-2. He struck out a season-best nine his last time out, while also walking a season-high five, in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gomez takes the hill in place of James McDonald, who was placed on the 15-day DL just hours before the start with lingering discomfort in his throwing shoulder. Gomez has faced the M's once before, tossing six innings of two-run ball on Sep. 5, 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Harang is coming off his best outing in which he went a season-high six innings, while allowing just two runs to pick up his first win of the season. It was a nice bounceback for Harang after not completing five innings in his first two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett will be seeking a fourth straight win in this marquee matchup between two of the Majors' top strikeout pitchers. At 36, he is off to the most efficient start of his 15 seasons, with a career-low WHIP (1.119), and leads the NL with 57 K's.
away_pitcher_note: Over his past four outings, the right-hander has allowed two earned runs over 30 innings -- good for a 0.60 ERA -- and has struck out 35 while walking just two. He has six quality starts in seven outings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Better defense might have saved Gee from much of the damage against him last Wednesday in Miami, but he did give up nine hits and four runs in five innings. Gee will be making his first start against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: The young lefty has been consistent in his past three starts, allowing a total of three runs in 18 innings. He keeps the ball down low, meaning he also keeps it in the park. Avoiding deep counts will let him go longer in games.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum allowed nine baserunners in 4 1/3 innings last time out against the Braves, resulting in three runs and a no-decision. As a member of the Brewers, he was 1-1 with a 0.75 ERA in two starts last year against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez began mixing in more changeups and changed the release point on his curve in the last two innings of his most recent start, and the difference in effectiveness was noticeable. He'll try to carry that over.

home_pitcher_note: Niese had no excuse for the six walks that plagued him in Sunday's loss to the Braves. But his defense also betrayed him, misplaying enough balls to result in seven runs against him. Niese is 2-0 lifetime against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano, signed as a free agent by the Pirates in February, makes his first appearance of the season and his first career appearance as a National Leaguer. The Mets' record in games in which they have been opposed by left-handed starters is 7-8.

home_pitcher_note: Harvey continued his 2013 dominance by nearly tossing the Mets' first perfect game against the White Sox, allowing just an infield hit with two outs in the seventh en route to nine scoreless innings. He struck out a career-high 12 in the no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Gomez earned a repeat start with his five shutout innings in a last-minute assignment on Tuesday against Seattle. He is holding batters to a .222 average -- after being hit at a .291 clip while with the Indians from 2010-12.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates have scored merely four runs in the four starts by Burnett that didn't result in a victory. His ERA in those games (23 innings) is 3.13. Right-handed hitters are batting .141 with 39 strikeouts in 92 at-bats against him this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers bumped Estrada by two days to allow for an extra bullpen session between starts. He has allowed 13 earned runs and four home runs over his past two starts, and felt "lost" while walking five Cardinals on May 5.

home_pitcher_note: Though Locke has allowed four runs in his two most recent starts (11 innings), he came away with no-decisions in both. Opponents have attempted one stolen base -- it was unsuccessful -- with him on the mound this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse has not been quite as sharp in his past two starts, but could still be winning games if the Brewers provided him with run support. They are 2-5 when he pitches and have scored a total of three runs in the five losses.

home_pitcher_note: That Rodriguez won his most recent start almost goes without saying. He beat the Mets, and he owns them. He walked none and struck out two in six innings, but needed 92 pitches to do so. He'd been winless with two losses in three previous starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo minced no words in discussing his lousy command against the Reds after throwing 100 pitches in four innings. He said it was a matter of mechanics and dismissed the fact he did not exceed 91 mph.

home_pitcher_note: Supported by an uncharacteristic run output, Liriano made his 2013 and NL debuts against the Mets and appeared to be in midseason form -- nine strikeouts, two walks, six hits and one run in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching for the first time in 10 days, Burgos allowed 12 runs (10 earned) in three ugly innings in Cincinnati. It was only the third time in Brewers history a starter allowed 10 or more earned runs in three or fewer innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gomez has been one of the Bucs' most dependable starters since getting a chance when Jonathan Sanchez was given his release, and he is making a strong case for tenure. His ERA is a staff low for anyone with 25-plus innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles will make his fourth start of the season as Houston returns to a National League park for the first time since joining the American League West. The right-hander is winless (0-4) in five career starts vs. the Bucs.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander continues his remarkable renaissance, consistently lowering his ERA while raising his strikeout total -- although the six in his last start were a season low. He has gone seven innings in each of his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard delivered five innings of four-hit, two-run ball in his return to the rotation on Saturday vs. the Rangers. The veteran left-hander returns to Pittsburgh for the first time since starting 24 games for the Pirates last year.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates gave Locke a job based on his Minor League resume, but even they may have been surprised by his consistency and borderline-dominant command. He has allowed 18 hits in his last 30 innings over five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell hasn't pitched beyond the fifth in any of his last three starts, going 0-2 with an 8.79 ERA in that span. Harrell made news after his most recent start, saying he wasn't a fan of the Astros' frequent defensive shifts.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates' biggest winner since his '12 midseason acquisition from Houston tries to become their first five-game winner. Rodriguez, coming off three straight quality starts, has a 1.35 ERA in four starts at PNC Park.
away_pitcher_note: Garza makes his first start of the season -- and first in exactly 10 months -- Tuesday against the Pirates. The right-hander missed the second half of 2012 with right shoulder issues before opening this season on the DL with a left lat strain.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano turned in carbon-copy starts in his first two outings for the Bucs, striking out a total of 16 in 11 innings. The former American Leaguer lost his only Interleague meeting with the Cubs, allowing four runs in 5 2/3 innings last June.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija returns to PNC Park, where he won on Opening Day. In that game, he whiffed nine and held the Bucs to two hits in eight shutout innings. He didn't get another win, though, until his last start vs. the Rockies. His splitter is his key pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Gomez continues to give the Bucs four solid innings every start, before he begins to wear down around the 60-pitch mark. That is owed to the fact he prepped for relief duty in Spring Training and is still building up arm strength.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson is coming off his best outing as a Cub, allowing three runs in 6 2/3 innings against the Mets, but took the loss against Matt Harvey. Jackson last faced the Reds on May 5 in Chicago, giving up four runs in five innings while taking the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada earned one of the Brewers' two wins on their 10-game road trip with a three-hit, seven-inning gem against the Pirates, allowing one run. But his last time out he was hit hard against the Cardinals, giving up four runs in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett leads the NL in strikeouts and hasn't surrendered more than three runs in a start this season. He has gone seven innings in each of his past four starts, as well. He lost his last start vs. the Brewers on May 13.

home_pitcher_note: Kyle Lohse was originally supposed to take the mound, but will miss a start due to right elbow irritation. Fiers lost his only start on April 6, allowing nine hits and six runs in five innings against the Diamondbacks.
away_pitcher_note: Locke has continued his steady 2013 behind A.J. Burnett in the Pirates' rotation after going 1-3 with a 6.30 ERA in six starts in September and October last season. He tossed seven shutout innings in a 1-0 win over the Astros on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo is 3-4 with a 4.50 ERA on the season but threw a quality start his last time out against the Dodgers. Gallardo tossed six innings, allowing eight hits and three runs while striking out seven and walking one.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has been a model of consistency in a strong Pirates rotation this month. He has thrown at least six innings in his four starts in May, going 3-1 with a 2.88 ERA. He has struck out 19 and walked two in those starts, as well.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander called his last outing a step in the right direction, though five Cleveland runs bumped his ERA up again. He tossed two complete-game victories against the Pirates last year, including a no-hit bid in Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty's sensational Pirates beginnings get a major test in Detroit, where the former AL Central rival has a lifetime 6.18 ERA in 11 games. The Bucs expect to again see the Liriano who has a 25-6 K-W ratio in 18 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello's curveball deserted him on a chilly night in Detroit last Thursday, and he looked to his changeup for outs against Minnesota's left-handed hitters. A warmer forecast should bode for better stuff from him.
away_pitcher_note: A long rain delay in his last start cost Gomez another victory, but he remained as consistent as ever, holding the Cubs to three hits and one run in 3 2/3 innings. Holding opponents to a .192 average with men in scoring position.

home_pitcher_note: Held back by poor run support, Burnett now butts heads with a guy who came within two outs of a no-hitter his last start. If anything, that will further fire up Burnett, who leads the NL with 85 whiffs.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez fell two outs shy of a no-hitter Friday against the Twins, losing it on a Joe Mauer single. Considering he has held Pirates hitters to a .192 average, including a one-hitter in 2011, he could make another bid.

home_pitcher_note: The young left-hander's sudden breakthrough has now stretched through seven starts, as he has allowed 24 hits and seven runs in the 43 innings they've covered. He's gone 5-0 since beginning his career 1-7.
away_pitcher_note: The Penguins will be a big story in Pittsburgh next week, but Fister comes to town with his own share of hard hits, leading the league with 11 hit batters compared with just 10 walks. He lost a 4-1 duel in Pittsburgh last June.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates have gone 8-2 in Rodriguez's starts, six of which have been quality. He has been displaying the sharpest command of his career, with a 24-to-2 strikeout-to-walk ratio in his last five starts, covering 30 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his second start since coming off the DL, Cueto did everything but get the win. He went seven innings, allowing one run on four hits and two walks. Although the Reds lost, Cueto was much sharper than his previous start.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano got passing grades in his biggest test with the Pirates yet, pitching five credible innings on Monday in Detroit. The three wins have improved his career record against National League teams to 12-5.
away_pitcher_note: In his last three starts, Leake has given up just one earned run. It came in his last outing vs. Cleveland on Monday, but the five hits and seven strikeouts in 7 1/3 frames were enough to help the Reds to their third straight win in his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Gomez comes off the best start of his career, a seven-inning no-decision in Detroit on Tuesday. He has allowed three hits or fewer in four of his last five starts, changing the perception that he is just keeping a spot warm for someone else.
away_pitcher_note: Although Latos didn't go deep in his last outing, he gave the Reds a chance to win by giving up just one run in 6 1/3 innings. He's had a knack for that this season, as he sits at a perfect 5-0, with four of those wins coming against the NL Central.

home_pitcher_note: After being hit by a line drive, Medlen exited his last start with a left upper-calf contusion that limited him to two innings. He's in a wait-and-see mode to learn whether the tightness subsides in the next few days.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett has set the tone for a Pirates rotation that has been one of baseball's best but doesn't have the wins to show for it. Pittsburgh has scored 13 runs in his last six starts, while he's allowed just 12 earned runs in that time.

home_pitcher_note: Minor turned in his sixth straight quality start on Thursday, striking out five and regaining his composure to limit the damage after an error sparked Toronto's three-run sixth. The Braves have won five straight Minor starts.
away_pitcher_note: Locke hasn't allowed a run in 19 1/3 innings and went 2-0 with a 1.78 ERA in May. He pitched 5 1/3 innings against the Tigers on Thursday, allowing seven hits and one walk. Locke is 1-0 with a 4.22 ERA in two career starts against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran surrendered two triples and a pair of soft singles in Friday's tough-luck loss to the Nats, in which he fanned a career-high nine. He has allowed three runs or fewer in each of his past seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' top winner lost one of his better starts of the season last time out, but other than not getting any runs was his usual reliable self. His best outing of season was against the Braves with seven one-hit innings on April 19.

home_pitcher_note: The Cubs took advantage of two off-days in one week to push back Wood, who has thrown 72 innings this year. The lefty has turned in 11 quality starts in 12 outings and held the Pirates to one hit in six shutout innings in his season debut.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano set a season high with 11 strikeouts and just one walk over six innings in Saturday's loss to Cincinnati. He dominated the Cubs on May 22, turning in seven shutout innings and allowing just two hits.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija followed an eight-inning shutout of the Pirates on Opening Day with seven innings of one-run ball in a hard-luck loss on May 22. He struck out 11 -- including six straight -- in 6 1/3 innings in his last outing against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett could not keep the ball in the yard on Monday, surrendering three home runs for the first time since he was with the Yankees. He struck out 10 Cubs on Opening Day, his only other meeting with Chicago this season.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson is 1-7 with a 7.87 ERA in nine career starts at Wrigley Field after losing his last outing one week ago to the D-backs. He gave up 12 hits, walked three and was charged with four wild pitches in the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Locke struggled with his fastball his last time out, using his off-speed stuff to escape a number of high-stress situations. He needed 103 pitches, one fewer than his season high, to get through 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates' top prospect gets his unveiling after going 5-3 in Triple-A. Cole arrives a hot pitcher, having thrown shutout ball in his past two starts for Indianapolis and has allowed only two earned runs in his last 20 innings.
away_pitcher_note: This will truly be a test for Lincecum, who hasn't made a quality start in five road outings this year. His road ERA is 5.67, compared to 4.20 at home. He also has struggled at PNC Park, where he's 0-1 with a 5.19 ERA in three career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano is only a couple of outs shy of five quality starts in his first six games with the Bucs. He might have been most impressive in his last start, when he lacked his usual command, yet wouldn't let the game get away from him.
away_pitcher_note: Zito must work on trimming his road ERA, which is 10.19 in four starts. And June traditionally hasn't been the best of months for Zito. His lifetime ERA for the month, 4.40, is his second-highest for any month.

home_pitcher_note: Morton will make his first start of the season just one day shy of the one-year anniversary of his Tommy John surgery. Morton was 2-6 with a 4.65 ERA last season, and starts Thursday in place of Wandy Rodriguez (forearm strain).
away_pitcher_note: Cain will be pitching on the one-year anniversary of his perfect game at AT&T Park against Houston. It was the 14th no-hitter in franchise history and the sixth since the team moved to San Francisco in 1958.

home_pitcher_note: Locke hasn't given up more than three runs in a start since April 18, and has been outstanding since the start of May. He's allowed just 11 earned runs in 46 2/3 innings since May 4 and limited batters to a .205 average.
away_pitcher_note: Fife earned a spot in the rotation with two solid outings this month. He tossed 5 1/3 innings of one-run ball to beat the Padres for his first Major League win, then went 6 2/3 innings against the Braves for his longest career outing.

home_pitcher_note: Brandon Cumpton will make his Major League debut, stepping in for the injured A.J. Burnett. The 24-year-old spent 2012 in Double-A and comes with only 11 games of Triple-A experience. He relies on control and inducing grounders.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw allowed one run over seven innings in his last start but settled for a no-decision against the D-backs. The left-hander has allowed three earned runs or fewer in all but one of his 14 outings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Cole drew more than 30,000 fans to PNC Park on Tuesday night for his big league debut and didn't disappoint. He threw 6 1/3 innings, allowing two runs and seven hits with no walks in an 8-2 win. He retired 12 batters in a row at one point.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has gone seven innings in each of his last two outings and is throwing the ball better than he has all season. The right-hander tossed 6 1/3 scoreless innings to beat the Pirates on April 5, his first start of the year.

home_pitcher_note: In his last six starts, Leake has been mostly dominant, going 4-1 with a 1.13 ERA. His last outing was no exception, as he surrendered only one run and three hits in eight innings against the Cubs on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano has been called an injury-depleted rotation's "anchor" by manager Clint Hurdle -- a deserved confirmation of his impressive comeback. The ex-American Leaguer will be making his second career start against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Latos enters Tuesday without a loss in his last 21 starts, a franchise record. Even when he's been upset with his performance, like after allowing four runs on eight hits on Thursday in Chicago, he's pitched well enough to keep the Reds in games.
away_pitcher_note: Making his second start after recovering from Tommy John surgery, Morton should be over the nerves that marred the outset of his first outing. He appears to have a little extra on his fastball, which reached 95 mph on Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: After giving up three runs and 12 hits, one shy of a career high, on Friday, Arroyo said it was the best he's felt pitching deep in a game this season. He lasted 7 2/3 innings against the Brewers before giving up a game-tying homer.
away_pitcher_note: Locke continued as a major revelation with seven shutout innings in his last start, his fourth scoreless outing of the past six. He has lowered his ERA a full run in those six outings and has allowed only 40 hits in his past 67 innings.

home_pitcher_note: One game after getting to .500, Bailey couldn't contain the Crew on Saturday, giving up six runs on eight hits over seven. Bailey has allowed six or more runs in two of his past four starts, but he also has an eight-inning shutout in that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Cumpton earned a repeat start with a fine showing in his Major League debut on Saturday, when he had the Dodgers blanked entering the fifth. He lived up to his reputation as a control pitcher, throwing 50 of 76 pitches for strikes with one walk.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver managed to get through six innings in his last outing, but gave up five earned runs on seven hits. The Angels ace has struggled his past two starts, but looks to improve his command this time out.
away_pitcher_note: Cole already out-pitched a pair of former Cy Young award winners in the Giants' Tim Lincecum and the Dodgers' Zack Greinke to win his first two starts. He's allowed five runs in 12 innings on 14 hits with no walks and three strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Williams will fill in for Jason Vargas, who was placed on the 15-day DL on Friday. Williams has made seven starts for the Angels this season and last pitched three innings of relief on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano made just two major mistakes in his last outing Monday against the Reds. Unfortunately for him, they led to the first two homers he's allowed this year in his eighth start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander is coming off arguably his best start of the season as he limited the Mariners to two runs in 6 2/3 innings. Although his record doesn't indicate it, Blanton has seven quality starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: In his second start since returning from Tommy John surgery, Morton pitched 5 1/3 scoreless innings against the Reds on Tuesday, giving up just three hits and no walks. He said he feels stronger after taking a year off post-surgery.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders has posted a 1.82 ERA over his past five starts, but won only twice thanks to limited run support, including a 1-0 complete-game loss in Anaheim on Thursday. The 31-year-old is 10-2 with a 2.31 ERA in 16 career starts at Safeco Field.
away_pitcher_note: Seven innings of four-hit shutout ball in Cincinnati Thursday were routine for the lefty. Of his last 12 starts, it was the seventh time he didn't allow a run and the ninth time he gave up four hits or fewer. He's given up one earned run in six wins.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez had a seven-run lead his last time out before giving up 12 hits and six earned runs in an eventual Mariners loss. He pitched only five innings, allowing seven consecutive hits at one point.
away_pitcher_note: Gomez return from a DL stint with right forearm tightness to make his first start since June 2. He's been a big surprise, with the Pirates having won each of his seven starts, in which he has walked only nine in 30 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cole's first three starts were remarkably similar, as he has gone either 6 1/3 or 5 2/3 innings while allowing an average of six hits. Cole is aware of needing to throw more offspeed stuff to get the most out of that 100-mph fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Hellweg will make his Major League debut, receiving the call after Alfredo Figaro landed on the DL. He will become the 10th Brewer to start a game this year. He was 7-4 with a 2.82 ERA in 14 starts for Triple-A Nashville.

home_pitcher_note: Five quality starts out of his first nine testify to the impressive comeback by the veteran lefty, who is still recording more than a strikeout an inning (61 in 54 2/3) while dramatically reducing his walks. He has received a decision in every start.
away_pitcher_note: Hand made his first big league start against the Braves on Saturday and held them scoreless on two hits over 4 2/3 innings. Hand has spent most of his time as a long reliever since his May promotion from Triple-A Nashville.

home_pitcher_note: Morton makes his fourth start on the road back from Tommy John surgery. He matched his career high of five walks the last time out -- when he also had his trademark sinker, with only one ball hit in the air to the outfield in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse is working on five straight quality starts. He has faced the Pirates plenty in his career and is 9-2 with a 3.41 ERA against them. That's the highest winning percentage (.818) against any opponent in his 13-year career.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates recalled Cumpton from Triple-A to start in place of Jeff Locke. Locke, who is 7-1 with a 2.06 ERA, warmed up extensively Sunday and was set to enter the game in the 15th inning. But the Pirates won.
away_pitcher_note: Pettibone allowed three runs in the first inning Thursday against the Dodgers, but he retired the final 15 batters he faced and 17 of the final 18 to give the Phillies a chance to win the game at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Locke will start Wednesday after missing his start Tuesday because he warmed up extensively Sunday against the Brewers, and he would have entered the game in the 15th had it gone that far. He hasn't lost since April 7.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan allowed one run in seven innings to pick up the first win of his Phillies career Friday against the Dodgers. He went 3-for-4, the first Phillies pitcher to have three hits in a game since J.D. Durbin in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: The Cole Train, the first Pirates pitcher in 105 years with wins in each of his first four starts, will roll for No. 5 at PNC Park, where he is already 3-0. Unexpectedly, he has been primarily a pitch-to-contact guy so far (11 K's in 24 1/3 innings).
away_pitcher_note: Hamels got off the hook for his 12th loss on June 26 in a victory over San Diego. He struggled, allowing seven hits, five runs, two walks and one home run in six innings at Petco Park. He has blown leads in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija got a no-decision in his last start against the Mariners, but did post a quality start and did make an in-game adjustment that was key. Seattle was aggressive, and he switched his approach to throw them off.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano had a superb June, allowing just nine earned runs in 37 2/3 innings. He went at least six innings in each of those six starts and has allowed two runs or fewer in all but two of his 10 outings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson scattered seven hits over six-plus innings in his last start against the Mariners, and picked up his third win in his last five starts. One of those wins came against the Pirates June 9 when he held them to one run over seven innings.
