away_pitcher_note: Morton was chased from his start against the Brewers on Sunday after two innings because of a two-hour rain delay. Since coming back from Tommy John surgery, he's allowed 11 runs (five earned) in 18 innings over four starts.

home_pitcher_note: This would've been Scott Feldman's spot, but the right-hander was traded July 2 to the Orioles. Villanueva, who began the season in the rotation, will get the start. He's expected to go 60-70 pitches in his first start since May 14.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander comes off a month on the DL with a torn calf muscle to make his return start on the same mound where he had last appeared, in a June 8 victory over the Cubs -- which was his first win in seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: The young lefty pursues his ninth consecutive win, and his sixth in a row at PNC Park, where he has allowed two earned runs in his past 25 innings. In his brief career, Locke is 2-0 with an 0.93 ERA in three starts against AL teams.
away_pitcher_note: Colon had his eight-game winning streak snapped for his first loss since May 15 at Texas. The 40-year-old right-hander threw seven innings of two-run ball vs. the Cubs, as well as his first wild pitch since May 26, 2009.

home_pitcher_note: The sensational rookie took his first loss in his previous start -- which he left with a 2-1 lead in the sixth but with two men on base -- but seemed more comfortable pitching to spots rather than just firing the ball over the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Straily tossed seven innings and allowed a career-low one hit, extending his winning streak to a career-high four games with a win over the Cubs. The right-hander is 4-0 with a 3.02 ERA over his last eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Already a frontrunner for Comeback Player of the Year, Liriano comes off a complete game in search of his fourth straight win. He has been even sharper at home, where he has a 2.05 ERA in five starts and has yet to allow a homer in 30 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Milone took a two-hit shutout into the ninth last Friday against the Royals, but was pulled with one out, having given up three runs in the inning in an eventual win.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has logged only seven innings at home this season, and still seeks his first PNC Park win since May 12, 2012, a month before he had Tommy John surgery. He stretched to six innings for the first time in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Hefner has pitched admirably of late. He's allowed one earned run in six of his last seven starts, and he only allowed two in the other. Last September, he shut out the Pirates over seven innings in his only career start against them.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett hopes the restraints come off after he was limited to 66 pitches in his return start from a torn calf muscle. He had good movement on his pitches in that outing against the Cubs, and he came away confident of being back in a groove.
away_pitcher_note: Torres, who has replaced the injured Shaun Marcum in the rotation, will start Saturday's game against the Pirates. Matt Harvey was scratched with a blister.

home_pitcher_note: After winning his first four decisions, Cole now has a losing "streak" to get over, but he's actually coming off the best of his six starts. He went seven innings for the first time, and was done in only by a two-run homer by Oakland's Brandon Moss.
away_pitcher_note: Gee has dominated the Pirates in four career starts, going 2-0 with a 1.73 ERA. He took a no-decision in his last start on Tuesday against the Giants, allowing five runs on nine hits in 6 2/3 innings. He also struck out three and walked five.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has allowed three or fewer earned runs in 10 of 11 starts, and while he's allowed six earned runs in 19 innings in three starts against Pittsburgh, he allowed one in 13 innings in two June starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' top winner gets the ball to open second-half play where he dropped a tough decision a month ago. Liriano has stepped up his game even more the last two times out, allowing two runs and eight hits in 16 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Latos has lost three of five since starting 6-0 and threw a season-low four innings, allowing a season-high six earned runs his last time out. He's 5-1 with a 3.53 ERA at home but is 0-1 vs. the Pirates at home.
away_pitcher_note: From being the Pirates' biggest '12 winner, Burnett has gone to being their hard-luck non-winner. Never before in his career has he had only four wins 16 starts into a season, but he has pitched consistently well, as reflected by the ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey allowed four earned runs, 10 hits in six innings in a loss at Atlanta last start but was victimized by several soft-but-well-placed ground-ball hits. He's 0-2 with a 6.17 ERA (eight earned runs in 11 2/3 innings) since his no-hitter.
away_pitcher_note: The southpaw will bear close watching after being scratched from his final pre-break start with lower back tightness. If physically fine and on, expect a low-hit game that keeps his defense busy. Has given the Reds one earned run in two prior starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Haren pitched his best game of the season, throwing six shutout innings against the Marlins, but he didn't get a decision. Haren said all he needed was to rest his inflamed right shoulder.
away_pitcher_note: Morton makes only his second career start at Nationals Park, where he had a sharp outing in 2011, allowing one run in 5 2/3 innings. His trademark sinker has shown up regularly, although he has been hurt by occasionally leaving it up for homers.

home_pitcher_note: As Ross Detwiler continues to deal with a strained back, the Nationals will once again hand the ball to Jordan. Despite two losses, Jordan hasn't allowed more than three earned runs in each of his first four Major League starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cole has betrayed a tendency to settle down after rough beginnings. In his seven starts, he has allowed six runs in the first innings -- and nine total in his other 34 2/3 innings combined. He's maintaining a sharp strikeout-to-walk ratio (25-9).

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg only made one big mistake in his last outing against the Dodgers: a two-run homer to Hanley Ramirez in the third inning. Strasburg was otherwise solid, striking out six and scattering seven hits over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano came back rusty following a nine-day layoff created by the All-Star break. The lefty went just 4 1/3 innings in his shortest outing of the year, giving up five runs on five hits and four walks in a loss to the Reds on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez allowed just four hits and tied a career high with 11 strikeouts over six scoreless innings against the Dodgers. But once again, the offense couldn't give him enough run support to win, and he received a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: After weather delayed his last start for an hour and 17 minutes, Burnett gave up four runs (one earned) in the first inning on Saturday against the Reds. He bounced back to go 5 2/3 innings, allowing 10 hits and striking out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Alvarez has made steady progress in each of his four starts since coming off the disabled list. He comes off a no-decision at Milwaukee, where he threw seven scoreless innings, retiring 13 of the final 15 he faced.
away_pitcher_note: PNC Park is viewed as a haven for left-handers because of the spacious left-center alley, but Locke has been even better on the road, with a 1.73 ERA accompanying a 5-1 record. Last start was 10th allowing fewer than four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Tom Koehler threw one of his best games at hitter-friendly Coors Field in a 3-1 Marlins win Monday, allowing just one run in seven innings. He didn't walk a batter and struck out seven, the only run coming on a homer.
away_pitcher_note: Morton depends on his sinker probably more than any other pitcher relies on any one pitch. When he is keeping his infielders busy, he can be as dominant as any fireballer. But when he misses his mark, the ball tends to fly a long way.

home_pitcher_note: Fernandez didn't look like he lost a step with extended rest over the All-Star break his last time out, allowing two runs over seven innings in a 4-2 win against the Rockies. The All-Star struck out eight and walked two in his Coors Field debut.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie has done most of his work at home, but has been virtually untouchable in a pair of road starts, winning both while allowing only six hits in 13 1/3 innings (.133 opponents average). He's gone seven in two of his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano will take the hill hoping to continue a stellar run since mid-June. He has recorded six quality starts in his past seven outings, including shutouts of the Nationals and the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook is just 1-7 in his career against Pittsburgh. In 14 appearances (10 starts) vs. the National League Central foe, the righty has posted a 4.81 ERA with 21 walks to 44 strikeouts over 67 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett has given up 26 hits and walked seven batters in 18 1/3 innings in his three most recent starts. He has managed to get out of trouble each time, allowing two runs or fewer in all three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn improved his pacing issues his last time out and showed better efficiency the deeper into the game he went. Lynn's results have been inconsistent as of late, but he continues to be the league's run-support leader.

home_pitcher_note: Cumpton will make his fourth start of 2013 in game two of a doubleheader. He's allowed seven earned runs and 18 hits over 15 2/3 innings in three spot starts, the first coming on June 15. He's 4-7 with a 3.69 ERA for Triple-A Indianapolis this year.
away_pitcher_note: The team will add Lyons to the roster for the day, giving the lefty his first Major League start since June 21. After his demotion in June, Lyons went 4-0 with a 1.33 ERA and held opponents to a .133 average in six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Locke hopes to improve from his most recent outing during which he gave up a season-high-tying eight hits while walking six batters. The southpaw has given up three earned runs or fewer in 17 straight starts, and in 18 of 20 overall.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright has pitched seven innings in 11 of his last 13 games, but was outpitched in his last start. He lacked his usual efficiency, though that was more a credit to the Braves' approach than command troubles on his end.

home_pitcher_note: Morton will conclude the five-game NL Central showdown hoping to put the negative aspects of his previous start behind. Although he issued no walks, he was unhappy with his command and his sinker was inconsistent.
away_pitcher_note: Kelly earned a stay in the rotation by throwing 6 1/3 scoreless innings in a spot start on Saturday. Now that he's pitching on regular rest, Kelly should be free to approach a pitch count of 100, if necessary.

home_pitcher_note: Cole will aim to notch his third straight quality start after he was outdueled by rookie Jose Fernandez in his most recent outing. Pittsburgh manager Clint Hurdle was impressed by Cole's slider.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin gave up three runs Sunday before finishing with three scoreless innings in his seventh quality start in eight outings. Chacin went seven innings, giving up eight hits and striking out four.

home_pitcher_note: Already the first pitcher in 94 years (Earl Hamilton, 1918-19) to have 11 wins in his first 15 starts for the Pirates, Liriano will try to improve to 7-1 at PNC Park, where he has allowed only eight runs in 44 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa struggled with his location throughout a loss to the Braves on Monday night, when he gave up eight runs, five earned, and 10 hits in five innings. He said his chronic thumb issues had no bearing on his performance.

home_pitcher_note: Despite consistently strong efforts, Burnett has won only two of his 10 home starts, the last on May 3. His ERA is a career low, but he has had five ultra-quality starts (seven-plus innings, two runs or fewer) in which he did not get a win.
away_pitcher_note: Before Tuesday night at Atlanta, Nicasio had given up one run in 19 innings over three starts. But he gave up six runs and six hits in the fourth inning, and eight runs and 10 hits in four innings overall in the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Locke has lost two of his last three decisions -- 2-1 and 2-0. He did struggle through his roughest outing in his last start, getting a no-decision after allowing 10 hits and four runs to St. Louis. He's lacked his pinpoint control of late.
away_pitcher_note: Alvarez has been Miami's best starter not named Jose Fernandez as of late, recording four straight quality starts. The right-hander had a scoreless innings streak of 18 snapped in his most recent outing.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran righty is going through a frustrating phase -- his sinker has been getting pounded into the dirt, but balls keep finding holes. He's being challenged to stick with his strength and trust that balls will start finding gloves.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler earned his third win by notching his first career scoreless start in six innings against the Mets on Thursday. The right-hander has six quality starts, two of which have come in his past three outings.

home_pitcher_note: Although Cole's record has evened out after a record 4-0 start, he has continued to pitch with the same consistency. His current ERA actually is a bit lower than when he was 4-0 (3.70). He has struck out 14 in last two starts over 12 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Fernandez struck out 14 in his last start, the highest total by a National League pitcher this season. He has pitched 14 straight scoreless innings and fanned 27 batters during his past two starts. He has 14 quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa finished with four innings and three runs against, but a high pitch count and a lack of command led to a loss at Pittsburgh last Saturday -- his second straight short start in which his pitches missed frequently.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano seeks to stay hot in his introduction to a park unkind to pitchers. Liriano has gone seven-plus innings, allowing one run or none, in four of his last five starts. He did match his season high of five walks last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio worked in and out of trouble early his last time out, and was removed in the fifth with one out and two on. Manny Corpas gave up a homer, and Nicasio was charged with four earned runs in 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his 15th season, Burnett sports an ERA more than a run below his career mark. Belying the low win total, he has 13 quality starts among his 20. Burnett's only 31 off the NL strikeout lead, despite missing a month with a calf injury.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough debut, Bettis pitched well against the Mets. He allowed only two runs on four hits over five innings. He's still adjusting to Major League lineups, but he's pitched well once he settles in and learns opposing hitters' tendencies.
away_pitcher_note: Locke will be closely watched after allowing 27 hits in 16 1/3 innings in his last three starts. A problem has been slowing down his pace when in trouble. He is more effective working quickly, which puts hitters on the defensive.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright had been scheduled to pitch on Saturday, but the Cardinals tweaked their rotation to give him an extra three days of rest. St. Louis has won four of his last 10 starts; he has a 3.44 ERA during that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Morton turned in one of his best starts of the year Wednesday, allowing just six hits and two runs in seven innings. Morton has surrendered three earned runs or fewer in eight of 10 starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Miller took a line drive off his right elbow last Tuesday and left the game after tossing just two pitches, but he was back to playing catch within 24 hours. Miller is 0-2 with a 3.86 ERA vs. NL Central rival Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano had the worst start of his career in a loss to the Rockies, surrendering 10 runs and 12 hits in 2 1/3 innings. Liriano struggled to command any pitches, his ERA climbing from 2.02 to 2.83.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn cruised through six scoreless innings before the Cubs got to him for three runs in the seventh. The Cardinals struggled to score as the right-hander's bid for a 14th win fell short.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett was dominant for 5 2/3 innings Saturday night but could not record the last out of the sixth, leaving after allowing six runs (five earned) with eight strikeouts and three walks.

home_pitcher_note: After his last regular turn was skipped, Cole returns to start on eight days' rest. He'll be making his ninth home start out of 12, so his PNC Park numbers are a bit skewed (4.53 ERA vs. 2.66 on the road). He's lost five of his last six decisions.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy is making his third start since a two-month stint on the disabled list. Despite taking the loss, he was sharp in his last outing against the Mets allowing two runs on six hits over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Locke makes a fifth start in search of win No. 10, but he regained his low-hit effectiveness last time, allowing three hits in 5 2/3 in Denver. That was his 11th start with three hits or fewer allowed. The Bucs scored 15 runs in his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill will be making his first start since June 30 in Atlanta. He was on the disabled list for a right hip contusion but also experienced some shoulder tightness. He has tweaked his mechanics in order to improve his command.

home_pitcher_note: Morton had to take a tough no-decision in his last start, which he was in position to win over St. Louis until Starling Marte dropped a ninth-inning fly. He has been impressively consistent returning from Tommy John surgery.
away_pitcher_note: Miley allowed four runs in seven innings in his last start against the Orioles. Prior to that, he had gone nine straight starts without allowing more than three runs. He has won his past three decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Cashner retired the final 14 hitters he faced in his last start, a loss to the Rockies, as he allowed three runs in seven innings. He's thrown a career-high 130 1/3 innings, but he's showing no signs of tiring.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano followed a career-worst start in Denver with a complete-game win in St. Louis -- his second in eight starts after having only one in his first 151 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: There's a lot to like about Ross return to the starting rotation. He's 3-1 with a 1.32 ERA in his 5 starts since rejoining the rotation. Telling stats? Try Ross' 4.50 hits per nine innings and 2.65 walks per nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett's inability to hold leads -- not his chronic low run support -- has been the big problem in his last two starts, during which he squandered leads of 3-1 and 4-0. He allowed 10 runs and 16 hits in 10 innings in those two outings.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander is coming off his worst start since he joined the Padres at the Trade Deadline. The four walks and three home runs Kennedy allowed vs. the Mets led to five runs and his first defeat with his new club.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie makes what could be his final start of August under the Pirates' plan to reduce his workload to keep him fresh for a possible postseason run. The righty's ability to keep the ball low is helping him keep the ball in the park.

home_pitcher_note: Cain is coming off his fifth consecutive quality start in a second half that has seen the right-hander return to form after a rough first half. He has a 2.25 ERA in his past five starts (nine earned runs in 36 innings) since July 26.
away_pitcher_note: The young lefty tries to reverse a second-half trend that has seen him allow hits at double his first-half rate. His opponents' average has gone from .196 to .233 and the ERA from 2.11 to 2.90 in that stretch, covering six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner struggled in his most recent outing and has failed to record a quality start in back-to-back outings after notching 10 straight between June 14 and August 7. He is the only Giants starter with double-digit wins.
away_pitcher_note: Morton is on a streak of three very strong, very consistent starts, going either seven or six innings each time with two runs allowed. He has an exceptional 34-8 strikeouts-to-walks ratio in his past seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum has been consistent wherever he has pitched, compiling ERAs of 4.57 at home and 4.48 on the road. He also has recorded a 5.07 night ERA and a 2.00 ERA under sunlight. That's deceiving, since he has started just four day games.
away_pitcher_note: If he goes at least six innings -- and he has done that in 14 of his first 19 starts -- Liriano will finally qualify for listing among league leaders. He has the lowest homer yield (five) among MLB starters, including two in his past 58 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Before his last start, against Boston, opponents were batting .389 (21-for-54) off Vogelsong with runners in scoring position. But he improved against the Red Sox, holding them to 2-for-8 in such situations. Moreover, neither hit produced a run.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett snapped a little personal slide with seven strong innings his last time out, and will try to win a second consecutive start for the second time this season (Apr. 27 - May 3.).

home_pitcher_note: Locke had his shortest start of the season (four innings) last time out, also his sixth straight winless start. Control has become a big issue, with 14 walks and 12 strikeouts in last 17 innings. Has gone 1-3 in his last eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse is proving that when healthy, he is outstanding. His victory over the Cardinals on Tuesday was the 13th quality start in his last 16 outings, all since the beginning of June. In May, Lohse was bothered by a sore elbow.

home_pitcher_note: A series of solid, consistent starts has raised Morton's stock to dependable No. 3 starter status. He's averaged seven innings and two runs allowed in his last four outings and has not allowed a home run in his last 38 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny made it through just 3 2/3 innings against the Cardinals his last time out, giving up seven runs on 10 hits and a walk. He's surrendered 12 total runs in two outings since tossing seven innings of shutout ball vs. the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Cole continues as a real homebody, making his 10th of 14 starts in PNC Park. Despite six losses in eight decisions since beginning his career 4-0, he has been impressively consistent, allowing either two or three runs in 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: In each of his two starts since coming off the disabled list, Gallardo has gone at least six innings. He's given up a total of two earned runs, both of which came on Friday against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: The last time Liriano came came off a poor outing, he had a four-hitter in St. Louis. He looks to repeat that sequence off his four-inning start in S.F. He could be the first Bucs pitcher in 67 years with a decision in season's first 21 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Miller served up a solo homer in his first inning Saturday but then didn't miss a beat, retiring 18 of his next 21 batters. Miller will open a three-game set in Pittsburgh, a team he is 0-3 against in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett makes his fifth start of the season vs. the Cards and has won both decisions with a 2.96 ERA. He's held the NL's top hitting club to a .193 average and struck out 27 in 24 1/3 innings. He's given up four homers at home in 74 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Cards have won just four of Lynn's last 12 starts. He has been hurt largely by letting one inning get out of control. Lynn continues to pitch deep into games, but the Cards need him to be more effective in the early going.

home_pitcher_note: The 28-year-old lifelong Minor Leaguer makes his first big league start, two weeks after a cameo relief appearance: On Aug. 18, in his Major League debut, he blanked Arizona for five extra-innings before allowing two runs in the 16th.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals are 8-1 in Kelly's starts since he joined the rotation July 6. The right-hander is 6-0 with a 2.24 ERA in his those nine outings and has allowed more than one earned run just three times in that span.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers decided they had seen enough of Tom Gorzelanny in the starting rotation and returned him to the bullpen in favor of Thornburg, who allowed only one earned run in 18 innings over his first three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hitting his stride following return from Tommy John surgery, Morton has been team's most consistent starter for a month, averaging seven innings with a 1.83 ERA his last five starts. Got Bucs' only win in recent series with Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo worked seven scoreless innings to beat the Pirates on Thursday, and will get a rematch. Since Gallardo debuted in 2007, only the Reds' Johnny Cueto has more wins against the Pirates than Gallardo's 11. Cueto has 13.
away_pitcher_note: Although Cole has gone 2-7 since starting his career with four straight wins, his ERA has hardly varied through 14 starts. His run support has suffered more than his pitching: eight runs in the last six losses. He has nine quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta's sinker should play at hitter-friendly Miller Park, but he has struggled in home games this season to the tune of a 5.12 ERA in 14 starts. On the road, he has a 3.94 ERA in 14 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano, who did not make his first start until Game No. 36, will finally qualify for listing among league leaders by pitching five innings; right now has fourth-best ERA. Coming off seventh scoreless start, against Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: No one on the Cardinals' staff has been better over the last two months than Kelly, who has won his last seven decisions. The Cards are 9-1 in his starts since moving Kelly into the rotation, and he's finished six innings in his last four games.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett goes after his fourth win of the season against the Cardinals, who have hit .188 against him in five prior starts, but .310 in two Busch Stadium meetings. He has 33 strikeouts in 31 1/3 innings against them.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright has faced the Pirates twice this season, both since the All-Star break, and he's come away with no decisions and a 4.50 ERA, allowing 13 hits and seven runs in 14 innings. He's allowed 18 hits and 15 runs over his past two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Returning from a brief "mental blow" on a Minor League option, Locke makes his first start since Aug. 27. He is seeking his first win in eight starts after posting a 7.02 ERA with a .373 opponents average in the past seven.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie was impressive in his start against the Reds on Tuesday, logging six shutout innings in which he allowed just three hits and two walks. Just one runner reached second base against Wacha, and that was on a wild pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Since the All-Star break, Morton is 6-1 with a team-low 2.90 ERA, and pits that recent trend against his lifetime trend opposite the Cardinals, against whom he is 2-8 with a 6.00 ERA in 13 starts, two of them this season.

home_pitcher_note: Darvish is 0-2 with a 4.50 ERA in his past four starts. Texas has lost all four. Darvish is 7-4 with a 2.82 ERA in 15 starts at home. He has never faced the Bucs, but is 4-0 with a 1.93 ERA in five career starts against National League teams.
away_pitcher_note: The high-profile rookie righty is very aware of his pitching circumstances and figures to get up for this duel with Yu Darvish. Cole has seen more action at home, but each of his five on the road have been quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Perez is 6-0 with a 2.54 ERA in his last starts. His nine wins ties the Rangers rookie record for most wins by a left-hander. He is 2-1 with a 2.20 ERA in five games at home this season. He is 2-1 with a 2.37 ERA in three Interleague starts.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano will try to repeat his bounce-back success after a third poor outing. He followed the first two with a complete game and another start of eight shutout innings. His control has never wavered; two walks or fewer in 14 of 22 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garza struggled his last time out, allowing six runs (five earned) on nine hits in seven innings. The right-hander has allowed four or more runs in six of his past seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran righty is running out of chances to post double-figure wins for a ninth straight season. His ERA is at its highest since April 12. He has to compensate for the slight drop in pitch movement and speed with sharper command.

home_pitcher_note: Locke appeared to get back on track in his last start but remained with one win in nine second-half starts because the Bucs were shut out. He was still fighting command issues, walking four more for an NL-leading total of 78.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin's high pitch count resulted in an abbreviated start in his last outing against the Brewers. He gave up two runs over 3 2/3 innings, and was pulled after 85 pitches. He has a 2.89 ERA, second-lowest among rookie left-handed starters this season.

home_pitcher_note: Morton got a scare when he had to leave his last start with two outs in the second when an old issue -- plantar fasciitis -- flared up. He hopes to be able to resume the hot streak he'd been in, with a 1.74 ERA in his six prior starts.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta has walked three or more batters in five of his six starts, and it hurt him in his last start against the Brewers. While command is an issue, he is holding opponents to a .178 opponents' batting average since joining the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off the best start of his young big league career, Cole hopes to find the success that has been avoiding him at home, where his ERA (4.27) is two points higher than on the road and where he has won only once in his last seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching on a Major League mound for the first time in more than two years, Baker limited the Brewers to two hits in five shutout innings on Sunday. He threw just 55 pitches, 39 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano has stumbled a few times on the road, but has been near infallible at PNC Park, where he's gone 8-1 with a 1.21 ERA while holding hitters to a .185 average. Most impressive is the fact he's yet to give up a home run at home in 59 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wood blanked the Reds for seven innings on Monday, as he picked up his first win against his former club. After the game, Cubs manager Dale Sveum said Wood is the team's undisputed No. 1 starter.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett struck out seven over 6 1/3 innings vs. the Rangers his last start. He faded late after retiring the first 13 batters. With his breaking ball working, Burnett struck out five in the first two innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching on nine days' rest, Cashner held the Phillies to two runs over 7 2/3 innings with one walk and seven strikeouts. He has a 2.78 ERA in his last 10 starts and hasn't allowed more than two runs in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Locke held the Cubs to one run and three hits over seven innings to win Thursday for the first time since July 21. Locke had been 0-3 with a 6.57 ERA in his previous eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Stults hasn't won since July 14, though he did pitch better his last time out, allowing two solo home runs in six innings in a no-decision against the Phillies. He's 0-6 with a 5.40 ERA in his past 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Morton was solid in a no-decision against the Cubs on Friday, surrendering three runs on four hits over his five innings of work. Morton walked a pair and struck out five, needing 93 pitches to get through his outing.
away_pitcher_note: Ross struggled from the outset in his last start against the Phillies, allowing six earned runs in two-thirds of an inning. His ERA jumped from 2.79 to 3.29. He had been good since rejoining the rotation prior to that start.

home_pitcher_note: Cole delivered another dominant performance in Saturday's victory over the Cubs, allowing just one run on five hits over his seven frames. The young right-hander punched out seven while issuing three free passes.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy got a no-decision in his last start against the Braves as he allowed two home runs (three runs overall)in six innings against the Braves. Kennedy has allowed the second-most (25) home runs in the National League.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty puts his 1.37 home ERA on the line. Three of his losses and three of the seven home runs off him belong to the Reds. But the key lefty hitters in Cincinnati's lineup (Joey Votto, Jay Bruce) are 2-for-16 against Liriano.
away_pitcher_note: Latos was nickel-and-dimed for five earned runs against the Brewers on Friday. Two bloop singles accounted for three runs, and a liner lost in the lights by Ryan Ludwick also worked against him. Latos is 4-1 with a 3.86 ERA in his career vs. Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett has allowed three runs or fewer in each of his 13 home starts this season. Is nine strikeouts away from his third season with 200, and first since 2008. Has not allowed a PNC Park homer in 36 1/3 innings since May 29.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start vs. the Brewers on Saturday, Bailey tied a season-high by walking four batters, but he made key pitches when he needed to. "I just wasn't very sharp," said Bailey after the game.

home_pitcher_note: Locke's away and home records are identical (5-3), but his ERA in PNC Park (4.41) is more than double the road mark. This could be his last chance to prove he'd belong on a postseason roster: His ERA has risen from 2.11 on July 21.
away_pitcher_note: With 192 1/3 innings heading into Sunday, Arroyo has a chance to crack the 200-innings mark for the eighth time in his last nine seasons. The only time he missed was 2011, when he pitched 199 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija reached the 200 strikeouts/200 innings mark vs. the Brewers. This will be his penultimate start. He is 1-3 against the Pirates, with the lone win coming Opening Day. He ranks among NL leaders in strikeouts with 203.
away_pitcher_note: Morton recovered quickly, and emphatically, from the scare of the left-foot injury he suffered on Sept. 8. He comes off possibly his best career start, allowing two infield singles in eight innings with a season-high nine strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin most recently lasted four innings vs. the Brewers. He had trouble keeping his pitches down, walking two batters in the first before serving up a grand slam. It was only the third time he failed to pitch beyond the fourth this year.
away_pitcher_note: Though he enters after pitching the best game of his young career in PNC Park (12 strikeouts), Cole has been far more effective on the road, with a 2.29 ERA. He is six strikeouts shy of reaching 100 for his rookie season.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Arrieta's last start of the season. He hopes he can duplicate his last start against the Brewers when he gave up three hits over seven innings. Milwaukee's Carlos Gomez said Arrieta had "filthy stuff."
away_pitcher_note: For all of his overall success, the left-hander has had a tough time on the road, with a 4.15 ERA in 14 starts, but not at Wrigley Field. He's won both of his starts there, allowing six hits and two runs in 16 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Reds have lost each of Bailey's three starts against the Pirates this season. Bailey has gone 0-2 with a 3.50 ERA in those starts, including Saturday's loss, in which he gave up four runs (two earned) in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett tries to keep the Bucs in the NL Central hunt, or at least book the NL Wild Card game for PNC Park, by reaching doubles-figures in wins for the ninth straight season. He was masterful in his last start, against the Reds in Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo will make his first start since Sept. 22, also against the Pirates. He earned the win in that outing despite allowing three runs on five hits and two walks in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Morton has been the picture of consistency since July, allowing two runs or fewer in eight of 10 starts. He made his second comeback start in Great American Ball Park and blanked the Reds on three hits for 5 1/3 innings on June 18.

home_pitcher_note: Reynolds was plugged in for another start as the Reds are now saving Johnny Cueto to start Tuesday's Wild Card Game. Reynolds lasted only 3 2/3 innings his last time out vs. Houston and three of his four hits allowed for two runs were extra bases.
away_pitcher_note: The young righty will start the regular season's final game, some exposure for the 24-year-old who will compete for a rotation spot next spring. In the last of four mid-season spot starts, Cumpton blanked the Cards on three hits for seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates' biggest winner has a home ERA (1.47) about one-third what it is on the road (4.33). Will that neutralize his issues against the Reds, who have accounted for three of his losses and four of the nine homers he's allowed?
away_pitcher_note: Making his third start since coming off the DL, Cueto will see the Pirates for the third time at PNC Park this season. In his previous two starts in Pittsburgh, he's allowed just one run and three hits, including eight scoreless frames on May 31.
series_status: PIT wins NL Wild Card Game

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright has been at his best in October, where he has a 2.48 ERA through 32.2 innings (four starts, nine relief outings). In Game 1 of the NLDS last year, he held Washington to one run while fanning 10 over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' most experienced postseason pitcher makes his seventh start, his first since Game 4 of the 2011 ALDS, in which he beat Detroit for the Yankees. Burnett equaled his career-low 3.30 ERA and topped 200 K's for the first time since 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn has been considerably better at home this season, posting a 2.82 ERA at Busch Stadium versus a 5.15 mark on the road. He overcame a rough stretch of outings to allow just three earned runs in his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander gets the postseason spotlight after tying for the second most wins on the staff despite not making his debut until early June. He has pitched less but been more effective on the road, and will be facing the Cardinals for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano overcame both a severe flu and the Reds in the Wild Card Game, continuing his mastery in PNC Park, where he has won nine of 10 decisions overall and allowed one home run in 80 2/3 innings. The Reds simply could not handle his hard slider.
away_pitcher_note: Kelly posted a 10-2 record and 2.18 ERA in 15 games after joining the rotation in early July. He won all three of his season starts against the Pirates, allowing just two earned runs in 18 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander would be going on eight days' rest, his last start coming on Sept. 28. The extra rest might benefit him, since he gave up three runs in 4 1/3 innings in that one after allowing one run in 15 innings in his two prior outings.
away_pitcher_note: Wacha gets the Game 4 nod over fellow rookie Shelby Miller because of how dominant he was in September. Wacha had a 1.72 ERA in five starts last month and carried a no-hitter through 8 2/3 innings in his last one.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright tossed a gem in Game 1 of the NLDS, allowing one run on three hits and fanning nine over seven innings, and now is tasked with keeping the Cards' season alive and leading his club to the NLCS.
away_pitcher_note: Cole punctuates his rookie half-season with an exclamation mark by getting the start in the Pirates' biggest game in 21 years. He earned that honor by posting a 1.66 ERA in his last six starts, including his six innings of two-hit pitching in Game 2.

summary: 2014-03-01 - Tampa Bay Rays @ Pittsburgh Pirates (Final: Tied)

home_pitcher_note: The 2013 NL Comeback Player of the Year already has his first comeback of '14: Liriano's Opening Day start was jeopardized by a tight left groin muscle suffered on March 20, but he made a quick recovery.
away_pitcher_note: This is Samardzija's second straight Opening Day start. Last year he held the Pirates to two hits over eight scoreless innings for the win. He's the first pitcher to make back-to-back Opening Day starts at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: The new anchor of the rotation begins to earn his three-year, $21 million contract against a Cubs team he has beaten only twice in nine career starts. Morton had a solid spring, putting up a 1.13 ERA in three Grapefruit League starts.

away_pitcher_note: Wood did not get a decision in his last start, giving up two runs on four hits over five innings. He walked a season-high five batters. However, he did help himself by hitting a two-run homer and driving in another run on a fielder's choice.

home_pitcher_note: The young righty has to diversify his stuff to become more competitive later in games. In his young career, has held batters to an average of .209 through the third inning, and the figure mushrooms to .339 thereafter.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez has turned into one of the Pirates' most consistent (fewer than three runs allowed in seven of his 12 starts) and durable (averaging six innings) starters. The confidence to pitch to contact has been a big key for him.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija got back on track Saturday with his 10th quality start in 13 outings. He held the Marlins to five hits over seven innings and struck out eight. He also collected a single, and now is two shy of matching his career high of seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Eovaldi comes off a no-decision at Wrigley Field, where he matched a season high with eight strikeouts. Eovaldi threw 7 2/3 innings. In his last two starts, he's combined to throw 15 2/3 innings, allowing five runs.
away_pitcher_note: Stepping into the Bucs' injury-ravaged rotation, Locke allowed just three hits and one run over seven innings of a tough-luck loss to the Brewers on Sunday. This will be his third start of 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf makes his fourth start since signing with Miami in May. The lefty has pitched at least five innings in each start. He comes off a loss at the Cubs, where he gave up four runs in 5 2/3 innings with two strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Morton turned a couple extra days of rest prior to his last start into one of the sharpest of his career. For only the third time in 121 starts, he went at least seven innings without a walk. In last 33 starts, ERA is 3.21.

home_pitcher_note: Alvarez had his streak of 26 straight scoreless innings snapped in his last outing, a no-decision against the Cubs. He suffered a strained left hip in that game, causing him to exit in the sixth inning, but he's fine for this start.
away_pitcher_note: Worley (3-2, 4.30 ERA for Triple-A Indianapolis) will make his Pirates debut on Sunday. He is 1-1 with a 1.80 ERA in three career games (two starts) against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Cumpton gave up two runs on five hits with two walks and five strikeouts vs. the Cubs in his previous start. He took a loss vs. the Reds in April despite notching a quality start in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto pitched six scoreless innings while tying a career high with 12 strikeouts and wanted to go a seventh against the Dodgers. But he was pulled, in part, because he had thrown 112 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez is coming off a scoreless seven-inning performance vs. the Cubs on Thursday. The righty is 1-1 (four starts) with a 3.55 ERA against his former team. He allowed the Reds two runs in seven innings in a 4-1 loss on April 22.
away_pitcher_note: Simon tossed eight strong innings against the Dodgers on Thursday, allowing one run on seven hits, walking one and and striking out five to earn his ninth win. He is 2-3 with a 2.57 ERA in 15 career appearances (one start) against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Locke got a no-decision vs. the Marlins on Friday in his previous start. He gave up two runs, struck out seven and walked none in a career-high eight innings. Against the Reds, he is 2-1 with a 3.04 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: In Friday's no-decision vs. the Crew, Bailey had a long fourth inning that brought him up to 70 pitches. He course-corrected and used only 22 over the next two scoreless innings. He seems to have righted himself the past 11 starts after a bad April.

away_pitcher_note: With his record finally catching up to his ERA, Morton will try to win a fourth straight start for the first time in his career. Making his fourth start of the season against Cubs, Morton's fanned 18 of them in 19 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wood had his best stuff of the season his last time out, throwing eight scoreless innings in Philly. The 2013 All-Star owns a 4.48 ERA this season, but has starts of seven and eight earned runs that have put a damper on an otherwise solid year.
away_pitcher_note: The former Phillies righty has posted a 1.20 ERA in two career starts against the Cubs. Despite throwing seven shutout innings in his Pirates debut, he's seeking his first win since May 11, 2013 -- and only his second since Aug. 1, 2012.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel had a tough time with his slider in his last start against the Marlins in Miami. He needed 29 pitches to get through the first inning, and gutted out six innings. He's 2-1 this season against the Pirates, losing in his last start on June 11.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his third quality start in the last six, Cumpton threw a career-high 99 pitches against the Reds on Tuesday. He's had to pitch out of a lot of trouble, but keeping the ball in the park (one homer in 38 2/3 innings) has helped.

home_pitcher_note: The Rays wasted a gem from Cobb in his last start, losing to the Orioles, 2-0, despite seven strong from their right-hander. Cobb allowed just one unearned run -- which lowered his ERA to 3.48 -- but that was enough to drop him to 2-5 on the season.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez will try to rebound from his shortest (2 1/3 innings) and poorest (eight runs) start of the season, with some suspecting he may have been overamped to face his former Reds team. He has allowed two homers in last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his second consecutive start against the Astros, Archer rebounded from a six-run outing (although only one of those runs was earned) to shut out Houston over 6 2/3 innings of work in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty again tries for that elusive first win, having departed three of his four starts with a lead that did not hold up. Last season's NL leader in walks has shown remarkable control, with only two bases on balls in 26 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Price recorded his 1,000th career strikeout during his last start, a loss to Houston in which the left-hander threw eight innings, allowed just two runs and struck out 12. He leads the bigs in K's (133) and double-digit strikeout games.
away_pitcher_note: Morton comes off a most unusual start in which he allowed six earned runs for the first time since July 29, 2011, along with two homers, of the season total of six he has allowed. He has a 1-5 Interleague record -- the win coming in first MLB start.

home_pitcher_note: Worley, who is 1-0 with a 1.98 ERA in two starts for the Pirates this season, opens the series against the Mets. The right-hander gave up three runs in 6 2/3 innings against the Cubs in his most recent start on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka was charged with his first loss since last September in his last start vs the Marlins. He threw 5 1/3 innings and gave up only one run while striking out four. Dating back to 2013, he is 5-1 with a 2.20 ERA in his last nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cumpton has split his time in 2014 between the Majors and Triple-A, but the right-hander has made four straight starts for the Bucs. Most recently, he beat the Cubs with seven innings of scoreless baseball.
away_pitcher_note: In his eighth start of the season, deGrom captured his elusive first career win. And he dazzled in doing so, striking out seven Marlins in seven shutout innings. He only allowed five hits after allowing 26 in his previous three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Pittsburgh manager Clint Hurdle announced Wednesday that Cole, who has been on the disabled list with right shoulder fatigue, would get the call. Cole last pitched on June 3 in San Diego, when he gave up one run in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Niese finally got some support in his start against the Marlins on Sunday. He gave up three runs in the sixth but was able to record his 12th quality start of the season. He hasn't allowed more than three earned runs in 19 consecutive starts.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez tries to even his record off his best effort in nearly two years on Monday vs. the Rays. He went eight frames for the first time since a complete-game one-hitter on July 19, 2012. He is 1-5 with a 6.63 ERA in eight career starts vs. the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Colon shut down the A's -- the most productive offense in baseball -- for eight innings Tuesday, allowing one run on four hits. In seven starts since May 17, the right-hander has a 1.58 ERA, 0.88 WHIP and 4.33 strikeout-to-walk ratio.

home_pitcher_note: Locke goes on two days' extra rest since earning his first win, and in 10 starts with more than five days of rest the results have not been pretty (2-5, 5.00 ERA). But he's been a new pitcher all around since a Minor League detour.
away_pitcher_note: Miley is searching for his first win since May 10, a span of eight starts. Last time out he allowed five runs (four earned) over four innings against the Indians. He has allowed a whopping 17 home runs this year.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has morphed into quite a power pitcher in his last five starts, with 39 strikeouts (versus nine walks) in 32 innings. Yet he will be trying to avoid a third straight loss. Has allowed one homer in PNC Park in 44 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson won his first five big league starts, but has now lost his last three. Last time out against the Indians he allowed four runs on seven hits over five innings. This is his first look at the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Little attention was paid when Worley was acquired from the Twins in late March, but he has been an instant hit, with three straight super-quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy is still looking for his first win over a team other than the Padres. Last time out, he held San Diego to just one run over seven innings. McCarthy's name has been mentioned prominently in trade talks.

home_pitcher_note: Cole's return start following 3 1/2 weeks on the DL with shoulder fatigue didn't go well (at four innings, his shortest career outing). It just took him a while to catch up to real-game speed, and he should now be able to adjust.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez allowed two earned runs on three hits, three walks and struck out two in seven innings on Saturday in a loss against Atlanta. It was just the second time in 15 starts he pitched seven or more innings.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez has an active streak of 13 shutout innings, which may seem modest, but not for someone who career-long has been plagued by inconsistency. Since allowing four homers in May 17 start against Yankees, he has gave up two in 45 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Buchanan allowed three runs in five innings in a loss to Atlanta on Sunday. The rookie has had some control issues over his last two starts, walking nine in just 10 innings. He's allowed three or fewer runs in three of his past four starts.

home_pitcher_note: A special occasion for Locke, dueling Burnett, a guy he idolized during their two seasons as teammates. Locke himself has been someone to admire since his return from Triple-A: He has issued just five walks in 41 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett allowed six hits, four runs (three earned), four walks and struck out 10 in six innings Tuesday in Miami. He generally has pitched well this season, although he could be dealt before the deadline.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright became the NL's first 11-game winner and ERA leader with 7 2/3 scoreless innings on Wednesday. He has not allowed a run in eight of his starts and half of his 26 runs allowed came in two games. He's scattered the other 13 among 15 outings.
away_pitcher_note: The sinkerballer ended a personal two-start losing skid in his latest outing, holding the D-backs to one run on five hits in six innings. Morton lowered his season ERA to 3.30 in the process.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez has made four starts since joining the rotation, and the Cardinals have won all four. He has a 2.45 ERA as a starter and is now stretched out to where he can push toward 100 pitches. To this point, 88 pitches remains his season high.
away_pitcher_note: Worley took a no-hitter into the sixth inning against Arizona in his previous start. However, it went downhill in a matter of batters as he surrendered three runs and picked up his first loss of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn proved again to be resilient as he followed up a two-inning, six-run start with 6 2/3 scoreless innings Friday against the Marlins. Lynn has been dealing with a blister on his middle finger, but said it doesn't pose a major problem.
away_pitcher_note: After having to return to Triple-A despite an undefeated June to make room for Gerrit Cole, Cumpton returns to step in for the DL-ed Cole. He made one Indianapolis start in the interim, allowing eight hits and four runs in six innings on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Miller worked out of jams in his Saturday outing, going 5 1/3 innings, allowing three runs on nine hits. The right-hander has been working through some kinks, as his previous outing had been one of five innings in which he allowed six runs.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez pitched around some early command problems to hold the Phillies to just one run in seven innings in his latest start. His scoreless streak was halted at 16 innings, but the righty has allowed one or no runs in four of his past five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Latos tossed eight innings, allowing two runs on four hits to earn the win over the Brewers on Sunday. He has posted a 1.64 ERA over his last three starts. In 11 career starts against the Pirates, he is 5-1 with a 2.96 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: After never before going past the seventh inning, Locke has pitched into the eighth in four of his last five starts. He's averaging less than a walk per start (six in seven) after leading the NL last season with 84 walks in his 30 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Leake allowed three runs (two earned) on nine hits over seven innings, walking one and striking out seven to earn the win against the Cubs on Monday. In 17 career starts against the Pirates, he's 6-3 with a 3.40 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Morton has won four of his last six decisions, but his record still doesn't square with his ERA. He has won only two of his six ultra-quality starts of seven-plus innings pitched and no more than two earned runs allowed.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto went 6 1/3 innings in a win over the Cubs on Tuesday, allowing two runs on six hits, walking one and striking out four. The All-Star is 15-4 with a 2.18 ERA in 24 career starts against the Pirates, including four complete games.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano makes his return after a month-long absence with a strained left oblique. He has one win in his last 17 regular-season starts. He lasted longer than five innings in only one of his last nine starts before landing on the DL.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano also started in the Pirates' final game of the first half -- his first outing since his side forced him to the DL. Liriano lasted just four innings in his return, as he walked six batters and gave up three runs.
away_pitcher_note: In four starts since June 24, De La Rosa -- pitching most of the season with a lower back strain and a bruised left middle finger is 4-0 with a 3.76 ERA and has been all the Rockies could count on in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: The sinkerballer enters his second half coming off a start in which one inning went wrong. Morton faced one more than the minimum through five innings in his last start, but then gave up five runs in the sixth against Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson gave up five runs in the first inning of his return last Sunday against the Twins, but went five more innings and yielded one more run. The Rockies need for him to be efficient and effective.

home_pitcher_note: Locke has had staying power in the Pirates' rotation since joining full time in early June. The lefty has made seven consecutive quality starts, including his last outing when he worked around nine hits to allow only one run in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Matzek has been more competitive than effective overall as a rookie, but he has had stronger run prevention on the road (3.63 ERA in three starts) than at home (5.92 in four starts).

home_pitcher_note: Volquez tossed a complete game in his last start, just the second of his career. He got his eighth win of the season as he held the Cardinals to one run on six hits and struck out five.
away_pitcher_note: After closing out the first half with six scoreless innings of two-hit ball in which he struck out 10, Ryu will attempt to carry that success into his first second-half start. In all, 13 of his 18 outings have been quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander will be making his first start since July 8 on Monday against the Dodgers. Worley also pitched two innings of relief on July 13 and has a 7.71 ERA in his last two appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Battling a hip impingement, which was revealed to be a torn labrum with two cysts in his left hip, Beckett will return to the rotation after a 40-pitch bullpen session Saturday. The 34-year-old right-hander has a 2.26 ERA in 17 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano settled down after a first two innings full of baserunners in his first start after the break. The lefty didn't allow a hit in his final three frames and gave up one run in his second start since a month-long DL stint (strained left oblique).
away_pitcher_note: For the second straight start, Haren couldn't get out of the fifth inning Friday, surrendering three runs in 4 2/3 innings. The right-hander hasn't pitch six innings in six of his last nine outings and has a 9.64 ERA in three July starts.

home_pitcher_note: He faces off again with the Pirates, whom he held to one run and four hits in seven strong innings. Anderson finished with eight strikeouts, including three in his final inning when he relied solely on a slider he placed well.
away_pitcher_note: With his specialty sinker, Morton is not worried about the long-ball dangers of pitching in Coors Field, where he is 1-0. He has seven ultra quality starts (seven-plus innings, two earned runs or fewer), winning only two of them.

home_pitcher_note: While he hasn't won since his stellar debut on June 11, Matzek has been one of the Rockies' most effective starters. The 23-year-old has produced a quality start in half of his eight outings and registered a career-high eight K's in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: The only left-handed starter not named Clayton Kershaw to have fewer walks (eight) than games started (nine), Locke has departed four games with a lead in which he did not get the victory. He's working on a streak of eight straight quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Morales had his longest outing for the Rox since rejoining the rotation. He lasted six frames, surrendering four runs (three earned) to the Nats. It could have been a lot worse, considering he permitted nine hits and four walks.
away_pitcher_note: With 10 days between starts around the All-Star break, Volquez was out of sync on Monday, ending his four-start winning streak. Since allowing four homers to the Yankees on May 17, he has given up three in 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: The two-time All-Star is still striving to improve his fortunes at AT&T Park, where he's 4-5 with a 5.22 ERA this year. Bumgarner struck out 10 batters in three of his first 11 starts but has not reached double-digits in his last 10 outings.
away_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old righty was thrust into the rotation thanks to injuries to Gerrit Cole and Francisco Liriano and has made the most of his opportunity -- he's 3-1 with a 3.10 ERA in seven appearances.

home_pitcher_note: The four-time All-Star has lost his last three starts at AT&T Park. Yet, Hudson's home statistics overall remain above average. Hudson's 5-3 with a 3.13 ERA in the bayside ballpark.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano has allowed only one earned run in his last 14 innings. Interestingly, the Pirates are 7-1 in his no-decision starts. His '13 start in AT&T Park was one of his poorest (nine hits and four runs allowed in four innings).

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum's 27-inning home scoreless streak was snapped in the first inning of his last start, an 8-1 loss to the Dodgers. He's still 6-3 with a 3.09 ERA at AT&T Park, compared to 3-4, 5.44 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Morton's mistakes in his last go were a hanging curveball and a sinker that never sunk. Ernesto Frieri didn't do him any favors when he took over, but Morton looked like the same pitcher who had a 2.73 ERA over his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter had the worst start of his big league career last time out against the Phillies. He allowed six runs on 11 hits and was removed with two outs in the third. He had allowed just two runs in his previous two starts.
away_pitcher_note: The theory that Locke is a more confident pitcher not shaken by a bad outing will be tested as he comes off having allowed 10 hits in his last start, including three homers -- matching the total he had given up in his first eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nuno deserved a better fate his last time out against the Phillies. He allowed four runs (two earned) in 6 2/3 innings. He threw a career-high 117 pitches. Nuno was victimized by some poor defense in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez labored the last time out -- managing only 4 1/3 innings out of 99 pitches, his briefest start of the season. He has a losing career record against the NL West (11-18), but has held his own against the D-backs (3.86 ERA in nine starts).

home_pitcher_note: Anderson pitched well enough to win last time out against the Reds, allowing just one run over seven innings, but got a no-decision. In two starts since getting 14 days to freshen up his arm Anderson has a 2.08 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Vanimal was spectacular in twirling his first career shutout Monday in San Francisco, but that was only the best of his six quality starts -- out of the seven he has made. He's shown exceptional control, averaging a walk per start.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill had his best start since coming back up from the Minors last time out against the Reds, allowing three runs in six innings. He has not walked a batter in two straight starts for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Unlike the guy who struggled before, Liriano has been his old self since recovering from a strained left oblique. He has allowed two earned runs in his last 21 innings, with 26 strikeouts in them. His opponents' average is down to .231.

home_pitcher_note: Morton will try to bounce back from having allowed four-plus runs in consecutive starts for the first time since early in May 2012. Needs only two strikeouts to match his career high of 110 in 2010 in 171 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Before the Nats scored two in the eighth, Hand had retired 21 of 24 batters after a first-inning run. He took the loss, but in his seven-plus innings, allowed just five hits and two walks. He's gone at least seven in three straight.

home_pitcher_note: Locke has been roughed up in his last two starts, in which he has allowed as many homers (five) as in the first nine starts combined. In a June 13 meeting in Miami, went eight innings for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler was enjoying his best start Thursday vs. the Reds, needing just 83 pitches to get through seven-plus innings, but it all went for naught as an overturned call saddled him with a loss. He was charged with two runs, none earned.

home_pitcher_note: Though he remained winless since the All-Star break, Volquez followed his last start by saying he finally felt back where he was at the end of the first half, which he finished by reeling off four straight wins (3 runs in 30 innings).
away_pitcher_note: Flynn was called up on Tuesday to be used in long relief. But Jarred Cosart has a sore left oblique and has been scratched. Flynn is getting the nod. This will be his fifth MLB start and sixth appearance.

home_pitcher_note: Worley has been dominant in three starts since the All-Star break. Since the Midsummer Classic, Worley has an 0.86 ERA -- a number heavily boosted by a shutout he tossed against the Giants on July 28.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy hasn't lost since June 25 and has been very durable, missing only one start due to a sore left oblique toward the end of July. Better still, he's been good on the road, posting a 3.18 ERA away from Petco Park.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty has not allowed more than four hits in any of his last seven starts, a streak dating back to early June. And in five starts since coming off the DL (strained left oblique), Liriano has a 2.17 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Stults won his last time out, for only the second time since May 10, when he held the Braves to no earned runs on two hits over 6 1/3 innings. He's struggled on the road, posting a 5.78 ERA in 12 starts away from spacious Petco Park.

home_pitcher_note: Morton's last start didn't yield a victory after the Pirates' bullpen blew an eighth-inning lead. However, Morton was able to limit the Marlins to one run on six hits and four walks in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ross hasn't lost since July 13 and it's easy to see why. The Padres' All-Star selection has dominant stuff and logs a lot of innings. He's fourth in the league in innings (154 2/3) and he's allowed two or fewer runs in each of his past nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Locke was a bit shaky in the early going vs. the Fish, giving up three runs to the first 10 batters he faced. But the lefty settled in and retired 16 of the last 17 he faced, including the final 13 in a row. He also tied a season high with seven K's.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander's 25-2 record in Interleague Play includes a 14-game winning streak since 2010 and four wins this season, most recently over the Rockies last homestand. He has never beaten the National League five times in a season.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander had by far the best start of his second half on Thursday against Miami. Volquez gave up just one fifth-inning hit in seven frames and struck out seven Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Ray received his first big league experience filling in for an injured Anibal Sanchez for three starts in May. With Sanchez on the DL with a pectoral muscle strain, Ray will reprise the role in a potential audition for next year.

home_pitcher_note: Up until two weeks ago, Farmer was pitching in low Class A ball. After two starts for Double-A Erie, he'll make his Major League debut way sooner than anyone expected. He ranks eighth on MLB.com's Tigers top prospect rankings.
away_pitcher_note: Worley has been a great addition for the Pirates since being called up in mid-June, but even more so since the All-Star break. Worley has not allowed more than one earned run in any of his four starts since the Midsummer Classic.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer has tossed back-to-back gems with seven innings of two-run ball against the Yankees in the Bronx and eight innings with a lone run vs. the Blue Jays in Toronto, only to suffer a loss and a no-decision, respectively.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano is on a roll, having lowered his ERA in each of his last five starts -- at 3.82, it's the lowest since his first start of the season. He has allowed six earned runs and 18 hits in his last five turns, covering 32 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Roark took a no-decision after pitching seven innings on Saturday. He allowed a run on six hits against the Braves in a rain-delayed game the Nationals won, 4-1, in 11 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Morton is the only member of the Pirates' rotation who has not missed a start, and he is approaching his career high for innings. Fatigue, however, has not been as responsible as hung pitches for his inconsistencies.

home_pitcher_note: For the third straight start, Gonzalez wasn't himself on the mound. He threw too many pitches Sunday -- 111 in 4 2/3 innings -- while allowing two runs on six hits and striking out eight. It didn't help that Gonzalez didn't have fastball command.
away_pitcher_note: Locke issued a season-high four walks in his last start -- but his development is merely highlighted by that fact, since he had as many walks eight different times last season. The Bucs have won eight of his last 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Fister showed Tuesday why he is the ace of the staff. He pitched seven shutout innings and guided the team to a 7-1 victory over the Mets. Fister, who has a team-leading 12 wins, started the game by retiring nine of the first 10 hitters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' only 10-game winner focused on inducing grounders in his last start, a victory over Detroit. Ten of the 13 in-play outs he recorded came via the groundout. Volquez has allowed just two earned runs in his last 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Worley will try to recover from his second start (of 10) in which he didn't make it through six innings. Even with that hiccup, has a 1.62 ERA in five second-half starts. Control continues to be his main weapon, with just 11 walks in 68 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Santana's health and dependability were questioned as he produced a 5.96 ERA in eight starts from May 16-June 22. But the right-hander has regained a feel for his slider as he's gone 7-1 with a 2.95 ERA in his past nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander's record remains quite misleading as he has managed a win in only two of his eight quality starts. Has twice as many strikeouts (57) as hits allowed (28) in his last nine starts, covering 50 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Harang has allowed more than four earned runs in just three of his 25 starts. Two of these starts, including his most recent, were completed in afternoon games. He has a 4.25 ERA in 13 starts at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Cole makes his first start since July 4, after which he landed on the DL with a sore lat. He returns after four Triple-A rehab starts, the last two shutout efforts totaling 12 innings. His seven wins still rank second among Pirates starters.
away_pitcher_note: Wood is pitching to a 1.45 ERA over his last six starts and is at .500 despite the Majors' second-lowest run support. He had more walks (two) than strikeouts (1) last time out, but still shut down Oakland (two runs, four hits in six frames).

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo is 12-4 with a 2.57 ERA in 23 starts plus one relief appearance against the Pirates. He's already started four times against them this season, three of which became Brewers wins.
away_pitcher_note: A rematch of an earlier duel, in which on June 8 Locke dropped a 1-0 gem to Gallardo - the first of six quality starts in which he hasn't gotten the win. Locke's control has slipped a bit but still has walked only 19 in 14 starts.

home_pitcher_note: By beating the Dodgers on Sunday, Peralta joined NL Central foes Johnny Cueto and Adam Wainwright with an MLB-best 15 wins. No Brewer has led his league in victories since Pete Vuckovich in strike-shortened 1981.

away_pitcher_note: Worley comes off his poorest start of the season, but already rebounded by blanking Atlanta for five innings after surrendering six first-inning runs. Hurt by the long ball in last two starts after giving up a total of four in first nine starts.
