away_pitcher_note: Lackey has allowed two earned runs in three of his four starts since joining the club and has stepped up as the workhorse the Cardinals hoped they were acquiring in a Trade Deadline deal. He struck out seven and walked one in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Cole has a chance to build on his strong start off the DL, in which he held Atlanta to two runs in seven innings. This will be his third regular-season meeting with the Cardinals, whom he held to three runs in two NLDS starts in 2013.
away_pitcher_note: If not for a late rain delay, Lynn may have made a run at his second career complete game on Wednesday. As it was he pitched seven scoreless innings in his seventh start of such length this season. Lynn has a 1.84 ERA since the All-Star break.

home_pitcher_note: Locke posted a mystifying win Friday in Milwaukee, walking six -- his most since July 26, 2013 -- yet pitching two-hit ball through six. It was his 13th start of at least six innings while allowing fewer than four hits the last two seasons.
away_pitcher_note:
Wainwright took a loss Friday vs. Philly,
allowing four earned runs in six innings, settling down after a four-run third. The veteran said he's made an adjustment that he hopes will fix the issues he's had over his last seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez allowed a career-high 11 hits, yet wouldn't break on Saturday vs. the Brewers in picking up his 11th win. That improved his lifetime mark against NL Central clubs to 26-12, but he was 0-2 against the Reds last season.
away_pitcher_note: Leake tossed 6 2/3 scoreless innings to beat the Braves on Saturday, allowing two hits, walking three and striking out six. In three starts against the Pirates this season, he allowed 11 earned runs in 19 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Worley will make a concerted effort to be more aggressive from the get-go after his early woes in his last three starts (11 runs allowed within the first two innings). He'll be making his first start against Reds since Aug. 22, 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Simon was stellar against the Braves on Sunday, allowing one run on five hits in seven innings to earn the win. He's 2-0 in two starts against the Pirates this season, allowing five earned runs in 13 innings (3.46 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Liriano didn't record a win in his last start, but he shut out St. Louis for six innings on Monday, striking out eight. The lefty allowed more than two earned runs in one of his five starts so far in August, but the Bucs are 0-5 in those games.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto was beaten by the home run in his last start, a 3-0 loss to the Cubs on Tuesday. He gave up two homers among seven total hits, walked two and struck out eight. In four starts against the Pirates this season, he is 3-0 with a 1.80 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn will face the Pirates for a second straight start, coming off a strong showing in Pittsburgh when he allowed two runs over six innings. Lynn has pitched through the sixth in 19 starts this year and finished August with a 1.99 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Cole will be making his third start since returning from injury. He was great in his first two games back, with a 2.77 ERA and 15 strikeouts in 13 innings -- nine of which came in his last start, when he took a no-hitter into the sixth vs. the Cards.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright lost to the Pirates in his last start when they tagged him for three runs in six innings. The Cardinals have won only three of Wainwright's eight second-half starts after going 15-4 behind him prior to the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Locke had a 4-0 August, which he capped by allowing just one run over 7 1/3 innings against the Cardinals last Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Miller pitched well his last time out, allowing just two solo homers in a seven-inning no decision. He showed improved efficiency, though homers continue to sting Miller. He's allowed eight over his last seven starts and 20 this season.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez took a no-hitter into the seventh inning of his last start vs. the Reds and lasted 7 2/3 innings on 114 pitches. He was charged with one run and struck out six. In his last five starts, Volquez owns a 1.65 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wada has settled in nicely at Wrigley Field. The lefty is 4-1 with a 2.83 ERA in six starts at home, holding opponents to a .203 batting average. He took the loss in his last start, giving up three earned runs over six innings against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Worley earned his first win as a Pirate in Wrigley Field, going 6 2/3 innings in a 5-3 victory over the Cubs on June 21. He continues to rely on pinpoint control, having yet to issue more than two walks in any of his 13 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wada has settled in nicely at Wrigley Field. The lefty is 4-1 with a 2.83 ERA in six starts at home, holding opponents to a .203 batting average. He took the loss in his last start, giving up three earned runs over six innings against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Worley earned his first win as a Pirate in Wrigley Field, going 6 2/3 innings in a 5-3 victory over the Cubs on June 21. He continues to rely on pinpoint control, having yet to issue more than two walks in any of his 13 starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start for the Cubs last Saturday in St. Louis, Doubront picked up the win, giving up one run over seven innings. It was his 11th start this season, and the plans are for the lefty to stay in the rotation for the final month.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander is glad to put August behind him: He was winless in the month, despite five quality starts out of six. In fact, he has gone 2-3 since the All-Star break, with a 2.78 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wood is 1-1 in three starts against the Pirates this year. He's coming off a no decision against the Cardinals in which he failed to finish the fifth inning. The lefty is 3-4 with a 3.89 ERA at home, 5-7 with a 5.68 ERA on the road.
away_pitcher_note: By all accounts, Cole made only two bad pitches among the 94 in his last start, but they cost him in a 5-4 loss to the Cards. Three starts into his comeback from a sore lat, "he is in a good place," manager Clint Hurdle says.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick had his best start of the season Tuesday against the Braves. He allowed three hits, two walks and struck out four in seven scoreless innings. It was his first start of seven or more scoreless innings since April 26, 2013.
away_pitcher_note: Locke, who "fell behind everybody" in a poor three-inning outing Sept. 2 in St. Louis, has to dial up his control after 19 walks in his last five starts, following 13 in the first 12. Has won all three career starts against Phillies, with a 1.37 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Buchanan had hoped for better on Wednesday against the Braves at Turner Field. He grew up a Braves fan in Georgia and this was his first start in Atlanta. He allowed four runs (one earned) in just four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez has given up one total run in his last two starts, without winning either. He is keeping the ball in the park (two HRs in his last 39 innings). He has won both lifetime starts in Citizens Bank Park, allowing only one run in 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Williams struggled in the Phils' wild 9-8 road win in 11 innings vs. the Nats on Friday. He allowed five runs in five innings, but avoided his first loss thanks to the late rally. In his four previous starts, he posted a 3-0 record with a 2.03 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: This will be a special assignment for Worley, who spent the first three years of his career with the 2010-12 Phillies. He went 9-7 in Citizens Bank Park in the home whites, but this will be his first appearance there as a visitor.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett is coming off a solid outing against Washington, in which he went seven innings and allowed just one earned run on six hits. He'll make his second start of the season against the team he pitched for from 2012-13.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano is pitching his best ball of the season down the stretch, having allowed two runs or fewer in nine of 10 second-half starts. His opponents' average (.225) is almost identical to the figure in 2013 (.224), when he was a 16-game winner.

home_pitcher_note: Cole was backed with great run support in his last start, as the Bucs finished off a sweep of the Cubs in a 10-4 victory Sunday. Cole struck out eight and gave up three earned runs in six innings, and he also hit his first career Major League homer.
away_pitcher_note: Wada had to leave his last start after 3 2/3 innings because of cramping in his left leg. It was most likely caused by dehydration and the 88-degree temperatures. This will be his second straight start vs. the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Locke retired the first 10 and final 10 he faced in a win against Philadelphia on Monday. All three hits and the lone run against the left-hander came in a four-batter span during the fourth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Doubront's high pitch count cost him in his last start vs. the Pirates. He needed 64 pitches to get through three innings, and he admitted he had trouble with his command in the third inning, though he did last five.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez got his second consecutive no-decision Tuesday, after leaving with six innings and 92 pitches under his belt. The veteran righty wanted to stay in the game longer, but he still has a 2.18 ERA in his last 14 starts and is 7-1 in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Turner took the loss against Toronto the last time out, going six innings while allowing seven hits and four earned runs. Turner is 1-2 with a 4.50 ERA in three starts with the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Morton makes his first start following a month-long timeout with a sports hernia. He has pitched with that condition since June 2, going 4-5 with an ERA of 4.29 in 14 subsequent starts. Morton is 0-4 with a 5.91 ERA vs. the AL East.
away_pitcher_note: After starting three straight games against division foes, Ranaudo crosses leagues in his sixth MLB start. Ranaudo was roughed up last Tuesday in a 4-1 loss to Baltimore. He allowed four runs in 3 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The 2013 NL Comeback Player of the Year could also be the second-half comeback player of this season: Is 4-3 with a 2.22 ERA in 11 starts since the All-Star break, compared to 1-7 and 4.72 in 15 starts before. Still looking for PNC mojo (4.58 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: Buchholz lowered his ERA to 2.10 over his last four starts in Boston's 6-3 win Thursday over the Royals. He allowed three runs (two earned) in 6 1/3 innings and struck out seven in his third straight victory.

home_pitcher_note: Of Cole's 19 career wins, six have come in seven September decisions. His September ERA (3.04) is also his second lowest monthly mark (2.97 in July). He has a 3-1 Interleague record and has allowed three HRs in last nine starts and 52 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Workman struggled last Wednesday in the Red Sox's 10-6 loss to the Orioles. He fell to 1-9 on the season and allowed six runs (five earned) in just three innings. Workman has a 10.95 ERA in his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Locke has alternated poor and strong starts for a month, and he's on schedule for another good one. He has held the Brewers to a .122 average in two starts this season and is averaging 6 2/3 innings in 10 home starts.
away_pitcher_note: After missing the Cardinals for the second straight series, Gallardo draws a much more favorable matchup. He's 12-5 with a 2.67 ERA in 25 games (24 starts) against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez is 2-1 vs. the Brewers this season and has improved his career record against NL Central teams to 27-12 -- accounting for 42 percent of his total wins. He is 4-0 with a 1.73 ERA over his last eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Garza has gradually worked back to full strength since a month-long stint on the DL. He's worked three innings, four innings and six innings in his three starts so far, and should be back to the 100-pitch mark now.

home_pitcher_note: Worley steps back into his original rotation spot, after moving aside for one turn to make way for Charlie Morton (sports hernia) and make his first start in 11 days. His seven wins are tied for second on the team since mid-June.
away_pitcher_note: Thanks to a resurgent slider, Peralta has authored a turnaround. He had a 4.81 ERA and a .294 opponents' average in August, and has lowered that to a 2.75 ERA and a .243 batting average against in three September starts.

home_pitcher_note: Harang is coming off of two solid starts after a stretch of three starts when he couldn't get out of the sixth inning. Harang has been solid at home this season, but a lack of run support has saddled him six losses and six no-decisions in 16 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Saving his best for the end, Liriano has posted a 2.16 ERA in 12 second-half starts and will be looking for his fourth straight win. His road ERA (2.36) is a full two runs lower than at home. This will be his first Turner Field outing.

home_pitcher_note: Wood has come on strong over the last two months, recording a quality start in each of his last 10 outings. Over that stretch, Wood has thrown the ball by batters more and has seen more groundouts than flyouts, resulting in fewer homers allowed.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' young Mr. September is 7-1 in nine career starts in the season's money month. He has five quality starts in his last six as he tries to run his win streak to four straight starts. His next win will also top his rookie total of 10.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran will attempt to cap this season with a start similar to those that helped him gain his first All-Star selection. Since struggling in his first two August starts, he has posted a 2.18 ERA in his past seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Last September's forgotten pitcher is making good use of his second stretch chance, with five second-half wins, compared to two last year that cost him his spot in the rotation. He won his only decision against Atlanta, his original team.

home_pitcher_note: Hale will be starting in place of Mike Minor, who was shut down because of a sore left shoulder. After stretching out with Saturday's 59-pitch outing, Hale is hoping to be able to last at least five innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' latest reclamation project has been sensational down the stretch, having gone 4-0 with a 0.59 ERA in his last nine starts. He has yielded only eight homers in his last 136 innings. He's 0-2 in his career at Turner Field.

home_pitcher_note: Leake will seek to end his season on a strong note as he hasn't pitched well lately. He has a 7.71 ERA over his four September starts while not lasting more than six innings in any of them.
away_pitcher_note: Despite not making his first start until mid-June, Worley's eight wins rank third in the Bucs' rotation. Worley, whose homer rate (0.78/9 IP) is one of the best in the Majors, is looking to win four straight for the first time since his rookie year.

home_pitcher_note: Simon overcame a calf cramp and pitched a solid six innings for a victory on Sunday at St. Louis. He has three straight quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty continued his sensational second half with six shutout innings in his last start in Atlanta. Liriano has allowed one earned run in his last 28 innings, and he has a 2.17 ERA and a .174 opponents average in 13 starts on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto will try to become the first 20-game winner for the Reds since Danny Jackson in 1988 when he takes the mound against the Pirates. In five starts against the Bucs this season, the All-Star right-hander is 4-0 with a 1.89 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Mr. September is 8-1 in 10 career starts in the money month. He allowed five runs in six innings in an April start in Cincinnati, his only one against the Reds. Cole's seeking to win a fifth straight start (in the same season) for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Arguably the hottest of the Bucs' quartet of hot pitchers down the stretch, Volquez has pitched to a 1.78 ERA in his last 12 starts and finished the season with a scoreless streak of 18 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Confidence in the Giants' clubhouse rises each day Bumgarner starts, so it's no surprise the ace will start the Wild Card Game. He has recorded career highs in wins and strikeouts this season and is 11-4 with a 2.22 ERA in 18 road starts.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Cueto's fourth straight Opening Day start for the Reds. In his three other openers, the Reds ace is 1-1 with a 0.86 ERA (two earned runs and nine hits over 21 innings).
