home_pitcher_note: In a contract year, Leake is coming off of his best season where he established career highs in strikeouts (164), starts (33) and innings pitched (214 1/3). He's increased his starts and innings totals in each of the past four years.
away_pitcher_note: Cole hopes to pick up 2015 where he left off 2014: He pitched arguably the best game of his young career on the season's final day, striking out 12 Reds without a walk while holding them to four hits and a run in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired in the Mat Latos trade with the Marlins, DeSclafani only has eight games, including five starts, under his belt in the Majors. However, he had a strong spring to earn a rotation spot out of camp.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett formally makes his Pittsburgh return with the first start of his final season. He did not face the Reds with the Phillies last season, but was 5-3 with 65 strikeouts in 60 2/3 innings against them with the Pirates in 2012-13.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers made a last-minute switch to their starting rotation that positioned Fiers to open a series against the division-rival Pirates. Manager Ron Roenicke said he valued Fiers' experience over the younger Jimmy Nelson.
away_pitcher_note: Locke makes the start he earned by prevailing over Vance Worley in a tight spring competition for an open spot in the Pirates' rotation. The lefty pitched two-hit ball for six innings in his only Miller Park start last season.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson finished his first Spring Training as a full-fledged member of the Major League starting rotation with a 6.23 ERA, and that didn't count the 10 runs he surrendered last week in a Minor League game.
away_pitcher_note: The "loser" of the rotation showdown with Jeff Locke got paroled from the bullpen when Charlie Morton went on the disabled list (recovering from labrum surgery). Worley was one of only 30 starters with 110-plus innings and a sub-3.00 ERA in 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse cruised through Spring Training until being roughed up by the Cubs in his final tune-up, and he was roughed up again on Opening Day against the Rockies. Colorado's eight earned runs matched Lohse's career high.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates are touted for having several high-profile pitching prospects, but for now this 25th-round 2010 Draft choice gets the call to step in for Francisco Liriano, who is on paternity leave. Sadler went 11-4 last season in Triple-A.

home_pitcher_note: Cole draws home opener honors and takes a good personal history into the assignment against the Tigers. He has a 4-1 Interleague record in six starts, with 39 strikeouts in 38 1/3 innings, and an 11-6 career mark in PNC Park.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez looked a lot like the 2013 AL ERA champ in 6 2/3 shutout innings against the Twins Wednesday in Detroit. He allowed just three hits, walked two and struck out six. He has allowed a .204 career average to the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran righty was drawn back to Pittsburgh, and to PNC Park: He went 13-10 with a sub-3.00 ERA there as a Pirate from 2012-13, and even last season, with the Phillies, he had one of his finer efforts vs. the Bucs (five hits in seven innings).
away_pitcher_note: Not even a 3 1/2-hour rain delay could throw off Greene against the Twins, tossing eight innings with an unearned run on four hits. He faced the Pirates in Spring Training and gave up three runs, two earned, over 3 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Making a second start delayed by the birth of his fourth child, Liriano faces a familiar AL Central foe. The former Twin is 5-9 lifetime versus the Tigers with an ERA (5.82) that is his highest against any opponent he has faced 10-plus times.
away_pitcher_note: Simon had a gem going in Cleveland last Friday before five straight hits and three sixth-inning runs knocked him out. He's 3-4 with a 3.50 ERA in 18 meetings with the Pirates, more games than he has against any other opponent.

home_pitcher_note: Worley struggled in his season debut Saturday, giving up six runs on seven hits and two walks while striking out four in 6 1/3 innings. Worley will get a rematch with the Brewers, looking to get on track and recapture his 2014 form.
away_pitcher_note: This will be a rematch from Saturday in Milwaukee, where Nelson debuted his new curveball and set a career high with nine strikeouts. The trick will be adjusting now that the Pirates have had a look.

home_pitcher_note: Locke was able to get his fastball in on Brewers right-handed hitters in beating them last Friday, and his challenge now will be to respond to their expect adjustments. He's owned Aramis Ramirez (2-for-17).
away_pitcher_note: It's a rematch with Andrew McCutchen, who hit a misplaced slider for a go-ahead, three-run home run to beat Lohse on Sunday at Miller Park. Before that pitch, it appeared Lohse had righted some recent command woes.

home_pitcher_note: Cole kicked off the Pirates' homestand with a win over the Tigers, carrying a 1-hitter into the seventh before leaving with the bases loaded and no outs. Cole has racked up 14 strikeouts and only four walks in 11 innings over his first two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Downright ebullient out of Spring Training, Garza is searching for that good feeling in the regular season. In a win against the Cardinals, he was forced to work almost exclusively with his fastball. The slider remains a project.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett allowed one run following two seventh-inning walks and lost to the Tigers as the Pirates were shut out in his return to PNC Park on Tuesday. Burnett has racked up 15 strikeouts and only three walks in 12 innings over his first two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta has allowed no runs in 12 2/3 of his 13 2/3 innings this season. He allowed three runs in the fourth inning against the Reds on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Six times during 2014, Liriano pitched six-plus innings and allowed no more than two runs without a win, and that has been his fate in this season's first two starts. He's gone 2-6 at PNC Park since being 8-1 at home in '13.
away_pitcher_note: Wood is coming off his first win, in which he threw seven scoreless innings, holding the Reds to three hits. The key was being able to locate his fastball. He's 5-7 with a 4.28 ERA in 14 games vs. the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Worley has won six of eight home decisions as a Pirate, with a 2.36 ERA in eight starts at PNC Park. As a team, current Cubs are batting .213 (10-for-47) against him, with Anthony Rizzo owning the only HR.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel has been consistent in his two starts, allowing three runs in six innings against the Rockies and four runs in 6 1/3 innings against the Padres. He does have three hits, including a double.

home_pitcher_note: Locke will be seeking to win a third consecutive start for the first time in his career following two straight victories over the Brewers. The lefty has gone 5-1 in his last 10 starts at home, with the club winning nine of those games.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks allowed a two-run Matt Kemp home run in the first inning of his last start but then threw five scoreless innings to complete his outing against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter, who made his first career Opening Day start this year, was outstanding in his last start against the Giants. He tossed a four-hitter, the first shutout in the Majors this year, in a 9-0 Arizona win at AT&T Park.
away_pitcher_note: In his young career, Cole has garnered a reputation as a big September pitcher, and this time the dominance has spilled over into a new season. He'll be seeking his seventh straight victory in a place he hasn't pitched before.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa is still very much a work in progress. At times he displays electric stuff, but at others he is far too hittable. He made strides last time out against the Giants, allowing three earned runs over 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett remained winless following Monday's start against the Cubs, allowing one run over six innings in a no-decision. Burnett allowed eight hits and a pair of walks while striking out only one batter.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson picked up his first win in a D-backs uniform last time out against the Giants when he allowed just one run on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings of work. He was acquired from the Rays last November.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano allowed three runs in five innings, getting a no-decision as the Pirates lost late to the Cubs on Tuesday. Liriano allowed only three hits and two walks while striking out nine on the evening.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel should have a good idea on how to handle the Pirates. He lost to them in his last start, giving up four runs on six hits over five innings at PNC Park. Hammel will be on his turf at Wrigley, where he's 4-1 with a 2.75 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Worley limited the Cubs to one unearned run over 5 2/3 innings en route to a win on Wednesday. It was a windy, snowy affair in Pittsburgh. Worley battled through it, working around six hits and two walks while striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Wood did not get a decision in his last start, giving up three runs over five innings against the Pirates. He beat the Reds at Wrigley on April 15, holding them to three hits over seven innings. The lefty is 3-5 with a 2.69 ERA vs. his former team.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates have won each of Locke's first three starts. Commanding offspeed stuff has been behind early season effectiveness, resulting in an up-tick of missed swings. Will be his first Wrigley Field start since June 9, 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks didn't pitch badly in his last outing against the Pirates, but he wasn't sharp, giving up three runs on five hits over 5 1/3 innings. The Cubs need him to go deeper in games, and that will be the goal.
away_pitcher_note: Coming into his own in his second full big league season, Cole will try to extend the Majors' longest current win streak to eight straight. His 5-0 lifetime record against the Cubs (of 24 total wins) includes a 3-0 mark in Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn tallied 48 wins over the past three seasons with the aid of generous run support, something he hasn't gotten much of this year. Lynn didn't help himself on Sunday, though, allowing six extra-base hits and as many runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett continued his strong start to the season Saturday against the D-backs, allowing one run on five hits over seven innings. Burnett has pitched at least six innings and permitted one run in each of his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey threw his second quality start of the season on Monday, going seven innings in a loss to the Phillies. He's been burned by the big inning recently, as all eight of the runs he allowed in his past two starts were in the span of two innings.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano struggled with his command, walking six batters, but struck out seven and held the D-backs to two hits over 6 1/3 scoreless innings Sunday in Arizona. Liriano has struck out at least seven in each of his four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha was knocked around for four runs in his last start but did become the first Cardinals pitcher age 23 or younger to win his first four starts of the season. Wacha has opened the season throwing more cutters and curves than he did in 2014.
away_pitcher_note: A two-out walk led to a three-run third inning that spoiled Worley's otherwise-solid six-inning outing against the Cubs on Monday. Worley scattered nine hits but only walked one batter in his second loss of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty gets to face someone other than the Brewers (1.93 ERA) or Cubs (9.35 ERA) and would accept an outing between those two extremes. The Reds' big lefty bats (Joey Votto, Jay Bruce) combined 5-or-27 lifetime off Locke.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old right-hander is coming off his Major League debut on Wednesday, when he gave up three runs on eight hits -- including three home runs -- in an 8-3 loss to the Brewers in Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Cole has all sorts of streaks going -- he has won his last eight decisions, reverting to September -- and here is another: He has dropped only one of his last 14 PNC Park starts since August of his rookie 2013 season, going 9-1.
away_pitcher_note: Leake did it all in his last start on Thursday, throwing eight shutout innings and adding a home run in a 5-1 win over the Braves at Turner Field. He struck out three and walked two in a 97-pitch effort.

home_pitcher_note: At 38, Burnett is in the midst of the best stretch of his career, which translates to also the most frustrating since he is winless despite a 1.45 ERA. Needs three strikeouts to become 27th right-hander all-time to reach 2,400.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a career-high five walks in a 4-3 loss in Atlanta, DeSclafani makes his PNC Park debut. He took a no-decision in his first start vs. the Bucs, also his first start of '15, allowing two runs and five hits over six innings

home_pitcher_note: Liriano held the Cardinals hitless through five innings Saturday in St. Louis, and wound up going eight on a yield of three hits. He has gone 3-1 with the Bucs against the Cards, allowing a total of only 31 hits in 51 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wacha has allowed one or fewer runs in four of his five starts and has pitched into the seventh in just as many. He continues to show confidence in throwing a cutter and curveball to complement his fastball-changeup mix.

home_pitcher_note: Worley put together his best start of the season Sunday, holding the Cardinals to one run on four hits while striking out five over six innings in St. Louis. He went 2-0 with a 1.54 ERA in two starts at PNC Park in April.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez had a terrible start to his last outing, allowing five first-inning runs while walking three in the inning. He steadied enough to pitch into the fourth but saw his ERA rise nearly two points in allowing seven runs over 3 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Locke battled through two tough innings in a loss to the Reds at PNC Park on Tuesday, but he settled down well enough to pitch seven. The left-hander is 2-2 with a 3.76 ERA in five career starts against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Lyons, likely just a temporary rotation fill-in as the Cards wait for others to get healthy, will be making his second spot start for the club. He's made 13 starts for the Cardinals since 2013, but hasn't won a game since winning his first two.

home_pitcher_note: Williams got roughed up in his last start Wednesday, allowing six runs in 4 1/3 innings against Atlanta. He has allowed three or fewer runs in four of his first six starts, but pitched six-plus innings just three times.
away_pitcher_note: Cole suffered his first loss of the season Wednesday at PNC Park, allowing three runs over five innings against the Reds while receiving no run support. He's 1-1 with a 2.61 ERA in two career starts against the Phils.

home_pitcher_note: O'Sullivan returns to the rotation following a stint on the 15-day disabled list because of left knee tendinitis. He fills a spot vacated recently by Severino Gonzalez, who made a couple of starts before being optioned.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett will take the mound in Philadelphia, where he pitched last season, after picking up his first 2015 win on Thursday at PNC Park. Burnett held the Reds to two runs over seven innings in his fifth straight quality start.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels put together one of his best performances of the season, outpitching Mets ace Matt Harvey in Friday's 3-1 victory. He allowed four hits, one run and struck out eight in seven innings to earn his second win.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty comes off a rare poor game -- six runs in 6 1/3 innings -- but has an impressive bounce-back record. He has allowed six runs four previous times, and in the four ensuing starts, gave up six runs in 26 innings (2.08 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Harang made one bad pitch and it cost him in Saturday's 3-2 loss to the Mets. An elevated cutter turned into a two-run home run, spoiling an otherwise fine effort, allowing two earned runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: After a quality start in St. Louis, Worley gave up five runs in the fourth inning and didn't record a strikeout in his five-inning outing Saturday vs. the Cardinals at PNC Park. He's 0-2 with a 5.40 ERA in three road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks did not get a decision in his last start but did well, throwing 5 1/3 scoreless innings against the Brewers. He has faced the Pirates twice this season, and given up five earned runs over 10 1/3 innings combined.
away_pitcher_note: Locke struggled in two April starts against the Cubs, giving up four runs in five innings on April 23 at home, then six runs (five earned) in 3 2/3 innings on April 28 in Chicago. He's allowed 15 hits in 9 2/3 innings on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Lester has won his last three starts. After going 0-2 with a 6.23 ERA in April, he's now 3-0 with a 1.80 ERA in May. This will be his second career start vs. the Pirates; the other was June 24, 2011, and he lost despite a quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Cole won't have to flash back far for his last win at Wrigley Field, where he didn't give up an earned run in six innings of a 6-1 victory 17 days ago. He has given up one homer in his last 45 2/3 innings on the road, going back to 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta struck out a season-high 10 batters and held the Mets to three hits over eight innings in his last outing Tuesday. He beat the Pirates on April 20 at PNC Park, giving up one run over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran tries to keep his season-opening streak of not allowing more than two runs alive, which would set a franchise record. Keeping the ball in the strike zone (13 walks) and in the park (two homers) have been the keys.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano takes on his longtime former team for the first time as a Pirate, but he did face the Twins twice in 2012 with the White Sox, going 1-0 with a 2.77 ERA. The '15 Twins are tough on lefties, hitting them at a .292 average.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco turned in his best outing of the year on Wednesday in a win against the Tigers. He allowed just two unearned runs over 5 1/3 innings, but was hurt by a high pitch count.

home_pitcher_note: Locke gets a chance to get right at home, where the lefty has consistently fared better, after a winless five-start stretch during which he sports an ERA of 7.27. He is also 4-1 vs. AL teams, with a 2.56 ERA in six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey had his worst outing of the year on Thursday against the Tigers, giving up four runs (five earned) on 10 hits over 4 2/3 innings. The sinkerballer said the issue was leaving his fastball up in the zone.

home_pitcher_note: Cole struck out eight over six strong innings, but lost to the Cubs on Saturday. He has allowed only two homers over 48 2/3 innings this year. He's walked fewer than three batters in each of his eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Syndergaard will get at least one more start while Dillon Gee rehabs a groin injury. New York's No. 1 prospect was as advertised last time out against the Brewers on Sunday, when he earned his first big league win.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett continued his dominant start to the year on Sunday vs. the Cubs, scattering three hits and striking out seven over seven scoreless innings. The veteran right-hander has yet to allow more than two runs in a start this year.
away_pitcher_note: Though he owns a 1.29 ERA and an active 16-inning scoreless streak over his last three starts, Harvey is 0-1 over that stretch. The Mets have blown two saves in those games, supporting him with a total of three runs.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano struggled through his toughest start of the season Tuesday, a two-inning outing vs. the Twins. He allowed seven runs and two homers while walking two. It was the first time all year Liriano pitched less than five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Niese tied a career high by allowing eight earned runs in five-plus innings his last time out and has lost four of his last five decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Morton will make his first start of the season after three rehab starts. The 31-year-old had offseason hip surgery, struggled in Spring Training and was placed on the disabled list after the Pirates' final exhibition game.
away_pitcher_note: Phelps had a string of five straight starts of working at least six innings come to a halt in his last outing, a loss to the D-backs. He gave up four runs in five innings. He won his last road start, beating the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing three runs in the first, Locke bounced back with five scoreless innings Wednesday. He'll try to carry that momentum into his start against the Marlins, against whom he was 1-0 with a 3.00 ERA in two starts last year.
away_pitcher_note: Urena will be recalled from Triple-A New Orleans to make his first MLB start against Pittsburgh. One of the Marlins' top prospects, Urena has a 4-0 record and a 1.21 ERA in the Minors this year. He made two relief appearances for Miami in April.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off the best start of his big league career, Cole will face the Marlins for the first time since 2013. He is 0-1 with a 5.25 ERA over two starts vs. Miami, but with 12 strikeouts and only three walks in 12 innings.
away_pitcher_note: A former starter who's worked exclusively in the 'pen this year, Hand will fill in with Miami's rotation plagued by injuries. Hand's lone start vs. Pittsburgh was a no-decision on Aug. 5, 2014, in which he surrendered just two runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy had one of his best outings to date the last time out against the Dodgers, allowing two runs over six innings with no walks and six strikeouts. Unlike last season, lefties (.333) are hitting him hard. They hit .240 off him in 2014.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett captured the league's best ERA (1.37) with his dominant performance on Saturday, shutting down the Mets with 10 strikeouts in seven innings of work. He's allowed more than one earned run just twice this season.

home_pitcher_note: Shields is the first Padres starter to begin a season with a 6-0 record since Andy Hawkins did so in 1985. He leads the NL in strikeouts (82) and has induced the most swing-and-misses (157) in the league this season, second in the big leagues.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano clamped down on the Mets on Sunday, going six innings and allowing one earned run while striking out 12. It was the sixth time in nine starts that Liriano recorded seven or more strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Ross allowed a season-high 10 hits his last time out, vs. the Angels, but just one walk. It's the first time this season he's walked one batter or fewer in a game. That's a good sign. Last season, Ross had one or fewer walked in 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Morton's return to action went about as well as the Pirates could have hoped for, as he induced 16 groundouts and held the Marlins to two runs over seven innings Monday. He is 2-0 with a 2.61 ERA in two starts at Petco Park.

home_pitcher_note: Despaigne had his best outing of the season the last time out against the Angels, striking out six over six scoreless innings. He's been very good pitching at Petco Park, posting a career 2.91 ERA with opponents hitting .207 against him.
away_pitcher_note: Locke has thrown 10 2/3 consecutive scoreless innings, most recently shutting out the Marlins over 5 2/3 frames Tuesday. The lefty has only faced the Padres once, giving up four runs in five innings in a loss two years ago.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong has not faced his former teammates since Aug. 25, 2013, when he blanked Pittsburgh for eight innings on two hits. Since his 2011 return to the Giants, Vogelsong is 2-3 with a 3.38 ERA in five starts against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Cole tossed seven efficient innings against Miami on Wednesday, allowing two runs on a pair of homers. Eight of Cole's 10 outings have been quality starts, and he has yet to allow more than three earned runs in a game.

home_pitcher_note: Heston continues to prove himself. In his last start, he shut out the Braves for 7 1/3 innings to outpitch Shelby Miller and lower his ERA to 3.82. Heston has a 2.16 home ERA compared to 5.79 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett was 5-0 in his six May starts with a 1.84 ERA and 39 strikeouts with only 13 walks. It's the second time in his career he's had a 5-0 month. The other was July 2012 in his first tour with Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Hudson bounced back from a rough outing and allowed one run over seven innings in the Giants' 4-2 win over the Braves. He's been better at AT&T Park this season, and he has a 0.68 ERA in his last two starts at home.
away_pitcher_note: He's coming off six innings of three-hit shutout ball on Friday night in San Diego. Manager Clint Hurdle pulled him out after 94 pitches because of the shorter four-day rest caused by a day game in San Francisco. Has 23 whiffs in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Perez has excelled since moving into the starting rotation, going 1-0 with a 1.00 ERA in three starts. The rookie faces the Pirates for the first time, looking to give up one or zero runs for the fourth straight start.
away_pitcher_note: Morton has acquitted himself well in two starts -- both wins -- since coming off the DL after hip surgery. He threw seven innings Saturday in San Diego, allowing two runs (one earned) on three hits, with 16 of his 24 outs coming on ground balls.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran looks to find some consistency after an up-and-down May, in which he had a 2-1 record and a 5.03 ERA in six starts. He has had success against the Pirates in the past, going 2-0 with a 2.70 ERA in four appearances (three starts).
away_pitcher_note: Locke's rotation incumbency gets a stiff test in Turner Field, where in two starts he has allowed nine runs in 9 2/3 innings. He had a 10 2/3-inning shutout string before allowing seven runs in four innings in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Wood has been on a roll of late, with his only three starts of seven innings or more this season coming the last three times out, all of which were wins. He is 0-1 in his career against the Pirates, but has a 2.87 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Cole returns to the scene of his postseason clinching effort of Sept. 23, when he held the Braves to four hits and two runs in seven innings in his only Turner Field start. He has made 16 straight starts without walking more than two men.

home_pitcher_note: Going for a seventh straight win, Burnett takes on a Milwaukee team against which he is 0-4 with the Pirates. He hasn't faced the Brewers since '13, but their current players have accumulated 130 at-bats against him -- with one homer.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing five runs (four earned) in the first inning against the Cardinals on Wednesday, Nelson has surrendered 11 earned runs and 14 hits in that frame in 11 starts. The Brewers will work with Nelson on a fix.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano takes another stab at adjusting his home/road splits, which are totally opposite to what they were in 2013, when he dominated in PNC Park (8-1, 1.47 ERA). This season, he has an ERA of 6.04 at home compared to 1.52 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Jungmann, who is ranked as the club's No. 13 prospect, will be making his Major League debut. He was the Brewers' top Draft pick in 2011 at No. 12 overall. The righty was 2-3 with a 6.37 ERA at Triple-A this season.

home_pitcher_note: Morton will seek a couple of career firsts: He has never begun a season 4-0, and has never won four straight starts in a season. But he'll have to be sharper than in his previous start, when the offense picked him up in a 10-8 decision.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse struggled again in his last outing, surrendering a five-run lead and taking an no-decision. The veteran is now 3-6 with a 6.59 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Locke has been much sharper at home, and he gets to face the team against which he has had his most historic success: 4-0 lifetime with a 1.35 ERA vs. the Phillies. The lefty also has a 7-4 career record on five days' rest.
away_pitcher_note: Correia, signed by Philadelphia on Monday, will make his first big league start of 2015. The veteran right-hander, who earlier asked for his release from San Francisco, has a career 4.59 ERA for five Major League teams.

home_pitcher_note: Cole's ERA for the first two months of this season is exactly half of the cumulative mark for his first two seasons (3.45). His next win will leave him one shy of his total of 11 in 2014. He's coming off his first three-walk start since Sept. 1.
away_pitcher_note: O'Sullivan has been hittable of late, giving up 27 hits over 17 1/3 innings during his last three starts. His only win in eight starts this season came May 17 against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett goes for his second win in a month over his '14 teammates. He has been sharp in five home starts, with a 1.60 ERA and a 4-to-1 strikeouts-to-walks ratio in 33 2/3 innings. Has allowed two homers in last 83 innings in PNC Park.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels made his 14th career start (including postseason) against Cincinnati on Monday and took his first loss to the Reds. His 13 starts have included nine good (1.54 combined ERA) and four bad (7.83).

home_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty meets a familiar foe in this Interleague matchup, frequently facing the White Sox in his 2005-12 tenure in Minnesota, then joining them for the second half of 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Rodon has thrown 83 sliders over his last two starts combined, which is not exactly ideal in the White Sox mind, but he's also battling for victories. Rodon enters with an 11-inning scoreless streak and will get his first career at-bats.

home_pitcher_note: Morton won his fourth straight start since coming off the disabled list, holding the Brewers to three hits and three walks while striking out six over 7 1/3 scoreless innings Wednesday. Morton has never faced the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana's victory over the Astros marked his first win since May 13, covering four starts in between. He has made six starts in which he has worked seven innings and eight starts where he has allowed two runs or less.

home_pitcher_note: Danks wasn't done in by solid contact on Friday night against the Rays, but more so the Tampa hitters just finding open ground. He has lost two straight decisions and has allowed eight earned runs on 19 hits over his last 10 innings pitched.
away_pitcher_note: Locke took another step forward Friday against the Phillies at PNC Park, tossing six scoreless innings while allowing six hits and one walk with two strikeouts. This will be Locke's first career start against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija pitched well enough to win Saturday, allowing three runs on six hits over seven innings, while striking out seven and walking one. His improvement against the Rays stemmed from simply keeping the ball down, per the right-hander.
away_pitcher_note: Cole became the first Major League pitcher to record 10 wins this season as he limited the Phillies to two runs (one earned) on five hits and struck out seven over six innings on Saturday. Cole has never faced the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Joe Ross' Major League career is only two starts deep, but his last outing - eight innings, seven hits, two earned runs - was one the Nationals hope he can repeat. Friday will be the third time Ross pitches against a National League Central team.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett put together his best start of the year Sunday against the Phillies, tossing nine shutout innings as the Pirates went on to win in the 11th. The veteran is 1-2 with a 4.57 ERA in four career starts at Nationals Park.

home_pitcher_note: Max Scherzer's last start was one of baseball's best pitching performances of the season, a 16-strikeout one-hitter against the Brewers. The ace is 3-2 with a 3.05 ERA vs. the Pirates in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano struck out 12 over eight innings in Monday's 11-0 win over the White Sox. The lefty owns a 1.29 ERA over his last five starts. He threw 7 2/3 shutout innings in his only career start vs. the Nationals in 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Gio Gonzalez has started against the Pirates five times in his career with some success. He is 2-0 with a 3.64 ERA in those games. His last outing against the Bucs came in 2014 when he allowed three earned runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Morton improved to a perfect 5-0 in his fifth start of the season, holding the White Sox scoreless on four hits over seven innings on Tuesday night. He is 2-3 with a 4.70 ERA in six starts against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Locke has solidified his spot in the Bucs' rotation with consecutive quality starts. He's been successful being in attack mode, aggressively getting ahead in the count to put batters on the defensive. His last win over Reds came in 2013.
away_pitcher_note: With Johnny Cueto pushed back to Friday, Smith is being called up from Triple-A Louisville to make his Major League debut. In 13 starts combined this season with Louisville, Double-A Pensacola and Class A Dayton, Smith is 4-4 with a 3.04 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cole remains on an impressive run that dates to last Sept. 7, his 15 wins since then leading the Majors. In 124 innings during that stretch, he has allowed a crooked number only three times. A 12th win would be a career high.
away_pitcher_note: Leake retired the first 13 batters he faced as he flirted with a no-hitter on Friday, tossing seven innings of two-hit ball in a 5-0 win over the Marlins. Leake is 2-0 with a 2.42 ERA and 21 strikeouts in four starts in June.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran righty looks to bounce back from a weird outing that yielded the most hits he has ever surrendered (14) yet only three earned runs. He has a 1.27 ERA in six home starts, despite merely a split in four decisions.
away_pitcher_note: DeSclafani is 0-1 with a 4.09 ERA in two starts this season against the Pirates. In his most recent matchup against Pittsburgh, DeSclafani surrendered three earned runs on seven hits and four walks in five innings pitched in a 7-2 loss on May 7.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano was on the wrong side of a no-hitter Saturday, giving up five runs on seven hits as he lost to Max Scherzer and the Nationals. He's actually been worse at home (2-4, 4.35 ERA) than on the road (2-2, 2.30) this season.
away_pitcher_note: Perez has earned the nickname Magic Man as he has managed to post a 2.14 ERA, despite allowing opponents to produce a .324 on-base percentage in his first seven starts. A ground-ball pitcher, he allowed two homers his last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Morton yielded nine runs on eight hits and a walk while recording two outs against the Nationals on Sunday. The good news for Morton is he's pitching at PNC Park, where he's allowed only two runs over three starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran halted his struggles as surrendered just one hit over seven scoreless innings in his last start. But he had the fortune of facing a right-handed-heavy Mets lineup. Left-handers have compiled a .396 OBP against him.

home_pitcher_note: After a couple of encouraging starts, Locke allowed four runs (two earned) in four innings Tuesday vs. the Reds. He is 1-1 with a 6.08 ERA in five career starts against the Braves, who drafted him in the second round in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Though he surrendered a season-high 10 hits against the Nationals on Tuesday, Wood completed seven innings for the fourth time in his past seven starts. He has produced a 2.72 ERA during that span.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander, who missed his last scheduled start with a stiff back, threw a bullpen session on Saturday without any issues, paving the way for his return.
away_pitcher_note: Cole will look to rebound from allowing five runs in 4 2/3 innings to the Reds on June 24. He needs to correct mechanical issues that had him throwing across his body, flattening his pitches. He has a career 6-1 record in Interleague Play.

home_pitcher_note: According to manager Brad Ausmus, Simon has been the most consistent pitcher for the Tigers this year, but the righty has struggled lately, allowing 12 runs over his last two outings -- including three homers.
away_pitcher_note: Bouncing back from his first sour start of the season, Burnett turned in his 12th quality start on June 25 and continues his All-Star campaign in a park that has been tough on him (6.26 ERA in five starts, despite 3-2 record).

home_pitcher_note: Ryan was supposed to pitch Saturday until a rainout and Justin Verlander's return forced the Tigers to push back his start. The lefty has started three games this year, but his last outing was 12 pitches in relief on June 24.
away_pitcher_note: Dealing with a losing record despite his 1.01 WHIP and .189 opponents' average, Liriano could find some reward under ideal conditions: ERAs of 2.30 ERA on the road and 2.25 in daylight, balanced by the 5-10 record vs. Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Finding the bite of his sinker, Morton got on a roll mid-game in his last start, retiring 11 straight Braves at one point on Saturday. Bucs have won six of his seven starts. He has 18 consecutive scoreless innings against AL teams.
away_pitcher_note: Taking the mound in Pittsburgh might be a good thing for Bauer (6-5, 3.96 ERA), who has a 1.69 ERA in seven starts on the road this season. On Sunday in Baltimore, the righty took a loss after giving up four runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Locke will be mindful of more aggressively attacking the strike zone to avoid the deep counts that have shortened each of his last two starts. Besides a high walk rate (33 in 83 innings), he deals with a lot of three-ball counts.
away_pitcher_note: For his third career start, Anderson (1-0, 0.57 ERA) will finally face a team other than the Rays. On Monday, "Big Country" carried a perfect game through 19 Tampa Bay batters, and ended with one run yielded over eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cole rarely leaves his games in other people's hands - the no-decision in his last start was only his third in 22 starts reverting to last season. He allowed season highs in hits (eight, then nine) in each of his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Salazar (7-3, 3.80 ERA) logged five perfect innings on Tuesday en route to a win over the Rays. The hard-throwing righty struck out two, walked two and allowed two runs (one earned) over 7 2/3 innings for the Tribe.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett improved to 7-3 on Wednesday, holding Detroit to two runs in seven innings. He's been lights-out in every environment this season, but particularly at PNC Park, where he's 2-2 with a 1.29 ERA in seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Shields started off July with a loss against the Mariners. The right-hander pitched 6 2/3 innings, allowing four hits, two runs, walking four and striking out seven batters. In June, Shields had a 5.52 ERA in 29 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano limited the Braves to two runs on six hits and three walks but only struck out three over seven innings. He has put together a 1.97 ERA with 43 strikeouts in 32 innings over five career starts against San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Ross battled command issues the last time out, walking five for the third time in his last four starts. He allowed three runs on four hits in six innings and even connected for his first career home runs in a no-decision against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Morton put up another quality start Friday but took his second loss of the season against the Indians. The righty is 4-1 with a 2.65 ERA in six career starts against the Padres and 4-1 with a 2.43 ERA at home this year.
away_pitcher_note: Cashner opened his most recent start by retiring the first 10 hitters he faced. He allowed one earned run on three hits in six innings before leaving. After scuffling in June, he has allowed three runs in his last 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Locke is coming off arguably the best start of his career, holding the Indians scoreless over eight two-hit innings Saturday. While he's struggled on the road, he is 3-2 with a 2.64 ERA in 10 starts at PNC Park this season.
away_pitcher_note: Since allowing seven earned runs in 5 1/3 innings against the Pirates at PNC Park on May 9, Martinez has turned things around in a dramatic way with a 1.52 ERA in his last 10 outings to go with nine straight quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Majors' leader in wins will go for No. 13 in his last start before his first All-Star Game. Cole is 7-1 with a 2.19 ERA over his last nine starts, and he's 1-2 with a 3.42 ERA in four career starts against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn posted a season-high 10 strikeouts and a no-decision when he faced the Pirates in a 2-1 St. Louis win on May 1. He has struggled to receive run support, but created his own with two runs scored in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: The first-time All-Star has pitched at least six innings in each of his last six starts, most recently throwing 7 2/3 innings of one-run ball against the Padres. Burnett is 2-2 with a 1.28 ERA in eight starts at PNC Park this year.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey has thrown seven or more innings in seven of his last eight starts. He helped the Cardinals to a win over Pittsburgh on May 2 by allowing one run over six innings. He is 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA in two previous starts at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano held the Padres to two runs in six innings Tuesday. The lefty made two drastically different starts against the Cardinals earlier this season: eight innings, one run on May 2; 6 1/3 innings, six runs on May 8.
away_pitcher_note: Cooney, making his fourth career start, turned in his best effort in his last outing when he tossed 5 1/3 innings of one-run ball against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers was the Brewers' most valuable starter in the first half, leading the team in WAR (1.0, per FanGraphs' measure), strikeouts per nine innings (8.6) and FIP (3.87). He gets the ball first coming out of the break.
away_pitcher_note: Morton will get the Pirates' second half underway against the Brewers, who saw the best of Morton earlier this season. He scattered three hits and struck out six in 7 1/3 scoreless innings in a win over Milwaukee on June 10.

home_pitcher_note: A loss in Nelson’s final first-half start snapped his three-game win streak, but it might have been his best outing of the year. He didn’t allow a hit until the sixth inning, and lost on three unearned runs in the seventh.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano wasn't named an All-Star, but he's pitched like an ace lately, going 4-2 with a 2.15 ERA in his last 10 starts. Liriano has been better on the road, going 3-2 with a 2.00 ERA in eight starts away from PNC Park.

The lefty, who in the past has flamed out after good starts, is trying something different, with an ERA of 1.59 in his last six starts compared to 5.37 up to that point. Confidence in all of his pitches has played a major role.

home_pitcher_note: Ventura earned his first win in nearly two months in his last outing, giving up three runs in five innings with eight runs of support. He looks to continue improvement in his second start since coming off the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran righty begins the second half of his farewell tour facing a team against which he has an ERA of 2.69 in 11 career starts. However, he has not dealt with the “new” Royals, whose speed in particular could trouble him.

home_pitcher_note: After he was sidelined with a strain in his flexor muscle on his left elbow, Vargas will make his first start since June 8. He has worked his pitch count back up through rehab assignments, but has not pitched more than six innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates have won nine of Cole’s lifetime 10 Interleague starts (the only loss by a 2-1 score to Oakland in 2013) and he has already beaten three other AL Central teams this season. He is 17-3 since Sept. 7, going seven-plus innings a dozen times

home_pitcher_note: Volquez is coming off a 2-0 loss to the White Sox in which he lasted 6 1/3 innings and gave up two runs. He has given up two or fewer runs in four of his last five starts. This is his first start against his 2014 team, the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Few pitchers work with Morton’s slim margin for error, and he continues to be hurt by bad bounces and misplays. His sinker at times has been unhittable, but sometimes also uncontrollable -- breaking so much it clips batters on the foot.

home_pitcher_note: Due to the All-Star break and then skipping his last turn with a stiff neck, Liriano will be pitching on 12 days’ rest. He figures to be rusty, since the neck issue prevented him from a full slate of side work until Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Fister is 0-2 in July, with nine earned runs and 24 hits allowed over 17 innings. In his career against Pittsburgh (four starts), he is 1-1 with a 1.07 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Locke is in his best extended stretch since his All-Star first half of the 2013 season, carrying an ERA of 1.96 over his last seven starts. He pitched into the eighth twice in those seven, and has an overall 2.58 ERA in 11 home starts.
away_pitcher_note: The last time Scherzer faced the Pirates, on June 20, he threw a no-hitter, striking out 10 and allowing only one baserunner.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett will be seeking to curb his strange trend in PNC Park, where he has pitched to a 1.58 ERA in nine starts, and got a win in only two of them. His next victory will be his 35th with the Pirates -- topping his total with the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Since the start of June, Gonzalez has a 2.81 ERA. He has worked around 37 hits and 18 walks in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Cole, a tough-luck loser in his start last Tuesday against the Royals, does a lot of things well, and bouncing back is one of them. He has not dropped consecutive starts since Aug. 2013, when his big league career was two months old.
away_pitcher_note: Ross, who has 27 strikeouts and two walks over four Major League starts, has never faced the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey turned in his first quality start since June 23 on Wednesday against the Angels, but wasn't helped by his defense. The right-hander gave up four runs over six innings, but two of the runs were unearned.
away_pitcher_note: Morton has struggled lately, going 1-4 with a 7.76 ERA over his past six starts after opening his season 5-0 with a 1.62 ERA. He's never pitched against the Twins, and the only Minnesota hitter he's faced is Torii Hunter.

home_pitcher_note: Santana has started off the second half strong, tossing 15 2/3 straight scoreless innings coming out of the break. He's coming off a strong start against the Angels, throwing eight shutout innings vs. his former club.
away_pitcher_note: The last time Liriano faced the Twins, his former team, he had arguably the worst start of his career, giving up seven runs in two innings. He's turned it around since then, going 5-2 with a 2.10 ERA in his past 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Holmberg will be called up from Triple-A Louisville to take the spot of Johnny Cueto. He doesn’t have sterling numbers there this season but allowed one run over six innings in his last start on Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett's command eluded him in Saturday's loss to the Nationals. He's allowed 11 earned runs on 22 hits over 11 2/3 innings in two second-half starts and admitted it'd be "nuts" to expect a repeat of his dominant first half.

home_pitcher_note: Lorenzen will be coming off of the worst start of his big league career -- 2 1/3 innings with eight earned runs and seven hits, including two homers in a 17-6 loss. Once again, some inopportune walks and strike zone command issues hurt him.
away_pitcher_note: Locke will wrap up an up-and-down month in which he's looked brilliant (eight scoreless innings on July 4) and average (four runs in five innings Friday). He's 0-1 with a 4.91 ERA in two starts against the Reds this year.

home_pitcher_note: Iglesias has been strong in the early portion of his starts, with a 1.29 ERA in the first three innings. But as he cycles through the lineup a second and third time, he has problems. In innings 4-6, his ERA is 10.26.
away_pitcher_note: Cole tries to stay ahead of the MLB class with his 15th win, but it will have to come against a team (0-3, 5.53 in five starts vs. Reds) and in a place (4.50 ERA in three winless starts at GABP) that have been rough on him.

home_pitcher_note: Sampson will make his first career start after making his Major League debut on Thursday with one scoreless inning of relief work. He gave up only five hits across eight scoreless frames in his last start with Triple-A Louisville on July 24.
away_pitcher_note: Morton is winless in his past five starts. Solving his first-inning troubles would help snap that streak: In his 12 starts, he has allowed 16 runs (15 earned) in the first. He is undefeated in past six GABP starts (3-0, 2.70 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Liriano comes off allowing a season-high 10 hits in only 5 2/3 innings against the Twins, but he's also started six consecutive wins (going 3-0 across that stretch). He's had homer troubles at home (8 in 66 2/3 innings).
away_pitcher_note: Lester had what he called his best outing of the season his last time out, striking out a season-high 14 Rockies. He's thrown at least seven innings in each of his starts in July, including another season-high eight innings in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty makes his Pittsburgh debut by stepping into the shoes of A.J. Burnett (on the DL with elbow inflammation). Happ slumped his way out of Seattle and will try to regain his early-season form (3.31 ERA across first 11 starts).
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta's next win will be his career-high 12th. In his last start, against the Brewers, he struggled with command yet lasted long enough to post his 17th quality start. He has a 1.53 ERA in his last eight starts, with 58 K's over 58 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The young lefty has developed into a consistent performer in the Pirates' current rotation, having worked to an ERA of 3.06 in his last six starts. He has become adept at finding his rhythm in games that begin erratically.
away_pitcher_note: Acquired on Friday from the Marlins, Haren will make his Cubs debut. At age 34 and pitching in his 13th season, Haren has hinted that this could be his last season, and he hopes he can contribute to a winner.

home_pitcher_note: Despite limiting the Reds to two runs in his last outing, Cole needed 98 pitches to get through five innings. He's been a workhorse this year, especially recently, averaging 106 pitches per start in his last eight showings.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw puts his scoreless innings streak of 37 on the line against the Pirates. He is 2-1 with a 2.39 career ERA against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano’s last start was washed out by rain after two innings, so he gets a mulligan in search of his fourth straight win. The lefty is unbeaten in three career starts vs. the Dodgers, two last season, with an ERA of 1.37.
away_pitcher_note: Latos, who allowed one run in six innings of his first Dodgers start, returns against the Pirates. He is 5-1 with a 3.13 ERA against the Pirates lifetime.

home_pitcher_note: Morton emphatically rebounded from a bad stretch in his last start, blanking the Reds on five hits for seven innings. Remarkably, his 148th career start will be only his second -- the first was in 2010 -- against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Wood delivered six solid innings in his Dodgers debut before the inning got freaky. He is 1-1 with a 2.19 ERA against the Pirates in two starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez has experienced both the good and bad against the Bucs this season. He allowed seven runs on seven hits in a loss to Pittsburgh on May 9, but struck out eight and didn't give up a run in 7 1/3 against them two months later.
away_pitcher_note: In seven starts against the Cardinals, Locke owns a 2-3 record and 3.55 ERA. The southpaw has faced St. Louis twice this season, most recently allowing one earned run in five innings on July 9.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha hasn't allowed a run over his last 14 innings (two starts) and has struck out a combined 13 batters. The right-hander is 1-0 with a 1.42 ERA in two outings against the Pirates this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cole has had five quality starts in his last six outings, adding to that total a lackluster six-inning, three-run showing against the Dodgers on Friday. Cole walked three hitters for the first time since June 24.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn struggled with fastball command in six scoreless innings against the Brewers last time out. He admitted to throwing the ball down the middle and "hoping for the best." He's 0-1 with a 4.91 ERA in two starts this season vs. Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano's mechanics were out of whack Saturday afternoon, when he allowed four runs on seven hits and two walks. He'll look to get back on track vs. the Cardinals, against whom he has posted a 3.48 ERA in three starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: That the 42-year-old has factored in the decision in all but one start this year is telling: he continues to seesaw between dominant and ineffective. He allowed four runs in 6 2/3 innings last time, so maybe Colon is due for a gem.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty starts on nine days’ rest -- his turn was skipped the last time around -- after allowing eight hits and four runs in 4 1/3 innings in his Pirates debut. This will be his first Citi Field start since April 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Niese and Mets manager Terry Collins engage in good-spirited arguments "every game" when Collins pulls Niese. Lately, the lefty has backed up his pleas to remain in the game more often that not. Niese owns a 2.77 ERA over his last 12 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Morton takes a second stab at win No. 8, which would be a career second-best (he went 10-10 in 2011). He's still battling the first-inning blues, having allowed 17 runs in the opening frame of 14 starts, typical for “feel” pitchers.

home_pitcher_note: Pick the time frame of your choice to examine Harvey's recent dominance. They're all impressive. Harvey owns a 1.45 ERA over his last 10 starts and just a 0.40 ERA over his last three. He’s 7-2 with a 2.47 ERA overall at Citi Field.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty will look to get out of another of his extended ruts, having allowed 22 runs (19 earned) in 33 innings in his last six starts. He has also walked three in four of those, and concedes he has to be more aggressive in the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: Cole has downplayed the defense that has betrayed him in his last three starts, and has also battled rare command issues. The net result, he is out to avoid a fourth straight winless start for the second time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Hellickson is coming off his best start of the season as he blanked the Phillies for eight innings. His two starts prior to that were a struggle as he allowed 10 earned runs in just eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty, 13-8 after the All-Star Game in his first two Pirates seasons, seems primed for another strong second half, going 4-0 since July 2. As significant, the Bucs have won 11 of his last 14 starts, including eight straight.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Anderson's third start since a three-week stint on the DL and the results since his return have been mixed. He tossed seven shutout innings his first time out before giving up five runs in five innings the next.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty earned his rotation keep, and regained his confidence, with 5 1/3 innings of one-run, seven-strikeout pitching vs. the Mets on Friday. Yet, he remains with only one win in 17 starts since early May with Seattle and Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: When Ray has command of his fastball he can be tough to hit, but control is an issue for him at times. He has lost his last three starts and has a 5.87 ERA with eight walks in 15 1/3 innings over that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: In 11 career starts against San Francisco, Morton owns an impressive 2.84 ERA. Despite a 5.04 ERA in July, he's rebounded nicely since with a 3.44 ERA and 22 strikeouts in three August starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Giants have won five of Peavy’s last six starts and he has a 3.86 ERA during that stretch. Peavy was the beneficiary of an offensive outburst his last time out, getting the win despite giving up five runs in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Locke held the Mets to one run on four hits over 5 1/3 innings on Sunday. He has been much better at PNC Park this season, going 3-3 with a 3.16 ERA in 13 home starts, compared to 3-4 with a 6.02 ERA on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner dominated the Nationals his last time out, joining Juan Marichal as the only two Giants pitchers in the San Francisco era to throw a complete game, strike out 10 batters and hit a home run.

home_pitcher_note: Cole hasn't been sharp recently, lacking command over both his fastball and slider. However, the 24-year-old has the Giants' number. In three career starts against San Francisco, Cole has three wins and a 2.11 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Leake will make his first start since hitting the 15-day disabled list with a hamstring issue. Leake was acquired from the Reds on July 31, and made one start before the injury, going 6 1/3 innings and allowing two runs on Aug. 2.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano was charged with five runs over seven innings vs. Arizona on Tuesday, but he settled down and pitched five strong innings in the middle of that start. Liriano held the Giants to one run over seven innings on June 3.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong will be familiar with his surroundings -- he played with the Pirates from 2001 to 2006. However, he has struggled at PNC Park, posting a 6-13 record and 6.06 ERA in 20 starts (54 appearances).

home_pitcher_note: Since his last win on July 23, Koehler has dropped five straight starts, and he has a 7.48 ERA in that stretch. At Marlins Park, he is 4-3 (3.07). In two of his last four starts, he's lasted just 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Concerns after Happ’s debut start in Pittsburgh were allayed by two ensuing efforts, one run allowed in 11 1/3 innings. He picked up his first win in eight starts since July 3 by two-hitting Arizona for six innings in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Hand is settling into the rotation, after bouncing back and forth from starter to reliever. He's worked at least six innings in each of his last three starts, allowing one run in six innings in a win over the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Morton has breezed through the first six innings of each of his last two starts, which have featured a devastating curve. He continues to give the Bucs their best chance to win, with the team victorious in 12 of his 16 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson, replacing the injured Kendry Flores, is making his first Major League start since 2012 with Milwaukee. While the lefty has made six relief appearances with Miami this season, he was a starter in Japan last season after missing all of 2013.
away_pitcher_note: Locke tries to rebound on the tough road (6.02 ERA in 10 starts this season) after being battered for 11 hits and six runs in five innings in his last start at PNC Park, where he is usually sharp (prior 3.16 ERA in 13 starts).

home_pitcher_note: The rookie left-hander is coming off his finest MLB start. Nicolino worked a personal high for innings (7 2/3) and pitches (101) in a no-decision against the Phillies. Counting Minor League innings, he's at 146 this year.
away_pitcher_note: Cole returned to form Saturday against the Giants, permitting only an unearned run while striking out eight in his first seven-inning start of the month. Cole is 1-1 with a 4.26 ERA in three career starts against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates have won each of Liriano's last 10 starts, and he is 5-0 with a 3.19 ERA during that stretch. He has struggled a bit of late with a 5.06 August ERA. He's 1-2 with a 5.48 ERA in four career starts vs. the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old, drafted No. 3 overall in 2013, makes his fifth Major League start. Gray, who has yet to figure in a decision, is coming off his shortest outing, (1 2/3 innings, seven runs on eight hits) vs. the Mets last Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Since his shaky Pirates debut on Aug. 4, Happ has allowed only one run in 17 1/3 innings over three starts. Happ has not faced the Rockies since 2011, but he has gone 1-0 with a 1.93 ERA in four career games against them.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin tries to get back on track in his first career start against Pittsburgh. He allowed a season-high 11 runs and 12 hits in two innings to the Mets last Saturday at Coors Field. He’d allowed four runs over 20 innings in his previous three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Morton will look to finish an up-and-down August on a high note. The right-hander has logged three quality starts over his last five outings, but he's permitted five runs without completing six innings in the other two.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa seeks his first win since Aug. 1. He allowed five runs, including two homers, his last time out, Monday in Atlanta. He’s gone at least six innings in all five starts this month.

home_pitcher_note: After a 14-start stretch in which he posted a 2.98 ERA, Nelson walked a career high eight batters and allowed five runs in 3 1/3 innings in Cleveland on Aug. 26. Nelson is 3-1 with a 1.85 ERA in four starts against the Pirates this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cole notched his 15th win after limiting the Marlins to one run in 7 1/3 innings Thursday. Cole had been stuck at 14 wins since July 26, though that was due to a lack of run support as much as any problems he encountered on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: This will be the Major League debut of Davies, a 22-year-old righty acquired from the Orioles at the non-waiver Trade Deadline. He's generously listed at 6-foot and does not throw hard, but he features a terrific changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Locke pitched seven innings of two-run ball to earn a win over the Marlins last Wednesday. He gave up five hits and a walk while striking out three. The quality outing was one of only a few for the lefty in the second half.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie bounced back from a poor start to toss six scoreless innings vs. Cincinnati on Friday. Jungmann has a 1.29 ERA in two starts vs. Pittsburgh this season, including limiting the Pirates to one run over seven innings in his debut on June 9.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano posted a quality start in Friday's no-decision against the Rockies, allowing three runs on four hits over six frames. He is unbeaten in 11 consecutive starts, all games the Pirates have won.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez had his start pushed back a few days after experiencing some back discomfort in his last outing. He’ll be pitching on eight days' rest as a result. He allowed three runs in eight innings in an August start against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates inject a new element into their recent struggles in St. Louis, with Happ kicking off a crucial series. It will be Happ’s first outing versus the Cards since June 2012, but he is 1-8 against them with a 6.79 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia has finished at least six innings in 13 of his 14 starts this year and has won his last four decisions. He has given up four earned runs in a start just once, that being his most recent. Garcia has not faced the Pirates this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates have lost each of the last nine starts against the Cardinals by Morton, who is 2-10 with a 5.58 ERA lifetime against them. Yet -- Morton pitched one-hit ball through seven shutout innings in his last Busch Stadium start, on July 7, 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey continues to be the workhorse of the rotation, as he has made 15 consecutive starts of at least six innings. He’s allowed more than three earned runs in just one of those. He allowed one run in each of his two season starts against the Bucs.
away_pitcher_note: Cole has been looking forward to this start since leaving his last outing after allowing five runs in four innings, eager to fix what went wrong. His pitches lost movement, not speed. He is 0-3 in three Busch Stadium starts, one this season.

home_pitcher_note: DeSclafani was on his way to another fine start on Tuesday at Wrigley Field before the Cubs broke through with two hits, a walk and two runs. It was a hot, muggy night and the righty seemed to be tiring somewhat, but he didn’t use that as an excuse.
away_pitcher_note: Locke could be pitching for his rotation spot after a rough 3 2/3-inning outing in Milwaukee on Sept. 2. He has had a tough time finishing batters -- he induced only eight swings and misses in that last start -- and innings, allowing 30 two-out runs.

home_pitcher_note: Iglesias has put together seven straight quality starts since Aug. 1, including double-digit strikeout performances in each of his past three starts. The rookie beat the Pirates on Aug. 1, allowing two runs over 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty will be looking to start a new winning streak off his first loss since June 20. He says he still feels strong -- and his stuff corroborates the claim -- despite his August ERA (4.94) more than doubling the July (2.03) mark.

home_pitcher_note: Sampson has a 9.00 ERA over his last five starts and hasn't pitched more than four innings his last four games. With more September callups expected  -- namely pitching  -- there could be backup should Sampson have another short start.
away_pitcher_note: The stretch-drive savior will be looking for a sixth straight start without allowing more than one run, which would equal a franchise best (by John Candelaria, in 1982) since 1969. Has a 26-5 strikeouts-to-walks ratio in last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: After he worked his way back from a flexor strain in his right elbow, Burnett will make his first start since July 30. His only outing vs. the Brewers this year was a strong one: one run over seven innings with six strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta will be well-rested, since his last start was cut short after two innings and 39 pitches by rain. He is trying to author a positive finish after missing two months of this season with a rib cage injury.

home_pitcher_note: Morton pitched well in his last start, holding the Cardinals to two runs (one earned) over six innings. He lost to the Brewers at Miller Park in July but threw 7 1/3 scoreless innings against them at home on June 10.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has done some of his best work against the Pirates, going 4-1 with a 1.72 ERA in five starts. He has a 1.64 ERA in two starts at the spacious PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Locke couldn't overcome a pair of early errors behind him but rebounded well in a loss to the Reds on Monday. While he's struggled on the road, Locke has fared much better at home this season, going 3-4 with a 3.62 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Davies worked quickly and effectively for seven innings in Miami on Labor Day for his first Major League win. Thirteen of his 21 outs came on the ground, and he faced the minimum in six of those innings.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano had his best swing-and-miss stuff on Tuesday in Cincinnati, striking out 10 over six shutout innings. The Bucs have won 12 of his last 13 starts. He's 0-2 with a 4.85 ERA in two starts against Milwaukee this season.
away_pitcher_note: Jungmann's 3 2/3-inning, seven-hit, six-run outing in Miami on Tuesday was his poorest showing in 17 big league starts. He set a career high for earned runs allowed and came within one hit of his high for that category.

home_pitcher_note: Cole makes his first start in nine days, given an extra break after his last start, although it was very strong (seven scoreless innings on two hits in St. Louis). Lifetime records of 6-1 against the Cubs and 9-2 in September.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Hammel said his warmup was his worst, and joked he was going to throw a no-hitter (which is what happened to Jake Arrieta). Instead, Hammel gave up three runs over six-plus innings vs. the Cardinals and got the win.

home_pitcher_note: If performance by Trade Deadline acquisitions were an Olympic sport, Happ would have medaled already: 5-1 with a 1.79 ERA in seven starts, with 42 strikeouts vs. seven walks. The Cubs did rough him up in his Bucs debut.
away_pitcher_note: Lester did not get a decision in his last start against the Cardinals, despite posting his 18th quality start. He gave up one run over seven innings but the bullpen couldn't hold a 3-1 lead. He beat the Pirates May 16, giving up one run over seven in

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates are eager to see which recovered pitcher is the real Burnett: The one who allowed three runs in the first inning of his return from a strained flexor tendon, or the one who followed up that with four hitless innings?
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta will try for his 17th straight quality start. The right-hander leads the Major Leagues in wins and ranks among the leaders in ERA. He's one inning shy of 200 and one win away from becoming Cubs' first 20-game winner since Jon Lieber (2001).

home_pitcher_note: Morton has his first '15 meeting with the Cubs in the midst of one of his typical homer-miser stretches: He has allowed only three blasts in his last nine starts, covering 54 innings. Owns one win over the Cubs in nine starts since 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks picked up a win in his last start against the Phillies in one of his best outings of the season. He is 0-1 in three starts against the Pirates this season, giving up 10 runs over 16 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last 14 starts, Greinke is 12-1 with a 1.53 ERA, but he’s been pretty much that good the entire season. Curiously, he has a 5.37 ERA against Pittsburgh in nine career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Locke fortified his spot in the rotation with a terrific start on Saturday against Milwaukee, and he'll now be out to conquer Dodger Stadium, where he is 0-2, having allowed seven runs in nine innings, the most recent start in early 2013.

home_pitcher_note: He might not be the leading Cy Young candidate on his own team, but Kershaw has a nine-game win streak and has made seven straight starts without allowing more than one run.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty has a great track record in rebounding from bad outings, and he'll try to do so again after lasting only 2 1/3 innings on Sunday. He is 3-0 lifetime against the Dodgers, including a scoreless 2014 start at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Bolsinger slides back into the rotation after the Dodgers designated Mat Latos for assignment. Bolsinger is coming off his shortest outing of the season as he lasted just 3 2/3 innings and earned a no-decision against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Newport Beach-native Cole treats all of California as his home park: He has a career record of 4-0 when pitching in the state, including a 6-3 win on May 29, 2014 at Dodger Stadium. Bucs are 20-9 in his starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Gray is looking for his first career win after 8 starts. He pitched 4 2/3 innings and allowed two runs on six hits and two walks while striking out eight in LA on Monday, throwing a career-high 92 pitches. He has a 3.60 ERA in three September starts.
away_pitcher_note: With two solid starts after spending six weeks on the DL with an elbow tendon issue, Burnett goes after his first win since July 20. This will only be his third career start in Coors Field, where he's 0-2 with a 7.30 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After  his second complete game at Coors Field this season -- nine innings of three-run ball vs. the Giants -- Rusin has pitched two road outings and allowed a combined nine runs on 13 hits in nine innings. He is 4-2 with a 4.74 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty has allowed a total of six runs in his last seven starts, while fanning 44 versus seven walks in 41 2/3 innings. This will be Happ’s first career start in Colorado, where he did make one relief appearance in 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Bergman pitched 3 1/3 innings of one-run ball for his third win Saturday, allowing three hits and no walks while striking out three. He’s made one start in 2015, holding the Giants to four hits and two walks while fanning four on the road in April.
away_pitcher_note: Morton takes his second crack at a career-high-tying 10th win. The first inning is a bigger key for him than for most pitchers: He’s allowed first-inning scores in nine of his 20 starts, including the last one, on Thursday against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis was solid Friday, allowing one run on four hits and a walk, while striking out six over five innings. His 96 pitches kept him from going deeper. He threw seven shutout innings in his previous start, and is 2-1 with a 2.76 ERA in September.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start on Friday in Los Angeles, Locke again finished strong after a rocky beginning. To get it quicker, per manager Clint Hurdle, he needs to mix his pitches “from the beginning, not waiting till 10-12 fastballs into the game.”

home_pitcher_note: With an off-day on Thursday, the Cubs will bump Dan Haren and start Lester in the first game of an important series vs. the Pirates. Lester beat the Bucs on Sept. 15, giving up one run over nine innings in his only complete game this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hitting his familiar September stride, Cole is 2-1 this month. He was left with a no-decision against the Cubs after allowing them three runs in 6 1/3 innings on Sunday. He is 6-1 lifetime against the Cubs, including 4-1 in Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel continued to work through command issues in his last outing, allowing four runs in five innings. Over the month of September, he has a 6.86 ERA. He's gone more than six innings only once since the All Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano gave up two runs and five hits in seven innings, walking two and striking out nine, in a 3-2 win on Saturday at Los Angeles. He's 7-3 with a 2.47 ERA in 13 starts on the road.

home_pitcher_note: The stats speak for themselves after Arrieta became the Majors' first 20-game winner this season. He now has 18 straight quality starts, four complete games, three shutouts and a .086 ERA since the All-Star break -- he lowest in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, at Colorado, Burnett gave up six hits and three runs (two earned) in 5 2/3 innings. He walked four in the start, his most in an outing this season since May 17, when he issued five free passes vs. the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Happ is 6-1 with a 1.73 ERA in his past seven starts, with seven walks, 45 strikeouts and just two homers allowed over 41 2/3 innings in that span. He gave up seven hits and three runs in 5 1/3 innings on Tuesday at Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Needing to prove himself worthy of a postseason rotation spot, Lynn tossed six shutout innings his last time out. He has, however, struggled against the Pirates, allowing nine runs on 19 hits in 11 2/3 innings against them this year.

home_pitcher_note: Cole, already designated as the Pirates’ playoff-opening starter, makes his final regular-season start seeking his fourth straight win. He's undefeated in three career home starts against the Cards.
away_pitcher_note: Wacha can become the first Cardinals starter younger than 25 to win 18 games since Joe Magrane did so in 1989.

away_pitcher_note: Syndergaard hadn’t fully developed his legend the last time he faced the Pirates, allowing four runs to them in his third career start last May. At that point, his career record was 1-2. Since then, Syndergaard has gone 14-7 with a 2.83 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis, who gave up two home runs, but remained competitive despite giving up five runs and 10 hits in five innings in a loss to the Padres, will face the Pirates in a makeup of a scheduled April 28 game.
away_pitcher_note: Locke has won four starts in a row and has not walked a batter in his last two appearances. The lefty followed up his first career shutout in Miami by allowing three runs in seven innings vs. the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Cole allowed three runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings in a no-decision against the Angels on Sunday, his fifth quality start in his last six outings. Cole is 5-3 with a 2.91 ERA in nine career starts against the Cardinals.

away_pitcher_note: Taillon allowed three runs over six innings in his Major League debut, recording a quality start against the Mets on Wednesday in Pittsburgh. That was supposed to be a spot start, but Taillon may now be here to stay.

away_pitcher_note: Locke's strong four-start stretch ended abruptly with Thursday's makeup game at Coors Field. After posting a 2.76 ERA from May 19-June 4, Locke allowed 11 runs on 11 hits over 4 2/3 innings against the Rockies.

away_pitcher_note: Nicasio's last start against the Mets -- five innings, one run, seven strikeouts -- was solid. His last appearance? Six runs on four hits, a homer and two walks in a 44-pitch 12th inning Friday night against the Cardinals.

away_pitcher_note: Liriano took a step in the right direction Saturday, allowing four runs (one earned) while striking out eight over six innings. He induced 17 swinging strikes, his highest total in a month, but still walked three batters.

away_pitcher_note: Fresh off an eight-inning gem against the Mets, Taillon looks to build on his first career win on another big stage, against the Cubs at Wrigley Field on Sunday Night Baseball.

away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner is coming off an eight-inning, two-run performance at home against Milwaukee. He’s gone at least six innings in all but two of his starts this year and has a 1.91 ERA in 94 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Boscan was called up from Triple-A Indianapolis on Tuesday to make what will likely just be a spot start -- his first in the Majors -- in Juan Nicasio's place. Boscan owns a 2.92 ERA over five relief appearances this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto hasn’t allowed more than two earned runs in a game since May 2 and enters Tuesday’s matchup against Pittsburgh on a roll. He’s 18-4 with a 2.13 ERA in 28 career starts against the Bucs.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano flirted with trouble throughout Friday's loss to the Cubs, and it eventually caught up with him as he permitted four runs on six hits in 5 2/3 innings. Liriano has issued a Major League-high 46 walks on the year.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija is coming off a complete-game gem, holding the Rays to one run on four hits on Friday. He has a 2.25 ERA in 21 games (10 starts) against Pittsburgh.

away_pitcher_note: Suarez will make his fourth start of the season for San Francisco filling in for the injured Matt Cain. The Venezuelan right-hander owns a 4.50 ERA in 16 innings as a starter and a 2.87 ERA in 15 2/3 innings as a reliever this season.

away_pitcher_note: Tepesch signed a Minor League contract with the Dodgers after a five-year run in the Rangers organization, holding a 4.56 ERA in 219 Major League innings. He had a 2.00 ERA in 18 innings with Triple-A Oklahoma City.

away_pitcher_note: Maeda battled through mechanical issues and leg pain to deliver six innings of one-run ball against the Brewers on Sunday. The right-hander is striking out 8.7 per nine innings and holding opponents to a .318 slugging percentage.
