away_pitcher_note: Kershaw leads the Majors in ERA, innings pitched, strikeouts, WHIP, strikeout-to-walk ratio and shutouts. He hasn’t lost a start since April and he struck out eight Nationals in seven innings of one-run ball on Monday.

away_pitcher_note: Kazmir got his first quality start since May on Tuesday, holding Washington to two runs in six innings despite allowing six extra-base hits. He’s had a rough time at PNC Park, allowing 12 earned runs in two starts there.

away_pitcher_note: Since throwing eight scoreless innings at Citi Field, Taillon has allowed four runs in four innings in each of his last two starts. Control hasn't been Taillon's problem; he's only walked one batter per start since his debut.

away_pitcher_note: Locke continued his excellent recent work in his last outing, when earned a win after going seven innings and giving up one run on five hits at home against the Dodgers. He struck out three and did not walk a batter for the second straight start.

away_pitcher_note: Kuhl's Major League debut on Sunday was a successful one despite it being a brutally tough assignment facing the Dodgers and Clayton Kershaw. Kuhl, 23, gave up three runs on four hits in five innings, striking out five and walking four.

away_pitcher_note: Liriano's struggles with the strike zone continued in his most recent outing, a loss to Los Angeles on June 27. Liriano lasted only 4 1/3 innings and gave up five runs (four earned) on four hits while walking five and striking out three.

away_pitcher_note: Making his first start of July on Independence Day in St. Louis, Niese hopes to rebound from an ugly end to June. The left-hander lost his last four starts, with an 8.86 ERA in that span that's raised his season mark by more than a full run.

away_pitcher_note: Brault, 2-3 with a 2.57 ERA in eight Triple-A starts, will make his Major League debut in place of the injured Jameson Taillon. The Bucs' No. 17 prospect missed time earlier this season with a strained hamstring.

away_pitcher_note: Locke overcame two shaky innings to pitch five and earn his third consecutive win Friday night in Oakland. Locke allowed three runs in five innings. Locke is 3-4 with a 7.16 ERA and 1.59 WHIP in nine road starts this season.

away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' No. 1-ranked prospect is expected to make his Major League debut. In 17 starts for Triple-A Indianapolis, he was 7-2 with a 1.78 ERA and 113 strikeouts in 96 innings, although he also walked 52 batters.

away_pitcher_note: Lester is coming off the shortest outing of his career, in which he lasted just 1 1/3 innings against the Mets. He served up a season-high eight runs on nine hits, including three homers. He's 2-1 with a 1.96 ERA vs. the Pirates this year.

home_pitcher_note: Niese went 5 2/3 innings and allowed one run in a win over the Cardinals on Monday. He's lost both starts he's made against the Cubs this season, with an 8.71 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey will close the first half of the season, facing the Pirates for the first time this season. He's 0-2 with a 7.56 ERA in his last three starts after opening the season 7-3 with a 2.78 ERA in his first 14 starts.

away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' Opening Day starter will make the team's first start after the break, hoping for a better second half. Liriano struggled to a 5-8 record and 5.15 ERA over 17 first-half starts and leads the NL with 58 walks.

away_pitcher_note: Cole will come off the disabled list after missing more than a month with a strained right triceps, and the Pirates could use their ace in top form. Cole has a 2.77 ERA but pitched seven innings in only two of 12 starts.

away_pitcher_note: Kuhl was all over the map in his first three Major League starts -- solid in his debut, better in his second start and disappointing in his most recent outing. Ground balls are the key to success for the righty sinkerballer.

away_pitcher_note: Anderson is 0-5 with a 9.61 ERA and a 1.086 opponents' OPS over his last five starts, a stretch that included one skipped start intended to offer some rest. He has a 2.64 WHIP in two career starts at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano has struggled this season, walking an MLB-high 13.6 percent of the batters he's faced, but things have looked up his last couple starts. He had a promising outing against the Nationals his last outing, allowing three runs in six-plus innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garza has pitched better than his numbers suggest. Case in point: In his most recent start against the Reds, two of his four earned runs scored after Garza left the game, on a flare double off reliever Carlos Torres that landed two-feet fair.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Cole's second start after returning from a month-long stint on the disabled list with a right triceps strain. In Cole's first start back, he gave up four earned runs on seven hits against the Nationals on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie is going for his sixth consecutive quality start. Eflin has a 2.56 ERA in six starts following his debut and gave up three runs in six innings against the Mets in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Glasnow will make his home debut at PNC Park on Saturday, getting the callup for his second big league start. Glasnow allowed four runs on three hits while striking out five over 5 1/3 innings in a loss to the Cardinals on July 7.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since the Phillies skipped him to clear his mind, Nola pitched six scoreless innings Monday vs. the Marlins. Nola posted a 13.50 ERA in his previous five starts, but he looked like himself again.

home_pitcher_note: In Taillon's last start, he held the Brewers to one run on five hits despite taking a line drive to the back of the head in the second inning. He stayed in the game to last six innings and has four quality starts since his debut.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez is 3-0 with a 1.88 ERA (five earned runs in 24 innings) in four starts since he returned from the disabled list in June. His velocity jumped in Tuesday’s start against the Marlins, which he attributed to rest at the All-Star break.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano returned to form on Thursday, striking out 13 Brewers without a walk over 6 2/3 innings, one of his best starts of the season. A second-half surge from Liriano would be a huge boost for the inconsistent Pirates rotation.
away_pitcher_note: After missing nearly two months with a calf injury, Hernandez allowed five runs on five hits over 6 2/3 innings while striking out two in a no-decision against the Chicago White Sox on Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: After an admittedly "frustrating" return from the DL in D.C., Cole found his footing Friday against the Phillies, allowing one run on six hits while striking out seven over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Paxton will look to build off one of his finest outings of the season, as the 27-year-old held the Blue Jays in check on Friday, allowing one earned run on three hits over seven innings while striking out nine in the Mariners' 2-1 win.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra continues to dazzle in his rookie season as a 31-year-old. Last time out, he held the Cubs to one unearned run over 6 1/3 innings despite only striking out two batters.
away_pitcher_note: Brault will rejoin the Pirates in Milwaukee for his second Major League start. Limited by a pitch count in his debut, Brault struck out 16 and allowed three hits in 12 scoreless innings over his past two Triple-A starts.

away_pitcher_note: Taillon continued to pound the strike zone Sunday against the Phillies, but he gave up four runs on eight hits (two homers) over six innings and took a no-decision. The rookie has 31 strikeouts and only five walks this season.

away_pitcher_note: Liriano took a step backward against the Mariners on Tuesday, allowing seven runs over 3 1/3 innings in a 7-4 loss. He struck out 13 with no walks in his last start against Milwaukee, perhaps a sign that he'll rebound Sunday.

away_pitcher_note: Cole is coming off his first professional complete game, a nine-inning gem against the Mariners on Wednesday. In his last two starts, Cole has allowed two runs on nine hits and a walk while striking out 13 over 15 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Locke will rejoin the rotation after a brief but productive stint in the bullpen. Locke pitched well in one appearance and learned a few lessons that he hopes will improve his inconsistent work (8-6, 5.67 ERA) as a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Jenkins picked up his first career win on Friday vs. the Phillies, allowing one unearned run across six innings. He struggled at times with his command and has walked at least four batters in three straight starts.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran will come off the disabled list and make his first start since May 23, when he sustained multiple facial fractures in a scary moment at the plate. It will be his third start and 13th appearance of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Nova will make his Pirates debut on Saturday after being acquired from the Yankees on Monday in exchange for a couple of players to be named later. He’s 8-3 with a 2.72 ERA in 17 games (16 starts) vs. National League clubs.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey had a solid outing first outing since his 2015 Tommy John surgery, allowing two runs over 5 2/3 innings and striking out six. His fastball velocity sat around 93 mph and topped out at 95, according to Pitch f/x.

home_pitcher_note: Cole has allowed just one earned run in three consecutive starts, lowering his season ERA from 3.11 to 2.73. Opposing hitters are batting just .219 against the right-hander during that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl is back in the Majors with a chance to claim a rotation spot. He struggled to keep his power sinker down in his first stint but pitched well in his last outing, holding Washington to one hit over six scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Padres pushed Perdomo to a career-high 113 pitches his last time out, knowing he’d have two extra days of rest between starts. Perdomo’s sinker has been nasty of late, and he leads the National League in ground-ball rate.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong will make his second start following a remarkable recovery from multiple fractures to his face. He held the Braves to one run on three hits while striking out six over six innings in his return from the 60-day DL.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson threw a season-high eight innings in his last start vs. the Brewers, and didn't allow his first run until that final inning. He allowed three earned runs but also managed a hit, run and RBI as a batter.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon will take the mound looking for his sixth straight quality start. He has thrown exactly six innings in each of his last five outings, putting together a 2.40 ERA with 28 strikeouts and one walk during that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Friedrich is coming off of his second seven-inning outing of the season, in which he allowed four earned runs vs. the Phillies. Three of the runs Friedrich surrendered came in one inning, with the box score likely underrating his performance.

home_pitcher_note: With Rich Hill's Dodgers debut delayed again, Stripling will step in. The rookie right-hander remains on an innings limit due to 2014 Tommy John surgery and was last seen throwing five scoreless innings against Boston.
away_pitcher_note: Nova made a good first impression Saturday, winning his Pirates debut against the Reds as he allowed three runs and struck out five without a walk over seven efficient innings. Nova has never pitched against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy has been haunted by a loss of fastball command in his past three starts, allowing seven earned runs and 12 walks in 10 2/3 innings. He hopes that some minor mechanical tweaks will solve the problem.
away_pitcher_note: Cole's inexplicable struggles against the Reds continued Sunday, when he gave up four runs on three hits and three walks in 5 2/3 innings and lost. The SoCal native is 2-0 with a 4.05 ERA in two starts at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has been out since March due to back surgery, and he will be making his 2016 debut on Sunday. The left-hander topped out at 71 pitches in five innings in his last rehab start with Triple-A Oklahoma City.
away_pitcher_note: Pittsburgh is 5-0 when Kuhl starts. After holding the Padres to two runs over six innings on Tuesday, he'll try to make it 6-0 in L.A. He debuted vs. the Dodgers, allowing three runs in five innings and picking up a win.

home_pitcher_note: Matt Moore will make his first start at AT&T Park. The left-hander has a 3.00 ERA in two starts with the club since being acquired from Tampa Bay. He's pitched somewhat erratic in those outings, surrendering a combined 11 walks.
away_pitcher_note: This will be an emotional reunion for Vogelsong, the Giants and their fans who came to love the veteran during his remarkable career comeback in San Francisco from 2011-15. He has a 3.34 ERA in 85 appearances at AT&T Park.

away_pitcher_note: The rookie continued to impress in his 10th start, tossing eight scoreless innings in a win over the Padres. The Pirates have won six of Taillon's past seven starts. He's thrown at least six innings in each of his past six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cain is 3-2 with a 5.82 ERA since returning from the disabled list July 20. He’s also allowed two or more home runs in three of those five starts. The right-hander surrendered a career-high 11 hits in his last outing.
away_pitcher_note: Nova held the Dodgers to one run over 5 1/3 innings Friday, improving to 2-0. He surrendered nine hits and a lot of hard contact, but he didn't walk anyone and went homer-free in a start for just the second time this season.

home_pitcher_note: Cole struggled to solve a Dodgers lineup loaded with lefties Saturday, allowing six runs (five earned) on 12 hits over 4 1/3 innings. He has fared better at PNC Park this season, posting a 2.94 ERA in nine home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Since July 21, Koehler has been Miami's most effective pitcher. Over the five-start stretch, he is 3-0 with a 1.36 ERA, allowing five runs in 33 innings. Overall, on the road, the right-hander is 5-5 with a 4.29 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl continues to make the most of his opportunity to stick in the Pirates rotation. He has thrown six innings of two-run ball in each of his last two starts, and he neutralized a lefty-laden Dodgers lineup his last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Phelps is stepping up in the rotation. In three starts since switching from the bullpen, he's posted a 1.84 ERA. But he has yet to complete six full innings; that is a process after going 5 1/3 and 90 pitches at Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Mentally and emotionally drained by his return to San Francisco, Vogelsong wasn't as sharp Monday as he was in his previous two starts. He admitted to making several mental mistakes as he allowed four runs in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: With Adam Conley on the disabled list, Urena again finds himself in the rotation, where he is 0-3 with a 6.14 ERA as a starter. He has a power fastball, which averages 96.19 mph. Consistent command remains an issue for the 24-year-old.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon turned in a quality start in Tuesday's no-decision against the Giants, surrendering three runs on six hits over six innings. He struck out five and walked one in the no-decision, throwing 91 pitches (65 strikes).
away_pitcher_note: The Astros’ most consistent starting pitcher all season, Fister has gone 1-1 with a 3.91 ERA in his last four starts, allowing 28 hits in 23 innings. His last start was a loss to the Cardinals, in which he allowed seven runs.

home_pitcher_note: Nova was less than stellar in his third start with the Pirates, allowing four runs on six hits over four innings in Wednesday's no-decision against the Giants. Nova has now allowed eight runs through his first 16 2/3 innings with the Bucs.
away_pitcher_note: Rookie is coming off his worst start with the Astros. He was rocked for eight runs and 11 hits in Baltimore on Thursday, but his first two career starts were terrific. He allowed three runs in 14 innings in his first two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cole yielded three runs over 6 2/3 innings in a no-decision vs. Miami on Friday. He gave up 12 hits for the second straight start. He allowed two homers on the night. He has given up 12 runs on 27 hits and eight walks over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: McHugh is searching for his first win since July 23. In his last five starts, he’s gone 0-4 with a 9.00 ERA and allowed 40 hits in 23 innings. He allowed four homers Friday at Baltimore before recording his first out.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta has a 3.50 ERA and a .250 opponents’ average in three starts since returning from a demotion to the Minors and will be facing the Pirates for the first time in 2016. He has a 3.55 ERA in six career starts against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl has pitched well since returning to the Majors, posting three quality starts. On Saturday, he held the Marlins to three runs (two earned) but lost. Oddly, Kuhl didn't record a strikeout or a walk in the six-inning start.

home_pitcher_note: Garza had allowed three or fewer runs in five straight starts before struggling in Seattle, where he lasted only 3 2/3 innings and surrendered six runs (five earned) on nine hits.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong bounced back from a shaky outing in San Francisco with a quality start on Sunday, but lost to the Marlins despite yielding three runs (one earned) in six innings. He is 1-2 with a 2.05 ERA in six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson’s quality start (six innings, two earned runs) against the Rockies on this homestand marked a breakthrough. It snapped a streak of six straight losses in which he didn’t throw a pitch past the sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Taillon continued his efficient and impressive rookie season last time out, holding the Astros to two runs on four hits and a walk while striking out a career-high eight over eight innings. His last eight outings have been quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has made two appearances since an Aug. 16 scare in Chicago, where he was drilled in the left thigh by a 107-mph Kris Bryant liner. Anderson pitched two relief frames at Seattle, then started and pitched five innings vs. Colorado on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Nova is coming off a 98-pitch complete game against the Astros on Tuesday, when he allowed one run on six hits and struck out six. He's 3-0 with a 3.20 ERA, 18 strikeouts and one walk in four starts since joining the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta, who improved to 10-2 with a 2.99 ERA on the road after his last outing, will open a homestand at Wrigley Field against the Pirates. This will be his fifth start vs. the Bucs; he's 3-1 with a 2.67 ERA in four games.
away_pitcher_note: Brault will be recalled from Triple-A Indianapolis to take Gerrit Cole’s scheduled turn in the rotation. He has made two starts for the Bucs this season, lasting four innings against St. Louis on July 5 and six innings against Milwaukee on July 29.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is on a roll. He's given up three or fewer earned runs in each of his last 17 starts, dating to May 22. It's the longest streak by a MLB starter this season. He has a 1.70 ERA in that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie has worked at least six innings with two or fewer earned runs in five consecutive starts. He will be facing the team his last non-quality start came against, as the Cubs knocked him around for four runs in 2 1/3 innings on July 9.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel wasn't happy after his last outing, when he was pulled after throwing 39 pitches over 2 1/3 innings vs. the Dodgers. He met with manager Joe Maddon after the game. It will be good to be back at Wrigley, where Hammel is 8-1 with a 1.79 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong has performed well since returning after missing over two months due to facial fractures, posting a 2.48 ERA in five starts. The veteran limited the Brewers to two runs over 5 1/3 innings his last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon will face the Brewers for the fourth time this season after a rough outing in Milwaukee on Saturday. The rookie allowed five runs on seven hits in three innings, his first non-quality start since June 24.
away_pitcher_note: After missing nearly the entire month of August with right elbow inflammation that landed him on the DL, Guerra will make his return to the rotation. Guerra has allowed only three runs in 14 2/3 innings against the Pirates this season.

home_pitcher_note: Nova reeled off another quality start Sunday in Milwaukee, holding the Brewers to one run on three hits in six innings. He is 4-0 with a 2.87 ERA, 22 strikeouts and one walk in 31 1/3 innings over five starts for the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Thankfully for Nelson, August will be over when he takes the mound against Pittsburgh. Nelson allowed 30 runs (28 earned) over 28 innings and six starts in August as his ERA jumped from 3.42 to 4.45.

home_pitcher_note: Brault quickly ran up a high pitch count in a loss to the Cubs on Monday, lasting only four innings on 92 pitches while allowing three runs. He held the Brewers to three runs on seven hits in six innings on July 29.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson's last start came against these same Pirates, as he worked five scoreless innings without any problems before giving up two solo homers in the sixth that decided the game.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl pitched well enough, but to no avail, at Wrigley Field on Tuesday. The rookie allowed three runs on four hits in five innings and lost. He held the Brewers to two runs over 6 1/3 innings at Miller Park on Aug. 25.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing 25 runs in a five-start span, Wainwright found his way back on track Tuesday. With a more aggressive delivery and added mphs on his fastball, he limited the Brewers to three hits and one run over seven strong innings.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong pitched five solid innings in Chicago on Wednesday, but couldn't record an out in the sixth, allowing five runs on six hits and three walks and losing. In his previous start, he limited Milwaukee to two runs in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver struck out a career-high 10 in his last start but was undone by a costly walk and three-run homer. Still, he made his second consecutive quality start and showed improved conviction with his pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon continued to pitch well as he began his first September stretch run, holding the Brewers to one run in six efficient, walk-free innings Friday at PNC Park. This will be the rookie's first start against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Leake will rejoin the rotation after being sidelined by shingles. Leake last started on Aug. 21, when he pitched seven scoreless innings. Fatigue could be a factor, as Leake has thrown off the mound only once since that last start.

home_pitcher_note: Nova made one mistake on Saturday and paid for it, allowing two runs on five hits, including a homer, while striking out six Brewers over six innings. Nova has been great for the Pirates, going 4-0 with a 2.89 ERA in six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Straily had command issues in his last outing against St. Louis, walking a career-high seven batters, but came away mostly unscathed, allowing one run on a homer over 5 2/3 innings. Of his three hits allowed, just one came after the first inning.

home_pitcher_note: Brault's fourth Major League start was perhaps his best, as he held the Brewers to one run on four hits and struck out five in five innings. He wasn't rewarded for his performance, however, as he still seeks his first win.
away_pitcher_note: Adleman was susceptible to the long ball on Sunday in a 5-2 loss to the Cardinals. All three runs he allowed in his five innings came via home runs. He also gave up two homers over six innings to the Angels two starts ago.

home_pitcher_note: Hutchison recently was called up from Triple-A Indianapolis. He'll start in place of right-hander Chad Kuhl. Hutchison was acquired from the Blue Jays in the Francisco Liriano deal. He was 1-1 at Indianapolis, with a 4.50 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Stephenson returned to the bigs for the first time since two April starts and acquitted himself well in a 5-0 loss to the Mets. He allowed two runs over 5 1/3 innings, both on solo homers. But while showing improved command, walking just one.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong has allowed five runs over his last nine innings, spanning two starts, after a strong return from the DL. He will try to get back on track against the Reds, whom he has not faced as a starter this season.
away_pitcher_note: Finnegan likely has two starts remaining, including Sunday, with a chance to end his season on a strong note. Efficiency was an issue Tuesday vs. the Mets. Seven of his 22 batters went to three-ball counts and he threw 105 pitches in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson hopes to get back on track after struggling recently. He is 0-3 with a 6.75 ERA in his last three starts, although he pitched six innings in two of those starts. Prior to that he had a 2.45 ERA in his previous 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cole, who has been sidelined since Aug. 25 with inflammation in his right elbow, will start in place of Jameson Taillon. The Pirates wanted to sit Taillon because of the amount of innings he has pitched, and Cole was pronounced ready to go.

home_pitcher_note: Asher made his season debut Thursday night against the Nationals after serving an 80-game suspension for PED use. He allowed just two hits and one walk in six scoreless innings, throwing a mere 75 pitches (55 strikes).
away_pitcher_note: Nova allowed a run on six hits in a complete game victory over the Reds on Thursday. Nova struck out four without issuing a free pass, needing just 94 pitches to complete the deed. Nova is 5-0 with a 2.53 ERA in seven starts with the Bucs.

home_pitcher_note: Thompson had a 9.78 ERA after his first four starts, but after he allowed two runs in 5 1/3 innings Friday night against the Nationals, he has a 2.33 ERA (five earned runs in 19 1/3 innings) in his last three.
away_pitcher_note: Brault yielded two runs in five innings in a no-decision against the Reds on Friday. The young left-hander allowed five hits and two walks while striking out two batters in the ballgame. He has 19 strikeouts and 12 walks in 24 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff pitched six scoreless innings in a pitchers' duel with the Max Scherzer and the Nationals on Saturday. He struck out five Nats, including Bryce Harper three times, all on curveballs
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates skipped Kuhl's turn on Saturday following a rocky outing Monday against St. Louis (2 IP, 4 H, 3 ER, 3 BB). Kuhl has logged 134 1/3 innings this year between Triple-A and the Major Leagues and may have been dealing with some fatigue.

home_pitcher_note: Stephenson lacked his best fastball as he labored through three innings with 62 pitches on Saturday at Pittsburgh. It was his first subpar start in four big league games.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong faces the Reds for the second straight outing after giving up six runs and walking three in four innings on Sunday. He has an 11.08 ERA in his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: DeSclafani’s turn was skipped Monday to give him extra rest after his stuff seemed to not be as effective in recent starts. There’s no belief that he’s hurt, but the club wanted him to give him rest so he could finish the season strong.
away_pitcher_note: Taillon is set to return to the rotation Saturday after skipping his last turn. The rookie is 2-2 with a 4.09 ERA in six road starts this season and 1-0 with a 1.93 ERA in his two afternoon starts for the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: In all likelihood, this will be Finnegan’s 30th and final start before he's shut down due an innings limit. Pitch efficiency and walks remain an issue, but he twice worked out of bases-loaded jams Sunday vs. the Bucs and threw five scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Williams will make his first Major League start in the second half of Saturday's doubleheader. The righty made two relief appearances after being called up in September. He recorded a 1.50 ERA in his last 13 Triple-A outings.

home_pitcher_note: Straily continued his excellent season last time out, allowing two runs over a career-high eight innings with eight strikeouts. Straily lived and died by the flyout, inducing just three ground balls the entire game and giving up two solo homers.
away_pitcher_note: Nova's post-Deadline excellence continued Tuesday night, as he struck out a season-high 11 in six strong innings against the Phillies. He is 5-0 with a 2.41 ERA, 43 strikeouts and three walks in eight starts for the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Garza took the loss against the Reds in his last start, but only one of the five runs he allowed was earned. It's a recent trend for Garza. He's given up 12 runs in his past four starts, but only three earned runs for a 1.16 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Brault is still looking for his first big league win. The rookie left-hander went 3 2/3 innings in his last start, allowing five runs (three earned) on nine hits against the Phillies. He's 0-2 with a 3.27 ERA in two prior starts against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson will be starting on five days' rest in what would've been a start for Junior Guerra, who was shut down for the season. Nelson earned a win Thursday against the Cubs in his last start, allowing three runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl won his last start, tossing six innings of two-run ball against the Phillies. He's gone at least six innings in six of his last eight outings. Kuhl allowed two runs on five hits in 6 1/3 innings against the Brewers in August.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson took a no-decision Friday against the Cubs at Wrigley Field in his most recent start, allowing two runs in six innings. Anderson is 2-1 with a 2.33 ERA in four starts against the Pirates this season, including a 3.20 strikeout-to-walk rate.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong hasn't completed five innings in any of his last three starts. He was charged with six runs (four earned) on seven hits in 4 2/3 innings against the Reds his last time out. He beat the Brewers on Aug. 26, allowing two runs in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon surrendered nine hits and a walk in his last start but came away with only three runs allowed. The rookie has never faced the Nationals and has a 3.39 ERA over 16 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: With his importance to the Nationals' playoff rotation heightened due to the injury to Stephen Strasburg, Gonzalez turned in an uninspiring outing last time out. He surrendered six runs on nine hits in 4 1/3 innings against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Nova's renaissance with the Pirates took a turn in the opposite direction his last time out, allowing 10 hits and five runs (four earned) over three innings in a loss to the Reds. He is still 5-1 with a 2.93 ERA with Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Ross returned to the mound for the first time in two months to toss three innings against the Braves last time out. This will be one of his final two starts of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates' top prospect will make his third Major League start after a September stint in the bullpen. Glasnow pitched well in relief, allowing two runs while striking out eight in seven innings over three appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Cole will make his seventh start of the season in the finale in Pittsburgh. In his last start against the Marlins, Cole lasted four innings and allowed two runs on four hits in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl put together his second straight quality start since having a turn skipped, holding the Brewers to one run in six innings on Wednesday. He's allowed seven runs on 11 hits in 7 1/3 innings in two starts vs. the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks has posted 21 straight starts in which he's given up three or fewer earned runs, the longest streak in the Majors. He leads the big leagues with a 2.06 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong bounced back from a rough five-start stretch, striking out seven and allowing two runs on two hits in four innings Thursday vs. the Brewers. He believes a mechanical tweak before that outing made the difference.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey will face the Pirates for the second time this season. He did not get a decision on July 10, giving up five runs over six innings. In four starts this month, Lackey is 1-1 with a 3.24 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon made his second straight five-inning, three-run start Friday against the Nationals, striking out seven without a walk. He may be tiring toward the end of the season, but the Bucs have won his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta won his 18th game in his past start vs. the Cardinals, throwing seven scoreless. He posted his 12th double-digit strikeout game. He was matched up with Miguel Montero, and it will be interesting to see if the Cubs stay with that battery.

home_pitcher_note: Nova’s defense did him no favors after a poor first inning in a shaky four-frame start against the Nats on Saturday. After an incredible eight-start run, Nova has allowed seven earned runs in seven innings his past two times out.
away_pitcher_note: Zastryzny will start in the series finale, although the rest of the bullpen will be on call. The lefty was a combined 10-5 with a 4.31 ERA in 24 games (23 starts) at Triple-A and Double-A this season. He has pitched only in relief in Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Martinez’s final regular-season start and what the Cards hope is a Wild Card tuneup. Martinez, who has allowed two or fewer runs in four of his last five starts, has a 2.41 ERA in three starts vs. Pittsburgh, but has lost twice.
away_pitcher_note: Glasnow will try to finish strong following a personally disappointing year. The top prospect’s success hasn’t followed him to the Majors, where he has a 6.35 ERA in three starts. He allowed four runs in St. Louis in his MLB debut.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha will make his first start since Aug. 8, when he went on the disabled list the next day. He has made three relief appearances since his return with a 15.88 ERA over 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl has likely pitched his way into the Pirates’ 2017 rotation, but he would like to bounce back from a three-inning, five-run outing vs. the Cubs on Monday and a 5.82 September ERA. This will be his first start at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals reworked their rotation so that Wainwright would line up to pitch a potentially critical game 162. He’s had an uneven season but fared better at home, and has helped the Cardinals to wins in five of his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong will make his 14th start of the season and perhaps the last of his career. The 39-year-old veteran has struggled down the stretch, posting an 8.77 ERA over his last six outings after logging a 2.48 ERA in his five starts prior to that.

2017-03-31 - Pittsburgh Pirates @ Toronto Blue Jays (Final: Tied)

home_pitcher_note: For the first time in his career, the sinkerballer will take the ball on Opening Day. This, after winning the American League's Cy Young Award last season. Porcello can't wait to get back to Fenway, where he went 13-1 with a 2.97 ERA last season.
away_pitcher_note: Cole will make his first Opening Day start and first career appearance at Fenway Park. Cole battled through injuries last year and posted a 3.88 ERA in 21 starts, but he put together an excellent spring and seems poised to bounce back.

home_pitcher_note: The power lefty makes his much-anticipated debut in a Boston uniform. In his career as a starter at Fenway, Sale is 1-1 with a 4.12 ERA. Sale is 15-4 lifetime in April with a 3.31 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Taillon made a strong debut last season, recording a 3.38 ERA in 18 starts. The right-hander, the No. 2 overall Draft pick in 2010, will look to avoid the dreaded sophomore slump and cement himself as a top-of-the-rotation arm behind Gerrit Cole.

home_pitcher_note: Nova said starting the home opener makes him feel like a "No. 1 in Pittsburgh," and he pitched like it down the stretch in 2016. A model of efficiency in a Pirates uniform, he posted a 3.06 ERA in 11 starts, including a 2.45 ERA in six home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Arguably the most talented member of Atlanta's rotation, Foltynewicz will attempt to avoid the mental lapses that have previously plagued him. Along with a plus fastball, he creates swings and misses with his curve and slider.

home_pitcher_note: After a solid debut last year (4.20 ERA in 14 starts), Kuhl solidified a rotation spot with a strong spring. The Pirates believe the power sinkerballer is capable of more, especially if he rediscovers a high ground-ball rate.
away_pitcher_note: The 42-year-old knuckleballer returns to the National League for the first time since winning the 2012 Cy Young Award with the Mets. He struggled last year with Toronto, but posted a 3.57 ERA in 14 road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cole started strong Monday, but a five-run fifth inning derailed his first career Opening Day start, a 5-3 loss to the Red Sox in Boston. The right-hander is 22-14 with a 3.32 ERA in 49 career starts at PNC Park.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran displayed confident command as he worked both sides of the plate with both his fastball and offspeed stuff during Monday's six scoreless innings in New York.

home_pitcher_note: Glasnow, the Pirates' top prospect, earned the final spot in the rotation by improving throughout the spring. He will try to improve on an up-and-down debut season in which he posted a 4.24 ERA in seven appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Finnegan is coming off of one of the finest starts of his career - seven innings and 88 pitches in a 2-0 win over the Phillies on Wednesday. His fastball was touching 96 mph and had full command of a changeup in a masterful effort.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon was in command in his season debut on Wednesday at Fenway Park, holding the Red Sox scoreless over seven innings while striking out six. He posted a 2.86 ERA in 11 starts at PNC Park last season.
away_pitcher_note: Davis lasted three innings in his big league debut vs. the Phillies and was often hurt when he was ahead in the counts and didn't execute a pitch. That included when he allowed two home runs to Daniel Nava in pitchers' counts.

home_pitcher_note: Nova allowed one unearned run in six innings in his first start of the season Friday, a 5-4 win over Atlanta. The right-hander did not issue a walk, following a season in which he walked three batters in 64 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In a stellar debut, Garrett pitched six scoreless innings vs. the Cardinals for a 2-0 win. He had good command of his four-seam fastball and threw it just more than half of his 78 pitches. He was also effective with his changeup and slider.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez will make his first Fenway start of 2017 after a shaky season debut vs. the Tigers in which he allowed four runs -- including two homers -- and walked three in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl won despite not being at his best Saturday, walking six batters (two intentionally) and hitting another as he allowed five hits over five innings. Kuhl will start the rescheduled game at Fenway, where he was scheduled to pitch last Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is eager to get back into a routine. His first start of the season came after a long layoff, and he admitted it was hard to find his groove. He does like Wrigley Field, posting a 9-2 record and a 1.32 ERA in 15 games there last year.
away_pitcher_note: Cole logged a quality start Sunday vs. Atlanta, giving up three runs on eight hits (including two homers) over six innings in his second start of the season. Cole enjoys pitching at Wrigley, where he is 6-1 with a 2.20 ERA in seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Arrieta's first start at home this year. In his first two outings, the radar readings have been around 91-92 mph. He's OK with that, especially because he has had good command. He's 9-3 with a 2.96 ERA in 15 starts vs. the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a rough '17 debut in which his command and control of the running game eluded him, Glasnow will face the Cubs for the first time in his career. He allowed five runs on four hits and five walks while recording five outs Monday vs. the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Lester did not get a decision in his last outing, giving up one run over six innings against the Dodgers. The Cubs have won his last 11 regular-season home starts, and he's 9-0 with a 1.41 ERA in that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Taillon put together another quality start against the Reds on Tuesday, holding Cincinnati to two runs on four hits over six innings. The right-hander allowed four runs over four innings in his only career start at Wrigley Field last season.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn allowed three homers in a game for the third time in his career his last time out. He will next be facing a Pirates team that has given him fits in the past. In 19 games (17 starts) against Pittsburgh, Lynn is 5-5 with a 4.74 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Nova had one rough inning but otherwise pitched well enough to win Wednesday, allowing four runs (three earned) in six innings, throwing 82 pitches. The eight-year veteran has never pitched at Busch Stadium or even faced the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Leake has allowed one run over 15 innings and limited opponents to one barreled ball in his first two starts. The average exit velocity on balls in play against him is 87.2 mph, more than two mph lower than it was last season.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl looked more like himself Thursday, holding the Red Sox to one run on five hits while striking out six over 6 1/3 innings. He has been a better pitcher outside of PNC Park, oddly, owning a 2.56 ERA in nine career road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha threw too many pitches up in the zone in his last start, and two of those were tagged for home runs. His fastball velocity is up a bit, though, which is encouraging after seasons plagued by shoulder injuries.
away_pitcher_note: Cole continued to round into form Friday at Wrigley Field, holding the Cubs' deep lineup to two runs over six innings while throwing 114 pitches. He owns a 2-3 record and 3.13 ERA in five career starts at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: After a poor season debut, Glasnow took a few steps forward Saturday against the Cubs. In his final four innings, manager Clint Hurdle said, Glasnow looked like a Major League pitcher. Plagued by control issues in his debut, Glasnow struck out seven
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia has provided the Yankees with two straight quality starts, rolling back the clock with a vintage 7 1/3-inning, one-run performance vs. the Cardinals his last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon continued to impress Sunday at Wrigley Field, holding the Cubs to one (unearned) run over seven strong innings. He has been at his best at home, carrying a career 2.88 ERA at PNC Park into his fourth start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Pineda has excelled in his last two starts, working at least seven innings while permitting two runs or fewer in victories over the Rays and Cardinals. Pineda has struck out 23 against just one walk in 18 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nova will face his former team for the first time. The veteran righty, who spent seven years in the Majors with the Yankees, is coming off a 78-pitch complete-game loss to the Cardinals at Busch Stadium. He has yet to issue a walk this season.
away_pitcher_note: Montgomery picked up his first Major League win his last time out, limiting the White Sox to three runs over six innings. A tall lefty with deception, Montgomery has been compared to former big leaguer Chuck Finley.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl pitched well, but he wasn’t rewarded for it Tuesday, holding the Cardinals to two runs on three hits and a walk over six innings while striking out three. After a rocky debut, Kuhl has put together back-to-back quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson had an abbreviated outing against the Brewers in his last start in which he gave up six runs over 3 2/3 innings. He also was hit on the right hamstring by a liner, but said it didn't affect him. In his previous start, he had a groin injury.

home_pitcher_note: Cole has strung together three straight quality starts, all six-inning outings. He shut down everyone Wednesday except Dexter Fowler, whose two solo homers accounted for the only two runs Cole allowed as he struck out eight.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks hasn't felt as strong as he wants to be, and has struggled with command. In his last start against the Brewers, he walked four over five innings. He's 3-2 with a 3.77 ERA in eight career starts vs. the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Glasnow was in “survival mode” and mostly minimized the damage over 4 2/3 innings Friday vs. the Yankees. He allowed six runs (four earned) on six hits while striking out seven at Wrigley Field on April 15, getting better as the game went along.
away_pitcher_note: Chicago's Opening Day hurler had to settle for his fourth consecutive no-decision Friday after allowing five runs over 5 2/3 innings at Cincinnati. A rotation tweak pits him against the Pirates instead of Boston.

home_pitcher_note: Conley held the Padres' offense in check during his last start, but he couldn’t come away with the win. He worked six innings, allowing one run on six hits and struck out five while throwing a season-high 93 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Taillon worked through his shortest start of the season Saturday, allowing four runs to the Yankees on five hits and three walks over 5 1/3 innings. Taillon is 4-2 with a 3.12 ERA in nine career starts on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a career-best 14 strikeouts at San Diego, Straily's strikeouts per nine innings has jumped to 10.45. His rate was 7.62 at Cincinnati last year. In his last three starts, his ERA is 2.08 with 24 Ks in 17 1/3 IP.
away_pitcher_note: Nova threw seven outstanding innings against his former team Sunday, holding the Yankees to one run on four hits while striking out seven. Each outing this season have been quality starts, and he’s yet to throw more than 93 pitches in a start.

home_pitcher_note: Fastball command has been spotty, and batters are hitting .282 off Koehler. They're .257 in their careers off the right-hander. His WHIP is 1.52, also above his career mark of 1.37. Twice he's gone as many as six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl didn’t have his best stuff Monday, and the Cubs made him pay, scoring nine runs on eight hits and four walks while recording five outs. He has given up three runs or fewer in 15 of his 18 career starts; the other three were against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: It was a learning experience for Garrett vs. the Brewers on Monday, getting roughed up for the first time in the big leagues for 9 earned runs. He got away from his fastball and went offspeed a lot, leaving several pitches up in the strike zone.
away_pitcher_note: Hoping to build on his previous outing, Cole makes his sixth start of the season. Despite suffering the loss, he pitched seven innings of two-hit ball and surrendered just one unearned run while striking out eight. He did not walk a batter.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman will be looking to bounce back after taking his second loss of the season vs. the Brewers on Tuesday, when he allowed four runs on five hits in five innings. He struck out five and walked five.
away_pitcher_note: Looking to turn things around in 2017, Glasnow makes his fifth start of the season still looking for his first win and initial quality start of the season. He got a no-decision in his last outing vs. the Cubs on April 26, going 3 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Davis will make his fourth career start and his second against the Pirates. He faced the Bucs on April 11 and allowed one run on two hits over four innings. The four innings marked the longest outing of his three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Making his sixth start of the season, Taillon has wasted little time in becoming one of the Pirates’ top starters. As a rookie last season he produced the second-lowest ERA (3.38) among National League rookie starters.

home_pitcher_note: Adleman got roughed up by the Cardinals on Friday in his second start of the season. The righty was tagged for six runs (five earned) in 5 1/3 innings and said afterward he struggled with his command. He’ll look to bounce back vs. the Bucs.
away_pitcher_note: Nova’s dominant start continued Saturday in Miami, where he threw his second complete game of the season: a 95-pitch shutout. Nova allowed four runs (three earned) in six innings against the Reds on April 12, tied for his shortest start of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl left his last start early after being hit in the right knee by a hard ground ball. He was swollen and sore in the following days but expects to be fine Friday. Kuhl had a 2.19 ERA in 12 1/3 innings over two starts against the Brewers last year.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has performed well historically at PNC Park, where he has a 2.96 ERA in five career starts. The right-hander hasn't completed six frames since he worked seven innings of one-run ball in his last win, at Cincinnati on April 13.

home_pitcher_note: Cole pitched well Monday in Cincinnati but was again not helped by his defense or lineup. Since a five-run outing on Opening Day, Cole has thrown at least six innings in each of five starts while posting a 2.61 ERA and 32 strikeouts in 31 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garza spent the spring working on offspeed stuff, and used it in a win over the Braves. Garza noticed he didn’t have his good, heavy fastball, so he worked off other pitches instead, including his changeup. Notably, he struck out 7 and walked none.

home_pitcher_note: Glasnow took a potentially significant step forward Tuesday in Cincinnati, logging his first MLB win and six-inning start against the Reds. He felt he turned a corner mechanically, and it showed in his aggressive approach on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Davies still has not pitched past the sixth inning this season, but his two most recent outings have been more like it. Davies has limited the Reds and Cardinals to two earned runs in 10 innings over those games.

home_pitcher_note: Wood is making the start instead of Brandon McCarthy, who was placed on the DL with left shoulder soreness. He went five innings in his last start and gave up five runs (four earned), but still pick up the win vs. the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Declared the Pirates’ sixth starter by manager Clint Hurdle, Williams will step in for the injured Jameson Taillon and make his second Major League start. He is 1-1 with a 5.40 ERA in 11 2/3 innings of relief over six appearances this season.

home_pitcher_note: Urias wasn’t efficient last time out, but he was effective in five scoreless innings. Three of four walks resulted from pitching around Brandon Belt, but they did run up the pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: Nova struggled, by his standards, against the Reds on Thursday, allowing four runs on 10 hits over six innings. He has only walked one batter this season, and he has pitched at least six innings in each of his six starts to begin the season.

home_pitcher_note: Eight strikeouts in five innings is proof that Maeda’s willingness to finally throw the cutter is a big plus. Now he needs to consistently pitch deeper in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl’s last two starts have been cut short -- first by a comebacker to the knee, then by rain -- but he felt good as he threw three scoreless innings Friday vs. Milwaukee. Kuhl posted a 4.09 ERA but won both of his starts vs. the Dodgers last year.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke is bouncing back in a big way to start the season after a down 2016. The veteran went 13-7 in '16 despite a 4.37 ERA, his worst since 2010. This year, however, he’s trending back toward his old ways, going 3-2 with a 3.09 ERA in 7 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cole was at his best against the Brewers last week, allowing just one run, a solo homer, in seven innings. Despite his 1-3 record, the right-hander owns a 2.37 ERA through six starts since his five-run Opening Day outing.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin makes his eighth start of the season on the heels of his worst outing so far in 2017. The lefty allowed a season-high eight earned runs while tying a season low with four innings pitched in a loss against the Rockies on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Glasnow tossed a career-high 6 1/3 innings his last time out, but was undone by a solo homer and the Pirates’ defensive miscues. The rookie is making his first appearance against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Walker finished April with his best start of the year, going eight innings with 11 K's in a win over the Padres. Since the calendar flipped to May, the righty has struggled to work deep into games, having to be pulled after 4 2/3 and 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Williams makes his second start after opening the season in the bullpen. He hopes it goes better than his first effort, when he was charged with six earned runs on seven hits and a walk in three innings Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Ray was not sharp in his last start against the Tigers, issuing five walks over five innings of work. That outing came on the heels of a dominant performance against the Nats, in which he fanned 10 in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nova has allowed more than two earned runs in only one of his previous seven starts. On the season, he is 3-3 but with a 2.23 ERA and has 29 strikeouts to just three walks.

home_pitcher_note: After having three starts cut short by ineffectiveness, injury and inclement weather, Kuhl allowed four runs in five innings in Wednesday's loss to the Dodgers. He held the Nats to one hit over six shutout innings last July.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg takes the ball against the team he faced in his electric Major League debut in 2010. In six career starts against the Pirates, he has posted a 2.51 ERA with 60 strikeouts in 43 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cole has pitched seven innings in three of his last four starts, and the Bucs won only once. He has made seven straight quality starts despite the lack of run support. He owns a 2.92 ERA in four starts against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: In seven appearances, including one start, spanning 16 1/3 innings, Turner is 2-1 with a 3.31 ERA. The only time he faced the Pirates was in 2014 while pitching for the Chicago Cubs. Turner gave up seven earned runs in 4 1/3 innings in the loss.

home_pitcher_note: After consecutive quality starts, Glasnow pitched two strong innings Friday in Arizona then served up seven runs in a brutal third that ended his night. Opponents are batting .315/.420/.559 off Glasnow in his seven starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: High pitch counts during his most recent outings have prevented Roark from pitching deep into games. He needed 110 pitches to get through 4 2/3 innings in his most recent start against the Phillies, when he gave up four runs on six hits.

home_pitcher_note: Williams rebounded from a shaky start in LA by throwing five strong innings in Arizona on Saturday. He allowed one run on a solo homer and retired the final 12 hitters he faced in order, leading the Pirates to a 4-3 win.
away_pitcher_note: Hellickson has a 7.90 ERA in three May starts, a stretch in which batters have posted a 1.204 OPS against him. This after a dominant April, when he became the first Phillies player since Roy Halladay in 2010 to begin a season with four straight wins.

home_pitcher_note: Nova put together another quality start Sunday, holding the D-backs to three runs over six innings. Nova has pitched at least six innings in each of his eight starts, though he has posted a 4.42 ERA this month after a 1.50 mark in April.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez threw 100 pitches in five innings Sunday in Washington, striking out five and giving up two earned runs on five hits and three walks. Batters are averaging an 89.7-mph exit velocity against him, ninth-highest in the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl has struggled mightily to give the Pirates length in his starts. The right-hander has completed six or more innings twice in eight outings, neither of which have come this month. He’s given up 10 runs in his past two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Nola rejoins the rotation after being sidelined from the big league club for a month with a strained lower back. He made two rehab starts, the most recent one on Monday, when he allowed two hits and one walk and struck out seven in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has allowed three earned runs or fewer in six of his seven starts. The young hurler still gets in trouble at times when he overthrows, but he has shown he has the stuff to be a front-line starter.
away_pitcher_note: Cole is coming off a string of quality starts. In his last five outings, Cole has struck out 31 batters, while issuing only six walks and allowing seven earned runs. He holds the fifth-lowest ERA among National League starters in May.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey has allowed three earned runs or fewer in 7 of his first 8 starts and has pitched into the sixth in each of his past four outings. He has gained a better feel for his knuckleball of late and has had more success changing speeds with it.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates are hoping to receive more quality innings from Glasnow. He has only lasted through six innings in two of his eight starts. He did, however, produce a solid outing Thursday, limiting the Nationals to only three hits in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran has struggled at home (10.50 ERA in five starts) and pitched like an ace on the road (0.71 ERA in  four starts). He'll attempt to buck this trend against the Pirates, who haven't tallied an earned run against him in 14 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Williams has pitched well in his last two outings, allowing only eight hits and four earned runs in that span. But he has struggled to strike out hitters, as he failed to record a strikeout in his last start against Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Colon has pitched more effectively in his past two outings and might have completed at least five scoreless against the Nationals on Saturday had he not committed a costly throwing error. He seems to be finding more comfort with his changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Nova has pitched at least six innings in all nine of his starts. His season debut came against the Braves on April 7. In that game, he struck out four, scattered six hits and didn’t allow a run over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl returned to form Sunday against the Phillies, allowing one hit and two walks, while striking out five, in five innings. He recorded seven outs on the ground, a good sign for the sinker-ball starter. He has never faced the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Last time out, deGrom became the first Mets pitcher in 18 games to record an out in the seventh inning. The Mets need performances like that more frequently from deGrom, who has personally gone longer than six just three times in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cole had a rare off night in Atlanta on Monday, allowing five runs on 10 hits in 4 2/3 innings. He had allowed 2 ER or fewer, while pitching at least six innings, in his previous seven starts. He has a career 4.15 ERA vs. the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Wheeler was en route to one of his best starts of the season before melting down in the sixth inning last time out. He requested an extra day of rest this turn through the rotation, lining him up to make his first career start at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Without a changeup or consistent curveball, Glasnow held the Braves to two runs over six innings Tuesday night. Three of his five outings this month have been quality starts, though he allowed a season-high nine hits last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Control remains a major issue for Harvey in his return from thoracic surgery. He has 26 walks in nine starts this season -- five fewer than he did in his entire 2013 All-Star campaign. Harvey is 0-1 with a 5.29 ERA lifetime against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Williams is coming off one of his best starts of the year, having struck out a career-high six while scattering six hits and allowing three earned runs in five innings. He was strong in his last outing vs. Arizona, striking out four in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Delgado's last outing earned him another start on Monday, manager Torey Lovullo said Friday. In his first start this season on Wednesday, Delgado allowed just one run and three hits over four innings in a win over the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Nova pitched 8 1/3 innings in his last start and has worked at least six innings in all 10 of his starts, including his last outing vs. the D-backs, on May 14. In that game, Nova struck out four and allowed three earned runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ray provided the D-backs with seven scoreless innings against the Brewers on Thursday. The lefty dealt nine strikeouts, allowing zero walks, and has a scoreless streak of 15 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl struggled in his last outing, allowing eight hits and five earned runs in just 4 1/3 innings against the Mets on Friday. He has never faced the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Godley lowered his ERA under two after dealing six scoreless innings against the Brewers on Friday. The right-hander has recorded a pickoff in back-to-back games and has four straight quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Quietly, Harvey is beginning to push aside his early-season struggles, going 2-0 with a 3.31 ERA his last three outings. He’ll start a second straight game against the Pirates, whom he held to one run over six innings last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Cole coughed up four runs on 10 hits in his last start on Saturday against the Mets. It was the second straight start Cole has allowed 10 hits and at least four earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: With Steven Matz and Seth Lugo nearing returns from elbow injuries, the Mets have indicated that Gsellman is likely to go to the bullpen following this outing. The move comes just as he’s rounding into form, with a 2.77 ERA his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Glasnow unraveled in his first career start vs. the Mets. After cruising through the first three frames, he surrendered five runs on seven hits in just the fourth and fifth innings. He has only lasted through six innings in three of his 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets need at least one more start from Pill, as Steven Matz and Seth Lugo continue working to return from elbow injuries. The rookie stranded seven runners in his first start, taking a no-decision despite giving up just one run in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Williams earned his first quality start of the season in his last start against the D-backs, limiting one of the best offenses in baseball to just one run on four hits in six innings. He has never faced the Mets in his career.

home_pitcher_note: After some early-season struggles, Gausman has a 3.00 ERA in his last three starts, including two quality starts. He picked up the win Wednesday, giving up three runs (two earned) on eight hits and five walks with four strikeouts over 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nova is coming off another quality start, his ninth in 11 starts this season. The veteran has pitched at least six innings every time out this year. The former Yankee has plenty of experience at Camden Yards, where he has a 5.44 ERA in eight outings.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty went seven strong innings and picked up the win on Thursday night against Boston, walking just one batter in a much-improved command game. Miley’s season ERA dropped to 2.82.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl’s up-and-down season continued Wednesday, when he held the high-scoring D-backs to two runs on three hits in five innings before being lifted for a pinch-hitter. Kuhl has been better on the road (3.80 ERA) than at PNC Park (7.71) this season.

home_pitcher_note: Cole is coming off of three straight starts where he didn't reach the sixth. Against the Mets on Friday, the righty allowed seven runs on eight hits, including three homers in five innings. After getting his ERA down to 2.84 mid-May, it's up to 4.27.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez was electric in his last performance, striking out 10 and recording the sixth no-hitter in Marlins history. He'll take the mound dealing with right ankle discomfort originating from a collision with Rey Fuentes on the first out of that game.

home_pitcher_note: Last time out, Glasnow allowed four runs on five hits, including a season-high three home runs. The righty has given up at least one home run in six of his last seven outings. Glasnow is now 2-5 with a 6.97 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Worley has made three starts this season, allowing 10 runs in 12 2/3 innings over those outings. He'll continue to start as Justin Nicolino works back from the DL. Nicolino will be eligible to come off the DL on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Williams is coming off of one of his best outings of the season: one run on seven hits in a season-high seven innings. The righty threw 95 pitches, which is the most he’s thrown all season. After his last start, Williams lowered his ERA to 4.57.
away_pitcher_note: Straily has been solid of late, and hasn't allowed more than three runs in an outing over his last six starts. The right-hander is coming off an outing against the Cubs in which he allowed three runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nova gave up a season-high three home runs in his last start Sunday against the Orioles, but he still earned another quality start, allowing three earned runs in six innings. He has given the Pirates a quality start in 10 of his 12 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Locke ran into some trouble in his last start against the Cubs, allowing four runs in 4 2/3 innings. The lefty has only made two starts after missing the first two months of the year due to injury.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon will be making his first start since May 3 after undergoing surgery for testicular cancer. He posted a 3.31 ERA in six starts before his diagnosis. He allowed five runs in six innings, striking out nine in his final rehab start at Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland held the Indians to one run and six hits, with five strikeouts in 6 1/3 innings in his last start, a win. He wanted to finish the seventh, but he was pulled at 100 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Cole struggled again in his last start Thursday against the Marlins, surrendering seven runs on 11 hits in only 4 2/3 innings. He has posted a 10.71 ERA (23 earned runs in 19 1/3 innings) in his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his past three road starts, Chatwood has held opponents to nine hits and two earned runs in 21 innings. Those games resulted in wins at Philadelphia on May 24, San Diego on June 3 and Thursday at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl is coming off back-to-back solid outings, allowing three earned runs in 10 innings in that span. He has never faced the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez has struggled in his past two starts. In a loss at San Diego, he was hit on the right hand by a batted ball, and in a no-decision at Chicago, a tight early strike zone upped his pitch count.

home_pitcher_note: Williams labored in his last start against the Marlins on Saturday, allowing five runs on six hits in just four innings. He surrendered two earned runs on five hits in five innings during two relief appearances against the Cubs earlier in the season.
away_pitcher_note: Butler will make his seventh start of the season on Friday. He's coming off a loss to the Rockies in which he gave up three runs over five innings. He needs to keep his pitch count down and go deeper in games.

home_pitcher_note: Nova struck out four batters and only gave up one hit in six scoreless innings against the Marlins in his last start on Sunday. He has earned a quality start in 11 of his 13 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta will try to get back on track, making his second start of the season against the Pirates. He's been bothered by a small cut on his right thumb, which isn't a big deal, but it has limited the amount of throwing he's done between starts.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon scattered five hits in five scoreless innings in his first start since being diagnosed with testicular cancer in early May. He produced a quality outing in his last start against Chicago, limiting the Cubs to one run in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey is coming off a bad outing against the Mets in which he served up three home runs over five innings. He's given up 11 homers in his last six starts, and 19 already this season. He's 3-3 with a 5.40 ERA on the road this year.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start off the disabled list Wednesday, Garza allowed four runs in five innings against the Cardinals but got the win. He threw seven innings of one-run ball earlier this season vs. the Pirates on May 6.
away_pitcher_note: Cole got back on track against the Rockies on Tuesday, firing seven one-run innings with three strikeouts. It was a good sign for Cole following a four-start, 10.71 ERA stretch. He has a 5.74 career ERA at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Davies allowed two runs in 5 2/3 innings against the Pirates earlier this season. The right-hander has allowed seven runs over his last four outings at Miller Park and has made his last two starts on the road.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates lost for the 10th time in Kuhl’s 13 starts on Wednesday, when he allowed three runs in five innings against the Rockies. Kuhl has not pitched more than five innings since April 18, and his lone win came in his first start.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing four first-inning runs to the Padres in his last outing, Guerra finished with five hitless frames. In his last three starts at Miller Park, Guerra has allowed five earned runs over 16 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Williams gave up three runs in an ugly first Friday, but recovered to retire the last 12 he faced, getting through five frames vs. the Cubs with no further damage. Williams has a 4.06 ERA in his last seven starts, and the Bucs are 5-2 in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Over Anderson's last five outings, totaling 34 2/3 innings, the right-hander has allowed four runs. Three of those came in his last start vs. the Padres when he allowed his first two homers since May 21.
away_pitcher_note: Nova is coming off two straight wins, including a seven-inning start vs. the Cubs on Saturday. In 12 IP vs. the Brewers, all in '16, Nova has fanned 10 and given up two homers, to Jonathan Villar (on the DL) and Chris Carter (now with the Yankees).

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright is coming off a career-short 1 2/3-inning start in which he tied a career high for runs (nine) and homers (three) allowed. He’s given up nine runs in two of his past three starts following a four-start stretch in which he gave up one run.
away_pitcher_note: Taillon is coming off a rough loss to the Cubs when he allowed four runs on eight hits in five innings. He allowed two runs over five innings in his only career start against the Cardinals, which came last season.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn has not finished six innings in any of his past five starts, and he lasted just 4 2/3 his last time out. In that loss, Lynn gave up a season-high seven runs and served up four homers for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: Cole threw seven strong innings for the second straight start on Monday in an 8-1 win over the Brewers. The right-hander is 3-4 with a 5.01 ERA in eight start on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: Leake dominates the Pirates more than any other team he's consistently faced in his career. His 3.29 ERA against Pittsburgh in 29 starts is his best vs. any team against which he's made double-digit starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl will make his second straight road start after earning a win against the Brewers on Tuesday. It took the righty 98 pitches to get through five innings, but he allowed just two earned runs and struck out six of the 25 batters he faced.

home_pitcher_note: Williams struck out a career-high seven batters while allowing three runs in six innings Wednesday at Miller Park. He has pitched into the sixth inning in five of his nine starts since moving out of the bullpen. He has a 5.34 ERA at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: In a 6-5 win over the Reds, Cobb delivered his third straight quality start and seventh in his last 10 games. He completed seven innings, striking out six and allowing two runs. It was his second straight outing of more than 110 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Nova allowed four runs on 11 hits in seven innings and lost to the Brewers on Thursday at Miller Park. He has pitched at least six innings in each of his 15 starts this season. The veteran owns a 2.53 ERA in seven home outings this year.
away_pitcher_note: Snell rejoins the rotation after making adjustments in Triple-A. Something clicked: he struck out 61 in 44 innings with a 2.66 ERA in Durham after fanning 34 in 42 innings with a 6.00 ERA with the Rays. He surpassed five innings in each start.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon threw six strong innings and struck out seven on Friday while holding the Cardinals to two runs on four hits at Busch Stadium. Since undergoing surgery for testicular cancer, Taillon has posted a 3.38 ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Archer received plenty of run support in a 15-5 win over the O's. The offense took care of the Rays righty, who wasn’t at his best: he gave up five runs (four earned) in six innings, with seven hits against. He also had a season-low four strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Cole put together a third straight strong outing against the Cardinals on Saturday, holding them to one run over six innings. Cole has posted a 1.35 ERA in his last three starts. He owns a 1.59 ERA in four career starts against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto, coming off a one-run, seven-inning effort, dropped his ERA from 4.42 to 4.20 following his start vs. the Mets. Although he has just one win in his last five starts, Cueto has been consistently strong with a 3.82 ERA in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl pitched into the sixth inning Sunday for the first time since April 18, but he wasn’t able to record an out. He was charged with four runs on eight hits while striking out six Cardinals. He has a 7.36 ERA in eight home starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Moore has struggled to find his touch recently -- an 8.85 ERA in his last four starts. Giants manager Bruce Bochy said this week Moore will remain part of the team’s rotation. “It's really I think important to keep him going,” Bochy said.

home_pitcher_note: Williams continues to prove worthy of the spot he has claimed in the rotation, posting a 3.91 ERA in his last nine starts. Tuesday may have been his best effort, as he held the Rays to 2 runs while striking out 7 and pitching into the eighth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija received an outpouring of run support in his last start for his third win of the season. The right-hander has a sub-four ERA (3.91) since the beginning of May but just three wins to show for his strong effort.

home_pitcher_note: Nola went 3-2 with a 3.24 ERA in five starts in June, but he has allowed just three earned runs in 14 1/3 innings in his last two starts. The Phillies hope he is returning to the form that made him a first-round pick in 2014.
away_pitcher_note: On Wednesday, Nova was unable to complete 6 innings for the first time in 16 starts this season; he had to settle for 5 innings with 2 runs allowed and only 1 strikeout. Nova remains dominant at PNC Park, posting a 2.63 ERA in 8 home outings.

home_pitcher_note: Leiter makes his third start in place of right-hander Jerad Eickhoff, who is on the 10-day disabled list with a strained upper back. Leiter allowed four runs in five innings in his last start against the Mariners in Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: Jameson Taillon will face the Phillies for the second time in his career Tuesday. He threw six innings and allowed three earned run while striking out seven when he pitched against Philadelphia in Pittsburgh last July.

home_pitcher_note: Lively walked four batters in his first two innings Friday against the Mets, but worked out of both jams. He settled down, allowing just two runs in 6 1/3 innings as the rookie continues to put up solid results.
away_pitcher_note: Cole allowed seven runs on 10 hits in 5 1/3 innings Friday against the Giants. He has given up 18 home runs in 17 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson is in the trade rumor mill again as the July 31 non-waiver Trade Deadline approaches. He is a free agent after the season, and the rebuilding Phillies hope to send him to a contender for a prospect or two.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl flirted with a no-hitter against the Giants on Saturday, going into the sixth without allowing a hit. He still allowed just one run on two hits in six innings, earning his first quality start since April 18.

home_pitcher_note: Butler cruised through the first three innings of his last start and then lost control. He gave up four runs in 3 2/3 innings and took the loss. He did not get a decision vs. the Bucs on June 16, going 5 2/3 innings. He's 2-1 with a 3.18 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Williams has seen the Cubs three times but just once as a starter (this June) when he allowed three runs on four hits, walked two, and struck out three across five innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta is coming off possibly his best start of the season in which he held the Reds to one hit over seven scoreless innings. The right-hander had good command of his pitches. He's 3-0 with a 3.86 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Nova has faced the Cubs twice in his career, allowing four earned runs in 12 1/3 innings (2.92 ERA). He last pitched against Chicago on June 17, allowing three runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lester served up six runs to the Rays in his last start, the most he's allowed at Wrigley Field since Aug. 19, 2015. He's 3-2 with a 3.19 ERA in 10 home starts. He faced the Pirates on April 16, throwing seven shutout innings at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: Replacing Jameson Taillon -- who has flu-like symptoms -- Chad Kuhl goes on just two days' rest after throwing 95 pitches over seven innings Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing seven earned runs in two straight outings on June 2 and 8, Cole bounced back over the final stretch of the first half, allowing two runs or fewer in four of his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Leake pitched just 3 2/3 innings, allowing eight runs on nine hits against the Marlins. In his three starts before that, however, he gave up six runs through 20 innings, including an 8-4 win over the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Scratched from his last start due to food poisoning, Taillon will start the second game of the second half. He finished the first half 5-2 with a 2.73 ERA. He owns a 3.27 ERA in two career starts against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn had an impressive outing in his last start, holding the Mets scoreless through seven innings and allowing just three hits. He has two starts this year of seven scoreless innings, with the other vs. the Pirates on April 17.
