home_pitcher_note: This start wraps up what has been one of Gonzalez’s best seasons. He could finish with the lowest ERA of his career and reach 200 innings for the first time since 2011. That could earn him consideration for the NL Cy Young Award.
away_pitcher_note: Brault will make his fourth start as the Pirates end their season in Washington. His Triple-A success has followed him to Pittsburgh, as he has posted a 2.37 ERA in 19 innings over his last four appearances (three starts).

away_pitcher_note: Bailey was effective Opening Day vs. Washington and the only run that scored against him in six innings was in the first inning after a double play was broken up. The recipient of three elbow surgeries showed good command of all his pitches.

away_pitcher_note: During a 13-7 loss to the Nationals on Saturday, Castillo notched six strikeouts and walked just one batter, but he wasn't sharp in his first start of the season. He lacked good command of his fastball, but was at least able to throw strikes.

away_pitcher_note: Romano lacked his changeup and curveball in a 6-5 loss to the Nats on Sunday and lived on his sinker. Despite a 34-pitch first inning with two runs, he grinded through and did well for six innings and it gave him confidence.

away_pitcher_note: Nova pitched five effective innings, but he struggled in a snowy sixth and lost on Wednesday. Nova is 2-1 with a 4.09 ERA in four career starts against the Cubs, three of those starts were last year.

away_pitcher_note: Williams has started the season on a high note, posting a 2.63 ERA in seven starts, but he took the loss his last time out by allowing a season-high three runs over 5 2/3 innings in a loss to the Nationals. Williams has never faced the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: After two brutal starts, Taillon has taken steps in the right direction his last two times out. He held Milwaukee to one run over five innings on Saturday. Taillon will be the first Pirates pitcher to face former teammate Andrew McCutchen as a Giant.
away_pitcher_note: Suarez is coming off his first Major League victory in three starts. As much as anything else, he has displayed impressive maturity despite his lack of Major League experience.

home_pitcher_note: Nova fell victim to some bad bounces, poor execution and long at-bats as he pitched only two innings of the Pirates' comeback win over the White Sox on Tuesday. After a strong April, Nova has given up 13 runs (10 earned) in 6 2/3 innings this month.
away_pitcher_note: Though Holland's numbers overall are less than impressive, he has shown isolated stretches of effective stuff, giving the Giants hope that he can put it all together soon.

home_pitcher_note: Williams faced the White Sox at Guaranteed Rate Field on Wednesday, allowing four runs on a pair of homers over five innings. After completing six innings in five of his first six starts, Williams hasn't done so in either of his past two outings.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez gets his second crack at the Pirates after going 7 1/3 with a no-decision in last Wednesday's loss. The right-hander made it into the 8th for the first time, but he looks for a better result against the Bucs this time around.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon left his last start vs. the Giants after just three innings due to a finger laceration on his right hand. Including those three frames, Taillon has allowed one run over his last two starts, spanning eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Santiago will make his third start of the season and first since May 5, when he gave up a season-high 8 earned runs in 3 1/3 innings against the Twins. In his first start, against the Royals, he gave up just two runs in 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chad Kuhl goes for his fifth win this season against the Padres on Thursday. Kuhl has worked at least 5 innings in seven of his eight starts, and is coming off a quality start against San Francisco on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old lefty is looking to bounce back from a dreadful Petco Park debut in which he allowed four homers and six runs over 2 2/3. Most concerning: His fastball velocity dipped to 89 mph and he struggled to locate the pitch.

home_pitcher_note: After throwing at least five innings in each of his first six starts, Nova is battling through a rough three-game stretch in May, during which he's allowed 14 earned runs on 25 hits in 12 1/3 innings pitched.

away_pitcher_note: On Sunday, the veteran left-hander became the first pitcher to record back-to-back eight-inning starts for the Padres since Andrew Cashner in 2014. Richard has bounced back from a rough month with 18 K's in those last two outings.

away_pitcher_note: The cut on Taillon’s middle finger held up well enough as he allowed two runs over 5 2/3 innings vs. the White Sox on Wednesday. Though he’s been interrupted by injury, Taillon has posted a 1.98 ERA with 11 strikeouts in 13 2/3 innings in May.

away_pitcher_note: Kuhl followed up two quality starts with a short, uneven outing against the Padres on Thursday, pitching two perfect frames before giving up four runs and exiting after 4 1/3 innings. He has a 3.24 ERA in three career starts against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Castillo made it five innings in his last start against Chicago, scattering one run on six hits, but did not factor in the decision. He'd won each of his previous two outings before that and reached the sixth inning in both of those starts.
away_pitcher_note: Nova believes he is moving in the right direction after holding the Padres to three runs (two earned) over six innings on Friday, his first quality start since April 26. The veteran right-hander is 1-4 with a 5.08 ERA in five starts at GABP.

home_pitcher_note: Set back all spring by a strained shoulder, Musgrove will finally make his Pirates debut against the Cardinals. He should be free of restrictions after a four-start rehab assignment. Musgrove lost his only career start at PNC Park on Aug. 23, 2016.
away_pitcher_note: This will be the third start of the year for Gant (1-1, 4.67), who has filled in for injured veterans Adam Wainwright and Carlos Martinez. Gant allowed five runs (three earned) over 4 1/3 innings his last time out against the Phillies on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Williams gave up four runs in six innings while striking out five against his hometown Padres on Sunday. After recording five quality starts in April, Williams has logged just one in his four May outings. He has a 2.97 ERA at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Flaherty, who is coming off his first win of the season, will pitch the middle game against the Pirates. The right-hander went 7 2/3 innings against the Phillies on Sunday, logging 13 strikeouts and allowing one run.

away_pitcher_note: Mikolas will look to go 7-0 to start the season in the series finale against the Pirates. The right-hander tossed his first career shutout on Monday against the Royals, allowing just four hits to go with nine strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl allowed just one earned run while registering six strikeouts over six innings against the Reds on Wednesday. Despite earning three straight no-decisions, the Pirates have won the last four games he's started on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Montgomery will make his first start of the year as the Cubs shuffle their rotation to compensate for the absence of Yu Darvish, who is on the DL. In 2017, Montgomery was 5-5 with a 4.15 ERA in 14 starts. He leads Cubs relievers in innings pitched.

home_pitcher_note: Kingham was recalled after Ivan Nova was placed on the disabled list with a sprained ligament in his right ring finger. Kingham has made three starts for the Pirates this season, allowing seven earned runs with 21 strikeouts over 18 1/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Archer made one mistake, a fastball that Buster Posey hit for a three-run homer, and paid for it in a 3-2 loss to the Giants on Sunday. Pitching on seven days' rest, the righty said his stuff was not sharp. He'll be on regular rest vs. the Dodgers.

away_pitcher_note: After holding the D-backs to two runs over seven innings on Tuesday night, Williams will face another NL West opponent. He has thrown a quality start in each of his five outings this season, and he owns a 1.67 ERA in 18 starts dating back to July 11.

home_pitcher_note: Sampson threw three scoreless innings in relief against the Athletics on Wednesday. He allowed two runs in 4 1/3 innings against the Astros in his last start on April 20. Left-handers are hitting .235 off him while right-handers are hitting .313.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles is coming off his toughest start of the season, in which he allowed five runs (four earned) in five innings at home against the D-backs. He'd allowed one run total in his first three starts combined.

away_pitcher_note: Taillon will aim to right the ship after getting tagged for five runs in five innings during his last time out vs. Arizona. He heads into Wednesday’s series finale against Texas with a 1-3 record and 4.06 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: After looking like the A's best pitcher through his first four starts, Anderson has not completed five innings in his past two outings. He has pitched well at PNC Park, though: 1-0 with a 1.38 in two career starts.

away_pitcher_note: Originally called up last month to fill in for the injured Marco Estrada, Bassitt has been a more than adequate replacement. The right-hander has allowed just one run over his first two starts with an impressive 16-4 strikeout-to-walk ratio in 12 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles was inefficient on Tuesday night in Texas, working only four innings on 96 pitches, but he held the hot-hitting Rangers to only two runs. He'll try to work deeper into the game at PNC Park, where he has a 2.25 ERA in three starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Montas has been the A's top pitcher this year, but his last start was bizarre as a Jurickson Profar error on a potential double-play ball opened the floodgates for six unearned runs. This will be his first career start against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: With two starters injured, Brault will come out of the bullpen to make his first MLB start in more than a year. The lefty's last outing was on Tuesday in Texas, where he struck out three in two scoreless innings and saw his fastball velocity tick up.
away_pitcher_note: Sampson threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings against the Pirates last Tuesday in Arlington. He allowed five hits, struck out five and did not walk a batter. He has not allowed a run in his last 9 2/3 innings over his last three appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Kingham has been up-and-down as a reliever this season, but he's hoping for better results as he steps back into the rotation against the Rangers at PNC Park. He has allowed nine runs while striking out 13 in 12 2/3 innings over eight relief outings.
away_pitcher_note: Miller faced the Pirates last Wednesday in Arlington and allowed four runs over 3 1/3 innings in a 7-5 loss, with all four runs having scored in the fourth inning. He has allowed three or more runs in a single frame in each of his last five starts.

away_pitcher_note: Musgrove is looking to bounce back from his first bad start of the year after allowing seven runs (five earned) while recording only eight outs in a 14-1 loss to the A's on Friday. He owns a 1.23 ERA in four road outings so far this season.

home_pitcher_note: Before allowing a season-high six runs his last time out, Wainwright had arguably been the team's most consistent starter. But he's yet to complete seven innings in an outing this year, and he's been pushed to 100 pitches just once.
away_pitcher_note: Williams completed six innings for the seventh time in seven starts on Saturday as he held Oakland to four runs while striking out five. He faced the Cardinals six times last season and went 2-2 with a 4.94 ERA in those outings.

home_pitcher_note: Mikolas threw a gem -- seven shutout innings -- on Monday and has recently looked much like his dominant self from 2018. That's in large part due to a reemerging curveball, which Mikolas is using more frequently and with greater success.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles bounced back from a four-inning start in Texas by holding the A's to one run on five hits over 6 2/3 innings on Sunday. Relying more than ever on his fastball and curveball, Lyles has allowed more than two runs in only one of his six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson had his last start complicated by errors around him, which led to six unearned runs. But he's also still having trouble getting left-handed hitters out and executing his sinker consistently. Both need to improve for him to stick as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Brault handled himself well in his first start in more than a year, allowing two runs in four innings while striking out five. He hopes to pitch deeper into the game at Busch Stadium, where he has allowed only one earned run in 9 1/3 career innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ray got a no-decision in his last outing against the Rays when he threw 5 2/3 shutout innings and struck out 11. He is six strikeouts away from 800 for his career and would be the second fastest lefty in terms of games pitched to reach that mark.
away_pitcher_note: Kingham will remain in the rotation for at least one more start after moving from the bullpen to start against the Rangers on Wednesday. Kingham allowed two runs in four innings but should be able to go deeper into games after increasing his workload.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver has allowed one run over seven innings in each of his last two starts. He gave up five runs (four earned) on Opening Day but since has not allowed more than three runs in any of his seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Musgrove will try to get back on track after his excellent April turned into a disastrous May. He has allowed 15 runs (13 earned) in 5 2/3 innings over his past two starts. He put together a quality start against the D-backs at PNC Park on April 22.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke has allowed five total runs over his last five starts, and he threw at least six innings in all of them. He faced the Pirates earlier this year and allowed just two hits in seven shutout innings.
away_pitcher_note: Archer will rejoin the rotation after missing more than two weeks with right thumb inflammation. The injury played a part in Archer's struggles on April 26, when he allowed six runs in four innings. The Bucs have lost four of his first five starts.

home_pitcher_note: The second-year left-hander was knocked around for eight runs over three innings in Colorado in his last time out. Lauer has yet to eclipse the six-inning mark this season, and he's not getting whiffs against his slider, like he did last season.
away_pitcher_note: Williams, coming off an excellent seven-inning, one-run start in St. Louis, will make his second career appearance in his hometown of San Diego. A longtime Padres fan growing up, Williams allowed four runs in 4 2/3 innings last year at Petco Park.

home_pitcher_note: The Padres want Lucchesi, who worked 5 1/3 innings of one-run ball on Saturday, to throw more strikes. But he's managed to limit his walks lately. Lucchesi's 3.37 FIP is 1.2 points lower than his ERA, indicating he could be due for a turnaround.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles will see some former Padres teammates in his return to San Diego, a familiar environment for the longtime NL West pitcher. Lyles has allowed one run or less in five of his seven starts. He owns a 4.42 ERA in 22 career appearances at Petco Park.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie lefty used a deceptive four-pitch mix to great success early this season, despite a fastball in the high 80s mph. But the league is making adjustments. Margevicius has allowed eight earned runs and 15 hits in his last two starts (10 2/3 IP).
away_pitcher_note: DuRapau will be the Pirates' "opener," the first time they have turned to a reliever for a short start. The 27-year-old rookie last started a game in 2011, his first pro season. He was a 32nd-round Draft pick by the Pirates in 2014.

home_pitcher_note: The Padres will dip into the Minors and go with Cal Quantrill to cap the four-game series with the Pirates. Quantrill (0-1), a former first-round pick from the 2016 Draft, is making his third start after the Padres lost in his two previous outings.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing only one hit over seven scoreless innings on Tuesday in Arizona, Musgrove will start the series finale in his hometown of San Diego. The righty enjoyed his Petco Park homecoming last year, firing seven scoreless innings on June 29.

home_pitcher_note: Archer went just 3 2/3 innings on Wednesday at Arizona in his first start after spending time on the injured list (right thumb inflammation). He allowed seven runs (six earned), four hits and four walks. His walk rate is a career-worst 4.7 per nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez gave up five early runs at Boston in his last start, then settled in and lasted 6 1/3 innings. His 2.55 road ERA ranked sixth in the National League.

home_pitcher_note: DuRapau will serve his second stint as the Pirates' opener after a successful first effort Saturday in San Diego. DuRapau struck out four over two scoreless innings against the Padres, setting up a well-executed bullpen game that the Bucs won, 7-2.
away_pitcher_note: Gray struck out eight but lasted just 4 2/3 innings in his last start, a loss at Philadelphia. He has high strikeouts (59 in 53 1/3 innings), but also has given up 10 home runs in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles is coming off his best start with the Pirates -- seven innings, one run, five hits, one walk and a career-high 12 strikeouts on Friday at San Diego. He’s pitching up in the zone with his fastball, making his curve and other offspeed stuff more effective.
away_pitcher_note: Battling a Phillies lineup that took close pitches and worked counts, Senzatela threw 101 pitches over five innings in his last start. But he limited the damage to two runs.

home_pitcher_note: As the "opener," Feliz will make his first career start in the series opener against Los Angeles. The 25-year-old has only faced the Dodgers once in his career, allowing two runs on two hits and two walks over two innings.
away_pitcher_note: Buehler was sharp his last time out, a six-inning effort during which he struck out seven and didn't walk a batter but took his first loss of the season when the Dodgers were shut out behind him. He has never faced the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Musgrove bounced back well after a two-start skid, winning each of his past two outings while allowing four runs (three earned) in 13 1/3 innings vs. the D-backs and Padres. He allowed three runs (one earned) in 6 2/3 innings vs. L.A. on April 27.
away_pitcher_note: Ryu is on a tear in May, having allowed just one run and posted a 0.28 ERA over four starts in the month. The lefty is 5-0 in his career against the Pirates with a 2.51 ERA over five starts (32 1/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Archer pitched better last time out, but he has allowed 11 runs (nine earned) on 10 hits and six walks over 8 2/3 innings in two starts since coming off the injured list. He lost to the Dodgers while pitching with an injured right thumb on April 26.
away_pitcher_note: Maeda will be seeing his first action since sustaining a left adductor contusion on May 15. The righty fanned a season-high 12 in that game while tossing 6 2/3 scoreless innings against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Castillo was not effective Wednesday and lasted a season-low 2 2/3 innings allowing four runs, five hits and three walks during an 11-9 loss at Milwaukee. In six career starts vs. Pittsburgh, he is 1-3 with a 3.58 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Kingham will step back into the rotation after allowing 13 runs on 19 hits in eight innings over his last two outings. The Pirates have lost the last seven games in which the right-hander has appeared.

home_pitcher_note: Gray tied a season high with nine strikeouts over six innings Tuesday, but worked out of jams while the Reds earned the 3-0 shutout win over the Brewers. In two career appearances at PNC Park (one start), he has a 1.04 ERA with no walks and 10 strikeouts over 8 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After adding a slider to his arsenal earlier this season, Keller will make his MLB debut in the nightcap of Monday's doubleheader. The Pirates' top prospect has rounded into form, going 5-0 with a 3.05 ERA and 47 strikeouts in his last seven Triple-A starts.

home_pitcher_note: Sims is being recalled from Triple-A Louisville to make the start. In nine games this season for Louisville, he is 3-0 with a 4.06 ERA. But he has a 2.37 ERA over his past three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles worked five clean innings against the Rockies on Thursday then gave up six runs in the sixth, which he couldn't finish. The Pirates picked him up after a rare slip-up and won, 14-6. The Bucs have won eight of Lyles' nine starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: DeSclafani has struggled in each of his past three starts as none has gone past four innings. He has lacked the location of his curveball, perhaps a reason he has tied a career high with three homers allowed in each of his past two starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates will abandon the opener in front of Brault in Wednesday's series finale. The lefty pitched better his last time out, holding the Dodgers to two runs on three hits in 5 2/3 innings, but he'll need to prove himself to stick in the rotation.

away_pitcher_note: Chacin has lost his last three starts, surrendering eight earned runs in 16 innings over that span. He allowed four runs in five innings in a loss against Philadelphia last time out.

away_pitcher_note: Woodruff is coming off a dominant outing vs. Philadelphia. He allowed one hit -- a solo homer by Andrew Knapp -- in eight innings and had a season-high 10 strikeouts. Woodruff hasn't allowed more than two runs in any of his past six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles avoided the IL after leaving his last start with left hamstring discomfort, a bit of good news for the Pirates. He'll face his former team, the Brewers, who helped him fine-tune the pitch mix that's led to his early success in Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Davies, who rebounded from his worst start of the year to work six scoreless innings his last time out, earns this start in place of Gio Gonzalez, who's sidelined with a tired arm.

home_pitcher_note: Brault is coming off one of his best starts in the Majors, as he shut out the Reds for 5 1/3 innings on Wednesday. He's only allowed two runs on six hits over his last 11 innings, the result of mechanical work with Pittsburgh's pitching coaches.
away_pitcher_note: Fried struggled to command his curveball as he surrendered a pair of season highs -- nine hits and three walks -- in Tuesday's loss to the Nationals. The lefty will be starting with two extra days of rest.

home_pitcher_note: May was a struggle for Musgrove, who allowed 30 runs in 30 innings over six starts. The Pirates always know they'll get innings from Musgrove, who has completed at least six innings in eight of his 11 starts this year.

away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has allowed 13 homers through 38 1/3 innings, four fewer than he surrenderd over 183 innings last year. His fastball and slider have significantly improved over his past three starts, but he's still battling inconsistent command.

away_pitcher_note: Davis will make his first MLB start since Sept. 20, 2017, as he steps into the rotation in place of righty Nick Kingham. Davis has allowed five runs on eight hits and three walks while striking out eight in 7 2/3 innings over four relief appearances.

away_pitcher_note: Lyles will make his second straight start against the Brewers after primarily using his fastball and curveball in a 4-2 loss at PNC Park on Sunday. Lyles allowed four runs on eight hits and struck out five while throwing 109 pitches in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson had mostly avoided his trouble with the long ball that marred his 2018 season, but that issue returned in his last start against the Marlins. Miami hit three homers against Anderson in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Brault will get another shot to start after working only four innings vs. the Braves on Tuesday night. Brault has more walks (12) than strikeouts (11) in his past 18 1/3 innings, but he's only allowed six runs (five earned) in those four appearances.

home_pitcher_note: With the Braves signing Dallas Keuchel and Gausman giving up 15 combined runs over his past two starts, his spot in the rotation could be in jeopardy. He faces the Bucs for the second straight outing, having allowed seven runs on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Musgrove may have turned his season around on Wednesday, when he held the Braves to three runs over a career-high eight innings at PNC Park. He leaned on his four-seamer and curveball in that outing, striking out six and walking only one.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz continues to be hurt by the homer since his return from the IL, surrendering 15 through 44 1/3 innings -- two fewer than he gave up during last year's All-Star campaign in 183 frames. Folty faces the Bucs for the second straight start.
away_pitcher_note: Archer is coming off a pair of strong starts, when he walked four batters in 13 innings after walking 12 in his three previous starts. He limited the Braves to one run while striking out six over six innings at home on Thursday.

away_pitcher_note: Musgrove was ejected after throwing 18 pitches in the first inning on Monday, but he will get another chance to face the Braves in the series finale. He pitched into the ninth inning against Atlanta in his last full start on June 5.

home_pitcher_note: Richards enters Friday coming off one of his best outings of the season. away_pitcher_note: Brault is coming off his best start of the season, as he worked into the seventh inning for the first time in his career while holding Milwaukee to two runs on Sunday at Miller Park. He has a 2.55 ERA in 24 2/3 innings over his last five outings.

home_pitcher_note: In two June starts, Lopez has a 0.75 ERA in 12 innings, and in his last three starts, he has allowed 2 earned runs in 18 innings with 19 strikeouts and three walks. Yet, he has one win to show for it in those games. Lopez's ERA at home this season is 1.78.
away_pitcher_note: Agrazal, who has gone 5-3 with a 3.27 ERA in 12 starts at Double-A and Triple-A this year, will make his Major League debut against Miami. Previously on Pittsburgh’s 40-man roster, Agrazal was removed in January before being re-invited to big league camp.

home_pitcher_note: After walking four in five-plus innings in a loss to the Cardinals, manager Don Mattingly spoke about wanting Alcantara to be more on the attack. He is averaging 6.2 K/9 and 4.3 BB/9. At home, the right-hander is 2-4 with a 3.25 ERA in seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: After two encouraging outings, Archer struggled vs. the Braves on Tuesday in Atlanta. The righty gave up five home runs, including four solo shots in one inning, though he struck out eight in six innings. He has allowed 16 homers in 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Top prospect Keller gets his third big league start when the Pirates open a five-game homestand following a 10-game trip and an off-day. Keller has struggled in his first two outings -- both on the road. Opponents are hitting .472.
away_pitcher_note: Norris makes his fourth Interleague start this season, looking for his first win of the bunch after having taken a loss in Atlanta and hard-luck no-decisions against the Marlins and Phillies. He’s 1-for-4 at the plate in 2019 with a run scored.

away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has been on the injured list since April 26 with a right UCL sprain. He completed two rehab outings in June, allowing three homers and six runs over 7 1/3 innings and the right-hander yielded six home runs over 30 1/3 innings before going on the IL.

away_pitcher_note: Save for his Coors Field struggles, Lauer has been excellent of late. In his last 10 starts, he's held the opposition to two earned runs or fewer seven times. But he also had starts in Colorado where he coughed up five runs and eight runs during that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Archer battled through a rough fourth inning and completed five frames with eight strikeouts in the Pirates' win over the Marlins on Sunday in Miami. The veteran righty owns a 7.33 ERA with only one quality start over his last nine appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Paddack was optioned June 12 to Class A Advanced Lake Elsinore, where he rested after throwing 65 2/3 innings in the Majors so far in 2019. But he also worked to strengthen his changeup, particularly on perfecting his arm speed for the offering.

home_pitcher_note: Brault has earned his spot in the rotation over the last month, posting a 2.05 ERA while holding opponents to a .677 OPS in 30 2/3 innings over six appearances. He has completed six innings in each of his last two starts while allowing only two runs.
away_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old lefty is quickly becoming a rotation anchor. With the Padres in need of a deep outing, Lucchesi blanked the Brewers for seven innings on Monday. His newfound cutter has given him a third weapon along with his fastball and "churve."

away_pitcher_note: Agrazal made his big league debut on June 15 at Miami, taking a no-decision after yielding three runs (two earned) over four innings. In 13 Minor League outings this year, he has a combined 3.87 ERA and 1.09 WHIP across 79 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing nine runs in five innings vs. the Braves on May 21, Anderson bounced back Thursday vs. the Cubs, allowing two earned runs (four total) in five innings. Against Miami, he’s 1-3 with a 3.96 ERA in five career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez, who rejoined the club in Buffalo, N.Y., is eligible to be activated off the 60-day injured list. He exited in the third inning of his season debut on April 3 with right biceps inflammation.

home_pitcher_note: Keller has been up and down in his results this season -- a trend he said he's noticed -- but he's coming off a strong one: five scoreless innings against the Rockies in a doubleheader sweep on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Poteet was terrific in the first three starts of his career but struggled with his execution last Friday in Boston, allowing five runs in 4 1/3 innings. His 0.84 WHIP is among the top rookie starters in MLB.

home_pitcher_note: De Jong said he feels like an entirely different pitcher than he was in 2019, when he was released by the Twins. He showed it on Sunday, allowing just one run in five innings against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Though he took the loss last Saturday in Boston, Rogers’ breakout season continued. He held the potent Red Sox lineup to a pair of runs with no walks in six innings and has now gone five straight starts without allowing more than two earned runs. He is the two-time reigning NL Rookie of the Month.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl returned from the injured list (right shoulder discomfort) on Tuesday to pitch four innings with three runs allowed in Kansas City. He has reached five innings only once this season.
away_pitcher_note: Alcantara allowed four runs, three on Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s homer, over six innings in a loss on Tuesday. That marked just the third time in 12 starts this season he has given up four earned runs or more.

home_pitcher_note: After coming off bereavement leave on Friday, Brubaker actually got an at-bat on Saturday before he makes his first start back on Tuesday. He pitched six scoreless innings vs. Colorado on May 29.
away_pitcher_note: In 11 starts this season, Buehler has recorded four wins without a loss. His 0.95 WHIP is ranked in the top 10 in the National League, and he's worked through 70 1/3 innings with a 2.82 ERA. The right-hander tossed six innings against the Cardinals on Wednesday, allowing three earned runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson felt his changeup was more effective in his start on Thursday against the Marlins, who scored three runs against him in 5 1/3 innings. It marked the first time he pitched into the sixth inning since going eight May 9.
away_pitcher_note: Gonsolin will be making his season debut after missing the first two months of the season with a shoulder injury. The right-hander made three appearances with Triple-A Oklahoma City, striking out nine over 10 1/3 innings. Gonsolin is built up to pitch five innings or 75 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Keller landed on the COVID injured list on Sunday, but GM Ben Cherington said the right-hander, who exited Friday's start due to a "heat illness," could still fill his slated start vs. the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Urías bounced back well following his worst start of the season with five innings of one-run ball against the Braves on Friday. Since the beginning of May, the left-hander has struck out 48 and walked five over seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Woodruff did not record a quality start for the first time since Opening Day. He'll look to get back on track in that area versus the Pirates, against whom he owns a 3-2 career record.

home_pitcher_note: Burnes will put his perfect 3-0 career record against the Pirates on the line in the second game of the series. In 14 career appearances (though only two starts), Burnes has struck out 34 Pittsburgh hitters in 27 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl reduced his swing-and-miss rate from his first start off the IL to his second, and it worked to his advantage. He drew a ton of weak contact from the Marlins on Sunday, resulting in an efficient six-inning outing.

home_pitcher_note: Houser goes against the Pirates at a high point of an inconsistent season. In each of his last three appearances (two starts), Houser has pitched at least five innings and not given up more than a run.
away_pitcher_note: Crowe allowed eight runs in four innings on June 1, and shortly after, he was optioned to Triple-A Indianapolis. He only pitched one inning there before he was called back up to fill Mitch Keller's spot in the Pirates' rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Lester's previous start lasted just 3 2/3 innings against the Rays on Tuesday. The southpaw had an elevated pitch count (91) and was unable to find the strike zone. He issued a season-high four walks in the no-decision outing.
away_pitcher_note: Brubaker allowed three runs in 4 2/3 innings last time out against the Dodgers. Since posting a 2.58 ERA through his first seven starts, he’s given up 15 runs across his past four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin is 2-2 with a 3.53 ERA over eight career starts against the Pirates. In five innings on Wednesday, he allowed three runs off three hits and four walks vs. the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson was tagged with a pair of solo homers by Justin Turner, but those were the only runs he allowed on Wednesday against the Dodgers. In that start, he went six innings -- the first time he'd done so in exactly a month.

home_pitcher_note: With Max Scherzer on the IL, Paolo Espino will make his second start of the season for the Nationals. On Friday he fanned five and allowed one run in 3 1/3 innings after Scherzer's early exit.
away_pitcher_note: De Jong struggled a bit with command in Milwaukee on Friday, when he issued four walks in five innings, but he was still able to limit the Brewers to two runs. He's given the Pirates five innings in all three starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl earned his fourth loss this year in his previous start, tossing 3 1/3 innings and allowing five earned runs on Saturday. The right-hander will face the Indians for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Mejía will work on short rest after being pulled from his last outing after four innings to preserve his pitch count. The Indians are trying to be creative to get through their lack of starters, and Mejía will likely remain around the 50-60 pitch count.

home_pitcher_note: Crowe fanned a career-high eight batters and allowed two runs on two hits over five innings of work in his last start in Milwaukee on Sunday. He cruised through the Brewers lineup, retiring 15 consecutive batters.
away_pitcher_note: Like J.C. Mejía, Quantrill will work on short rest and will likely stay in the 60-pitch range once again to continue the Indians' plan of piecing together their rotation. Last time out on Tuesday, Quantrill gave up one run in four frames against the Orioles, striking out four.

home_pitcher_note: In two career starts against the Indians, Brubaker owns a 9.00 ERA, both outings coming during the 2020 season. In his last start Brubaker and his slider kept the Nationals at bay, netting nine ground balls and allowing just two runs on Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Hentges will work his way back into a starting role to help fill holes in the rotation. He last worked in relief on Thursday against the Orioles, allowing one hit and striking out three in one inning.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson was hit hard for five runs in the first inning last time out in Washington. However, he gave the Pirates much-needed length, going six innings while allowing only one more run to the Nats.
away_pitcher_note: Giolito has not found great Interleague success, posting a 4-7 record with a 5.49 ERA over 14 career starts vs. National League teams. He is 1-0 vs. the Pirates, which just so happened to be the no-hitter he threw in Chicago last season.

home_pitcher_note: It was unclear how long De Jong's stay in the Majors would be when the Pirates selected his contract to start on May 30. He says each start is a job audition, and he's passed the test so far; three of his four starts have seen two runs or fewer.
away_pitcher_note: The real interest Wednesday will be in Cease’s hitting, as he enters 3-for-3 at the plate in his career from an earlier performance this season vs. the Reds. Cease is 1-4 with a 4.55 ERA over six career Interleague starts.
